values.label: Aitch-bone removed
values.definition: Refers to the meat has had the aitch-bone removed. Aitch bone is a cut of meat lying over the aitchbone

values.label: Assorted
values.definition: Refers to a description of a collection or group of various different items or things that are mixed together. It is often used to refer to a selection of different types or varieties of something, typically presented as a single package or set.

values.label: Backstrap/Backstrip
values.definition: Refers to a long, cylindrical muscle that runs along the spine on the inside of the ribs. It is located on the opposite side of the belly or brisket.

values.label: Banjo cut
values.definition: Refers to a meat cut named Banjo Cut and is named due to its oval shape after removal of the scapular and ribs from the square cut shoulder.

values.label: Belly
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that comes from the underside or abdominal area of an animal.

values.label: Blade bone
values.definition: Refers to the related cartilage, and overlying muscles (in their entirety) and fat shall be removed.

values.label: Blade removed
values.definition: Refers to the meat has had the blade bone removed. Blade bone is related cartilage, and overlying muscles (in their entirety) and fat shall be removed.

values.label: Block ready
values.definition: Refers to a large piece of meat, such as a primal or subprimal cut, before further processing into individual retail cuts.

values.label: Blood
values.definition: Refers to the process of slaughtering an animal, some blood can be collected for various purposes, such as further processing into blood-based products or used in specific culinary applications.

values.label: Bolar
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut taken from the shoulder region of a beef carcass. More specifically, it is the triangular-shaped cut located between the blade bone and the neck bone.

values.label: Boneless
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut that has been prepared by removing the bones from the piece of meat.

values.label: Bones
values.definition: Refers to the bone(s) with or without the meat.

values.label: Bottom/Bottom round
values.definition: Refers to the upper portion of the rear legs around the hip and rump area. The Bottom round comes from the Round primal.

values.label: Brain
values.definition: Refers to the organ that is a part of the central nervous system found in the heads of animals. In culinary terms, "brain" specifically refers to the brain of certain animals, usually those that are commonly consumed for food.

values.label: Breast
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut taken from the front chest area of an animal.

values.label: Brisket
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut that comes from the breast or lower chest area of an animal.

values.label: Brisket deckle off
values.definition: Refers to a specific preparation of the brisket cut where the deckle (also known as the point or deckle point) has been removed.

values.label: Brisket navel plate
values.definition: Refers to a specific part of the brisket. The navel plate is also known as the "navel end" or the "belly end" of the brisket. The brisket navel plate is the thinner, more pointy end of the brisket that tapers down towards the belly of the animal. It is located opposite to the thicker and more rectangular flat cut of the brisket.

values.label: Brisket point/Point end
values.definition: Refers to a specific part of the beef brisket. The brisket point is also known as the "point cut" or simply "point." The brisket point is the thicker, more heavily marbled, and triangular-shaped portion of the brisket. It is located on the opposite end of the brisket from the flat cut.

values.label: Butt
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut taken from the upper shoulder or the rear end of an animal, such as a pig (pork butt) or a cattle (beef butt). It is also known as "pork shoulder" or "pork butt" when sourced from a pig and "beef shoulder" or "beef butt" when sourced from cattle.

values.label: Cap off/Cap removed
values.definition: Refers to the meat cut has been trimmed to remove the layer of fat covering one side of the meat.

values.label: Cap/Cap on
values.definition: Refers to the meat cut still has a layer of fat (the "cap") covering one side of the meat.

values.label: Carcass
values.definition: Refers to the edible flesh or muscle tissue obtained from the body of an animal after it has been slaughtered and processed for consumption. When an animal is slaughtered, the body is typically referred to as a carcass until it is broken down into different cuts of meat.

values.label: Carcass side
values.definition: Refers to a specific section or portion of meat that is obtained from one side of an animal's carcass after it has been divided lengthwise.

values.label: Carcass telescoped
values.definition: Refers to the preparation from a full carcass, that the leg folded or placed into the chest cavity, a cut is made horizontally across the dorsal edge of the carcass at the junction of the 6th lumbar and 1st sacral vertebrae breaking the spine sufficiently to allow the legs to fold into the cavity of the carcass.

values.label: Centre cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion or section of meat that is obtained from the centre or middle of a larger piece, often a roast or a larger primal cut.

values.label: Chop
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion or piece of meat that is cut perpendicular to the backbone of an animal and includes a rib or bone-in portion.

values.label: Chuck
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of meat that is obtained from the front section of the animal's carcass, particularly from the shoulder and neck area. The chuck is a primal cut, and it contains a mix of muscles, connective tissue, and some bone.

values.label: Chuck roll
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut that is obtained from the chuck primal of a beef carcass. The chuck roll is a cylindrical piece of meat that runs along the front shoulder area of the animal. It is a boneless cut that consists of several muscles, connective tissue, and some fat.

values.label: Chump
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut that comes from the hindquarters of the animal, specifically the lower back and rump area. The chump is also sometimes called "chump chop" or "chump end".

values.label: Chump off
values.definition: Refers to the removal of the Chump by a cut at right angles across the leg at a specified measured distance from the acetabulum.

values.label: Chump on
values.definition: Refers to the leg prepared from a side by a straight cut through the 6th lumbar vertebrae to a point just clear of the tip of the ilium to the ventral portion of the flap. The lymph node gland (Subiliac) and gland fats situated on the flap are removed.

values.label: Clod
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of the animal that comes from the shoulder or forequarter of the animal. The clod is also known as the shoulder clod or simply "beef clod." It is a large, tough, and relatively inexpensive cut of meat that consists of various muscles, connective tissues, and some fat.

values.label: Collar butt
values.definition: Refers to a unique boneless cut that comes from the inner portions of the shoulder.

values.label: Crest
values.definition: Refers to various anatomical features appearing as a raised point or ridge, most prominently those on the head or back of an animal.

values.label: Cutaneous trunci (rose meat)
values.definition: Cutaneous Trunci or cutaneous muscle is a relatively thin muscle near the skin in the live animal. It begins on the shoulder and ends in the flank where it is much thicker. The cutaneous trunci on the beef shoulder is commonly called the Shoulder Rose. The flank portion is commonly called Elephant Ears.

values.label: Cutlet
values.definition: Refers to a thin, boneless piece of meat that is sometimes breaded and/or fried. The meat used for cutlets can come from various sources.

values.label: Diaphragm
values.definition: Refers to a large, dome-shaped muscle that separates the chest cavity (thoracic cavity) from the abdominal cavity in mammals.

values.label: Easy carve
values.definition: Refers to the process and skill of easily (low effort) cutting portions of meat, such as roast and poultry, to obtain a maximum or satisfactory number of meat portions.

values.label: Esophagus
values.definition: Refers to a muscular tube that connects the mouth to the stomach. Its primary function is to transport food from the mouth to the stomach through rhythmic contractions known as peristalsis.

values.label: Eye of forequarter
values.definition: Refers to the preparing the forequarter by removing the eye muscle portion lying along the spinous processes and transverse processes and the thoracic vertebrae. Also know as neck fillet.

values.label: Eye of loin
values.definition:
Refers to a major muscle in the beef rib and loin; lamb rack and loin; and the pork loin. It is
the longest and largest muscle in the back and is exposed when a carcass is ribbed. Also know as Longissimus dorsi, loineye.

values.label: Eye of round
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of meat obtained from the round primal section. The round primal is located on the rear leg of the animal and is known for being one of the leaner and less tender parts of the carcass. The "round eye" specifically comes from the round roast, which is a large, boneless cut that includes the eye of round muscle. The eye of round is a small, elongated, and somewhat cylindrical muscle located within the round roast.

values.label: Eye of rump/Rump eye
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of meat obtained from the rump or hindquarters of an animal, particularly from beef or lamb.

values.label: Eye of shortloin
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of meat obtained from the short loin section. It is also commonly known as the "eye of the short loin."

values.label: Fat
values.definition: Refers to the adipose tissue found in and around various cuts of meat. Additionally, there is also external fat, often referred to as "trimmable fat" or "fat cap," which is found on the surface of certain cuts of meat.

values.label: Fat removed
values.definition: Refers to the process of removing the fat from meat. Fat is adipose tissue found in and around various cuts of meat. Additionally, there is also external fat, often referred to as "trimmable fat" or "fat cap," which is found on the surface of certain cuts of meat.

values.label: Feet
values.definition: Refer to the edible parts of an animal's limbs, particularly the feet or hooves. The feet from various animals, can be consumed in certain cuisines and culinary traditions around the world.

values.label: Filleted
values.definition: Cut or prepared as a fillet.

values.label: Flank/Internal flank plate
values.definition: Refers to a meat cut that comes from the abdominal area of an animal. It is a long, flat, and lean cut of meat that is known for its rich flavor but can be relatively tough if not prepared correctly. Also known as flank plate or flank.

values.label: Flap
values.definition: Refers to a specific meat cut that comes from the abdominal area of an animal. It is also known as flap meat or flap steak.

values.label: Flat/Flat iron
values.definition: Refers to the flat iron steak which is obtained from the chuck primal section of the carcass, specifically from the top blade muscle. It is a rectangular-shaped, well-marbled cut that sits between the shoulder blade and the ribs.

values.label: Forequarter
values.definition: Refers to the front portion of an animal's carcass, specifically the front half of the body. It includes the front legs or limbs, shoulder, and associated cuts of meat.

values.label: Foreshank
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat obtained from the front leg or limb of an animal. The foreshank is located in the lower portion of the front leg, just below the shoulder and above the knee joint. Also known as front shank or shin.

values.label: Fore feet
values.definition: Refers to the front limbs or legs of an animal, typically referring to the front feet of larger animals. These front feet are also known as front trotters or front hooves.

values.label: Frenched
values.definition: Refers to a specific trimming technique applied to meat, particularly to bone-in cuts like racks of lamb, pork, or beef. When a cut of meat is frenched, the butcher or chef removes the meat and connective tissue from the ends of the bones, exposing them to create a clean and visually appealing presentation. This technique is commonly used to enhance the aesthetics of the dish. Also known as Frenching.

values.label: Half
values.definition: Refers to half of an animal.

values.label: Hanging tender
values.definition: Refers to a long, flat, and somewhat V-shaped muscle that hangs between the last rib and the loin of the animal. It is located in the plate primal section of the carcass, specifically near the diaphragm. Also known as hanger steak, onglet, butcher's steak.

values.label: Head
values.definition: Refers to the entire head of an animal. The head contains various parts, including the skull, brain, eyes, ears, snout, tongue, and sometimes the cheeks and jowls. Different cultures have varying culinary traditions and uses for the head of the animal.

values.label: Head cheek meat
values.definition: Refers to the meat from the cheeks of an animal's head.

values.label: Heart
values.definition: Refers to the muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the circulatory system of an animal. The heart is a vital organ and an edible part of the animal that is used for culinary purposes in various cuisines around the world.

values.label: Hindquarter
values.definition: Refers to the back half of an animal's carcass, specifically the rear portion of the body. It includes the hind legs or limbs, hip, and associated cuts of meat.

values.label: Hindshank
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat obtained from the lower portion of the hind leg or limb of an animal. The hindshank is located just below the knee joint, where the leg connects to the rest of the carcass.

values.label: Hind feet
values.definition: Refers to the back limbs or legs of an animal. Also known as hind trotters or hind hooves.

values.label: Hock
values.definition: Refers to the joint or the lower portion of the leg of an animal. In pigs, the hock is specifically known as the pork hock or ham hock.

values.label: Horn
values.definition: Refers to the pointed, hard, and often curved structures that grow from the heads of certain animals.

values.label: Inside
values.definition: Refers to the internal organs and offal of an animal that are removed during the process of dressing or evisceration. These organs are also commonly referred to as variety meats, organ meats, or offal.

values.label: Intestine large
values.definition: Refers to the large intestine of an animal, which is a part of the digestive system responsible for absorbing nutrients and water from the ingested food. The large intestine is also known as the colon. In certain culinary traditions, large intestines from certain animals are cleaned thoroughly and prepared as a specialty ingredient in various dishes. In culinary dishes known as chitlins, chitterlings, sausage casing, etc.

values.label: Intestine small
values.definition: Refers to the large intestine of an animal, which is a part of the digestive system responsible for absorbing nutrients and water from the ingested food. The large intestine is also known as the colon. In certain culinary traditions, large intestines from certain animals are cleaned thoroughly and prepared as a specialty ingredient in various dishes. In culinary dishes known as tripe, sausage casing, etc.

values.label: Jowl
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat from the cheek and jaw region of an animal. For pigs is also known as pork jowl or jowl bacon.

values.label: Kidney
values.definition: Refers to the organ found in the abdominal cavity that are part of the animal's urinary system and play a crucial role in filtering waste products and excess water from the blood to produce urine. Animal kidneys are also considered a type of offal or organ meat, and they have been a part of traditional diets in many cultures for centuries.

values.label: Knuckle
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that comes from the joint at the end of an animal's leg, particularly in larger animals. The knuckle is located at the lower end of the leg, where it connects to the animal's hoof. It is a part of the round primal cut, which is the rear leg of the animal. Also known as the knuckle bone or round knuckle.

values.label: Leg
values.definition: Refers to a specific primal cut of meat that comes from the hindquarters of an animal. The leg is also known as the hind leg or ham in certain animals.

values.label: Leg long cut style 1
values.definition: Refers to a leg cut is separated from the split carcass side by a straight cut approximately perpendicular to a line parallel to the vertebral column between the 6th and 7th lumbar vertebrae and passing through a point immediately anterior to the hip bone (ilium) and related cartilage. The hind foot is removed at the tarsal joint.

values.label: Leg long cut style 2
values.definition:
Refers to a leg cut that is the same as style 1 except the tail (caudal) vertebrae, flank
muscle (M. rectus abdominis), M. cutaneus trunci, and exposed lymph glands shall
be removed.

values.label: Leg long cut style 3
values.definition:
Refers to a leg cut that is the same as style 2 except that flank muscles (M. rectus
abdominis, M. obliquus internus abdominis, M. obliquus externus abdominis),
vertebrae, hip bone along with overlying lean and fat, lean and fat overlying the
quadriceps (fore cushion), M. psoas major, and M. iliacus shall be removed.

values.label: Leg outside eye
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of the leg primal cut from an animal. The outside eye is a particular muscle or portion within the leg that has distinct characteristics and culinary uses. In beef, the "leg outside eye" is commonly known as the outside round or bottom round. In pork is found in the ham primal cut. In lamb is located in the leg of lamb cut.

values.label: Lips
values.definition: Refers to the soft, fleshy, and often fatty tissues that surround the mouth of certain animals, particularly livestock and game animals.

values.label: Liver
values.definition: Refers to the large organ found in the abdominal cavity of animals, including livestock and game animals. The liver is responsible for performing essential functions such as filtering and detoxifying blood, producing bile to aid in digestion, storing certain nutrients, and metabolizing various substances in the body. the liver is considered an organ meat or offal, and it is highly valued for its nutritional richness and distinct flavour.

values.label: Loin
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of meat located along the back of an animal, between the ribcage and the pelvis. The exact location of the loin can vary slightly depending on the animal being butchered.

values.label: Long/Long cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut that involves slicing the meat parallel to its natural grain or muscle fibers. This results in longer, more elongated pieces of meat.

values.label: Lungs
values.definition: Refers to the respiratory organs found in the chest cavity of animals, including livestock and game animals. n many regions, laws and regulations govern the handling and disposal of lung tissues to prevent any risk of contamination to the food supply.

values.label: Middle
values.definition: Refers to the central portion of an animal's carcass, usually divided along the backbone.

values.label: Mixed offal
values.definition: Refers to a collection of various edible organs and organ meats from an animal, excluding the standard cuts of muscle meat. Offal, also known as variety meats or organ meats, consists of internal organs such as the liver, heart, kidneys, sweetbreads, tongue, brain, tripe (stomach lining), and sometimes even the lungs, spleen, and other lesser-known parts.

values.label: Mixed parts
values.definition: Refers to a combination of different cuts of meat and pieces obtained from an animal during the butchering process.

values.label: Mock tender
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of beef that is also known by several other names, such as Chuck Fillet Steak, Chuck Eye Steak, or Scotch Tender. This cut comes from the chuck primal, which is located in the shoulder region of the animal.

values.label: Neck
values.definition: Refers to the portion of meat from the animal's body located between the head and the shoulders.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Outside
values.definition: Refers to the outside part of an animal or meat cut.

values.label: Oyster cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of meat found in certain animals, particularly in beef and lamb. The term "oyster" is commonly used for this cut due to its shape and location, which bears a resemblance to an oyster shell.

values.label: Pair
values.definition: Refers to a pair of pieces of meat.

values.label: Pancreas
values.definition: Refers to an internal organ found in the abdominal cavity of animals, including livestock and game animals. The pancreas is a glandular organ that serves essential functions in the digestive and endocrine systems.

values.label: Partial bone
values.definition: Refers to a piece of meat that still has a portion of bone attached to it after it has been partially deboned.

values.label: Part piece
values.definition: Refers to part of an animal or meat cut.

values.label: Pistola hindquarter
values.definition: Refers to the preparation from a hindquarter by the removal of the thin flank, lateral portion ribs and portion of the navel end brisket. A cut is made commencing at the superficial inguinal lymph node separating the M. rectus abdominus and following the contour of the hip, running parallel to the bodies of the vertebrae approximately 50mm from the M. longissimus dorsi (eye muscle) to the specified rib.

values.label: Primal
values.definition: Refers to a large section of an animal carcass that is separated during the initial stages of butchering. Primal cuts are the basic, major divisions of the animal's body that form the foundation for further butchering into individual retail cuts.

values.label: Psoas minor removed
values.definition: Refers to the removal of a smaller, very skinny muscle called the psoas minor, commonly referred to as the chain, runs the length of the tenderloin and is often removed before the tenderloin is sold.

values.label: Rack
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that includes a portion of the animal's rib bones, usually from the rib section or rib primal.

values.label: Ribeye roll/Cube roll/Rack eye
values.definition: Refers to a meat cut that is a premium and highly prized cut of meat that comes from the rib primal section of the animal, specifically the ribeye area. Also known as ribeye roll, rack eye, eye of rib, cube roll or scotch fillet.

values.label: Riblets
values.definition: Refers to small, narrow, and flavorful cuts of meat that come from the ribs of an animal. Riblets are obtained by cutting the rib section into smaller pieces, creating individual portions that contain a portion of the rib bones and surrounding meat.

values.label: Ribs
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of an animal's skeletal structure that includes the bones and meat extending from the spine or backbone. Ribs are commonly obtained from various animals.

values.label: Ribs back/Baby back ribs
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of ribs obtained from the upper part of the animal's ribcage.

values.label: Ribs short/Short ribs
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of ribs that comes from the lower portion of the animal's ribcage.

values.label: Ribs spare/Spare ribs
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of ribs obtained from the lower portion of the animal's ribcage, closer to the belly.

values.label: Rib cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of meat that includes a portion of the animal's rib bones. This cut is typically obtained from the rib primal or rib section of the animal.

values.label: Rib plate
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that includes both ribs and meat from the lower belly of an animal. The rib plate cut is obtained from the rib section of the animal, and it typically extends downward to include some portions of the belly or "plate" area.

values.label: Roasting full
values.definition: Refers to the full animal carcass, suitable for roasting.

values.label: Roasting split
values.definition: Refers to a specific method of roasting where a cut of meat is split or opened along its natural seam or bone structure before being cooked.

values.label: Roast cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut that is intended for roasting. The term "roast cut" does not refer to a specific part of an animal but rather to the way the meat is prepared and cooked.

values.label: Round
values.definition: The roundcut comes from the animal's hind legs, thigh, butt, and hams.

values.label: Rump
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that comes from the hindquarters of an animal. The rump is located at the rear part of the animal, above the hind legs and just behind the loin.

values.label: Saddle
values.definition: Refers to a specific and prestigious cut of meat that includes the back and loin sections of an animal.

values.label: Semiboneless
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut where some of the bones have been removed from the meat, but not all of them. It is a term commonly used for cuts of meat that are intended to be easier to handle and cook while still retaining some of the benefits of bone-in meat.

values.label: Shank
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that comes from the lower leg portion of an animal. The shank is located between the knee and the hoof of the animal.

values.label: Shank end
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of a cut of meat or a joint that includes the shank or leg bone.

values.label: Shank off
values.definition: Refers to a specific cutting technique where the shank or leg bone is removed from a cut of meat or a joint. This technique is commonly used to create boneless cuts from portions that originally included the leg bone.

values.label: Shank on
values.definition: Refers to a specific cutting and preparation technique where the shank or leg bone is intentionally left attached to a cut of meat or a joint. This means that the meat portion includes the leg bone, typically from the lower leg of the animal.

values.label: Shortloin
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of meat obtained from the back of an animal, The shortloin is located in the upper part of the animal's back, just behind the rib section and before the sirloin.

values.label: Short/Short cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut that involves slicing the meat perpendicular to its grain, resulting in shorter and more compact pieces.

values.label: Shoulder
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of meat obtained from the upper part of an animal's front legs.

values.label: Shoulder Boston butt upper half
values.definition: Refers to a specific section of the pork shoulder cut known as the "Boston butt." The "upper half" of the Boston butt refers to a portion of the whole pork shoulder. The pork shoulder is typically divided into two parts: the upper half and the lower half. The upper half of the Boston butt contains more fat and marbling compared to the lower half.

values.label: Shoulder cushion
values.definition: Refers to a specific and relatively lesser-known cut of meat that comes from the shoulder area of an animal. The shoulder cushion is sometimes referred to as shoulder tender.

values.label: Shoulder pectoralis
values.definition: Refers to the pectoralis muscles are usually included in larger sections of shoulder meat.

values.label: Shoulder picnic lower half
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion of the shoulder cut known as the picnic shoulder or picnic ham. The shoulder picnic lower half comes from the lower portion of the front leg closer to the foot or hock area.

values.label: Shoulder teres major
values.definition: Refers to a specific and relatively lesser-known cut of meat that comes from the shoulder area of an animal. The teres major muscle is a small, triangular muscle located in the shoulder region, adjacent to the more well-known and larger shoulder tender or petite tender muscle.

values.label: Side
values.definition: Refers to one half of a large animal carcass that has been split lengthwise along the backbone. When an animal, is processed for meat, it is usually divided into two sides. Each side contains one half of the animal's carcass.

values.label: Silverside
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of beef that comes from the hindquarters of the animal. Silverside comes from the hind leg of the carcass, specifically from the outside of the upper leg, just above the knee joint.

values.label: Sirloin/Chump sirloin
values.definition: Refers to the meat cut that comes from the rear of the animal, specifically from the area along the back between the short loin and the round.

values.label: Skin on
values.definition: The animal with its skin on / with skin on.

values.label: Skirt
values.definition: Refers to a separate cut of meat that comes from the diaphragm area of the animal. It is a thin, long, and grainy cut. Also known as skirt steak.

values.label: Special trim
values.definition: Refers to a specific request or custom preparation of meat made by a customer or chef to meet their specific requirements or preferences. It involves trimming or cutting the meat in a particular way that differs from the standard or conventional cuts typically offered by the butcher.

values.label: Spencer roll
values.definition: Refers to meat trimmed from the ribs, rolled, and used for short steaks or for a roast.

values.label: Square cut/Squared
values.definition: Refers to a specific cutting technique used to prepare meat or poultry. When a piece of meat is square cut, it means that the butcher has made straight, even cuts across the meat, resulting in a block-like or square shape.

values.label: Steak
values.definition: A steak is a crosswise cut made perpendicular to the spine.

values.label: Sternum
values.definition: Refers to the breastbone, which is a bone located in the center of the chest of animals.

values.label: Stomach
values.definition: Refers to the organ that forms a part of the digestive system of animals. The stomach is responsible for breaking down and digesting food through the action of digestive juices and acids. In certain culinary traditions and cultures, the stomach is considered an edible part and used in various dishes.

values.label: Striploin
values.definition: Refers to a specific and popular cut of meat that comes from the loin primal section of the animal. The striploin is located in the loin primal section, which runs along the back of the animal, just behind the rib section and before the sirloin.

values.label: St. Louis style
values.definition: refers to a specific cut or trimming technique used for spare ribs. St. Louis style ribs are spare ribs that have been trimmed to remove the brisket bone and rib tips. The brisket bone is removed to create a rectangular and more uniform rack of ribs.

values.label: Sub-primal
values.definition: Refers to a large cut of meat that is derived from one of the primary sections of an animal carcass. The primary sections, known as "primal cuts," are large sections that are separated during the initial butchering process. Sub-primals are subsequently derived from these primal cuts and further broken down into retail cuts.

values.label: Tail on
values.definition: The animal with its tail on / with its tail.

values.label: Tail removed
values.definition: The animal with tail removed / without tail.

values.label: Tenderloin
values.definition: Refers to a specific and highly prized cut of meat that comes from the loin primal section of an animal. The tenderloin is located along the backbone, inside the ribcage, in the loin primal section of the animal.

values.label: Tendons
values.definition: Refers to the tough, fibrous connective tissues that connect muscles to bones in an animal's body.

values.label: Testicles/Testes
values.definition: Refers to the male reproductive organs of animals. In some culinary traditions and cultures, testicles are considered a type of offal or "variety meat" and are consumed as food. They are often referred to by specific names based on the animal they come from.

values.label: Thick
values.definition: Refers to the measurement or thickness of a meat cut. When the term refers to a cut of meat as "thick," it means that the cut has been sliced or portioned to be wider and have more depth than thinner cuts.

values.label: Thin
values.definition: Refers to the measurement or thinness of a meat cut. When the term refers to a cut of meat as "thin," it means that the cut has been sliced or portioned to be thinner and have less depth than thicker cuts.

values.label: Thymus
values.definition: Refers to a glandular organ found in the throat or neck region of animals. In culinary terms, the thymus is considered a type of offal or variety meat. It is also known as sweetbread in some regions.

values.label: Tip
values.definition: Refers to describe a specific portion or end of a meat cut. Depending on the meat cut, the tip may represent different meanings.

values.label: Tongue
values.definition: Refers to the muscular organ found in the mouth of animals. The tongue is a versatile and unique type of offal or variety meat that is consumed in many cultures and cuisines around the world.

values.label: Top butt
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut that comes from the sirloin primal section of the animal. The top butt is also known by other names, such as top sirloin butt or "op sirloin cap. The top butt is located in the sirloin primal section of the carcass. It is situated above the bottom sirloin and behind the tenderloin.

values.label: Top sirloin
values.definition: Refers to a specific and popular cut that comes from the sirloin primal section of the animal. The top sirloin is located in the sirloin primal section of the carcass. It is situated above the bottom sirloin and behind the tenderloin.

values.label: Trimmed
values.definition: Refers to the process of removing excess fat, connective tissue, and any undesirable or inedible portions from a meat cut. When a cut of meat is "trimmed," it is prepared to have a more uniform appearance, improve its presentation, and enhance its cooking qualities.

values.label: Tripe
values.definition: Refers to the edible lining of the stomach of animals. Tripe is considered a type of offal or variety meat and is consumed in various culinary traditions around the world.

values.label: Trunk
values.definition: Refers to the main body of an animal, particularly the torso or central part that contains the chest and abdominal cavities.

values.label: Undercut
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of meat that is taken from the underside or ventral portion of an animal. The undercut comes from the area of the animal that is located beneath the loin and rib primal sections. It is situated on the ventral side, closer to the belly.

values.label: Uterus
values.definition: Refers to the reproductive organ found in female animals. In some culinary traditions, the uterus is considered a type of offal or variety meat and is used as food. It is known by various names, such as womb or matrix.

values.label: Whole
values.definition: Refers to the animal as a whole.

values.label: Abdominal fat
values.definition: Refers to the fat deposits found in the abdominal cavity of poultry birds raised for meat production. This type of fat is distinct from subcutaneous fat, which is found directly under the skin, as it accumulates within the abdominal cavity surrounding the internal organs. Also known as abdominal fat pad or abdominal adipose tissue.

values.label: Assorted
values.definition: Refers to a description of a collection or group of various different items or things that are mixed together. It is often used to refer to a selection of different types or varieties of something, typically presented as a single package or set.

values.label: Lower back
values.definition: Refers to a specific part of the bird's anatomy. The lower back, also known as the lumbar region, is the area located on the back of the bird, just above the tail and towards the hindquarters.

values.label: Back portion
values.definition: Refers to the section of the bird's body located between the neck and the tail. This area includes the backbone, ribs, and surrounding meat.

values.label: Back removed
values.definition: Refers to a specific preparation of poultry meat where the back portion has been removed from the bird before further processing or cooking. This process is commonly done to create specific cuts or to modify the bird's shape for various culinary purposes.

values.label: Upper back
values.definition: Refers to the section located closer to the neck and is generally considered part of the poultry's breast.  The upper back is often referred to as the back half of the breast.

values.label: Whole back
values.definition: Refers to the entire back portion of a bird, including the backbone, ribs, and surrounding meat, remains intact without any specific preparation or removal. This would typically include the upper back (closer to the neck) and the lower back (towards the tail).

values.label: Belly
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry that comes from the underside or abdominal area of an animal.

values.label: Blood
values.definition: Refers to the process of slaughtering an animal, some blood can be collected for various purposes, such as further processing into blood-based products or used in specific culinary applications.

values.label: Boneless
values.definition: Refers to a specific poultry cut that has been prepared by removing the bones from the piece of meat.

values.label: Partial boneless
values.definition: Refers to a type of poultry meat preparation where some bones have been removed, leaving only certain bone-in portions intact. In this context, "partial" indicates that not all bones have been taken out, and the meat still retains some of its natural bone structure. Each cut may vary in the bones removed.

values.label: Bone or Bone in
values.definition: Refers to the bone(s) with or without the meat.

values.label: Brain
values.definition: Refers to the organ that is a part of the central nervous system found in the heads of animals. In culinary terms, "brain" specifically refers to the brain of certain animals, usually those that are commonly consumed for food.

values.label: Breast
values.definition: Refers to a specific poultry cut taken from the front chest area of an animal.

values.label: Split breast
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry meat where the breast section of the bird is split into two halves, creating two separate pieces.

values.label: Whole breast
values.definition: Refers to the entire breast portion of a bird that includes both the left and right sides, with bones and skin intact. Also known as a full breast.

values.label: Butterfly cut/V-style cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific method of preparing poultry by removing the backbone and flattening the bird to create a more even thickness. This technique involves cutting along the backbone and then spreading the bird open like a book, resulting in a butterfly-like appearance. also known as spatchcocking or butterflying.

values.label: Cap off/Cap removed
values.definition: Refers to a boneless, skinless cut of poultry where the top part, also known as the cap, has been removed. The cap is typically the upper portion of the breast meat that is attached to the skin.

values.label: Cap/Cap on
values.definition: Refers to a boneless, skinless cut of poultry where the top part, also known as the cap, is left attached to the breast meat. In other words, the skin and the uppermost portion of the breast are not removed, and the cut maintains its natural shape.

values.label: Carcass
values.definition: Refers to the edible flesh or muscle tissue obtained from the body of an animal after it has been slaughtered and processed for consumption. When an animal is slaughtered, the body is typically referred to as a carcass until it is broken down into different cuts of meat.

values.label: Crest
values.definition: Refers to a distinctive tuft or fleshy protuberance of feathers found on the top of the bird's head.

values.label: Cutlet
values.definition: Refers to a thin, boneless piece of meat that is sometimes breaded and/or fried. The meat used for cutlets can come from various sources.

values.label: Dark meat
values.definition: Refers to the meat from certain parts of the bird that is darker in colour compared to white meat. Dark meat is found in areas of the bird that are more active and used for sustained movement, such as walking or flying.

values.label: Drumstick
values.definition: Refers to the lower portion of the bird's leg, specifically the part between the knee joint and the ankle joint.

values.label: Drumstick incision
values.definition: Refers to making small cuts or slits in the flesh of the drumstick.

values.label: Fat
values.definition: Refers to the adipose tissue found in and around various cuts of meat. Additionally, there is also external fat, often referred to as "trimmable fat" or "fat cap," which is found on the surface of certain cuts of meat.

values.label: Feet (Paws, Claws)
values.definition: Refer to the edible parts of an animal's limbs, particularly the feet or hooves. The feet from various animals, can be consumed in certain cuisines and culinary traditions around the world.

values.label: Filleted
values.definition: Cut or prepared as a fillet.

values.label: Forequarter/Front half
values.definition: Refers to the front portion of an animal's carcass, specifically the front half of the body. It includes the front legs or limbs, shoulder, and associated cuts of meat.

values.label: Giblet
values.definition: Refers to a set of internal organs commonly found in birds raised for meat consumption.The typical poultry giblets include liver, heart,  gizzard, and/or neck.

values.label: Giblets removed
values.definition: Refers to the removal of  a set of internal organs commonly found in birds raised for meat consumption.The typical poultry giblets include liver, heart,  gizzard, and/or neck.

values.label: Gizzard
values.definition: Refers to a muscular pouch that helps birds grind and digest food by using small stones (grit) they ingest.

values.label: Half
values.definition: Refers to half of an animal.

values.label: Head
values.definition: Refers to the entire head of an animal. The head contains various parts, including the skull, brain, eyes, ears, snout, tongue, and sometimes the cheeks and jowls. Different cultures have varying culinary traditions and uses for the head of the animal.

values.label: Heart
values.definition: Refers to the muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the circulatory system of an animal. The heart is a vital organ and an edible part of the animal that is used for culinary purposes in various cuisines around the world.

values.label: Hindquarter/Back half
values.definition: Refers to the back half of an animal's carcass, specifically the rear portion of the body. It includes the hind legs or limbs, hip, and associated cuts of meat.

values.label: Intestines/Chitterlings
values.definition: Refers to the small intestines of birds raised for meat consumption. Like other animals, poultry have a digestive system that includes a long tube-like structure called the intestines, responsible for the absorption of nutrients from their food. also known as chitterlings or chitlins.

values.label: Kidney
values.definition: Refers to the organ found in the abdominal cavity that are part of the animal's urinary system and play a crucial role in filtering waste products and excess water from the blood to produce urine. Animal kidneys are also considered a type of offal or organ meat, and they have been a part of traditional diets in many cultures for centuries.

values.label: Leg quarter
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry that includes both the leg and thigh portions of the bird.

values.label: Leg whole/Leg
values.definition: Refers to the entire leg of a bird, which includes both the drumstick and the thigh in one piece. This cut is not separated at the joint, and the leg remains intact, preserving the natural connection between the thigh and the drumstick.

values.label: Liver
values.definition: Refers to the large organ found in the abdominal cavity of animals, including livestock and game animals. The liver is responsible for performing essential functions such as filtering and detoxifying blood, producing bile to aid in digestion, storing certain nutrients, and metabolizing various substances in the body. the liver is considered an organ meat or offal, and it is highly valued for its nutritional richness and distinct flavour.

values.label: Long/Long cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut that involves slicing the meat parallel to its natural grain or muscle fibers. This results in longer, more elongated pieces of meat.

values.label: Mixed parts
values.definition: Refers to a combination of different cuts of meat and pieces obtained from an animal during the butchering process.

values.label: Neck
values.definition: Refers to the portion of meat from the animal's body located between the head and the shoulders.

values.label: Neck half
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry that includes half of the bird's neck. A poultry neck half is obtained by cutting the neck in half lengthwise, dividing it into two roughly equal parts. Each half of the neck includes both the bone and the meat.

values.label: Non-traditional cut
values.definition: Refers to less common or unconventional ways of portioning the bird. These cuts are not typically found in standard culinary practices but can offer unique and creative ways to use different parts of the bird. Examples: Oyster, Cushion, Roulade, etc.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Part piece
values.definition: Refers to a specific portion or cut of poultry meat, such as a chicken breast or turkey thigh.

values.label: Quartered
values.definition: Refers to a specific preparation method where a whole bird is cut into four quarters by dividing it into four parts. Each quarter typically consists of a combination of the leg and thigh on one side and the wing and breast on the other side of the bird.

values.label: Removed fat
values.definition: Refers to the process of removing the fat from meat. Fat is adipose tissue found in and around various cuts of meat. Additionally, there is also external fat, often referred to as "trimmable fat" or "fat cap," which is found on the surface of certain cuts of meat.

values.label: Ribs
values.definition: Refer to the bones and meat found along the ribcage of a bird. While poultry ribs are smaller and more delicate compared to traditional pork or beef ribs, they still offer a flavorful and tender eating experience. The ribcage of a bird contains a combination of bones, cartilage, and intercostal muscles that contribute to the rib meat.

values.label: Ribs removed
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry meat where the rib bones have been removed from the bird, leaving the rib meat without the bones. This is a preparation method commonly used to create boneless poultry meat cuts.

values.label: Rib meat
values.definition: Refers to the meat found along the ribs of a bird. The rib meat is located on the underside of the bird's body, where the ribs are attached to the breast meat.

values.label: Rib meat removed
values.definition: Refers to the removal of the meat found along the ribs of a bird. The rib meat is located on the underside of the bird's body, where the ribs are attached to the breast meat.

values.label: Scapula meat
values.definition: Refers to the meat removed from the scapula bone (shoulder blade).

values.label: Short/Short cut
values.definition: Refers to a specific type of meat cut that involves slicing the meat perpendicular to its grain, resulting in shorter and more compact pieces.

values.label: Skin on
values.definition: The animal with its skin on / with skin on.

values.label: Slant cut
values.definition: Refers to the process of cutting the meat at a between 15 to 30 degree angle.

values.label: Sliced
values.definition: Cut into slices.

values.label: Special trim
values.definition: Refers to a specific request or custom preparation of meat made by a customer or chef to meet their specific requirements or preferences. It involves trimming or cutting the meat in a particular way that differs from the standard or conventional cuts typically offered by the butcher.

values.label: Square cut/Squared
values.definition: Refers to a specific cutting technique used to prepare meat or poultry. When a piece of meat is square cut, it means that the butcher has made straight, even cuts across the meat, resulting in a block-like or square shape.

values.label: Stomach
values.definition: Refers to the organ that forms a part of the digestive system of animals. The stomach is responsible for breaking down and digesting food through the action of digestive juices and acids. In certain culinary traditions and cultures, the stomach is considered an edible part and used in various dishes.

values.label: Stripped
values.definition: Refers to poultry meat that has been removed or separated from the bone, skin, or other connective tissues. This process of removing the meat from the bones and other parts is commonly referred to as "deboning" or "stripping" the poultry.

values.label: Tail on
values.definition: The animal with its tail on / with its tail.

values.label: Tail removed
values.definition: The animal with tail removed / without tail.

values.label: Tenderloins/Tender/Inner fillet
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of poultry meat known for its tenderness and are located on the underside of the chicken breast. These tenderloins are thin, long strips of meat that run parallel to the breastbone. Poultry tenders are distinct from the rest of the breast meat as they are not connected to the breastbone and do not have any tough connective tissues or bones.

values.label: Tenderloins removed
values.definition: Refers to the removal of the tenderloins. The tenderloins are thin, long strips of meat that run parallel to the breastbone. Poultry tenders are distinct from the rest of the breast meat as they are not connected to the breastbone and do not have any tough connective tissues or bones.

values.label: Tendons
values.definition: Refers to the tough, fibrous connective tissues that connect muscles to bones in an animal's body.

values.label: Tendon Clipped (Tip off)
values.definition: Refers to the protruding portion of the tendon is removed.

values.label: Tendon partially removed
values.definition: Refers to poultry meat from which some, but not all, of the tendons or tough connective tissues have been removed. In this case, the meat may still contain some small pieces of tendon or connective tissue that have not been fully trimmed away.

values.label: Tendon removed
values.definition: Refers to poultry meat from which the tendons or tough connective tissues have been removed. Tendons are fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones, and they can be tough and chewy when not properly cooked or removed.

values.label: Testicles/Testes
values.definition: Refers to the male reproductive organs of animals. In some culinary traditions and cultures, testicles are considered a type of offal or "variety meat" and are consumed as food. They are often referred to by specific names based on the animal they come from.

values.label: Thigh
values.definition: Refers to the lower part of the bird's leg, specifically the upper portion of the leg that is closer to the body.

values.label: Traditional cut
values.definition: Refers to the standard methods of dividing a whole bird into smaller, more manageable pieces for cooking or serving.

values.label: Trimmed
values.definition: Refers to the process of removing excess fat, connective tissue, and any undesirable or inedible portions from a meat cut. When a cut of meat is "trimmed," it is prepared to have a more uniform appearance, improve its presentation, and enhance its cooking qualities.

values.label: Trimmings
values.definition: Refers to the leftover pieces, scraps, or excess parts of poultry that are removed during the butchering and processing of the bird. These trimmings can include various parts, such as skin, fat, small bits of meat, connective tissues, bones, and other offcuts.

values.label: V wing (1st and 2nd segment)
values.definition: Refers to the process of dislocating the joint between the wingette and drumette, so that the two portions form an upright "V" shape.

values.label: White meat
values.definition: Refers to the lighter-coloured meat found in birds. It is typically located in the breast and wing portions of the bird. The primary difference between white meat and dark meat in poultry is the muscle type and function in the bird. White meat comes from fast-twitch muscles, which are used for short bursts of activity and are less active.

values.label: Whole
values.definition: Refers to the animal as a whole.

values.label: Wings removed
values.definition: Refers to the process of removal of the wings. The wings are located on the upper part of the bird's body, and they are essential for flight in wild birds.

values.label: Wing 2 joint (2nd and 3rd segment)
values.definition: Refers to a specific cut of the bird's wing, which has been divided into two distinct joints. The tip is usually removed, and the wing is separated into two sections: the drumette and the wingette (mid-wing). The two joints created by this cut are the connection points between the drumette and the wingette.

values.label: Wing drumette (1st segment)
values.definition: Refers to the upper part of the wing, closest to the bird's body. It is meatier and resembles a small drumstick.

values.label: Wing flat (2nd segment)/Wingette
values.definition: Refers to the middle portion of the wing. It contains two bones and is flatter in shape. Also known as the mid-wing, wingette or flat.

values.label: Wing tip (3rd segment)
values.definition: Refers to the pointed end of the wing. It is mostly skin and cartilage and has little meat. Also know as the flapper.

values.label: Whole wing/Wing
values.definition: Refers to a specific part of the bird's anatomy. The wings are located on the upper part of the bird's body, and they are essential for flight in wild birds.

values.label: Air-dried
values.definition: A product that is made or becomes dry through contact with unheated air.

values.label: Dehydrated
values.definition: A product having had the water extracted/removed as a means of preservation.

values.label: Dry
values.definition: A product that goes through a "drying process", not wet or semi-moist.

values.label: Freeze-dried
values.definition: A product preserved by rapid freezing followed by treatment in a high vacuum.

values.label: Fresh
values.definition: A product recently made or obtained, not canned, frozen, or otherwise preserved; may require refrigeration.

values.label: Frozen
values.definition: A product that has been subjected to rapid freezing and is kept frozen until used.

values.label: Live
values.definition: A product that is consumed in a condition as close as possible to their original, vibrant, living state.

values.label: Raw
values.definition: A product that has never been heated, refined, pasteurized, treated or otherwise processed in any way.

values.label: Semi-moist
values.definition: A product with low moisture or liquid, not wet or dry.

values.label: Wet
values.definition: A product with high moisture or liquid, not dry or semi moist.

values.label: Antlers
values.definition: Pieces of horns from a deer or other animal.

values.label: Bar
values.definition: A product that is formed to specific shape and size such as a rectangle.

values.label: Biscuit
values.definition: A product that is dry, crisp or hard and formed to a specific shape.

values.label: Bites
values.definition: An individual piece or product that is consumed in a single mouthful size.

values.label: Blended
values.definition: A combination of multiple food types into one product.

values.label: Bones
values.definition: Coming from the bones of an animal or a product in the shape of an animal bone.

values.label: Bovine penis
values.definition: A product that is made from the penis of male bovine also known as "Bully Stick".

values.label: Break apart
values.definition: A product that is made to be broken into smaller parts or components.

values.label: Broth
values.definition: A savoury liquid made of water in which bones, meat, and/or vegetables have been simmered then removed.

values.label: Chew
values.definition: A product designed specifically for repeat biting or chewing.

values.label: Chowder
values.definition: A variety of soup or stew with a thickening agent.

values.label: Chunks
values.definition: A product made up of short, thick pieces.

values.label: Creamy
values.definition: Prepared by slow simmering or poaching in milk, cream or a water / starch combination to form a smooth sauce.

values.label: Crunchy
values.definition: A product that is firm and makes a noise when bitten or crushed.

values.label: Curls
values.definition: A product formed or cause to form into a curved or spiral shape.

values.label: Flakes
values.definition: A product that easily breaks into small thin pieces.

values.label: Granola
values.definition: A mixture of fruit, nuts, oats and/or grains combined together, baked into a crisp toasted format.

values.label: Granules
values.definition: A product that is small formed particles.

values.label: Gravy
values.definition: A sauce made from the juices of cooked meat.

values.label: Grilled
values.definition: A product where dry heat is applied to surface creating grilled marks during cooking.

values.label: Ground
values.definition: A product made into small pieces resulting from grinding.

values.label: Hard
values.definition: A product that is solid, firm or rigid.

values.label: Himalayan chew
values.definition: A specific chew consisting of hard cheese made of boiling yak and cow milk and then drying for several weeks.

values.label: Hoof
values.definition: A product made from animal hooves.

values.label: Jelly
values.definition: A soft, semisolid food substance with a resilient consistency, made by the setting of a liquid.

values.label: Jerky
values.definition: Lean trimmed meat or other food that has been cut into strips and dried.

values.label: Juice
values.definition: A liquid that comes from meat when cooked, fruit or other food.

values.label: Kibble
values.definition: Ground meal formed into any shape.

values.label: Liquid
values.definition: A product having a consistency like that of water or oil, i.e., flowing freely but of constant volume.

values.label: Loaf
values.definition: An uncut product taking the shape of the container, typically firmer in texture.

values.label: Minced
values.definition: A product cut into very small pieces. This term means the smallest possible pieces, smaller than dice or chop, but not pureed.

values.label: Nugget/Morsel
values.definition: A product that comes as small chunks or lumps of another substance, designed to be fed in individual portions.

values.label: Paste
values.definition: A product in semi-liquid colloidal suspension, emulsion, or aggregation.

values.label: Pâté
values.definition: A paste, pie or loaf filled with a forcemeat, spread of finely chopped or diced meat.

values.label: Pellet
values.definition: A small rounded, spherical, or cylindrical mass of a substance.

values.label: Pig ears
values.definition: A product that is made of the ear of a swine.

values.label: Pill masker
values.definition: A moist, juicy, flavourful soft product that is designed for wrapping or shaping around pills.

values.label: Powder
values.definition: Fine, dry particles produced by the grinding, rushing, or disintegration of a solid substance.

values.label: Puree
values.definition: A paste or thick liquid suspension usually made from cooked food ground finely.

values.label: Rawhide
values.definition: The skin of animals such as cattle or pork that is removed, dried and prepared for an animal to eat.

values.label: Shredded/Pulled
values.definition: Products formatted into thin slices, strings or pieces using a mechanical or cooking process.

values.label: Sliced/Filet
values.definition: A product cut into somewhat uniform pieces with consistent width.

values.label: Soft
values.definition: A product easy to mould, cut, compress, or fold, not hard or firm to the touch.

values.label: Soufflé
values.definition: A fluffy light product that is made from a sauce, egg yolks, beaten egg whites, and a flavouring or purée and baked until puffed up.

values.label: Stew/Soup
values.definition: A liquid food generally with a meat, fish, or vegetable stock as a base and often containing pieces of solid food.

values.label: Stick
values.definition: A product in a long slender cylindrical form or shape.

values.label: Strips/Tenders
values.definition: A product cut or formed into varying sized thin shapes.

values.label: Stuffed
values.definition: A product which has one part filled with another edible mixture.

values.label: Tablet
values.definition: Ingredient(s) compressed into a specific shape (circular, disk-shaped, oblong or other shape).

values.label: Topping
values.definition: Topping is defined as a product that can be added with your pets normal meal to improve taste and palatability.

values.label: Waffle
values.definition: A product that is cooked between two plates that are patterned to give a characteristic size, shape, and surface impression.

values.label: Wraps
values.definition: A product where one component covers or partially covers another component of the product.

values.label: All
values.definition: The product can be used at all animals regardless of size.

values.label: Extra large
values.definition: The size of the animal is significantly bigger than normal or usual for a specific animal type.

values.label: Extra small
values.definition: The size of the animal is significantly less than normal or usual for a specific animal type.

values.label: Large
values.definition: The size of the animal is bigger than normal or usual for a specific animal type.

values.label: Medium
values.definition: The size of the animal is intermediate or moderate for a specific animal type.

values.label: Small
values.definition: The size of the animal is less than normal or usual for a specific animal type.

values.label: Active/Energy/Vitality support
values.definition: A product that supports an animal during active and everyday lifestyle.

values.label: Aging
values.definition: A product that is designed specifically for older/senior life stage.

values.label: Allergy relief
values.definition: A product to support and help maintain normal histamine levels to reduce allergy symptoms.

values.label: Appetite support
values.definition: A product that enhances palatability.

values.label: Arthritis
values.definition: A product that supports joint health and movement to reduce symptoms of arthritis.

values.label: Bone development
values.definition: A product that supports growth of bones.

values.label: Bone health
values.definition: A product that supports maintenance of bones.

values.label: Brain development
values.definition: A product that supports brain of a growing pet.

values.label: Brain health
values.definition: A product that supports healthy brain function.

values.label: Circulatory health
values.definition: A product that supports circulatory system.

values.label: Dander reduction
values.definition: A product for support in managing a dandruff skin condition.

values.label: Dental health
values.definition: A product that supports clean teeth and helps improve your animal's periodontal health.

values.label: Diabetic support
values.definition: A product that supports the nutritional needs of diabetic animals.

values.label: Digestive health
values.definition: A product that supports the gastrointestinal tract.

values.label: Ear health
values.definition: A product that supports hearing or otic health.

values.label: Eye health
values.definition: A product that supports help support eye function and vision.

values.label: Faeces deodorisation
values.definition: A product that has been designed to reduce or eliminate odours from animal faeces.

values.label: Faeces reduction
values.definition: A product that has been designed to reduce the amount or size of animal faeces.

values.label: Fresh breath
values.definition: A product that is designed to reduces smells from breath.

values.label: Grass protection
values.definition: A product which reduces the impact of animal waste on grass or lawns by reducing an animals pH waste levels.

values.label: Growth support
values.definition: A product designed to support growth and development throughout the animal's early life.

values.label: Hairball reduction
values.definition: A product that decreases number of hairballs.

values.label: Heart health
values.definition: A product that supports heart function.

values.label: Hip/Joint health
values.definition: A product that helps maintain optimal joint function, support cartilage production and protect existing cartilage from breaking down.

values.label: Holistic
values.definition: A product designed to support physical, emotional, social and over all well being of the animal.

values.label: Hormone support
values.definition: A product designed to support healthy hormone levels.

values.label: Immune support
values.definition: A product that supports the immune system.

values.label: Indoor
values.definition: A product for animals living indoor that usually do not go outside and have limited access to exercise.

values.label: Itch relief
values.definition: A product that reduces skin irritation.

values.label: Kidney health
values.definition: A product that supports kidney/renal function.

values.label: Liver health
values.definition: A product that supports liver function.

values.label: Milk replacement
values.definition: A product substitute for mother's milk. Doubles as a milk replacer for infants and complete nutritional supplement for pregnant, lactating and senior animals.

values.label: Muscle support
values.definition: A product that supports to improve muscle mass and function.

values.label: Neutered or spayed
values.definition: A product for neutered or spayed animals.

values.label: Pain relief
values.definition: A product to reduce pain for the animal.

values.label: Pregnancy support
values.definition: A product to meet the unique needs of pregnant animals.

values.label: Respiratory health
values.definition: A product that supports the respiratory system of the animal.

values.label: Sensitive skin
values.definition: A product for animals with sensitive skin.

values.label: Sensitive stomach
values.definition: A product for animals with sensitive stomach. Gastrointestinal distress, mild upset of the digestive system, which can range from a gurgling gut and gas from the rear end right through to sickness and diarrhoea.

values.label: Shedding reduction
values.definition: A product that reduces the amount of shedding by the animal.

values.label: Skin/Coat care
values.definition: A product that supports healthy skin and enhance or restore an animal's coat/fur or fur colour.

values.label: Stress/Anxiety reduction/Calming
values.definition: A product used to promote a positive emotional state/coping to reduce the effects of environmental stress, hyperactivity and anxiety.

values.label: Training/Behaviour
values.definition: A product used in teaching of a behaviour or action.

values.label: Urinary health (UTH)
values.definition: A product that supports a lower urine pH and other urinary condition. Example: Feline lower urinary tract disease.

values.label: Veterinary diet
values.definition: A product recommended or prescribed by a veterinarian that targets a specific animal health issue(s).

values.label: Vitamin/Mineral support
values.definition: A product designed to support and maintain healthy levels of vitamin & minerals.

values.label: Weaning
values.definition: A product for a young animal transitioning from mother's milk to solid food.

values.label: Weight management
values.definition: A product designed to address weight control, loss or maintenance.

values.label: Brain electrostimulation
values.definition: Brain electrostimulation

values.label: Contact lenses
values.definition: Contact lenses

values.label: High intensity electromagnetic radiation
values.definition: High intensity electromagnetic radiation

values.label: Equipment for adipose tissue
values.definition: Equipment to be used to reduce, remove or destroy adipose tissue.

values.label: Filling by injection
values.definition: Substances, combinations of substances, or items intended for filling by injection.

values.label: Product in human body
values.definition: Products intended to be totally or partially introduced into the human body.

values.label: Backpack
values.definition: Products that may be described/observed as a bag carried by straps over the shoulder, on the back, or by handles. These products are usually of a softer and less rigid construction than suitcases, but are designed to be particularly durable and in some cases suitable for outdoor activity. Excludes products such as Shoulder Bags, Shopping Bags, Briefcases and Suitcases.

values.label: Bucket Bag
values.definition: Bag that is taller than it is wide, with a rounded bottom.

values.label: Clutch
values.definition: Bag designed to be held in the hand.

values.label: Crossbody
values.definition: Bag designed to be worn across the body, without using hands.

values.label: Diaper Bag
values.definition: Bag designed to carry baby related items.

values.label: Duffel
values.definition: Cylindrical canvas bag closed by a drawstring and carried over the shoulder.

values.label: Hobo
values.definition: Bag that features a slouchy center and long strap.

values.label: Messenger Bag
values.definition: Bag designed to be worn across the back with the strap across the body.

values.label: Other Bag Type
values.definition: Code value not available in code list.

values.label: Pouch
values.definition: Small bag with drawstring closure.

values.label: Saddle Bag
values.definition: Bag designed with a curved bottom and strap closures.

values.label: Satchel
values.definition: Bag with a top closure, top handle and flat bottom.

values.label: Shopper
values.definition: Bag with a rectangular shape and open top.

values.label: Shoulder Bag
values.definition: Bag designed to be carried on the shoulder.

values.label: Tote
values.definition: Bag designed with double handles and large open compartment.

values.label: Waist Bag
values.definition: Bag designed to be worn around the waist.

values.label: Wristlet
values.definition: Small bag designed to be carried via a strap around the wrist.

values.label: Applique
values.definition: Ornamental needlework.

values.label: Banded
values.definition: With a band.

values.label: Bling
values.definition: Heavily decorated, especially with shiny or jewel like metal and plastic elements similar to rhinestones.

values.label: Cut
values.definition: Material cut out.

values.label: Decal
values.definition: A sticker or patch that can be applied to a product that using an adhesive.

values.label: Embossed
values.definition: Decorated with a relief element.

values.label: Etched
values.definition: Cut or carved into surface.

values.label: Fabric Applique
values.definition: Fabric decoration sewn onto base item. Does not include applique that are made of felt fabric.

values.label: Alkaline
values.definition: Battery dependent upon the reaction between zinc and manganese dioxide.

values.label: Carbon monofluoride lithium
values.definition: The lithium–carbon monofluoride system has been among the more successful early commercial lithium miniature batteries. It has been used extensively in cameras and smaller devices, providing about 3.2 volts per cell, high power density, and long shelf life.

values.label: Carbon Zinc
values.definition: Zinc carbon batteries are dry cell primary batteries that deliver about 1.5 volts of direct current from the electrochemical reaction between zinc and manganese dioxide.

values.label: Lead acid
values.definition: Batteries which use sponge lead and lead peroxide for the conversion of the chemical energy into electrical power, are called lead acid batteries. They are most commonly used in power stations and substations because they have higher cell voltage and lower cost.

values.label: Lead calcium
values.definition: Calcium batteries are a form of lead acid battery which are usually sealed and maintenance free. Calcium replaces antimony in the plates of the battery to give it improved resistance to corrosion, excessive gassing, less water usage and lower self discharge.

values.label: Lithium air
values.definition: Lithium air batteries are described as the "ultimate" batteries because they provide a high theoretical energy density of up to ten times the energy offered by regular lithium ion batteries.

values.label: Lithium cobalt
values.definition: Lithium ion batteries utilizing cobalt are primary used in laptop computers.

values.label: Lithium ion
values.definition: A lithium-ion battery or Li-ion battery (abbreviated as LIB) is a type of rechargeable battery. Lithium-ion batteries are commonly used for portable electronics and electric vehicles and are growing in popularity for military and aerospace applications.

values.label: Lithium Ion Polymer
values.definition: A type of battery in which lithium ions move from the anode to the cathode during discharge, and from the cathode to the anode when charged.

values.label: Lithium manganese oxide
values.definition: Lithium batteries are primary batteries that have metallic lithium as an anode. These types of batteries are also referred to as lithium manganese batteries. They stand apart from other batteries in their high charge density (long life) and high cost per unit. Depending on the design and chemical compounds used, lithium cells can produce voltages from 1.5 V (comparable to a zinc–carbon or alkaline battery) to about 3.7 V.

values.label: Lithium nickel
values.definition: Lithium ion batteries utilizing nickel and cobalt are primary used in automotive and power tool products.

values.label: Lithium phosphate
values.definition: Lithium ion batteries utilizing phosphate are primary use in automotive and power tool products.

values.label: Lithium thionyl chloride
values.definition: Lithium metal batteries utilizing thionyl chloride are primary used in portable electronics and memory backup.

values.label: Lithium titanate
values.definition: Lithium ion batteries utilizing titanate are primary used in automotive products.

values.label: Mercury oxide
values.definition: Mercury batteries (also called mercuric oxide battery, mercury cell, button cell, or Ruben-Mallory) are non-rechargeable electrochemical batteries, primary cells with primary uses in portable devices.

values.label: Metal Lithium
values.definition: A lithium battery that used metallic lithium as anode.

values.label: Nickel Cadmium
values.definition: A type of rechargeable battery using nickel oxide hydroxide and metallic cadmium as electrodes.

values.label: Nickel Metal Hydride
values.definition: A type of secondary electrochemical cell similar to nickel hydrogen cell.

values.label: Nickel oxide
values.definition: Nickel oxide, made from iron, batteries are a rechargeable battery having nickel(III) oxide hydroxide positive and iron negative plates, with an electrolyte of potassium hydroxide.

values.label: Nickel oxyhydroxide
values.definition: Nickel oxyhydroxide batteries are a type of primary cell. It is not rechargeable and must be disposed after a single use. They can be used in high-drain applications such as digital cameras.

values.label: Nickel zinc
values.definition: Nickel zinc batteries are a type of rechargeable batteries similar to nickel metal hydride batteries.

values.label: Other
values.definition: A battery technology not on otherwise on this list.

values.label: Silver calcium
values.definition: Silver calcium alloy batteries are a type of lead-acid batteries with grids made from lead calcium silver alloy, instead of the traditional lead antimony alloy or newer lead calcium alloy. They stand out for its resistance to corrosion and the destructive effects of high temperatures.

values.label: Silver Oxide
values.definition: Silver oxide batteries are common low capacity button cells with a nominal voltage of 1.55V. They have a higher open-circuit voltage than mercury batteries, and a flatter discharge curve than standard alkaline batteries

values.label: Silver zinc oxide
values.definition: Silver zinc oxide batteries share most of the characteristics of silver oxide batteries, and in addition, are able to deliver one of the highest specific energies of all presently known electro-chemical power sources. This type of battery has silver oxide as the positive electrode (cathode), zinc as the negative electrode (anode), plus an alkaline electrolyte, usually sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide metallic silver.

values.label: Zinc air
values.definition: Zinc air batteries (non-rechargeable) are metal air batteries powered by oxidizing zinc with oxygen from the air. They have high energy densities and are relatively inexpensive to produce.

values.label: Zinc chloride
values.definition: Zinc chloride batteries are an improved version of zinc carbon batteries. Zinc chloride batteries are generally labelled as a heavy duty battery. These batteries contain only zinc chloride paste as electrolyte and provide more current, more voltage and more life than general purpose zinc carbon batteries.
