values.definition: Silver oxide button cell identified by IEC SR910SW; 1.55V

values.label: Sub C
values.definition: Round single cell identified by IEC name KR22C429 (NiCd) and HR22C429 (NiMH).

values.label: Battery
values.definition: An electrochemical device used to store energy. The term is usually applied to a group of two or more electric cells connected electrically. In common usage, the term “battery” is also applied to a single cell, such as an AA battery.

values.label: Battery pack
values.definition: Two or more electrochemical cells electrically interconnected in an appropriate series/parallel arrangement to provide the required operating current and voltage levels.

values.label: Energy Cell
values.definition: An electrochemical device, composed of positive and negative plates and electrolyte, which is capable of storing electrical energy. It is the basic “building block” of a battery.

values.label: Bed Spread
values.definition: Decorative cover used over blankets and sheets.

values.label: Comforter
values.definition: Cover with insulating material internally used on the top of the bed.

values.label: Duvet Cover
values.definition: Cover used with comforter.

values.label: Fitted Sheet
values.definition: Sheet that the elastic corners wrap tightly around the corners of the mattress.

values.label: Flat Sheet
values.definition: Sheet used over the fitted sheet.

values.label: Other Bedding Type
values.definition: Code value not available in code list.

values.label: Pillowcase
values.definition: Cover for pillows.

values.label: Shams
values.definition: Decorative covers for pillows used for decoration.

values.label: Sheet Set
values.definition: Bedding consisting of fitted & flats sheet with pillowcases.

values.label: American Style Amber/Red Ale
values.definition: Amber ale is a pale ale brewed with a proportion of amber malt and sometimes crystal malt to produce an amber colour generally ranging from light copper to light brown.

values.label: American Style Barley Wine Ale
values.definition: American Style Barley wine ale is a style of strong ale, crafted originally in America, of between 6 11% alcohol by volume.

values.label: American Style Brown Ale
values.definition: American Style Brown ales are a style of beer, crafted originally in America, with a dark amber or brown colour. Brown ales are lightly hopped and brewed from 100% brown malt.

values.label: American Style Cream Ale
values.definition: American Style Cream ale is light in colour and are well attenuated, crafted originally in America.

values.label: American Style Fruit Beer
values.definition: Most fruit beers are ales however, they typically do not carry an ale character. In order to allow for the fruit flavour to come through nicely, the malt’s flavour is not dominant and there is a low bitterness level to the beer.

values.label: American Style Imperial Porter
values.definition: Imperial porter is a dark style of beer from well-hopped beers made from brown malt.

values.label: American Style Imperial Stout
values.definition: American Style Imperial stout is a strong dark beer, originally crafted in America. Imperial stouts have a high alcohol content, usually over 9% abv, and are among the darkest available beer styles.

values.label: American Style India Pale Ale
values.definition: American Style India Pale Ale (IPA) is a style of pale ale, originally crafted in America. The colour of an IPA can vary from a light gold to a reddish amber.

values.label: American Style Lager
values.definition: American Style Lager is a type of beer, originally crafted in America, conditioned at low temperatures. Lagers can be pale, amber, or dark. Pale lager is the most widely consumed and commercially available style of beer.

values.label: American Style Malt Liquor
values.definition: Malt liquor, in North America, is beer with high alcohol content. Legally, it often includes any alcoholic beverage with 5% or more alcohol by volume made with malted barley.

values.label: American Style Pale Ale
values.definition: American Style Pale ale is a top fermented beer, crafted originally in America, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: American Style Pilsner
values.definition: American Style Pilsners are made with neutral and hard water. They tend to be golden in colour with a dry, crisp, and somewhat bitter flavour. Pilsner stands out from other lagers due to its more distinctive hop taste.

values.label: American Style Porter
values.definition: American Style Porter is a dark style of beer made from brown malt, crafted originally in America.

values.label: American Style Stout
values.definition: American Style stout is a dark, top fermented beer, crafted originally in America, with a number of variations, including dry stout, Baltic porter, milk stout, and imperial stout.

values.label: American Style Strong Pale Ale
values.definition: Strong pale ales are ales made predominantly with pale malts.

values.label: Australian Style Pale Ale
values.definition: Australian Style Pale ale is a top fermented beer, crafted originally in Australia, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: Baltic Style Porter
values.definition: Baltic Style Porter is a dark style of beer made from brown malt, crafted originally around the Baltic Sea.

values.label: Belgian Style Blonde Ale
values.definition: Belgian Style Blonde ales are very pale in colour. They tend to be clear, crisp, and dry, with low to medium bitterness and aroma from hops, and some sweetness from malt.

values.label: Belgian Style Flanders Oud Bruin or Oud Red Ale
values.definition: Belgian Style Flanders Oud Bruin or Oud Red ale, is a style of sour ale, crafted originally in Belgium. Flanders red ale is fermented with organisms other than Saccharomyces cerevisiae, especially Lactobacillus, which produces a sour character attributable to lactic acid.

values.label: Belgian Style Fruit Beer
values.definition: Most fruit beers are ales however, they typically do not carry an ale character. In order to allow for the fruit flavour to come through nicely, the malt’s flavour is not dominant and there is a low bitterness level to the beer.

values.label: Belgian Style Fruit Lambic
values.definition: Belgian Style Fruit Lambic beers, originally crafted in Belgium, include gueuze and kriek Lambic and infused with fruit flavours. Lambic differs from most other beers in that it is fermented through exposure to wild yeasts and bacteria, as opposed to exposure to carefully cultivated strains of brewer's yeast. This process gives the beer its distinctive flavour: dry, vinous, and cidery, usually with a sour aftertaste.

values.label: Belgian Style Gueuze Lambic
values.definition: Belgian Style Gueuze is a type of Lambic beer, originally crafted in Belgium. It is made by blending young (1 year old) and old (2 to 3 year old) Lambic, which is bottled for a second fermentation. Because the young Lambic are not fully fermented, the blended beer contains fermentable sugars, which allow a second fermentation to occur.

values.label: Belgian Style Lambic
values.definition: Belgian Style Lambic beers, originally crafted in Belgium, include gueuze and kriek Lambic. Lambic differs from most other beers in that it is fermented through exposure to wild yeasts and bacteria, as opposed to exposure to carefully cultivated strains of brewer's yeast. This process gives the beer its distinctive flavour: dry, vinous, and cidery, usually with a sour aftertaste.

values.label: Belgian Style Pale Ale
values.definition: Belgian Style Pale ale is a top fermented beer, crafted originally in Belgium, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: Belgian Style Witbier
values.definition: Belgian Style Witbier, white beer, bière blanche, or simply witte is a barley/wheat, top fermented beer, crafted originally in Belgium. It gets its name from the suspended yeast and wheat proteins which cause the beer to look hazy, or white, when cold. It is a descendant from those medieval beers which were flavoured and preserved with a blend of spices and other plants such as coriander, orange, and bitter orange referred to as "gruit" instead of using hops.

values.label: Berliner Style Weisse
values.definition: Weisse is a cloudy, sour beer of around 3% alcohol by volume.

values.label: Bitter
values.definition: Bitter is a British style of pale ale that varies in colour from gold to dark amber, and in strength typically from 3% to 5.5% alcohol by volume.

values.label: Bohemian Style Pilsener (Pilsner)
values.definition: Bohemian Style Pilseners (Pilsner) are made with neutral and hard water. They tend to be golden in colour with a dry, crisp, and somewhat bitter flavour. Pilsener stands out from other lagers due to its more distinctive hop taste.

values.label: Brett Beer
values.definition: Brett beers vary in colour and can take on the hues of added fruits or other ingredients. Horsey, goaty, leathery, phenolic and some fruity acidic character derived from Brettanomyces organisms may be evident, but in balance with other components of a Brett beer.

values.label: British Style Barley Wine Ale
values.definition: British Style Barley wine ale is a style of strong ale, crafted originally in Great Britain, of between 6 11% alcohol by volume.

values.label: British Style Golden Ale
values.definition: First developed in the UK, Golden ales are straw coloured with a slight hint of citrus and vanilla. The beer can sometimes contain spicier flavours.

values.label: British Style Imperial Stout
values.definition: British Style Imperial stout is a strong dark beer, originally crafted in Great Britain. Imperial stouts have a high alcohol content, usually over 9% abv, and are among the darkest available beer styles.

values.label: Brown Porter
values.definition: Brown porter is a dark style of beer from well-hopped beers made from brown malt.

values.label: California Common Beer
values.definition: Steam beer or California Common Beer is a highly effervescent beer made by fermenting lager yeasts at warmer ale yeast fermentation temperatures.

values.label: Chilli Pepper Beer
values.definition: A lager or ale which has been infused with flavour from Chilli Peppers.

values.label: Chocolate or Cocoa Beer
values.definition: Chocolate beer can be an ale or lager that benefits from the addition of any type of chocolate or cocoa.

values.label: Coffee Beer
values.definition: Coffee beer can be either a lager beer or an ale beer, with coffee added to boost flavour.

values.label: Contemporary Gose
values.definition: Contemporary Gose is a warm fermented beer that originated in Goslar, Germany. It is usually brewed with at least 50% of the grain bill being malted wheat. Dominant flavours in gose include a lemon sourness, an herbal characteristic, and a strong saltiness (the result of either local water sources or added salt). Gose beers typically do not have prominent hop bitterness, flavours, or aroma.

values.label: Cream Ale
values.definition: Cream ale is light in colour and are well attenuated.

values.label: Czech Pale Lager
values.definition: Pale lager is a very pale-to-golden-coloured lager beer with a well attenuated body and a varying degree of noble hop bitterness.

values.label: Dark Mild
values.definition: Malt and caramel are part of the flavour and aroma profile of Dark Mild beer, while licorice and roast malt tones may sometimes contribute as well. Hop bitterness is very low to low.

values.label: Doppelbock
values.definition: Doppelbock or double bock is a stronger version of traditional bock. Historically, Doppelbock was high in alcohol and sweet, thus serving as "liquid bread" for the Friars during times of fasting, when solid food was not permitted. Today, Doppelbock is still strong—ranging from 7%–12% or more by volume.

values.label: Double IPA
values.definition: Double India Pale Ale (IPA) is a style of pale ale. They are a stronger, very hoppy variant of IPAs.

values.label: Double Red Ale
values.definition: Double Red Ale has intense hop bitterness, flavour and aroma balanced by high notable alcohol content, fruity esters and caramel malt character. It is dark reddish-copper in colour and full-bodied.

values.label: Dunkles Weissbier
values.definition: A dark wheat version of a Weizenbier.

values.label: Eisbock
values.definition: Eisbock is a traditional specialty beer made by partially freezing a Doppelbock and removing the water ice to concentrate the flavour and alcohol content, which ranges from 9% to 13% by volume.

values.label: English Style Brown Ale
values.definition: English Style Brown ales are a style of beer, crafted originally in England, with a dark amber or brown colour. Brown ales are lightly hopped and brewed from 100% brown malt.

values.label: English Style Dark Mild Ale
values.definition: Malt and caramel are part of the flavour and aroma profile of the English style mild while licorice and roast malt tones may sometimes contribute as well. Hop bitterness is very low to low.

values.label: English Style India Pale Ale
values.definition: English Style India pale ale (IPA) is a style of pale ale, originally crafted in England. The colour of an IPA can vary from a light gold to a reddish amber.

values.label: English Style Pale Ale
values.definition: English Style Pale ale is a top fermented beer, crafted originally in England, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: English Style Pale Mild Ale
values.definition: English Style Pale Mild ale is a top fermented beer, crafted originally in England, made with predominantly pale malt but with a milder flavor. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: English Style Porter
values.definition: English Style Porter is a dark style of beer made from brown malt, crafted originally in England.

values.label: English Style Summer Ale
values.definition: Seasonal ale brewed with lighter "summery" flavours.

values.label: European Style Dark Lager
values.definition: Dunkel, or Dunkles, is a word used for several types of dark German lager. Dunkel is the German word meaning dark, and Dunkel beers typically range in colour from amber to dark reddish brown. They are characterized by their smooth malty flavour.

values.label: Extra Special Bitter
values.definition: Extra Special Bitters are essentially more aggressive and more balanced Bitters, both in alcohol and hop character. The colour range will be similar, though ESBs lean toward the darker end of the scale; dark golds to copper. Low in carbonation.

values.label: Festbier
values.definition: Festbier is brewed with imported specialty malts to create a medium bodied, malty, amber lager with a smooth finish.

values.label: Field Beer
values.definition: Field beer is made with vegetables and herbs which are added during any portion of the brewing process, providing obvious yet harmonious qualities.

values.label: Flanders Red Ale
values.definition: Flanders Red ale or Flemish red brown, is a style of sour ale. Flanders red ale is fermented with organisms other than Saccharomyces cerevisiae, especially Lactobacillus, which produces a sour character attributable to lactic acid.

values.label: Foreign Extra Stout
values.definition: Foreign Extra Stout is brewed with generous hops and roasted barley for a bittersweet balance and full-flavoured, natural bite. Developed for export, the addition of extra hops ensured this Stout would arrive in perfect condition.

values.label: French & Belgian Style Saison
values.definition: French & Belgian Style Saison is a pale ale, crafted originally in France and Belgium, that is highly carbonated, fruity, spicy, and often bottle conditioned.

values.label: French Style Bière de Garde
values.definition: Bière de Garde, or "keeping beer", is a pale ale usually brewed by farmhouses in the winter and spring, to avoid unpredictable problems with the yeast during the summertime.

values.label: Fruit Lambic
values.definition: Fruit Lambic beers include gueuze and kriek Lambic and infused with fruit flavours. Lambic differs from most other beers in that it is fermented through exposure to wild yeasts and bacteria, as opposed to exposure to carefully cultivated strains of brewer's yeast. This process gives the beer its distinctive flavour: dry, vinous, and cidery, usually with a sour aftertaste.

values.label: Fruit Wheat Beer
values.definition: Wheat beer which has added fruit flavourings.

values.label: German Style Altbier
values.definition: Altbier is a style of beer which is top-fermented, an older method than the bottom fermentation of other lager beers.

values.label: German Style Bock
values.definition: Bock is a strong lager of German origin. Several substyles exist, including maibock (helles bock, heller bock), a paler, more hopped version generally made for consumption at spring festivals; doppelbock (double bock), a stronger and maltier version; and eisbock, a much stronger version made by partially freezing the beer and removing the ice that forms.

values.label: German Style Doppelbock
values.definition: German Style Doppelbock is a stronger version of traditional bock, crafted originally in Germany. Historically, Doppelbock was high in alcohol and sweet, thus serving as "liquid bread" for the Friars during times of fasting, when solid food was not permitted. Today, Doppelbock is still strong—ranging from 7%–12% or more by volume.

values.label: German Style Eisbock
values.definition: German Style Eisbock is a traditional specialty beer, originally crafted in Germany, made by partially freezing a Doppelbock and removing the water ice to concentrate the flavour and alcohol content, which ranges from 9% to 13% by volume.

values.label: German Style Heller Bock/Maibock
values.definition: The maibock style, also known as helles bock or heller bock, is a helles lager brewed to bock strength; therefore, still as strong as traditional bock, but lighter in colour and with more hop presence.

values.label: German Style Helles Exportbier
values.definition: Dortmunder Export or Dortmunder is a pale lager. It is a soft-textured beer influenced by the Pilsner lager brewed in Pilsen.

values.label: German Style Kölsch
values.definition: Kölsch is a style of beer originating in Cologne, Germany. It has an original gravity between 11 and 16 degrees Plato (specific gravity of 1.044 to 1.065). In appearance, it is bright and clear with a straw-yellow hue. "Kölsch" has had a protected geographical indication (PGI) within the European Union, indicating a beer that is made within 50 km/30 miles of the city of Köln and brewed according to the Kölsch Konvention as defined by the members of the Köln Brewery Association (Kölner Brauerei-Verband).

values.label: German Style Leichtes Weizen
values.definition: This German wheat beer has a lighter mouthfeel than a traditional hefeweizen. Leichtes weizen is bright and refreshing with notes of banana, clove and sweet bread highlighted in its aroma and flavour.

values.label: German Style Maerzen
values.definition: German Style Märzen or Märzenbier is a lager, crafted originally in Germany, with a medium to full body and may vary in colour from pale through amber to dark brown.

values.label: German Style Oktoberfest/Wiesn
values.definition: Lager which is brewed to celebrate Oktoberfest.

values.label: German Style Pilsner
values.definition: German Style Pilsners are made with neutral and hard water. They tend to be golden in colour with a dry, crisp, and somewhat bitter flavour. Pilsner stands out from other lagers due to its more distinctive hop taste.

values.label: German Style Rye Ale
values.definition: German Style Rye beer refers to any beer, crafted originally in Germany, in which rye (generally malted) is substituted for some portion of the barley. Rye beers are considered specialty beers that are brewed with unusual fermentables such as rice, corn, or wheat.

values.label: German Style Schwarzbier
values.definition: German Style Schwarzbier, or black beer, is a dark lager, crafted originally in Germany, which tend to have an opaque, black colour with hints of chocolate or coffee flavours, and are generally around 5% ABV. They are similar to stout in that they are made from roasted malt, which gives them their dark colour.

values.label: Golden or Blonde Ale
values.definition: Golden or Blonde ales are very pale in colour and tend to be clear, crisp, and dry, with low to medium bitterness and aroma from hops, and some sweetness from malt.

values.label: Gose
values.definition: Gose is a warm fermented beer usually brewed with at least 50% of the grain bill being malted wheat. Dominant flavours in gose include a lemon sourness, a herbal characteristic, and a strong saltiness. Gose beers typically do not have prominent hop bitterness, flavours, or aroma. The beers typically have a moderate alcohol content of 4 to 5% ABV.

values.label: Gueuze
values.definition: Gueuze is a type of Lambic beer. It is made by blending young (1 year old) and old (2 to 3 year old) Lambic, which is bottled for a second fermentation. Because the young Lambic are not fully fermented, the blended beer contains fermentable sugars, which allow a second fermentation to occur.

values.label: Helles Bock
values.definition: A strong, bottom-fermented spring beer, and one designed to bridge the chasm from hearty wintry brews to bright summer fare.

values.label: Herb and Spice Beer
values.definition: An herb and spice beer is a lager or ale that contains flavours derived from flowers, roots, seeds or certain fruits or vegetables. Typically the hop character is low, allowing the added ingredient to shine through. The appearance, mouthfeel and aromas vary depending on the herb or spice used. This beer style encompasses innovative examples as well as traditional holiday and winter ales.

values.label: Honey
values.definition: A full-bodied beer with a creamy texture and copper colour. Honey beers are slightly sweet with hints of caramel.

values.label: Imperial or Double India Pale Ale
values.definition: Imperial or Double India Pale Ale is a style of pale ale. They are a stronger, very hoppy variant of IPAs.

values.label: Imperial Red Ale
values.definition: Imperial Red Ale is a beer ranging from amber to deep crimson in colour, with a robust, sweet, toasted malt character that is balanced by a bold, pronounced hop profile.

values.label: Imperial Stout
values.definition: Imperial stout is a strong dark beer. Imperial stouts have a high alcohol content, usually over 9% abv, and are among the darkest available beer styles.

values.label: International Style Pale Ale
values.definition: International Style Pale ale is a top fermented beer, crafted from various recipes around the world, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: International Style Pale Lager
values.definition: International Style Pale lager is a top fermented beer, crafted from various recipes around the world, made with predominantly pale malt. The highest proportion of pale malts results in a lighter colour.

values.label: International Style Pilsner
values.definition: International Style Pilsners are made with neutral and hard water. They tend to be golden in colour with a dry, crisp, and somewhat bitter flavour. Pilsner stands out from other lagers due to its more distinctive hop taste.

values.label: Irish Style Dry Stout
values.definition: Dry stout are stout beers which are less sweet than other stout beers.

values.label: Irish Style Extra Stout
values.definition: Extra Stout is a dark, top-fermented beer which are stronger than traditional stout beers.

values.label: Irish Style Red Ale
values.definition: Irish red ale, red ale, or Irish ale is a name used by brewers in Ireland.

values.label: Irish Style Stout
values.definition: Irish Style stout is a dark, top fermented beer, crafted originally in Irish, with a number of variations, including dry stout, Baltic porter, milk stout, and imperial stout.

values.label: Kölsch
values.definition: Kölsch is a style of beer with an original gravity between 11 and 16 degrees Plato (specific gravity of 1.044 to 1.065).

values.label: Lambic
values.definition: Lambic beers include gueuze and kriek Lambic. Lambic differs from most other beers in that it is fermented through exposure to wild yeasts and bacteria, as opposed to exposure to carefully cultivated strains of brewer's yeast. This process gives the beer its distinctive flavour: dry, vinous, and cidery, usually with a sour aftertaste.

values.label: Leipzig Style Gose
values.definition: Leipzig-Style Gose is a warm fermented beer that originated in Goslar, Germany. It is usually brewed with at least 50% of the grain bill being malted wheat. Dominant flavours in gose include a lemon sourness, an herbal characteristic, and a strong saltiness (the result of either local water sources or added salt). Gose beers typically do not have prominent hop bitterness, flavours, or aroma.

values.label: Lime
values.definition: Typically light in flavour with a refreshing lime taste. The intensity of the lime can differ from very subtle to strong.

values.label: Märzen
values.definition: Märzen or Märzenbier is a lager with a medium to full body and may vary in colour from pale through amber to dark brown.

values.label: Mixed-Culture Brett Beer
values.definition: Mixed Culture Brett beers vary in colour and can take on the hues of added fruits or other ingredients. Horsey, goaty, leathery, phenolic and some fruity acidic character derived from a mixed variety of Brettanomyces organisms may be evident, but in balance with other components of a Brett beer.

values.label: Münchner (Munich) Style Dunkel
values.definition: Dunkel, or Dunkles, is a word used for several types of dark German lager. Dunkel is the German word meaning dark, and Dunkel beers typically range in colour from amber to dark reddish brown. They are characterized by their smooth malty flavour.

values.label: Münchner (Munich) Style Helles
values.definition: Helles or Hell is a traditional German pale lager beer, produced chiefly in Southern Germany, particularly Munich.

values.label: Oatmeal Stout
values.definition: Stout is a dark, top-fermented beer with a number of variations, including dry stout, Baltic porter, milk stout, and imperial stout. Oatmeal stout is a stout with a proportion of oats, normally a maximum of 30%, added during the brewing process.

values.label: Old Ale
values.definition: Old ale is a term commonly applied to dark, malty beers in England, generally above 5% ABV, also to dark ales of any strength in Australia

values.label: Ordinary Bitter
values.definition: Ordinary Bitter is a variation of a British style of pale ale that varies in colour from gold to dark amber, and in strength typically from 3% to 5.5% alcohol by volume.

values.label: Oud Bruin
values.definition: Oud Bruin, is a style of sour ale fermented with organisms other than Saccharomyces cerevisiae, especially Lactobacillus, which produces a sour character attributable to lactic acid.

values.label: Pumpkin Spice Beer
values.definition: Perhaps the most seasonal of seasonal beers, the Pumpkin Spice beer style is brewed with pumpkin spices. Since the fruit does not have much of a taste by itself, many craft brewers have taken to adding spices typically found in pumpkin pie, like cinnamon and clove.

values.label: Pumpkin/Squash Beer
values.definition: Perhaps the most seasonal of seasonal beers, the Pumpkin/Squash beer style can be brewed with pumpkin or even winter squash. Since the fruit does not have much of a taste by itself, many craft brewers have taken to adding spices typically found in pumpkin pie, like cinnamon and clove.

values.label: Robust Porter
values.definition: Robust porter is a dark style of beer from well-hopped beers made from brown malt.

values.label: Rye Beer
values.definition: Rye beer refers to any beer in which rye (generally malted) is substituted for some portion of the barley. Rye beers are considered specialty beers that are brewed with unusual fermentables such as rice, corn, or wheat.

values.label: Sahti
values.definition: Sahti is a traditional Finnish unfiltered beer brewed with fresh yeast. The raw materials used are mainly barley malt and, in small quantities, rye malt, and sometimes wheat and oats.

values.label: Saison
values.definition: Saison is a pale ale that is highly carbonated, fruity, spicy, and often bottle conditioned.

values.label: Schwarzbier
values.definition: Schwarzbier, or black beer, is a dark lager which tend to have an opaque, black colour with hints of chocolate or coffee flavours, and are generally around 5% ABV. They are similar to stout in that they are made from roasted malt, which gives them their dark colour.

values.label: Scotch Ale
values.definition: Scotch ale tends toward sweetness from residual sugars, malty notes, and a full body.

values.label: Session India Pale Ale
values.definition: Session India Pale Ale (IPA) is a style of pale ale. The colour of an IPA can vary from a light gold to a reddish amber.

values.label: Smoke Porter
values.definition: Smoke porter is a dark style of beer from well-hopped beers made from brown malt.

values.label: South German Style Bernsteinfarbenes Weizen
values.definition: Bernsteinfarbenes Weizen is a style of Weizenbock. Weizenbock is a style of bock brewed using wheat instead of barley. The style combines darker Munich malts and top-fermenting wheat beer yeast, brewed at the strength of a doppelbock.

values.label: South German Style Dunkel Weizen
values.definition: The German-style Dunkelweizen can be considered a cross between a German-style Dunkel and a hefeweizen. Distinguished by its sweet maltiness and chocolate-like character, it can also have banana and clove (and occasionally vanilla or bubblegum) esters from weizen ale yeast.

values.label: South German Style Hefeweizen
values.definition: Hefeweizen is particularly noted for its low hop bitterness (about 15 IBUs) and relatively high carbonation (approaching four volumes), considered important to balance the beer's relatively malty sweetness. Another balancing flavour note unique to Hefeweizen beer is its phenolic character; its signature phenol is 4-vinyl guaiacol,[8] a metabolite of ferulic acid, the result of fermentation by top-fermenting yeast appropriate for the style.

values.label: South German Style Kristal Weizen
values.definition: This wheat beer, sometimes called “Kristal Weissbier,” is filtered after fermentation to remove yeast. The result is a crystal-clear weizen beer with no haze or clouds. Exhibiting aroma and flavour characteristics similar to Hefeweizen, Kristalweizen German beer is generally perceived as more crisp and clean on the palate.

values.label: South German Style Weizenbock
values.definition: South German Style Weizenbock is a style of bock. Crafted originally in Southern Germany brewed using wheat instead of barley. The style combines darker Munich malts and top fermenting wheat beer yeast, brewed at the strength of a Doppelbock.

values.label: Specialty Honey Beer
values.definition: Specialty honey Beer is a style of Honey beer.

values.label: Specialty IPA
values.definition: Specialty India pale ale is a style of pale ale.

values.label: Specialty Saison
values.definition: Specialty Saison is a style of Saison.

values.label: Special or Best Bitter
values.definition: Special or Best Bitter Saison is a style of Bitter.

values.label: Sweet Stout or Cream Stout
values.definition: Stout is a dark, top-fermented beer with a number of variations, including dry stout, Baltic porter, milk stout, and imperial stout. Milk stout (also called sweet stout or cream stout) is a stout containing lactose, a sugar derived from milk. Because lactose cannot be fermented by beer yeast, it adds sweetness and body to the finished beer.

values.label: Tropical Stout
values.definition: Stout is a dark, top-fermented beer with a number of variations, including dry stout, Baltic porter, milk stout, and imperial stout. Tropical stout is a stout containing tropical flavouruings.

values.label: Vienna Lager
values.definition: Distinctly amber coloured Vienna lager is a reddish-brown or copper-coloured beer with medium body and slight malt sweetness. The malt aroma and flavour may have a toasted character.

values.label: Vienna Style Lager
values.definition: Vienna Style Lager is a type of beer, originally crafted in Vienna, conditioned at low temperatures. Lagers can be pale, amber, or dark. Pale lager is the most widely consumed and commercially available style of beer.

values.label: Wee Heavy
values.definition: Wee Heavy is a version of Scotch Ale. Scotch ale tends toward sweetness from residual sugars, malty notes, and a full body.

values.label: Weissbier
values.definition: Weizenbier or Hefeweizen or Weißbier is a beer, traditionally from Bavaria, in which a significant proportion of malted barley is replaced with malted wheat.

values.label: Weizenbock
values.definition: Weizenbock is a style of bock brewed using wheat instead of barley. The style combines darker Munich malts and top fermenting wheat beer yeast, brewed at the strength of a Doppelbock.

values.label: Wild Beer
values.definition: Wild beer is brewed with something in addition to—or in place of—traditional brewer’s yeast, such as Brettanomyces.

values.label: Witbier
values.definition: Witbier, white beer, bière blanche, or simply witte is a barley/wheat, top fermented beer. It gets its name from the suspended yeast and wheat proteins which cause the beer to look hazy, or white, when cold. It is a descendant from those medieval beers which were flavoured and preserved with a blend of spices and other plants such as coriander, orange, and bitter orange referred to as "gruit" instead of using hops.

values.label: Wood and Barrel-Aged Beer
values.definition: A Lager aged in wood barrels. Lagers can be pale, amber, or dark.

values.label: Wood and Barrel-Aged Dark Beer
values.definition: A dark beer which has been aged in wood barrels. They range in colour from amber to dark reddish brown. They are characterized by their smooth malty flavour.

values.label: Wood and Barrel-Aged Pale to Amber Beer
values.definition: A Pale lager, aged in wood barrels, which is a very pale-to-golden-coloured lager beer with a well attenuated body and a varying degree of noble hop bitterness.

values.label: Wood and Barrel-Aged Sour Beer
values.definition: A sour beer, aged in wood barrels, which has an intentionally acidic, tart or sour taste.

values.label: Wood and Barrel-Aged Strong Beer
values.definition: A strong beer, aged in wood barrels.

values.label: Bioengineered product
values.definition: A required disclosure where a product is a 100% bioengineered product as defined by and compliant with regulatory bodies, remaining consistent within markets (an example would be the US National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard).

values.label: Contains bioengineered ingredient(s)
values.definition: A required disclosure where a product is a product with less than 100% of the ingredients being bioengineered as defined by and compliant with regulatory bodies within specific markets (an example would be the US National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard).

values.label: Derived from bioengineering
values.definition: A voluntary disclosure where a product is 100% derived from bioengineering as defined by and complaint with regulatory bodies, remaining consistent within specific markets (an example would be the US National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard).

values.label: Ingredient(s) derived from a bioengineered source
values.definition: A voluntary disclosure where a product is a product with less than 100% of the ingredients being derived from a bioengineered source as defined by and compliant with regulatory bodies, remaining consistent within specific markets (an example would be the US National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard).

values.label: European Bitterness Units
values.definition: European Bitterness Units are a chemical measurement of the number of bittering compounds, specifically isomerized and oxidized alpha acids, polyphenols, and a few other select bittering chemicals, that make your beer taste bitter. The beer sample is not handled in a pipette dipped in octanol.

values.label: International Bitterness Units
values.definition: International Bitterness Units are a chemical measurement of the number of bittering compounds, specifically isomerized and oxidized alpha acids, polyphenols, and a few other select bittering chemicals, that make your beer taste bitter. The beer sample is handled in a pipette dipped in octanol.

values.label: Brand label
values.definition: A product that is not produced strictly for a trading partner or a purchasing group. It can be sold through any retailers. The formula/design is owned by the manufacturer, not the ultimate recipient trading partner or purchasing group. Also known as national brand.

values.label: Bulk
values.definition: Any product which has completed all production processing stage up to, but not including final packaging or shipped as mass product not to be sold individually to end consumer. Usually sold to re-packaging, institutional, cash and carry type trade channels.

values.label: Custom Label
values.definition: A product that is produced strictly for a trading partner or a purchasing group. There is a distinction that the formula/design is owned by the ultimate recipient trading partner or purchasing group. In foodservice this is a unique distinction from private label distribution. For example a salad dressing made for a large fast food restaurant i.e. Burger King, Subway, etc.

values.label: Plain Label
values.definition: A product that is produced strictly for a trading partner or a purchasing group. There is a distinction that the formula/design is owned by the ultimate recipient trading partner or purchasing group. This type of product is intended to be the lowest price in its range. It is also known in markets as White Label, No-Frills, Entry-Level, First Price, Lowest Price, etc.

values.label: Private Label
values.definition: A product that is produced strictly for a trading partner or a purchasing group. The brand name is owned by the recipient trading partner or purchasing group. There is a distinction that the formula/design is owned by the manufacturer or distributor not the ultimate recipient trading partner or purchasing group.

values.label: Restricted Distribution
values.definition: The Data Source has restrictions on where, how and/or to whom the product may be sold. The brand label is NOT owned by the trading partner recipient or purchasing group

values.label: Unrestricted Distribution
values.definition: The Data Recipient has the permission to sell the Trade Item as per their trading partner agreement.  The brand label is NOT owned by the trading partner recipient or purchasing group

values.label: Extra soft

values.label: Hard

values.label: Medium
values.definition: Medium bristles, e.g., for toothbrushes not recommended for everyday use on natural teeth because it can be too hard on gums and tooth enamel.

values.label: Soft

values.label: Super soft

values.label: Dish brush

values.label: Duster

values.label: Dustpan and brush set

values.label: Floor scrub brush
values.definition: A brush that consists of short stiff bristles with a long handle that is intended for cleaning hard floors.

values.definition: The cannabinoid content stated as the total amount found in the product package. Example: Cannabinoid content in a bag of cannabis gummies.

values.label: Discrete content

values.label: Cannabichromene (CBC)
values.definition: Cannabichromene (CBC) is found in the cannabis plant. It is an anti-inflammatory which may contribute to the pain-killing effect of cannabis. It is also called cannabichrome, cannanbichromene, pentylcannabichromene or cannabinochromene. CAS number: 20675-51-8

values.label: Cannabidiol (CBD)
values.definition: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a compound that is one of the main constituents of cannabis, having mild psychoactive effects. CAS number: 13956-29-1

values.label: Cannabidiolic acid (CBDA)
values.definition: Cannabidiolic acid (CBDA) is found in the cannabis plant and it is the chemical precursor to cannabidiol (CBD). Also known as: CRM, β-Resorcylic Acid. CAS number: 1244-58-2

values.label: Cannabigerol (CBG)
values.definition: Cannabigerol (CBG) is a compound found in the cannabis plant.  CBG is the decarboxylated form of cannabigerolic acid, the parent molecule from which other cannabinoids are synthesised. CAS number:  25654-31-3

values.label: Cannabinol (CBN)
values.definition: Cannabinol (CBN) is a mildly psychoactive cannabinoid found in trace amounts from cannabis. CAS number: 521-35-7

values.label: Delta-10 THC (D10-THC)
values.definition: Delta-10 -tetrahydrocannabinol (Delta-10 THC) is a psychoactive cannabinoid found in trace amounts in the cannabis plant. CAS number: 95588-87-7

values.label: Delta-8 THC (D8-THC)
values.definition: Delta-8-tetrahydrocannabinol (Delta-8 THC) is a psychoactive cannabinoid found in the cannabis plant. CAS number: 5957-75-5

values.label: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)/Delta-9 THC
values.definition: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or Delta-9 THC is the principal psychoactive constituent of cannabis. CAS number:  1972-08-3

values.label: Tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA)
values.definition: Tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA) is a precursor of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), an active component of cannabis. CAS number: 23978-85-0

values.label: Tetrahydrocannabivarin (THCV)
values.definition: Tetrahydrocannabivarin (THCV) is a homologue of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) which produce psychoactive effects. CAS number: 31262-37-0

values.label: THC-0 acetate (THC-0)
values.definition: THC-0-acetate (THC-0) is the acetate ester of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). CAS number: 23132-17-4

values.label: Broad Spectrum
values.definition:
Broad spectrum CBD (cannabidiol) is a bit of a mix between Full Spectrum CBD and CBD Isolate.
Like Full Spectrum CBD, the other compounds found within the plant are preserved in the extract; however, like CBD Isolate, THC is completely removed.
Because Broad Spectrum CBD contains multiple cannabinoids, it can deliver the enhanced benefits of the “entourage effect,” without the risk of psychoactive effects of THC.Broad Spectrum contains all phytocannabinoids in the plant but does not contain any detectable amount of THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

values.label: Full Spectrum
values.definition: Full spectrum CBD (cannabidiol) is an extract that contains all compounds found naturally occurring in the plant, including terpenes, essential oils, and other cannabinoids.Full Spectrum refers to cannabis-derived from the whole plant that contains CBD and other phytocannabinoids such as THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) , CBN (cannabinol) , THCA (Tetrahydrocannabinolic acid), CBC (cannabichromene), and CBG (cannabigerol).

values.label: Hemp Seed Oil
values.definition: Hemp seed oil is cold pressed from hemp seeds. It does not contain CBD (cannabidiol) or any phytocannabinoids.

values.label: Isolate
values.definition: CBD (cannabidiol) isolate is the purest form of CBD, which is produced by removing all other compounds found in the plant including terpenes, flavonoids, plant parts, and other cannabinoids. CBD isolate, which is a purified CBD molecule. CBD isolate is white and powdery in its appearance. It does not contain other phytocannabinoids like full or broad spectrum.

values.label: Nano CBD
values.definition: Nano CBD (cannabidiol) is a compound where the molecules of CBD are shrunk down to extremely small sizes (less than 100nm) and turned into a water-based form. This process allows the CBD to pass through skin much more easily and quickly than any oil-based form.

values.label: Indica Dominant
values.definition: A species of Cannabis native to India and neighbouring countries. Indica strains often have higher levels of Cannabidiol (CBD), but the tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content isn’t necessarily less. - Family/Genus/Species: Cannabaceae/Cannabis/C. indica

values.label: Surrounding Nets
values.definition:
A surrounding net is a fishing net which surrounds fish and other aquatic animals on the sides and underneath.
Surrounding nets are divided into:
• Purse seines           
• Surrounding nets without purse lines                            
• Surrounding nets (not enough information)

values.label: Seine Nets
values.definition:
A seine net is a fishing net that hangs vertically in the water with its bottom edge held down by weights and its top edge buoyed by floats. Seine nets can be deployed from the shore as a beach seine, or from a boat.
Seine nets are divided into:
• Beach seines                                                
• Boat seines                                                   
• Seine nets (not enough information)

values.label: Trawls
values.definition:
Trawls are cone-shaped net (made from two, four or more panels) which are towed, by one or two boats, on the bottom or in midwater (pelagic).
Trawls are divided into:
• Beam trawls                                                 
• Single boat bottom otter trawls                    
• Twin bottom otter trawls                              
• Multiple bottom otter trawls                          
• Bottom pair trawls                                        
• Bottom trawls                                               
• Single boat midwater otter trawls                
• Midwater pair trawls                                       
• Midwater trawls (not enough information)          
• Semi-pelagic trawls                                      
• Trawls (not enough information)

values.label: Dredges
values.definition:
Dredges are gears which are dragged along the bottom to catch shellfish. They consist of a mouth frame to which a holding bag constructed of metal rings or meshes is attached.
Dredges are divided into:
• Towed dredges                                            
• Hand dredges                                               
• Mechanized dredges                                      
• Dredges (not enough information)

values.label: Lift Nets
values.definition:
Lift nets are horizontal netting panels or bag shaped like a parallelepiped, pyramid or cone with the opening facing upwards which are  submerged at a certain depth, left for a while, the time necessary for light or bait to attract fish over the opening, then lifted out of the water.
Lift nets are divided into:
• Portable lift nets                               
• Boat-operated lift nets                     
• Shore-operated stationary lift nets  
• Lift nets (not enough information)

values.label: Gillnets and Entangling Nets
values.definition:
Gillnets and entangling nets are strings of single, double or triple netting walls, vertical, near by the surface, in midwater on on the bottom, in which fish will gill, entangle or enmesh. Gillnets and entangling nets have floats on the upper line (headrope) and, in general, weights on the ground-line (footrope).
Gillnets and entangling nets are divided into: 
• Set gillnets (anchored)                                                
• Drift gillnets                                                                   
• Encircling gillnets                                                         
• Gillnets and entangling nets (not enough information)

values.label: Traps
values.definition:
Traps, large stationary nets or barrages or pots, are gears in which the fish are retained or enter voluntarily and will be hampered from escaping. They are designed in such manner that the entrance itself became a non-return device, allowing the fish to enter the trap but making it impossible to leave the catching chamber.
Traps are divided into:
• Stationary uncovered pound nets      
• Pots                                                                          
• Fyke nets                                      
• Stow nets                                     
• Barriers, fences, weirs, etc         
• Aerial traps                                     
• Traps (not enough information)

values.label: Hooks and Lines
values.definition:
Hooks and lines are gear where the fish is attracted by a natural or artificial bait (lures) placed on a hook fixed to the end of a line or snood, on which they get caught. Hooks or metallic points (jigs) are also used to catch fish by ripping them when they pass in its range of movement.
Hooks and lines are divided into:
• Handlines and hand-operated pole-and-lines 
• Mechanised lines and pole-and-lines
• Set longlines
• Drifting longlines
• Longlines (not enough information)
• Vertical lines                                                 
• Trolling lines                                                  
• Hooks and lines (not enough information)

values.label: Attributional
values.definition: An attributional life cycle assessment (ALCA) is focusing on describing, assessing and quantifying environmentally relevant physical flows of specific life cycle(s) and its subsystems. An ALCA gives an estimate of what part of the global environmental burdens belongs to the study object. An ALCA does not include environmental benefits or other indirect consequences that arise outside the life cycle of the investigated product.

values.label: Consequential
values.definition: A consequential life cycle assessment (CLCA) is focusing on describing, assessing and quantifying environmentally relevant flows and how they will change in response to possible decisions. A CLCA gives an estimate of how the production and use of the study object affect the global environmental burdens. For example, an increased use of a material in the studied system can lead to less material being used in other systems.

values.label: Cradle to consumption
values.definition: Total amount of CO2 emission from a life cycle assessment (LCA) model that assesses a product’s environmental footprint from raw materials extraction until it is consumed. (PEF guidance, the European Commission 2021b)

values.label: Cradle to gate
values.definition: Total amount of CO2 emission from a life cycle assessment (LCA) model that assesses a product’s environmental footprint from raw materials extraction until it leaves the factory gate.

values.label: Cradle to grave
values.definition: Total amount of CO2 emission from a life cycle assessment (LCA) model that assesses a product’s environmental footprint from raw materials extraction until its disposal, including manufacturing, transportation, product use.

values.label: End of life
values.definition: The emission of the product when it is disposed, recycled, recovered after use.

values.label: Manufacturing
values.definition: The emissions resulting from the manufacturing/production of the product.

values.label: Raw materials
values.definition: The emissions resulting from the production/extraction, packaging, storage, warehousing and transportation of raw materials.

values.label: Transport of final product
values.definition: The emissions resulting from the distribution of the product to the retail network or to downstream stakeholders. This stage includes transport of the final product and its packaging, storage and warehousing.

values.label: Use
values.definition: The emissions of the product when used by the consumer.

values.label: Carbon footprint standard
values.definition: Product-specific value, based on carbon footprint standard (ISO 14067).

values.label: ENVIMAT
values.definition: Value for the product-group from an input-output study, based on ENVIMAT in Finland (Nissinen et al. 2019, SYKEra 15/2019).

values.label: EPD
values.definition: Environmental Product Declaration (EPD).

values.label: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol
values.definition: The Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard can be used to understand the full life cycle emissions of a product and focus efforts on the greatest Greenhouse Gas (GHG) reduction opportunities.

values.label: ISO 14064
values.definition: ISO 14064 specifies requirements for selecting Greenhouse Gas (GHG) validators/verifiers, establishing the level of assurance, objectives, criteria and scope, determining the validation/verification approach, assessing GHG data, information, information systems and controls, evaluating GHG assertions and preparing validation/verification statements.

values.label: Li/SvDH
values.definition: A methodology developed by Livsmedelsföretagen (Li) and Svensk Dagligvaruhandel (SvDH), based on a report and established standards from RISE (Research Institutes of Sweden AB). The approach employs a screening Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) from cradle to gate, encompassing transport, packaging, and processing stages.

values.label: Not classified
values.definition: A standard calculation method, not classified in the codelist.

values.label: PCR
values.definition: Product Category Rules.

values.label: PCR EDF
values.definition: Product-specific value, based on Product Category Rule (PCR) of an Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) system.

values.label: PEF
values.definition: The Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) methodology is performed following the PEF guidelines published by the European Commission and, if available, specific category rules (PEFCRs).

values.label: ReCiPe
values.definition: Based on National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM), Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Product Category Rule (PCR).

values.definition: Kilogram CO2 equivalent per 100 millilitre.

values.definition: Kilogram CO2 equivalent per functional unit.

values.label: External verification
values.definition: The values have been verified by an external party.

values.label: Not verified
values.definition: The values have been calculated according to the reported calculation method, but have not been verified.

values.label: Peer reviewed
values.definition: The values and methodology have been reviewed internally or by 3rd party.

values.label: Brine Solution
values.definition: A salt water or whey solution that cures cheese during the maturing process.

values.label: Foil
values.definition: A type of container used in the process of cheese making, usually made in small forms and wrapped and then wrapped in foil to mature.

values.label: Mould
values.definition: A type of container used in the process of cheese making, usually the maturing is performed in a wooden, metal, plastic type container. This is not the type of mould like spores which also can be referenced in cheese making

values.label: Other
values.definition: The type of container in which the process of maturing cheese is not specified or is of a type other than the codes available

values.label: Textile
values.definition: A method that a cheese is matured while wrapped in a cloth or textile of some sort during the maturing process.

values.label: Dairy
values.definition: "Dairy" cheese(artisanal or industrial) is made from milk from several farms, transformed into cheese in a dairy. Manufacturing is more or less automated, the milk is mixed and often standardized. The milk used can be raw, pasteurized, heat treated or micro-filtered.

values.label: Farm
values.definition: The "farmer" cheese is produced with milk from a single farm, typical of its region. It is almost always made from raw milk.

values.label: Fruitier
values.definition: The "fruitier or fruit" cheese is made in a common place where milks of the same origin are gathered. Producers respect traditional regional customs and are grouped into cooperatives. The use of raw milk is essential.

values.label: Blue veined
values.definition: The cheese that is exposed to mould is ripened and the veins of mould appears within the body of the cheese.

values.label: Ripened
values.definition: The ripening process develops within the whole body of the cheese.

values.label: Surface ripened
values.definition: The ripening process starts from the surface and moves into the body of the cheese. These cheeses are often one colour on the exterior and another on the interior; the interior is usually soft and buttery.  The outer "rind" can be consumed and may be washed prior to packaging.

values.label: Unripened or fresh
values.definition: The cheese has not undergone any ripening.  They are "fresh" and often spreadable.

values.label: American cheese
values.definition: A type of processed cheese that is smooth hard white or yellow cheese similar to a mild Cheddar.

values.label: Bavarian blue
values.definition: A soft, blue-veined cheese produced with the pasteurized cow’s milk. The cheese is injected with the Penicillium roqueforti during its maturation period and the fungus develops inside the cheese.

values.label: Beaufort
values.definition: A firm, raw cow's milk cheese with pale yellow colour. It has a smooth and creamy texture and lacks holes like other Gruyère-style cheeses, Comté, Vacherin Fribourgeois or Emmental.

values.label: Beer cheese
values.definition: A cheese spread usually consists of a processed cheese base with a sharp cheddar flavor. To this, enough beer is added to provide flavour and texture, as well as garlic, and a variety of spices including dry mustard, horseradish and cayenne pepper.

values.label: Blue Cheshire
values.definition: A dense and crumbly cheese that has blue veins like Stilton or Shropshire Blue but is less creamy than Stilton and is not coloured orange as Shropshire Blue.

values.label: Blue Shropshire
values.definition: A blue cheese that is made from pasteurised cows' milk and uses vegetable rennet. The orange colour comes from the addition of annatto, a natural food colouring. Penicillium roqueforti produces the veining.

values.label: Blue Stilton
values.definition: A blue cheese that is made from pasteurized milk. Penicillium roqueforti is added to generate a characteristic smell and taste.

values.label: Brick cheese
values.definition: A semisoft, sweet-tasting cheese, made from the whole milk of cows and produced in brick form.

values.label: Brie
values.definition: A soft cow's-milk cheese that is pale in color with a slight grayish tinge under a rind of white mould. The rind is typically eaten, with its flavour depending largely upon the ingredients used and its manufacturing environment.

values.label: Brunost or Gjetost
values.definition: A farmhouse and creamery semi-hard cheese which is made with whey, milk, and/or cream. Also known as Geitost, Mysost, Brown cheese.

values.label: Buttercheese
values.definition: A semi-soft, cow's milk cheese (Butterkäse) that has a buttery flavour and appearance. It is often described as mild, partly due to its brief aging time.

values.label: Caboc
values.definition: A cream cheese made with double cream or cream-enriched milk. This rennet-free cheese is smooth, slightly thicker and grainier than clotted cream, while the colour is a pale primrose yellow.

values.label: Cabrales
values.definition: A blue cheese that can be made from pure, unpasteurized cow’s milk or blended in the traditional manner with goat and/or sheep milk, which lends the cheese a stronger, spicier flavor.

values.label: Caciocavallo
values.definition: A type of stretched-curd cheese made out of sheep's or cow's milk. Shaped like a teardrop, it is similar in taste to the aged Southern Italian Provolone cheese, with a hard edible rind.

values.label: Caerphilly
values.definition: A hard, crumbly white cheese that is made from cow's milk, and generally has a fat content of between 45% and 55%. It has a mild taste, with a tang of lemon.

values.label: Camembert
values.definition: A moist, soft, creamy, surface-ripened cow's milk cheese. It is sometimes compared in look and taste to brie cheese.

values.label: Cantal
values.definition: An uncooked firm cheese with a strong, tangy butter taste that grows with age. A well ripened Cantal has a vigorous nutty and tangy taste, while a young cheese has a hint of sweet and buttery taste of raw milk.

values.label: Chaource
values.definition: A cow's milk cheese with cylindrical in shape. It has a soft-ripened, creamy and a little bit crumbly, non-elastic texture and is surrounded by a white Penicillium candidum rind.

values.label: Cheddar
values.definition: A relatively hard, off-white (or orange if colourings such as annatto are added), sometimes sharp-tasting, natural cheese. The style and quality of cheeses labelled as cheddar may vary greatly, with some processed cheeses being packaged as "cheddar" while bearing little resemblance.

values.label: Cheese in brine
values.definition: A cheese that is matured in brine in an airtight or semi-permeable container. This process gives the cheese good stability, inhibiting bacterial growth even in warmer climates. Brined cheeses may be soft or hard, varying in moisture content and in colour and flavour according to the type of milk used.

values.label: Colby
values.definition: A semi-hard cow's milk cheese with a Hazel-nutty flavour and an orange colour. It is often found blended with Manchego cheese. It is similar to cheddar cheese but does not undergo the cheddaring process. Considered a semi-hard cheese, Colby is softer, moister, and milder than cheddar because it is produced through a washed-curd process

values.label: Colby jack
values.definition: A cheese that is made from Colby and Monterey Jack. It is classified as semi-hard in texture and is mild due to its two-week aging process.

values.label: Colwick
values.definition: A fresh cheese that is soft, curdy similar to cream cheese in texture but slightly more sour in flavour. The cheese is produced in such a way that it has a distinctive bowl shape and traditionally locals would fill the bowl with different fillings, both sweet and savoury.

values.label: Cottage cheese
values.definition: A simple fresh cheese curd product with a mild flavor and a creamy, non-homogenous, soupy texture. It is also known as curds and whey. It is made from cow's milk by draining the cheese, as opposed to pressing it to make cheese curd—retaining some of the whey and keeping the curds loose.

values.label: Coulommiers
values.definition: A soft ripened cheese that is made from cow's milk and is usually in the shape of a disc with white, bloomy, edible Penicillium candidum rind.

values.label: Cream cheese
values.definition: A soft, usually mild-tasting fresh cheese made from milk and cream. Stabilizers such as carob bean gum and carrageenan are often added in industrial production.

values.label: Curd cheese
values.definition: Curd cheese is the moist pieces of curdled milk that are made from fresh pasteurized milk in the process of creating cheese.  After the milk clots, it is then cut into cubes; the result is a mixture of whey and curd. This mixture is then cooked and pressed to release the whey from the curd, creating the final product of cheese curd.

values.label: Danbo
values.definition: Danbo is a ripened firm/semi-hard cheese. The body has a near white or ivory through to light yellow or yellow colour and a firm-textured (when pressed by thumb) texture, suitable for cutting, with few to plentiful, evenly distributed, smooth and round pea sized gas holes, but a few openings and splits are acceptable. The shape is flat squared or parallelepiped. The cheese is manufactured and sold with or without hard or slightly moist smear ripened rind, which may be coated.

values.label: Danish blue
values.definition: A strong, blue-veined cheese (Danablu). It is a semi-soft creamery cheese typically drum- or block-shaped and has a yellowish, slightly moist, edible rind. Made from full fat cow's milk and homogenized cream. Danablu often marketed under the trademark Danish Blue Cheese within North America.

values.label: Dolcelatte
values.definition: A blue veined soft cheese that is made from cow's milk and has a sweet taste.

values.label: Double Gloucester
values.definition: A traditional, full fat, hard cheese made from pasteurised or unpasteurised cow's milk.

values.label: Dunlop
values.definition: A sweet-milk cheese made from pasteurized cow's milk. When young, the cheese develops a nutty flavour and smooth, close texture. As it matures, the texture becomes firm and builds up sharp flavours.

values.label: Edam
values.definition: A semi-hard cheese that is traditionally sold in flat-ended spheres with a pale-yellow interior and a coat, or rind, of red paraffin wax.

values.label: Emmenthal
values.definition: A yellow, medium-hard cheese with savory but mild taste that is classified as a Swiss-type or Alpine cheese. Also know as Emmental or Emmentaler.

values.label: Epoisses
values.definition: Époisses is a pungent soft-paste cow's milk cheese with distinctive soft red-orange colour.

values.label: Esrom
values.definition: A Trappist-style pale yellow semi-soft cow's milk cheese which has a pungent aroma and a full, sweet flavour. Esrom is a porous cheese, with many small holes throughout, and is slightly elastic and buttery in texture. It is also known as Danish Port Salut.

values.label: Farmer cheese
values.definition: A pressed cottage cheese that is made by adding rennet and bacterial starter to coagulate and acidify milk. Farmer cheese may be made from the milk of cows, sheep or goats, with each giving its own texture and flavour.

values.label: Feta
values.definition: A brined curd white cheese that is soft, with small or no holes, a compact touch, few cuts, and no skin. It is formed into large blocks and aged in brine. Its flavour is tangy and salty, ranging from mild to sharp.

values.label: Fontina
values.definition: A semi-soft to hard cheese that is mild to medium-sharp in flavour from cow's milk. The characteristic flavour of Fontina is mild but distinctively nutty and savoury.

values.label: Fourme d'Ambert
values.definition: A semi-hard blue cheese that is made from raw cow's milk with a distinct and narrow cylindrical shape. It is inoculated with Penicillium roqueforti spores and aged for at least 28 days.

values.label: Fromage blanc
values.definition: A creamy soft cheese made with whole or skimmed milk and cream.

values.label: Fromage de Chevre
values.definition: A cheese made from goat's milk (Goat cheese). It is made in a wide variety of styles, from soft fresh cheese to hard aged cheese.

values.label: Fromage frais
values.definition: A type of a white cheese, usually made with skim milk, with a variety of textures depending upon how it has been produced. It is often used in combination with other ingredients such as savory spices or sweet berries.

values.label: Geheimratskaese
values.definition: A pasteurised cow's milk cheese that has a light-yellow colour with small holes and a mild, aromatic flavour. It has a waxed rind, which is usually red.

values.label: Gorgonzola
values.definition: A veined blue cheese made from unskimmed cow's milk. It can be buttery or firm, crumbly and quite salty, with a "bite" from its blue veining.

values.label: Gouda
values.definition: A sweet, creamy, yellow semi-hard to hard cow's milk cheese.

values.label: Gruyere
values.definition: A hard yellow cheese that is classified as a Swiss-type or Alpine cheese, and is sweet but slightly salty, with a flavour that varies widely with age.

values.label: Halloumi
values.definition: A semi-hard, unripened cheese made from a mixture of goat's and sheep's milk, and sometimes also cow's milk.

values.label: Havarti
values.definition: A semi-soft cow's milk cheese. Havarti is a washed-curd cheese, which contributes to the subtle flavour of the cheese. It is an interior-ripened cheese that is rindless, smooth, and slightly bright-surfaced with a cream to yellow colour depending on type.

values.label: Jarlsberg
values.definition: A mild cheese made from cow's-milk, with large, regular eyes. It has a yellow wax rind and a semi-firm yellow interior. It is a mild, buttery cheese and the flavour has been described as "clean and rich, with a slightly sweet and nutty flavour".

values.label: Kochkaese
values.definition: A spreadable, creamy sour milk cheese (cooked cheese).

values.label: Lancashire
values.definition: A cow's milk cheese with a crumbly texture and a mild flavour when the cheese is young, but as it becomes older, the taste matures and becomes sharper.

values.label: Leyden
values.definition: A semi-hard, cumin and caraway seed flavoured cheese made from cow's milk.

values.label: Manchego
values.definition: A firm and compact sheep's milk cheese with a buttery texture, often containing small, unevenly distributed air pockets. The colour of the cheese varies from white to ivory-yellow, and the inedible rind from yellow to brownish-beige.

values.label: Marbled cheese
values.definition: A name given to cheeses with marbled patterns. It is usually hard, processed cow's milk cheese produced by combining either two different coloured curds, cheese curds or processed cheeses.

values.label: Monterey jack
values.definition: A white, semi-hard cheese made using cow's milk. It is noted for its mild flavour and slight sweetness.

values.label: Mozzarella
values.definition: A semi-soft fresh cheese made by the pasta filata (stretched-curd) method. Fresh mozzarella is generally white but when seasoned, it turns to a light yellow depending on the animal's diet.

values.label: Muenster
values.definition: A semi-soft cheese that is pale in colour and smooth in texture with an orange rind. The cheese is made from pasteurized cow's milk. Also known as Munster.

values.label: Mycella
values.definition: A soft, artisan, blue-veined cow's milk. It is moist and creamy, little salty but not bitter and belongs to blue cheese family. It comes with a blue-green mold and mild aromatic taste. Also know as Danish Gorgonzola.

values.label: Neufchatel
values.definition: A soft, slightly crumbly, mold-ripened cow's milk cheese.

values.label: Ossau iraty
values.definition: A medium firm sheep's milk. Ossau-Iraty cheese crust is yellow-orange to gray, and the body color ranges from white to cream depending on how it has been matured. It is smooth, creamy and firm, and may have some small eyes.

values.label: Parmesan
values.definition: A hard, granular cheese produced from unpasteurised cow's milk.

values.label: Pecorino
values.definition: A hard cheese made from sheep's milk. Pecorinos are traditional, creamery, hard, drum-shaped cheese. They come in a variety of flavours depending on ageing period.

values.label: Petit munster
values.definition: A semi-soft, wash-rind cheese that has a strong aroma and slightly sticky outer surface.

values.label: Pimento cheese
values.definition: In the cuisine of the Southern United States, pimento (or pimiento) cheese is a spread or relish made with cheese, mayonnaise and pimentos. Elsewhere, different ingredients may be used. It is served on bread, crackers and vegetables, or in sandwiches. The basic recipe has few ingredients: sharp cheddar cheese or processed cheese (such as Velveeta or American cheese), mayonnaise or salad dressing, and pimentos, blended to either a smooth or chunky paste.

values.label: Pipo crem
values.definition: A soft to semisoft blue cheese made with cow's milk. It has a smooth, creamy, ivory paste with blue veining and a thin white penicillin rind.

values.label: Processed cheese
values.definition: A food product made from cheese and other unfermented dairy ingredients mixed with emulsifiers. Additional ingredients, such as vegetable oils, salt, food coloring, or sugar may be included. As a result, many flavours, colours, and textures of processed cheese exist.

values.label: Provolone
values.definition: An aged pasta filata (stretched-crud) cheese.

values.label: Queso quesadilla
values.definition: A semi-soft, white, string-type, Hispanic-style cheese made from cow's milk. Belonging to the pasta filata (stretched-crud)  family, similar to a Mozzarella, Queso Quesillo is a stretched curd cheese, kneaded and sold in long ropes gently wound in balls. Also known as Queso Oaxaca, Asadero or Quesillo.

values.label: Raclette
values.definition: A raw, semi-hard, mildly flavoured cheese made from cow's milk which is used for melting and grilling.

values.label: Reblochon
values.definition: A soft washed-rind and smear-ripened cheese made from raw cow's milk.

values.label: Red Cheshire
values.definition: A dense and crumbly cheese that is coloured with annatto to a shade of deep orange.

values.label: Red Leicester
values.definition: A cheese made in a similar manner to Cheddar cheese, although it is crumbly in texture, and typically sold at 6 to 12 months of age. The rind is reddish-orange, with a powdery mould on it. Also know as Leicester or Leicestershire cheese.

values.label: Ricotta
values.definition: A whey cheese made from sheep, cow, goat, or  water buffalo milk whey left over from the production of other cheeses. Like other whey cheeses, it is made by coagulating the proteins that remain after the casein has been used to make cheese, notably albumin and globulin.

values.label: Romano
values.definition: A term used in the United States and Canada for a class of hard, salty cheese suitable primarily for grating similar to Pecorino Romano, from which the name is derived. Romano cheese can be made from cow, goat, and/or sheep's milk.

values.label: Roquefort
values.definition: A semi-hard sheep's milk cheese that is white, tangy, crumbly and slightly moist, with distinctive veins of blue mold.

values.label: Roule
values.definition: A cheese with a soft and creamy texture, that is usually flavoured with herbs and garlic.

values.label: Saint-Marcellin
values.definition: A soft, mold ripened cheese made from unpasteurized cow's milk.

values.label: Saint-Paulin
values.definition: A creamy, mild, semi-soft cheese made from pasteurized cow's milk. Saint-Paulin is a buttery cheese, but firm enough for slicing.

values.label: Samsø
values.definition: Samsø is a ripened hard cheese. The body has a near white or ivory through to light yellow or yellow colour and a firm-textured (when pressed by thumb) texture suitable for cutting, with few to plentiful, evenly distributed, smooth and round pea to cherry sized gas holes, but few openings and splits are acceptable. The shape is a flat cylindrical, flat square or rectangular. The cheese is sold with or without a hard, dry rind, which may be coated.

values.label: Sapsago
values.definition: A traditional hard cheese that is made out of the skimmed cow milk and a special kind of herb, blue fenugreek. Also know as Schabziger.

values.label: Sbrinz
values.definition: A very hard cheese made from cow's milk. It is often used instead of Parmesan cheese in Swiss cuisine.

values.label: Swiss cheese
values.definition: A generic name for several varieties of cheese. It is an American version of the Swiss Emmental and is known for being a shiny, pale yellow colour. While it has a firmer texture than baby Swiss, its flavour is mild, sweet, and nut-like. It has a savoury, but not very sharp taste.

values.label: Taleggio
values.definition: A semisoft, washed-rind, smear-ripened that has a thin crust and a strong aroma, but its flavour is comparatively mild with an unusual fruity tang.

values.label: Tilsiter
values.definition: Tilsiter is a ripened firm/semi-hard cheese. The body has a near white or ivory through to light yellow or yellow colour and a firm-textured (when pressed by thumb) texture suitable for cutting, with irregularly shaped, shiny and evenly distributed gas holes. The cheese is manufactured and sold with or without a well-dried smear-developed rind, which may be coated.

values.label: Tomme au raisin
values.definition: A variety of Tommee cheese that is pressed, uncooked. Fruity and mellow with a very slight sharpness. The cheese is aged under a thick blanket of grape marc, the residue that's left after pressing the fruit to make wine. The taste of the marc permeates through to the heart of the cheese.

values.label: Weisskaese white cheese
values.definition: Weisskaese or Weichkaese is a soft cheese. It is a generic term for all soft cheeses with a relatively high-water content. Weichkaese white cheese has a velvety white coating of a mould.

values.label: Wensleydale
values.definition: A historic mild cheese that is made from pasteurised cow's milk. Wensleydale is a medium cheese that is supple and crumbly and has a slight honey aroma.

values.label: White Cheshire
values.definition: A dense and crumbly cheese that is dense and semi-hard, and is defined by its moist, crumbly texture and mild, salty taste.

values.label: Gas
values.definition: A material, which has a vapor pressure greater than 300 kPa (43.5 psia) at 50°C (122°F) or is completely gaseous at 20°C (68°F) at a standard pressure of 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).  Including: ·       Aerosol:  Any non-refillable receptacle containing a gas compressed, liquefied or dissolved under pressure, the sole purpose of which is to expel a nonpoisonous (other than a Division 6.1 Package Group III Material) liquid, paste, or powder and fitted with a self-closing release device allowing the contents to be ejected by the gas. ·       Asphyxiant Gas:  A gas, which dilutes or replaces the oxygen normally in the atmosphere. ·       Compressed Gas in Solution:  A non-liquefied compressed gas, which is dissolved in a solvent. ·       Liquefied Compressed Gas: A gas, which when packaged under pressure for transportation is partially liquid at temperatures above -50° C (-58° F).  A liquefied compressed gas is further categorized as follows:  o    High Pressure Liquefied Gas: A gas with a critical temperature between -50 °C (-58° F) and + 65° C (149° F). o    Low Pressure Liquefied Gas:  A gas with a critical temperature above + 65° C (149° F).  ·       Non-Liquefied Compressed Gas:  A gas, which when packaged under pressure for transportation is entirely gaseous at -50° C (-58° F) with a critical temperature less than or equal to -50° C (-58° F). Oxidizing Gas:  A gas, which may, generally by providing oxygen, cause or contribute to the combustion of other material more than air does.

values.label: Liquid
values.definition: A material, other than an elevated temperature material, with a melting point or initial melting point of 20°C (68°F) or lower at a standard pressure of 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).  A viscous material for which a specific melting point cannot be determined must be subjected to the procedures specified in ASTM D 4359 "Standard Test Method for Determining Whether a Material is Liquid or Solid”.

values.label: Mixed
values.definition: Any combination of the other states.

values.label: Refrigerant Or Dispersant Gas
values.definition: All non-toxic refrigerant gases, dispersant gases (fluorocarbons) and mixtures thereof, or any other compressed gas having a vapor pressure not exceeding 260 psia at 54°C (130°F), used only as a refrigerant, dispersant or blowing agent.

values.label: Refrigerated Liquid
values.definition: Cryogenic Liquid . A refrigerated liquefied gas having a boiling point colder than -90°C (-130°F) at 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).

values.label: Solid
values.definition: A material that does not meet the definition of a liquid or gas (i.e., powder, pellet, flake).

values.label: Antineoplastic
values.definition: Agents that inhibit or prevent the development, maturation, and proliferation of malignant cells.
