values.label: Bioaccumulation
values.definition: A hazard associated with the gradual accumulation of some chemical substances into a product's ingredients or raw materials.

values.label: Biohazard
values.definition: Biohazard substances pose a threat to the health of living organisms, primarily that of humans.   Biohazards normally come from biological sources or substances used in the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of diseases.    Having the knowledge of whether a trade item contains biomedical hazards will allow for the item to be handled and administered safely.

values.label: Biologic
values.definition: A preparation, such as a drug, a vaccine, or an antitoxin, that is synthesized from living organisms or their products and used as a diagnostic, preventive, or therapeutic agent.

values.label: Carcinogen
values.definition: Carcinogen is a substance capable of causing cancer in living tissue.

values.label: Cardiovascular toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with cardiovascular organs or process.

values.label: Cytotoxic
values.definition: A Cytotoxic is a compound that is toxic to cells.

values.label: Dermatotoxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the skin or dermal layers.

values.label: Developmental toxicity
values.definition: Any structural or functional alteration caused by an environmental toxin causing harm or reaction that interferes with normal growth, differentiation, development, and/or behaviour.

values.label: Endocrine toxicity
values.definition: Endocrine toxicity results when a chemical interferes with the synthesis, secretion, transport, metabolism, binding action, or elimination of hormones necessary for endocrine functions resulting in loss of normal tissue function, development, growth, or reproduction.

values.label: Environmental persistence
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that will persist in the environment.

values.label: Environmental toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances which causes environmental toxicity concerns.

values.label: Genotoxicity
values.definition: Genotoxicity is the property of chemical agents that damage the genetic information within a cell causing mutations, which may lead to cancer.

values.label: Hazard trait under review
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances which is under review to determine the type of toxicity which can result from the use of the product.

values.label: Hematotoxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the blood and blood-forming tissues.

values.label: Hepatotoxicity and digestive system toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the liver or its processes.

values.label: Immunotoxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the immune system or on other systems as a result of immune system dysfunction.

values.label: Musculoskeletal toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with muscles, tendons, and bones.

values.label: Nephrotoxicity and other toxicity to the urinary system
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the kidneys and their functioning.

values.label: Neurodevelopmental toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with brain growth and development.

values.label: Neurotoxicity
values.definition: Adverse change in structure and/or function of the central nervous system and/or peripheral nervous system measured at the neurochemical, behavioural, neurophysiological, or anatomical levels.

values.label: Not Biohazard
values.definition: Confirms the product has no biohazardous substance

values.label: Ocular toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that cause one or more adverse changes that effect the structure or function of the eye.

values.label: Other
values.definition: Any other chemical property not include in this list.

values.label: Ototoxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the ears or hearing.

values.label: Radioactive
values.definition: The hazards from radiation of radioactive materials taken into the body. The effects depend on the dose, the duration of exposure, and the organs exposed.

values.label: Reactivity
values.definition: The tendency of a substance to undergo chemical reaction, either by itself or with other materials, and to release energy.

values.label: Reproductive Toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that they will interfere in some way with normal reproduction. Such substances are called reprotoxic. It includes adverse effects on sexual function and fertility in adult males and females, as well as developmental toxicity in the offspring.

values.label: Respiratory toxicity
values.definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with respiratory system or its processes.

values.label: Stability
values.definition: The thermodynamic stability of a chemical system.

values.label: Toxicity
values.definition: Degree to which a substance can damage an organism

values.label: Beans/Peas/Legumes
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Vegetable Section of the Food Buying Guide. Vegetables that are fresh, frozen, or canned vegetables and full-strength vegetable juice may contribute toward the vegetable requirement. The minimum creditable amount is 1/8 cup. The vegetable component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Beans and legume vegetables may be counted towards the meats/meat alternates or vegetable component, but not as both simultaneously. Vegetable crediting for beans/peas (legumes) is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup. Examples of bean/peas (legumes) include:black beans, black-eyed peas (mature, dry), garbanzo beans (chickpeas), kidney beans, lentils, navy beans, pinto beans, soy beans, split peas, and white beans.

values.label: Bread or Bread Alternative
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Grains Section of the Food Buying Guide and/or Exhibit A: School Lunch and Breakfast Whole Grain-Rich Ounce Equivalency for School Meal Programs. *Regulations on APP are fond in 7 CFR Parts 210, 220, 225, 226 Appendix A. The minimum creditable amount is 0.25 ounce equivalents. Crediting is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 0.25 ounce equivalent increment. Foods that qualify as grains/bread in the Child Nutrition Program are enriched or whole-grain or are made from enriched or whole-grain meal and or flour.  All grains must meet the whole grain-rich criteria: a blend of whole-grain meal and/or flour and enriched meal and/or flour of which at least 50 percent is whole grain, with the remaining grains, if any, being enriched.

values.label: Dark Green Vegetable
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Vegetable Section of the Food Buying Guide. Vegetables that are fresh, frozen, or canned vegetables and full-strength vegetable juice may contribute toward the vegetable requirement. The minimum creditable amount is 1/8 cup. The vegetable component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Crediting for dark green vegetable is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup. Examples of dark green vegetables include: bok choy, broccoli, collard greens, dark green leafy lettuce, kale, mesclun, mustard greens, romaine lettuce, spinach, turnip greens, and watercress.

values.label: Fluid Milk
values.definition: Fluid milk means pasteurized unflavored or flavored low fat (1%), lactose free milk, lactose reduced milk, buttermilk, and acidified milk, all of which meet State and local standards for such milk. The milk must contain vitamins A and D at levels specified by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and must be consistent with State and local standards. School food authorities must offer at least two different options of fluid milk. Milk (flavored or unflavored) must be fat-free or low fat (1% fat or less). The fluid milk component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Minimum credit is 1/2 cup. Crediting for fluid milk is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/4 cup. Non-dairy beverages offered as fluid milk substitutes may also be offered in the NSLP, SBP, and CACFP. However, they must be nutritionally equivalent to milk and provide specific levels of calcium, protein, vitamins A and D, magnesium, phosphorus, potassium, riboflavin, and vitamin B-12.

values.label: Fruit
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Fruit Section of the Food Buying Guide. Fresh, frozen, dried, canned (packed in water, full-strength juice, or light syrup) and full-strength fruit juice may contribute toward the fruit requirement. The minimum creditable amount for fruit is 1/8 cup. The Fruit component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Crediting for fruit is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup.

values.label: Fruit Vegetable or Fruit Vegetable Alternative
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Fruit Section of the Food Buying Guide.  Fresh, frozen, dried, canned (packed in water, full-strength juice, or light syrup) and full-strength fruit juice may contribute toward the fruit requirement. The minimum creditable amount for fruit is 1/8 cup.  The Fruit component is credited on a volume measure.  The unit of measure is “cup”.  Crediting for fruit is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup.

values.label: Grains
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Grains Section of the Food Buying Guide and/or Exhibit A: School Lunch and Breakfast Whole Grain-Rich Ounce Equivalency for School Meal Programs. *Regulations on APP are fond in 7 CFR Parts 210, 220, 225, 226 Appendix A. The minimum creditable amount is 0.25 ounce equivalents. Crediting is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 0.25 ounce equivalent increment. Foods that qualify as grains/bread in the Child Nutrition Program are enriched or whole-grain or are made from enriched or whole-grain meal and or flour.  All grains must meet the whole grain-rich criteria: a blend of whole-grain meal and/or flour and enriched meal and/or flour of which at least 50 percent is whole grain, with the remaining grains, if any, being enriched.

values.label: Meat or Meat Alternative
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Meat/Meat Alternates Section of the Food Buying Guide.  The M/MA must be served in the main dish or in the main dish and one other menu item.  In order for a food to contribute to the M/MA component, it must contain a minimum of 0.25 oz.  Crediting for M/MA is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 0.25 oz. Examples Include: meat, poultry, fish, cheese, yogurt, dry beans and peas, whole eggs, alternate protein products (APP)*, soy yogurt, tofu, peanut butter or other nut or seed butters, and nuts and seeds. may also be counted as meeting part of the M/MA requirement.  Enriched macaroni-type products with fortified protein as defined in 7 CFR Part 210 Appendix A.

values.label: Other Vegetable
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Vegetable Section of the Food Buying Guide. Vegetables that are fresh, frozen, or canned vegetables and full-strength vegetable juice may contribute toward the vegetable requirement. The minimum creditable amount is 1/8 cup. The vegetable component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Crediting for other vegetable is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup. Examples of other vegetables include: artichokes, asparagus, avocado, bean sprouts, beets, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, cauliflower, celery, cucumbers, eggplant, green beans, green peppers, iceberg lettuce, mushrooms, okra, onions, parsnips, turnips, wax beans, and zucchini.

values.label: Red/Orange Vegetable
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Vegetable Section of the Food Buying Guide. Vegetables that are fresh, frozen, or canned vegetables and full-strength vegetable juice may contribute toward the vegetable requirement. The minimum creditable amount is 1/8 cup. The vegetable component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Crediting for red/orange vegetable is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup. Examples of red/orange vegetables include: sweet potatoes, acorn squash, butternut squash, carrots, hubbard squash, pumpkin, red peppers, tomatoes, tomato products and tomato juice.

values.label: Starchy Vegetable
values.definition: Foods can be found in the Vegetable Section of the Food Buying Guide. Vegetables that are fresh, frozen, or canned vegetables and full-strength vegetable juice may contribute toward the vegetable requirement. The minimum creditable amount is 1/8 cup. The vegetable component is credited on a volume measure. The unit of measure is “cup”. Crediting for starchy vegetable is expressed by rounding down to the nearest 1/8 cup. Examples of starchy vegetables include:potatoes, corn, cassava, green bananas, green peas, green lima beans, plantains, taro, water chestnuts, and fresh cowpeas, field peas, or black-eyed peas (not dry).

values.label: Acetone
values.definition: Acetone is the trivial name for the organic chemical compound propanone or dimethyl ketone.

values.label: Additives
values.definition: Substances added to foods to prevent spoilage, improve appearance, enhance flavor or texture, or increase nutritional value.

values.label: Agar
values.definition: White, semi-translucent, flavourless substance consisting of polysaccharides obtained from the red algae species (primarily from Gracilaria and Gelidiaceae genus). It is commonly used as vegan substitute of gelatine, gelling agent in food, pharmaceutical drugs, photography and cosmetic manufacturing, growth medium in microbiology and other medical materials.

values.label: Agave Syrup
values.definition: Syrup from the Agave plant.

values.label: Alcohol
values.definition: Alcohol

values.label: Almonds
values.definition: The almond is a species of tree native to the Middle East and South Asia. "Almond" is also the name of the edible and widely cultivated seed of this tree. Within the genus Prunus, it is classified with the peach in the subgenus Amygdalus, distinguished from the other subgenera by the corrugated shell (endocarp) surrounding the seed. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed (which is not a true nut) inside.

values.label: Aloe vera
values.definition: A gelatinous substance obtained from a kind of aloe. E.g., used in cosmetics, food.

values.label: Aluminium
values.definition: Aluminium-based compounds are the active ingredients in antiperspirants. They block the sweat glands to keep sweat from getting to the skin's surface.

values.label: Amino acids
values.definition: A group of organic molecules that consist of a basic amino group, an acidic carboxyl group, and a unique organic side chain. Building blocks of protein.

values.label: Ammonia
values.definition: Compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH₃. A stable binary hydride, and the simplest pnictogen hydride, ammonia is a colourless gas with a characteristic pungent smell.

values.label: Ancient Grains
values.definition: Ancient grains are considered to be uncommon grains cultivated before modern times. They are high in protein, calcium and magnesium. Some ancient grains include polenta, farro, spelt, millet, barley, oats, sorghum and quinoa.

values.label: Animal by-products
values.definition: Materials of animal origin that people do not consume.

values.label: Animal Cruelty
values.definition: Cruelty to animals, also called animal abuse, animal neglect or animal cruelty, is the infliction by omission (animal neglect) or by commission by humans of suffering or harm upon any non-human. More narrowly, it can be the causing of harm or suffering for specific achievement, such as killing animals for food, for their fur or even their tusks; opinions differ about the extent of cruelty associated with a given method of slaughter.

values.label: Animal protein
values.definition: Animal proteins are widely used for the formation of protein particles in the food industry, e.g., casein, whey protein, gelatin, egg proteins, and fibroin.

values.label: Animal testing
values.definition: Any scientific experiment or test in which a live animal is forced to undergo something that is likely to cause them pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm.

values.label: Antibiotics
values.definition: Antibiotics are used in the care of livestock.

values.label: Antioxidants
values.definition: Antioxidants are defined as substances which inhibit oxidation. Oxidation reactions or oxidative stress can damage or kill cells, and are thought to play an important part in many human diseases.

values.label: Artificial Colour
values.definition: Artificial colour is defined as colour formed by chemical synthesis and is not identical to substances found in nature.

values.label: Artificial flavour
values.definition: Artificial flavours are formed by chemical synthesis and not identical to substances found in nature. They are used to improve the taste or smell (aroma) of the product.

values.label: Artificial Preservatives
values.definition: Artificial preservatives are preservatives formed by chemical synthesis.

values.label: Artificial Sweeteners
values.definition: Artificial sweeteners are sugar substitutes that are synthetic.

values.label: Ash
values.definition: The inorganic component of an organic carbon containing substance. It predominately consists of minerals.

values.label: Aspartame
values.definition: An artificial, non-saccharide sweetener used as a sugar substitute

values.label: Azodicarbonamide
values.definition: Azodicarbonamide (ADC) is a dough strengthener used by commercial bakers.

values.label: Azo Dye
values.definition: Any of a large class of synthetic dyes whose molecules contain two adjacent nitrogen atoms between carbon atoms.

values.label: Backbone
values.definition: The backbone is made up of series of vertebrae that supports the body, and also protects the spinal cord.

values.label: Barley
values.definition: Barley a hardy cereal that has coarse bristles extending from the ears. It is widely cultivated, chiefly for use in brewing and stock feed.  The grain of the barley plant.

values.label: Beef Gelatine
values.definition: Translucent, colourless, brittle (when dry), flavourless substance derived from collagen obtained from various  beef animal materials (connective tissues (skin) and bones). It is commonly used as a gelling agent in food, pharmaceutical drugs, photography, and cosmetic manufacturing.

values.label: BHA
values.definition: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA) is an antioxidant which retards rancidity in fats, oils, and oil-containing products.

values.label: BHT
values.definition: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is an antioxidant which retards rancidity in oils, and oil-containing products.

values.label: Biodegradable material
values.definition: Biodegradable refers to the ability of things to get disintegrated (decomposed) by the action of micro-organisms such as bacteria or fungi biological (with or without oxygen) while getting assimilated into the natural environment.

values.label: Biogas
values.definition: Biogas is a naturally occurring and renewable source of energy, resulting from the breakdown of organic matter.

values.label: Biotin
values.definition: Biotin, also known as vitamin B7 or vitamin H or vitamin I, is a water-soluble vitamin from the B complex. As a prosthetic group of enzymes, it plays an important role in metabolism, but is also important in the nucleus for the epigenetic regulation of gene function. It plays an essential role in the production of energy from nutrients, as well as in the synthesis of fatty acids and amino acids. It is both provided by the diet and manufactured by the intestinal flora. Many countries like France often refer to biotin as vitamin B8. However, the name recommended by IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) is only biotin.

values.label: Bleach
values.definition: Generic name for any chemical product which is used industrially and domestically to clean, to lighten hair colour and to remove stains. It often refers, specifically, to a dilute solution of sodium hypochlorite, also called "liquid bleach".

values.label: Bones
values.definition: Bones are parts of the skeleton of animals.

values.label: Bisphenol A (BPA)
values.definition: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a synthetic organic compound with the chemical formula C₁₅H₁₆O₂, primarily used in the production of polycarbonate plastics and epoxy resins.

values.label: Brazil nuts
values.definition: The Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa) is a South American tree in the family Lecythidaceae, and also the name of the tree's commercially harvested edible seed. Order[edit]. The Brazil nut family is in the order Ericales, as are other well-known plants such as blueberries, cranberries, sapote, gutta-percha, tea, gooseberries, phlox, and persimmons.

values.label: Brine
values.definition: Brine is a simple solution of water and salt that commonly used to preserve or season the food.

values.label: Broth
values.definition: Broth is a savory liquid made of water in which bones, meat, fish or vegetables have been simmered.

values.label: Cadmium
values.definition: A soft, silver-white or blue, lustrous metal typically found in mineral deposits with lead, zinc, and copper.

values.label: Caffeine
values.definition:
Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant of the methylxanthine class.[10]
It is the world's most widely consumed psychoactive drug.

values.label: Calcium
values.definition: Calcium

values.label: Calorie
values.definition: Calories.

values.label: Camphor
values.definition: White, crystalline substance obtained from the wood of the camphor tree.

values.label: Cane Sugar
values.definition: Sugar from sugar cane.

values.label: Carbohydrates
values.definition: Mainly sugars and starches, together constituting one of the three principal types of nutrients used as energy sources (calories) by the body. Carbohydrates can also be defined chemically as neutral compounds of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

values.label: Carrageenan
values.definition: Carrageenan is a thickening, gelling, and stabilizing agent obtained from certain seaweeds.

values.label: Cashews
values.definition: The cashew nut is served as a snack or used in recipes, like other nuts, although it is actually a seed. The cashew apple is a fruit, whose pulp can be processed into a sweet, astringent fruit drink or distilled into liqueur. The shell of the cashew nut yield derivatives that can be used in many applications from lubricants to paints, and other parts of the tree have traditionally been used for snake-bites and other folk remedies.

values.label: Cauliflower
values.definition: Cauliflower is one of several vegetables in the species Brassica oleracea in the genus Brassica, which is in the Brassicaceae family. It is an annual plant that reproduces by seed.

values.label: Celery
values.definition: Celery (Apium graveolens) is a marshland plant in the family Apiaceae that has been cultivated as a vegetable since antiquity. Celery has a long fibrous stalk tapering into leaves.

values.label: Ceramides
values.definition: Ceramides help to renew the natural skin protection barrier and maintain an adequate moisture balance.

values.label: Chemical
values.definition: A substance with a distinct molecular composition that is produced by or used in a chemical process.

values.label: Chemical Treatment
values.definition: Technologies that use chemicals or chemical processes to treat materials or wastes.

values.label: Chloride
values.definition: Chloride

values.label: Chlorine
values.definition: A chemical used as a disinfectant.

values.label: Cholesterol
values.definition: A claim that a food is free from Cholesterol. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Choline
values.definition: Choline

values.label: Chromium
values.definition: Chromium

values.label: Cloned Foods
values.definition: Meat and milk from cloned cattle, pigs, plants, etc. and from the offspring of clones of any species traditionally used as food.

values.label: Coconut/Copra oil
values.definition: An oil extracted from dried or fresh coconut.

values.label: Coconut cream
values.definition: Coconut cream is much thicker and richer than coconut milk. It is made from simmering four parts shredded coconut in one part water. The cream that rises to the top of a can of coconut milk is also considered coconut cream.

values.label: Coconut water
values.definition: Coconut water, less commonly known as coconut juice, is the clear liquid inside coconuts.

values.label: Coenzyme Q10 Ubiquinone
values.definition: A coenzyme family that is ubiquitous in animals and most bacteria.

values.label: Collagens
values.definition: Collagens are a group of structural proteins mainly found in multicellular animals / humans. Collagens are found in the white and inelastic fibres of tendons, ligaments, bones, layers of the skin and cartilages.

values.label: Colour
values.definition: Colour is defined as colour found without any specific chemical synthesis, but not specified as natural colour.

values.label: Colouring Agents
values.definition: Natural or synthetic dyes used as coloring agents in processed foods.

values.label: Copper
values.definition: Copper

values.label: Corn
values.definition: Corn is a grain as well as a vegetable. It grows within a tall grass-like stalk and produces large kernels on a cob.

values.label: Corn Syrup
values.definition: Corn syrup.

values.label: Cream
values.definition: Cream is a dairy product composed of the higher-fat layer skimmed from the top of milk before homogenization. Please refer to local regulations for full definition.

values.label: Crustacean
values.definition: The crustacean is an arthropod of the large, mainly aquatic group Crustacea, such as a crab, lobster, shrimp, or barnacle.

values.label: Dairy
values.definition: Milk or milk products including ingredients, processing aids and additives.

values.label: Dark meat tuna
values.definition: This tuna typically comes from either Skipjack or Yellowfin tuna.  The meat is darker in colour, more red and pink than light tan and tan-ish pink, than its "Light Meat" counterpart.

values.label: DEET
values.definition: DEET, or N,N-diethyl-meta-toluamide, is a synthetic chemical in many insect repellents.

values.label: Detergent
values.definition: A cleansing agent, especially synthetic, used for cleaning fabrics, dishes, and other surfaces.

values.label: Dietary Fibre
values.definition: The USFDA definition for Dietary fibre that can be declared on the Nutrition Facts label includes certain naturally occurring fibres that are “intrinsic and intact” in plants, and added isolated or synthetic non-digestible soluble and insoluble carbohydrates that FDA has determined have beneficial physiological effects to human health. www.fda.gov

values.label: Drug
values.definition: A substance used for medical treatment, particularly one that affects the mind or body.

values.label: Dye
values.definition: A substance used to add colour to materials such as fabrics, hair, or food.

values.label: Eggs
values.definition: Eggs

values.label: Energy
values.definition: Energy

values.label: Essential oil
values.definition: An essential oil is a concentrated hydrophobic liquid containing volatile chemical compounds from plants. Essential oils are also known as volatile oils, ethereal oils, aetheroleum, or simply as the oil of the plant from which they were extracted, such as oil of clove.

values.label: Estrogen
values.definition: Primary female sex hormone which regulates the reproductive system and sexual characteristics.

values.label: Fat
values.definition: Fat

values.label: Fibre
values.definition: The undigestible material in the fruits, vegetables and whole grains.

values.label: Fish
values.definition: A limbless cold-blooded vertebrate animal with gills and fins and living wholly in water.

values.label: Fishbones
values.definition: Bones are bony, more tender parts of the skeleton of bony fish such as ribs and fin rays, but especially the connective tissue ossifications, which are inclined transversely backwards to the ribs between the muscle segments and have no contact with the spine.

values.label: Flavour
values.definition: Flavours are defined as flavours found without any specific chemical synthesis, but not specified as natural flavours.

values.label: Flavour Enhancers
values.definition: Flavour enhancers (e.g. monosodium glutamate, MSG).

values.label: Flax
values.definition: A flowering plant, Linum ustiatissimum, that is cultivated as a food and fibre crop.

values.label: Fluoride
values.definition: Fluoride

values.label: Folate
values.definition: Folate

values.label: Folic Acid
values.definition: Folic acid is a stable, artificial form of vitamin B9. It's not found naturally in food but often added to processed foods and used in multivitamin-mineral supplements. However, folic acid must be converted into active vitamin B9, known as 5-MTHF, before your body can use it.

values.label: Formaldehyde
values.definition: Formaldehyde is a naturally occurring organic compound with the formula CH₂O. It is the simplest of the aldehydes. The common name of this substance comes from its similarity and relation to formic acid. Formaldehyde is an important precursor to many other materials and chemical compounds.

values.label: Formaldehyde Releasing Chemicals
values.definition: In personal care products, formaldehyde can be added directly, or more often, it can be released from preservatives such as quaternium-15, DMDM hydantoin, imidazolidinyl urea, diazolidinyl urea, polyoxymethylene urea, sodium hydroxymethylglycinate, bromopol and glyoxal.

values.label: Fragrance/Perfume
values.definition: Something (such as a perfume) compounded to give off a sweet or pleasant odor.

values.label: Fructose
values.definition: Fructose.

values.label: Fruit
values.definition: Fruit is the sweet and fleshy product of a tree or other plant that contains seed and can be eaten as food.

values.label: Fruit Juice
values.definition: Fruit juice.

values.label: Fruit juice concentrate
values.definition: Fruit juice concentrate is where the water content from the fruit has been removed.

values.label: Fruit puree
values.definition: Fruit puree is cooked fruits that has been ground, pressed, blended or sieved to the consistency of a creamy paste or liquid.

values.label: Fruit Syrup
values.definition: A syrup made from fruit and other ingredients such as sugar, corn syrup and water.

values.label: Fully hydrogenated vegetable oil
values.definition: Fully hydrogenated vegetable oils are solid fats, produced from liquid, typically vegetable, oils by full hydrogenation. Full hydrogenation results in fats very high in saturated fatty acids (SAFA). Fully hydrogenated vegetable oils do not contain significant amounts of artificial trans fatty acids (TFA).

values.label: Fungicide
values.definition: A chemical substance used to kill fungus or prevent it from growing.

values.label: Gelatine
values.definition: Translucent, colourless, brittle (when dry), flavourless substance derived from collagen obtained from various animal raw materials (connective tissues (skin) and bones). It is commonly used as a gelling agent in food, pharmaceutical drugs, photography, and cosmetic manufacturing.

values.label: Giblets
values.definition: The liver, heart, gizzard, and the like, of a fowl.

values.label: Gluten
values.definition: Gluten.

values.label: Glycaemic
values.definition: A glucose response after a meal.

values.label: Glyzyrrhizin
values.definition: Glyzyrrhizin.

values.label: GMO
values.definition: GMOs (genetically modified organisms), are novel organisms created in a laboratory using genetic modification/engineering techniques. Scientists and consumer and environmental groups have cited many health and environmental risks with foods containing GMOs.

values.label: Grains
values.definition: Wheat or any other cultivated cereal crop used as food.

values.label: Grass
values.definition: Vegetation consisting of short plants with long narrow leaves, growing wild or cultivated in lawns or pastures.

values.label: Hazelnuts
values.definition: A hazelnut is the nut of the hazel and is also known as cobnut or filbert nut according to species. A cob is roughly spherical to oval, about 15–25 mm long and 10–15 mm in diameter, with an outer fibrous husk surrounding a smooth shell. A filbert is more elongated, being about twice as long as it is round. The nut falls out of the husk when ripe, about seven to eight months after pollination. The kernel of the seed is edible and used raw or roasted, or ground into a paste. Hazelnuts are also used for livestock feed, as are chestnuts and acorns. The seed has a thin, dark brown skin, which is sometimes removed before cooking.

values.label: Herbicide
values.definition: A chemical that is used to destroy plants, especially weeds.

values.label: High Fructose Corn Syrup
values.definition: High fructose corn syrup (HFCS) (also called glucose-fructose, isoglucose and glucose-fructose syrup) is a sweetener made from corn starch that has been processed by glucose isomerase to convert some of its glucose into fructose.

values.label: Honey
values.definition: Honey.

values.label: Hormones
values.definition: Hormones are used in the grown of livestock. Common hormones are rBST, rBGH, and others.

values.label: Hyaluronic acid
values.definition: Hyaluronic acid is a moisture binder and belongs to the mucopolysaccharide. These are multiple sugars, i.e. long molecular chains, which are composed of disaccharide subunits (double sugars), which in turn consist of glucuronic acid and an amino sugar.

values.label: Hydrocarbon Propellant
values.definition: Propellants commonly used in pharmaceutical aerosols cover both liquefied gases (CFC, hydrocarbons, hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC), and HFC) and compressed gases (nitrogen, nitrous oxide, and carbon dioxide) [1].

values.label: Hydroquinone
values.definition: A crystalline compound made by the reduction of benzoquinone.

values.label: Ice cream
values.definition: Ice cream is a sweetened frozen food typically eaten as a snack or dessert. Please refer to local regulation how Ice Cream is defined in target markets.

values.label: Insecticide
values.definition: A chemical substance made and used for killing insects, especially those that eat plants.

values.label: Insoluble Fibre
values.definition: Insoluble fibre does not dissolve in water and passes through the gastrointestinal tract relatively intact and, therefore, is not a source of calories.

values.label: Iodine
values.definition: Iodine

values.label: Iron
values.definition: Iron

values.label: Juice
values.definition: The liquid obtained from or present in fruit or vegetables.

values.label: Keratin
values.definition: Structural protein in the outer layer of human skin, hair, and nails, and animal hooves and horns.

values.label: Kidneys
values.definition: A pair of organs in the abdominal cavity of mammals, birds, and reptiles, excreting urine.

values.label: Lactose
values.definition: Lactose.

values.label: Latex
values.definition: A milky fluid found in many plants, such as poppies and spurges, which exudes when the plant is cut and coagulates on exposure to the air. The latex of the rubber tree is the chief source of natural rubber. Also, a synthetic product resembling latex, consisting of a dispersion in water of polymer particles, used to make paints, coatings, and other products.

values.label: Lead
values.definition: A dense metallic element with the symbol Pb, often used in batteries, shielding, and various alloys.

values.label: Legume Protein
values.definition: A seed, pod, or other edible part of a leguminous plant, used as food.

values.label: Light meat tuna
values.definition: This tuna typically comes from either Skipjack or Yellowfin tuna.  The meat is darker in colour – somewhere between a light tan and tan-ish pink, than "White meat tuna". It has a soft texture and is more flavourful than white meat tuna.

values.label: Liquorice
values.definition: Liquorice

values.label: Lobster meat
values.definition: Lobster meat is typically harvested from the tail, legs, knuckles, and the large claws which can be done commercially after cooking.

values.label: Lotion
values.definition: Preparation with a creamy consistency, applied to the skin for moisturizing or medicinal purposes.

values.label: Low fat ice cream
values.definition: Low fat or reduced fat ice cream contains a lesser percent of total fat than the referenced product (either an average of leading brands, or the company's own brand). Please refer to target market regulations for definition of 'low fat'.

values.label: Low fat milk
values.definition: Low fat milk is a reduction in fat and claim based on regulation what "Low fat" means.

values.label: Lye
values.definition: Strong alkaline substance, typically sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide.

values.label: Macadamia
values.definition: Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees indigenous to Australia and constituting part of the plant family Proteaceae.[1][2] They grow naturally in north eastern New South Wales and central and south eastern Queensland. Common names include macadamia, macadamia nut, Queensland nut, bush nut, maroochi nut, queen of nuts and bauple nut; and from Indigenous Australians' languages bauple, gyndl, jindilli, and boombera. Previously, more species, with disjunct distributions, were named as members of this genus Macadamia.

values.label: Magnesium
values.definition: Magnesium

values.label: Malt
values.definition: Malt

values.label: Manganese
values.definition: Manganese

values.label: Maple Syrup
values.definition: Maple syrup is a syrup usually made from the xylem sap of sugar maple, red maple, or black maple trees, although it can also be made from other maple species.

values.label: Meat
values.definition: Meat is animal flesh that is eaten as food.

values.label: Mercury
values.definition: A heavy, silvery d-block element, liquid at room temperature, used in thermometers and barometers.

values.label: Milk
values.definition: Milk is a nutrient-rich liquid food produced in the mammary glands of mammals.

values.label: Milk Protein
values.definition: Milk proteins.

values.label: Mineral Oil
values.definition: Any of various colourless, odourless, light mixtures of higher alkanes from a mineral source, particularly a distillate of petroleum, as distinct from usually edible vegetable oils.

values.label: Missing parts
values.definition: A product that has parts missing. Example: Poultry missing a leg.

values.label: Molasses
values.definition: Molasses is a viscous by-product of refining sugarcane or sugar beets into sugar.

values.label: Molluscs
values.definition: The mollusc is an invertebrate of a large phylum that includes snails, slugs, mussels, and octopuses. They have a soft, unsegmented body and live in aquatic or damp habitats, and most kinds have an external calcareous shell.

values.label: Molybdenum
values.definition: Molybdenum

values.label: Mono protein
values.definition: Mono-protein is particularly effective for treating allergies and intolerances. Most of the allergens are generated by proteins, so the single source protein foods can help limit the exposure to potential allergens. A single source protein food can be used as a diagnostic method or as a long-term treatment.

values.label: Mono Unsaturated Fat
values.definition: Monounsaturated Fat

values.label: Monosodium Glutamate
values.definition:
Monosodium glutamate (MSG, also known as sodium glutamate) is the sodium salt of glutamic acid, one of the most abundant naturally occurring non-essential amino acids. Monosodium glutamate is found naturally in tomatoes, cheese and other foods.
MSG is used in the food industry as a flavour enhancer with an umami taste that intensifies the meaty, savoury flavour of food, as naturally occurring glutamate does in foods such as stews and meat soups.

values.label: Multigrain
values.definition: More than one type of grain. Could be several whole grains, several refined grains or a combination of both.

values.label: Mustard
values.definition: Mustard is a pungent-tasting yellow or brown paste made from the crushed seeds of certain plants, typically eaten with meat or used as a cooking ingredient.  The yellow-flowered Eurasian plant of the cabbage family whose seeds are used to make this paste.

values.label: Nanoparticle
values.definition: A particle between 1 and 100 nanometres in size.

values.label: Naturally Occuring Sugars
values.definition: Naturally Occuring Sugars

values.label: Natural colour
values.definition: Indicates a colour additive that has been derived from a natural source to be added to a product for the primary reason of modifying the colour of the product.

values.label: Natural Flavour
values.definition: Flavouring substances obtained from plant or animal raw materials, by physical, microbiological or enzymatic processes.

values.label: Natural Gluten
values.definition: Gluten is a group of proteins, termed prolamins and glutelins,[1] stored with starch in the endosperm of various cereal (grass) grains.

values.label: Niacin
values.definition: Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid, is an organic compound and a form of vitamin B3, an essential human nutrient. It has the formula C6H5NO2 and belongs to the group of the pyridinecarboxylic acid.

values.label: Nitrate
values.definition: The chemical formula is NO3.

values.label: Nonylphenol Ethoxylates (NPEs)
values.definition: NP/NPEs, also known as nonylphenols and nonylphenol ethoxylates, are nonionic surfactants, or detergent-like substances, with uses that lead to widespread release into aquatic environments.

values.label: Non-Caloric Sweeteners
values.definition: Non-Caloric Sweeteners are sugar substitutes that do not contribute any caloric value.

values.label: Nuts
values.definition: Nuts

values.label: Oat
values.definition: The oat is a cereal plant cultivated chiefly in cool climates and widely used for animal feed as well as human consumption.  The grain yielded by this, used as food.

values.label: Octinoxate
values.definition: Octyl methoxycinnamate or ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate or octinoxate is an organic compound that is an ingredient in some sunscreens and lip balms. It is an ester formed from methoxycinnamic acid and 2-ethylhexanol.

values.label: Octocrylene
values.definition: Octocrylene is an organic compound used as an ingredient in sunscreens and cosmetics. It is an ester formed by the reaction of 3,3-diphenylcyanoacrylate with 2-ethylhexanol.

values.label: Odor
values.definition: A distinctive smell, often detected by the sense of olfaction.

values.label: Oil
values.definition: Oil is a viscous liquid derived from petroleum, plant, animal fat or synthetic fat.

values.label: Olive oil
values.definition: Olive oil is a liquid fat obtained from olives, a traditional tree crop of the Mediterranean Basin, produced by pressing whole olives and extracting the oil. It is commonly used in cooking or as a salad dressing.

values.label: Omega 3 Fatty Acids
values.definition: Omega-3 Fatty Acids

values.label: Omega-6
values.definition: A class of fatty acids, double bond on 6th carbon from the methyl end of the fatty acid (most common linoleic acid and arachidonic acid).

values.label: Optical Brighteners
values.definition: Synthetic chemicals added to liquid and powder laundry detergents to make clothing appear whiter and brighter, and thus cleaner.

values.label: Organotin
values.definition: Organotin substances (organotins) are tin compounds having 1, 2, 3 or 4 organic groups attached and are designated as mono-, di-, tri- or tetra-organotin depending on the number of tin-carbon bonds in the molecule. E.g., tributyltin, dibutyltin.

values.label: Oxybenzone
values.definition: Oxybenzone is a benzophenone derivative used as a sunscreen agent. Oxybenzone absorbs UVB and UVA II rays, resulting in a photochemical excitation and absorption of energy.

values.label: Paba
values.definition: Para-aminobenzoic acid, a chemical compound often used in sunscreen formulations.

values.label: Palm oil
values.definition: Palm oil is a yellow oil which comes from the fruit of certain palm trees and is used in making soap and sometimes as a fat in cooking.

values.label: Palm oil derivatives
values.definition: Substances derived from palm oil such as fatty acids, fatty alcohols and glycerol and their fractions such as olein and stearin. It is used in pharmaceuticals, oleochemical production, fuel, paint and plastics manufacturing and food production.

values.label: Pantothenic Acid
values.definition: Pantothenic acid, also called vitamin B5 (a B vitamin), is a water-soluble vitamin. Pantothenic acid is an essential nutrient. Animals require pantothenic acid in order to synthesize coenzyme-A (CoA), as well as to synthesize and metabolize proteins, carbohydrates, and fats. The anion is called pantothenate. Not to be confused with pantethine.

values.label: Paraben
values.definition: Any of a group of compounds used as preservatives in pharmaceutical and cosmetic products and in the food industry.

values.label: Paraffin
values.definition: Paraffin refers to a mixture of acyclic alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons) with the general total formula CnH2n+2.

values.label: Partially Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil
values.definition: Partially Hydrogenated Vegetable Oils (PHOs are the most common source of artificial trans fats within processed foods. The US FDA has revoked PHOs GRAS status and food manufacturers must remove PHOs from products.

values.label: Peanuts
values.definition: A claim that a food is free from peanuts. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Pea protein
values.definition: It is a source of protein derived and extracted in powder form from the yellow and green split peas (Pisum sativum).

values.label: Pecans
values.definition: A  species of hickory, native to south-central North America, in Mexico from Coahuila south to Jalisco and Veracruz,[1][2] in the United States in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Texas.

values.label: Peel
values.definition: The peel is the outer covering, mostly solid, of a fruit, nut or shellfish.

values.label: PEG emulsifiers
values.definition: Polyethylene glycols (PEG) are a humectant (which help retain or preserve moisture) or emulsifiers that can be found in many cosmetic products.

values.label: Perfume
values.definition: A fragrant liquid made from essential oils and aroma compounds used to provide a pleasant scent.

values.label: Peroxide
values.definition: Peroxides are a group of compounds with the structure R−O−O−R. The O−O group in a peroxide is called the peroxide group or peroxo group. In contrast to oxide ions, the oxygen atoms in the peroxide ion have an oxidation state of −1. The most common peroxide is hydrogen peroxide, colloquially known simply as "peroxide".

values.label: Pesticide
values.definition: Pesticides are substances that are meant to control pests, including weeds. The term pesticide includes all of the following: herbicide, insecticides (which may include insect growth regulators, termiticides, etc.) nematicide, molluscicide, piscicide, avicide, rodenticide, bactericide, insect repellent, animal repellent, antimicrobial, and fungicide.

values.label: Pesticide residues
values.definition: Pesticide residue refers to the pesticides that may remain on or in food after they are applied to food crops. The maximum allowable levels of these residues in foods are often stipulated by regulatory bodies in many countries. Regulations such as pre-harvest intervals also often prevent harvest of crop or livestock products if recently treated in order to allow residue concentrations to decrease over time to safe levels before harvest. Exposure of the general population to these residues most commonly occurs through consumption of treated food sources, or being in close contact to areas treated with pesticides such as farms or lawns.

values.label: Petrolatum
values.definition: Semi-solid mixture of hydrocarbons, commonly used for its moisturizing properties.

values.label: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)
values.definition: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a group of man-made chemicals that includes PFOA, PFOS, GenX, and many other chemicals.

values.label: Phenoxyethanol
values.definition: Germicidal and germistatic glycol ether, phenol ether, and aromatic alcohol often used together with quaternary ammonium compounds.

values.label: Phenylalanine
values.definition: A essential amino acid.

values.label: Phosphate
values.definition: The chemical formula is PO3−4.

values.label: Phosphorus
values.definition: Phosphorus

values.label: Phthalate
values.definition: Phthalates or phthalate esters, are esters of phthalic acid. They are mainly used as plasticizers, i.e., substances added to plastics to increase their flexibility, transparency, durability, and longevity.

values.label: Pinenuts
values.definition: The  edible seed of various pine trees.

values.label: Pistachios
values.definition:
The pistachio is the edible pale green seed of an Asian tree.
The pistachio is the evergreen tree of the cashew family that produces this nut, with small brownish-green flowers and reddish wrinkled fruit borne in heavy clusters. It is widely cultivated, especially in the US and around the Mediterranean.

values.label: Plant based alternative to meat
values.definition: A product whose structure and protein content mimic that of a type of meat. Also known as meat replacement in some markets. The determination of this is made by the supplier and is subject to target market regulations or trade organisation guidelines.

values.label: Plant protein
values.definition: The protein is derived from plant-based sources. There may be one or more sources of protein. Examples of vegetable protein sources are soy, oats or broad bean.

values.label: Plant sterols
values.definition: Plant sterols are defined as cholesterol‐like substances that occur naturally at low levels in many fruits, vegetables, nuts and cereals. Plant sterols can help to improve cholesterol levels.

values.label: Polyethylene Microbeads
values.definition: Microbeads are really tiny plastic particles usually smaller than two millimeters. The composition of microbeads can vary and often include polyethylene (PE).

values.label: Polyphosphate
values.definition: A chemical compound that contains phosphorus.

values.label: Polyunsaturated Fat
values.definition: Polyunsaturated Fat

values.label: Pork Gelatine
values.definition: Translucent, colourless, brittle (when dry), flavourless substance derived from collagen obtained from various pork raw materials (connective tissues (skin) and bones). It is commonly used as a gelling agent in food, pharmaceutical drugs, photography, and cosmetic manufacturing.

values.label: Potassium
values.definition: Potassium

values.label: Potato
values.definition: Widely cultivated edible, starchy root vegetable of the nightshade family (solanum tuberosum).

values.label: Poultry
values.definition: Domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, their meat or their feathers.

values.label: Powder
values.definition: Fine, dry particles produced by the grinding, crushing, or disintegration of a solid substance.

values.label: Prebiotics
values.definition: Compounds in food that induce the growth or activity of beneficial microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.

values.label: Preservatives
values.definition: A preservative is a natural or synthetic substance or chemical that is added to products to prevent decomposition by microbial growth or by undesirable chemical changes.

values.label: Probiotics
values.definition: Probiotics.

values.label: Protein
values.definition: Protein

values.label: Pulp
values.definition: Pulp is the juicy, soft part inside of fruits. Many consumers would like to avoid fruit pulp in fruit juices for personal reasons.

values.label: PVC (polyvinyl chloride)
values.definition: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) is a common, strong but lightweight plastic used in construction. It is made softer and more flexible by the addition of plasticizers.

values.label: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) without Phthalates
values.definition: Polyvinyle Chloride (PVC) with Phthalates is a common, strong but lightweight plastic used in construction. It is made softer and more flexible by without the addition of Phthalates as plasticizers.

values.label: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) with Phthalates
values.definition: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) with Phthalates is a common, strong but lightweight plastic used in construction. It is made softer and more flexible by the addition of Phthalates, used to plasticise PVC.

values.label: Quinine
values.definition: A bitter crystalline compound present in cinchona bark.

values.label: Raisins
values.definition: Raisins are dried grapes. The term "raisins" is both the generic term for all dried raisins and the specific term for the dried fruit of a particular grape variety.

values.label: Raspberries
values.definition: The raspberry is the edible fruit of a multitude of plant species in the genus Rubus of the rose family, most of which are in the subgenus Idaeobatus.

values.label: Raw  Beet Sugar
values.definition: Raw sugar derived from the sugar beet.

values.label: Recycled material
values.definition: A recycled material refers to any substance that has undergone a process of reprocessing or reclamation to be used again in the manufacturing of new products. Recycled materials can encompass a wide range of items, including paper, glass, metal, plastics, textiles, and more.

values.label: Recycled material, Mass balance
values.definition: Recycled material and feedstock are combined with virgin raw materials in the production process, resulting in a final product that contains both virgin and recycled content. Mass balance involves mixing fossil and recycled/renewable materials to meet this objective. It's important to note that individual trade items may not necessarily include recycled material, but the plastic material producer is certified for mass balance and incorporates a specific percentage of recycled materials in their feedstock. Refer to local regulations.

values.label: Renewable material
values.definition: A renewable material is a material made of natural resources that can be replenished, generation after generation.

values.label: Renewable material, Mass balance
values.definition: Renewable material and renewable feedstock (raw material used in industrial process or as fuel) with virgin raw materials in the production process. This creates a final product that is a mixture of virgin and renewable content. Mass balance is about mixing fossil and renewable/recycled materials.  It's important to note that individual trade items may not necessarily include renewable material, but the plastic material producer is certified for mass balance and incorporates a specific percentage of renewable materials in their feedstock. Refer to local regulations.

values.label: Retinyl Palmitate
values.definition: Retinyl Palmitate (Vitamin A Palmitate) is an ingredient composed of palmitic acid and retinol (Vitamin A).

values.label: Riboflavin
values.definition:
Vitamin B2, corresponding to riboflavin, or lactoflavin, is a water-soluble vitamin necessary for the synthesis of flavine adenine dinucleotide and flavine mononucleotide, two essential cofactors for flavoproteins.
Vitamin B2 plays an important role in converting simple foods (carbohydrates, fats and proteins) into energy. It is involved in muscle repair metabolism.

values.label: Rye
values.definition: A wheat like cereal plant that tolerates poor soils and low temperatures.

values.label: Saturated Fat
values.definition: A claim that a food is low in saturated fat, and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains no more than 1.5g of saturates per 100g for solids or, 0.75g of saturates per 100ml for liquids and in either case saturated fat must not provide more than 10% of energy. In the case of foods naturally low in saturated fat, the term "naturally" may be used as a prefix to this claim.

values.label: Sauce
values.definition: A liquid or semiliquid mixture that is added to a food as it cooks or that is served with it. Sauces provide flavour, moisture, and a contrast in texture and colour. They may also serve as a medium in which food is contained.

values.label: Seeds
values.definition: A seed is a plant's unit of reproduction, capable of developing into another such plant.

values.label: Selenium
values.definition: Selenium

values.label: Sesame
values.definition: The edible seeds of the sesame plant, which are used whole or have the oil extracted.

values.label: Shea butter
values.definition: A fatty substance obtained from the nuts of the shea tree. E.g., used in cosmetics, food.

values.label: Silicone
values.definition: Silicones, also known as polysiloxanes, are polymers that include any synthetic compound made up of repeating units of siloxane, which is a chain of alternating silicon atoms and oxygen atoms, combined with carbon, hydrogen, and sometimes other elements.

values.label: Skin
values.definition: The layer of tissue forming the natural outer covering of the body of an animal, fish or plant.

values.label: Smoke Flavour
values.definition: Smoke flavourings are produced by thermal degradation of wood. As an alternative to traditional smoking, they can be added to a range of different foods to give a “smoked” flavour.

values.label: Soap
values.definition: Soap is a substance used with water for washing and cleaning, made of a compound of natural oils or fats with sodium hydroxide or another strong alkali, and typically having perfume and colouring added.

values.label: Sodium lauryl sulfate
values.definition: Surfactant and detergent commonly found in personal care products and cleaning agents.

values.label: Sodium Nitrite
values.definition: The chemical formula is NaNO2

values.label: Sodium Salt
values.definition: Sodium or salt.

values.label: Soluble Fibre
values.definition: Soluble fibre dissolves in water to form a thick gel-like substance in the stomach. It is broken down by bacteria in the large intestine and provides some calories.

values.label: Sorbitol
values.definition: A sugar substitute with a sweet taste which the human body metabolizes slowly.

values.label: Soy/Soya
values.definition: Soybean (or soyabean); protein derived from soybeans, used as a replacement for animal protein in certain foods.

values.label: Soybean oil
values.definition: Soybean oil is extracted from the seeds of the soybean. It is one of the most widely consumed cooking oils and the second most consumed vegetable oil.

values.label: Steroid
values.definition: Organic compound with a molecular structure containing four rings, used to treat inflammation.

values.label: Stevia
values.definition: Stevia is a high-potency sweetener extracted from the leaves of the plant species stevia rebaudiana.

values.label: Sugars
values.definition: Includes sugars that are present naturally in the food such as lactose in milk and fructose in fruit, sucrose in fruits and vegetables, as well as sugars added to the food during processing, such as sugar / sucrose, corn syrup, honey, high fructose corn syrup, fruit juice concentrates and dextrose."

values.label: Sulfate
values.definition: A salt or ester of sulfuric acid, containing the anion SO42− or the divalent group —OSO2O—.

values.label: Sulphites
values.definition: Sulphites or sulfites are substances that are naturally found in some foods. They are used as an additive to maintain food colour, shelf-life and prevent the growth of fungi or bacteria.

values.label: Sunflower oil
values.definition: Sunflower oil is the non-volatile oil pressed from the seeds of sunflower. Sunflower oil is commonly used in food as a frying oil or cooking.

values.label: Sweeteners
values.definition: Any substance that sweetens such as sugar or a low-calorie synthetic product used instead of sugar.

values.label: Talc
values.definition: Mineral composed of hydrated magnesium silicate, used for its soft and absorbent properties.

values.label: Taste aversive agent
values.definition: A taste aversive or bittering agent is a chemical substance that is added to a product to help deter inappropriate ingestion and prevent poisonings from occurring. Denatonium benzoate, commonly sold under brand names like Bitrex® or Denatrol®, is one of the most widely used substances.

values.label: THC (Tetrahydrocannabinol)
values.definition: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is a chemical found in cannabis and is the principal psychoactive constituent.

values.label: Thiamin
values.definition: Thiamin, or vitamin B1, is involved in the transformation of glucose into energy and in the metabolism of amino acids. It is essential to the functioning of the nervous system and seems indispensable for memory and intellectual faculties.

values.label: Toluene
values.definition: Clear liquid aromatic hydrocarbon, used as an industrial solvent and in paint, varnish, adhesive.

values.label: Trans fat
values.definition: Trans fatty acids

values.label: Tree nuts
values.definition: Tree nuts include, but are not limited to, walnut, almond, hazelnut, cashew, pistachio, and Brazil nuts.

values.label: Triclocarban
values.definition: Triclocarban is an antibacterial agent common in personal care products like soaps and lotions as well as in the medical field, for which it was originally developed. Studies on its antibacterial qualities and mechanisms are growing.

values.label: Triclosan
values.definition: Triclosan (sometimes abbreviated as TCS) is an antibacterial and antifungal agent present in some consumer products, including toothpaste, soaps, detergents, toys, and surgical cleaning treatments.

values.label: Triticale
values.definition: Triticale is a hybrid grain produced by crossing wheat and rye, grown as a fodder crop.

values.label: Ultra-filtered nonfat milk
values.definition: Ultrafiltered nonfat or skimmed milk, also known as diafiltered, is a subclassification of milk protein concentrate that is produced by passing nonfat or skim milk under pressure through a thin, porous membrane to separate the components of milk according to their size. Please refer to target market regulations for definition of 'nonfat' or 'skimmed' and the allowable percentage of fat to be contained.

values.label: Unsaturated Fat
values.definition: Unsaturated Fat

values.label: Urea
values.definition: Urea, also known as carbamide, is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH₂)₂.

values.label: Vegetables
values.definition: Vegetables are parts of plants that are consumed by humans or other animals as food.

values.label: Vitamins and or Minerals
values.definition: Vitamins and/or minerals.

values.label: Vitamin A
values.definition: Vitamin A is also known as retinol.

values.label: Vitamin B12
values.definition: Vitamin B12

values.label: Vitamin B6
values.definition: Vitamin B6

values.label: Vitamin C
values.definition: Vitamin C

values.label: Vitamin D
values.definition: Vitamin D

values.label: Vitamin D2
values.definition: Vitamin D2 also known as ergocalciferol.

values.label: Vitamin D3
values.definition: Vitamin D3 also known as cholecalciferol.

values.label: Vitamin E
values.definition: Vitamin E is also known as tocopherol.

values.label: Vitamin K
values.definition: Vitamin K

values.label: Volatile organic compound (VOC)
values.definition: An organic compound that has a high vapor pressure at room temperature and low water solubility.

values.label: Walnuts
values.definition: A large wrinkled edible seed of a deciduous tree, consisting of two halves contained within a hard shell that is enclosed in a green fruit.

values.label: Water
values.definition: Water is a chemical substance with the chemical formula H2O. Water is an inorganic, transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colourless substance and it is used in food preparation.

values.label: Wheat
values.definition: Wheat

values.label: White meat tuna
values.definition: The only species of fish that can be called “White Tuna” is Albacore, refers to the relatively white-coloured flesh versus other tuna species, which have light tan or hint of pink flesh.

values.label: White Sugar
values.definition: White or granulated sugar is refined sugar (pure white crystalline sucrose) ground to granules or grains.

values.label: Whole grain
values.definition: The intact grain or the dehulled, ground, milled, cracked or flaked grain where the constituents – endosperm, germ and bran – are present in such proportions that represent the typical ratio of those fractions occurring in the whole cereal.

values.label: Whole wheat
values.definition: Whole wheat refers to wheat which contains all constituents of the wheat grain.

values.label: Wind power
values.definition: Wind power or wind energy is mostly the use of wind turbines to generate electricity. Wind power is a popular, sustainable, renewable energy source that has a much smaller impact on the environment than burning fossil fuels.

values.label: Yeast
values.definition: A microscopic fungus consisting of single oval cells that reproduce by budding, and capable of converting sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

values.label: Zeolite
values.definition: Zeolite is a group of porous minerals composed of aluminum silicates. Zeolites are used in industry for applications such as filtration, odour removal, molecular sieves, and water softening.

values.label: Zinc
values.definition: Zinc

values.label: Added
values.definition: A claim stating that a substance (e.g. sugar) has been added to a food.

values.label: Contains
values.definition: A claim that a food contains the ingredient/nutrition/etc specified in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Decaffeinated
values.definition: Indicates most or all of the caffeine is removed from the product.

values.label: Enriched With
values.definition: A claim that a food is enriched with the substance in the ClaimElementCode.  Enriched means adding back (to original levels) nutrients that were lost during food processing. e.g., Adding back certain B-vitamins lost in processing wheat to make white flour. Note the amount that determines enrichment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Excellent Source of
values.definition: The claim made is the trade item is an "Excellent Source of" the element specified. This is determined by any regulatory bodies what "Excellent" means or is just a marketing claim.

values.label: Excess
values.definition: A claim stating the specified element is in excess of some set value either by the manufacturer or according to local regulations.

values.label: Extra Lean
values.definition: The item is considered to be extra lean. USFDA criteria of this term can be found in 21 CFR at www.fda.gov.

values.label: Fed with
values.definition: A claim that the animal product is fed with the substance in the ClaimElementCode.

values.label: Fed without
values.definition: A claim that the animal product is fed without the substance in the ClaimElementCode.

values.label: Fortified
values.definition:
A claim that a food is fortified with the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Fortified means adding vitamins or minerals to a food that weren't originally present in the food.  This is often do for "Nutrition Policy", to ensure a population has a sufficient intake of an essential nutrient.  Some foods "may" be voluntarily fortified; for others, fortification is mandatory.  e.g., Adding vitamin D to milk.
Note the amount that determines fortified is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Free From
values.definition: A claim that a product is completely free from the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Fresh
values.definition: The item is considered to be fresh.USFDA criteria of this term can be found in 21 CFR at www.fda.gov.

values.label: Frozen
values.definition:
A product is frozen, for a longer shelf-life or
preserved by freezing temperature and does not include any surface freezing that may occur during holding and transportation.

values.label: Good Source of
values.definition: The claim made is the trade item is a "Good Source of" the element specified. This is determined by any regulatory bodies what "Good" means or is just a marketing claim.

values.label: Grown without
values.definition: A claim stating that a substance (e.g. herbicide) has not been used in the process of growing fruits, vegetables, plants or flowers.

values.label: Guaranteed Free From
values.definition: A claim that a food is regularly analysed to guarantee that the product is free from the substance in the ClaimElementCode.

values.label: Guaranteed Source of
values.definition: A claim that a food is regularly analysed to guarantee that the product contains the substance in the ClaimElementCode.

values.label: Healthy
values.definition: The item is claimed to be healthy. USFDA criteria of this term can be found in 21 CFR at www.fda.gov.

values.label: High
values.definition: A claim that a food is high in the substance specified in the ClaimElementCode. Any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: High Potency
values.definition: Item is considered to be High Potency.  USFDA criteria of this term can be found in 21 CFR at www.fda.gov.

values.label: Human grade
values.definition: A product that is suitable for consumption by a human.

values.label: Increased
values.definition: A claim that a food is increased specific ingredient/nutrition/etc. and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations. In the case of foods naturally increased amount specific ingredient/nutrition/etc.in the ClaimElementCode, the term "naturally" may be used as a prefix to this claim.

values.label: Lean
values.definition: The item is considered to be lean. USFDA criteria of this term can be found in 21 CFR at www.fda.gov.

values.label: Light Lite
values.definition: A claim stating that a product is "light" or "lite", and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, shall follow the same conditions as those set for the term "reduced"; the claim shall also be accompanied by an indication of the characteristic(s) which make the food "light" or "lite".

values.label: Limited ingredients
values.definition: A product formulated with a minimal number of ingredients.

values.label: Low
values.definition: A claim that a food is low in specific ingredient/nutrition/etc in the ClaimElementCode. Any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Made in Facility Free From
values.definition: Trade item is made in a facility that is free from a specified element. This usually is regulated in a market by an authority. Please refer to the regulation specific to your market.

values.label: Made with from
values.definition: A claim that the item is made with or from a specific ingredient/nutrition/etc. and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

values.label: Made with from 100%
values.definition: A claim that the item is made with/from 100% of a specific ingredient/nutrition/etc. and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

values.label: Made with fresh
values.definition: Food that is made with fresh ingredient that has never been frozen and it is raw, uncooked, unprocessed and not preserved.

values.label: Made with fresh and frozen
values.definition: Food that is made of both fresh and previously frozen ingredient.

values.label: Made with frozen
values.definition: Food that is made with previously frozen ingredients.

values.label: Made with minced
values.definition: Food that is made with mechanically recovered flesh which may include blood, pigments, skin, and membrane particles, bones, and other material.  It may be formed into large frozen blocks which are cut to make value-added products. It is usually used for formed fish products e.g., (breaded) fingers, nuggets or balls, fish cakes or surimi.

values.label: Made with natural
values.definition: A claim describing the product is made with some natural element.

values.label: Made with Organic
values.definition: A claim the trade item is made with specified element which is organic.

values.label: Made with pasteurized
values.definition: A food product that is made with specified ingredient which is pasteurized.

values.label: Made with unpasteurized or raw
values.definition: A food product that is made with specified ingredient which is not pasteurized or it is raw.

values.label: May contain
values.definition: The claim to state the product may contain some element.

values.label: May have
values.definition: The claim to state the product may have some descriptive element.

values.label: Natural
values.definition: A claim that a product does not contain synthetic or artificial ingredients.

values.label: Naturally free from
values.definition: A claim that a product is naturally free from the substance specified in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Naturally high
values.definition: A claim that a product is naturally high in the substance specified in the ClaimElementCode. Any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Naturally low
values.definition: A claim that a product is naturally low in the substance specified in the ClaimElementCode. Any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Naturally vegan
values.definition: Products that are aligned to the definition of vegan, but in addition are made from a single natural product without additional ingredients or additives. Local regulations, where they exist, prevail since a vegan or vegetarian declaration for naturally vegan or vegetarian products could be objected to by the authorities as advertising with self-evident facts, especially for mono-products.

values.label: Natural Source of
values.definition: A claim that a food is a natural source of the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines if the product is a significant source of a given substance is based on target market regulations.

values.label: No
values.definition: A claim that a product does not contain (verifiably) the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Non-alcoholic
values.definition: A claim that a food contains no alcohol. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: No Added
values.definition: A claim that the manufacturer has not added the substance in the ClaimElementCode.

values.label: Packed in
values.definition: A claim the trade item is packed in a specified element. Example Juice.

values.label: Partially made with from
values.definition: A claim that the item is partially made with/from specific ingredient/nutrition/etc. and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

values.label: Previously frozen
values.definition: Meat, poultry, or fish that has been frozen and thawed prior to sale.

values.label: Pure
values.definition: A claim that a food is Pure for a specific ingredient/etc. in the ClaimElementCode or the trade item itself. Note the determination a product/ingredient is "Pure" is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Raised Without
values.definition: A claim the trade item is raised without any of a specified element.

values.label: Real
values.definition: A claim that a food contains "Real" not imitation, specific ingredient/trade item/etc.in the ClaimElementCode or the trade item itself. Note the determination that a ingredient/trade item is "Real" is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Reduced Less
values.definition: A claim that a food has a reduced amount of the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines a reduced amount is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Source of
values.definition: A claim that a food is a source of the substance in the ClaimElementCode . Note the amount that determines containment is based on target market regulations

values.label: Sweetened With
values.definition: A claim that a food is sweetened with a specific ingredient/nutrition/etc. and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Unsalted
values.definition: Without salt (sodium chloride). Salt has not been added.

values.label: Unscented
values.definition: Unscented refers to a product having no added fragrance or scent.

values.label: Unsweetened
values.definition: Without sugar or a similar substance having been added

values.label: Vegan
values.definition: Products that are not of animal origin and at no stage of production and processing has use been made of, or the product been supplemented with ingredients or processing aids or substances that are of animal origin. The product has not been tested on animals. Local regulations, where they exist, prevail since the term may be a combination or all of the above statements.

values.label: Very Low
