values.definition: A claim that a food is very low in specific ingredient/nutrition/etc in the ClaimElementCode Any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer, may only be made where the product contains the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Without
values.definition: A claim that a product is without intentional addition of the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

values.label: Dishcloth
values.definition: A cloth used to clean dishes and surfaces.

values.label: Dust cloth
values.definition: A cloth used to dust surfaces.

values.label: Glass cleaning cloth
values.definition: A cloth used for cleaning glass, mirrors, porcelain, screens, and more.

values.label: Microfiber cleaning cloth
values.definition: A cloth made from very small fibers which is used for cleaning.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Shammy
values.definition: A soft cloth of chamois leather that is used to clean or to dry smooth objects. Originally, the chamois consists of natural chamois leather, made from the skin of a chamois. Nowadays, chamois is increasingly made from synthetic materials.

values.label: Squeegee cloth
values.definition: A piece of flannel cloth to clean floors.

values.label: Buckles or Clasps
values.definition: A pin buckle or clasp is a device used for fastening two loose ends, with one attached to it and the other held with a pin (also named prong) in a secure but adjustable manner, e.g. for watches or belts.

values.label: Buttons
values.definition: A button is usually a disk-like piece of solid material having holes or a shank through which it is sewed to one side of an article of clothing and used to fasten or close the garment by passing through a loop or hole in the other side.

values.label: Cable Tie
values.definition: A cable tie or tie-wrap, also known as a hose tie, zap-strap, or zip tie,[1] is a type of fastener, for holding items together, primarily electric cables or wires.

values.label: Clip Bulldog
values.definition: A bulldog clip is a device for temporarily binding sheets of paper together. It consists of a rectangular sheet of springy steel curved into a cylinder, with two flat steel strips inserted to form combined handles and jaws. The user presses the two handles together, causing the jaws to open against the force of the spring, then inserts a stack of papers and releases the handles. The spring forces the jaws together, gripping the papers firmly.

values.label: Clip Paper
values.definition: A paper clip (or sometimes paperclip) is an instrument used to hold sheets of paper together, usually made of steel wire bent to a looped shape.

values.label: Folding Clasp
values.definition: The folding clasp is a type of closure for watch straps. It is most commonly found in metal bandes. In contrast to the pin buckle, the bracelet is not fully opened with the folding clasp but is opened (folded up) on hinges. This widens the bracelet and it can be removed from the arm.

values.label: Grommets
values.definition: Round grommets look like metal or plastic rings that help reinforce holes. A cord or lace threads through the hole, also known as the eye. A grommet press or a grommet setting tool and a small hammer help fasten the grommet to the garment. (See Reference 3) Examples of grommets are found on laced running shoes and laced clothing. A grommet belt allows a person to adjust the fit by inserting a buckle's metal pin through a reinforced hole.

values.label: Hook and Eyes
values.definition: Hooks and eyes consist of two parts that interlock. The hook part features a curved shape. The eye has an opening which resembles a U-shape into which the hook is inserted to clsoe the item.

values.label: Hook and Loop Fasteners
values.definition: This variety of fastener is closed by pressure and opened by pulling it apart.  These fasteners are made of tiny, firm, hooks on one part and softer loops on the other. The size of the fastener indicates its holding strength.

values.label: Jeans Button
values.definition: A Jeans Button is generally used as a method of fastening for denim trousers or denim jackets.

values.label: Laces or Shoelaces
values.definition: Shoelaces, sometimes called shoestrings (US English) or bootlaces (UK English), are a system commonly used to secure shoes, boots and other footwear. Laces can also be used for other types of items, but function similarly to shoelaces.  Laces typically consist of a strings or cords, finished off at both ends with stiff sections, commonly known as aglets. The lace typically passes through a series of holes, eyelets, loops or hooks on either side of the closure. Loosening or removing the lacing allows the item to open, while tightening the lacing and tying off the ends secures the item.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Pin Push
values.definition: A thumb tack (North American English) or push pin is a short nail or pin used to fasten items to a wall or board for display and intended to be inserted by hand, generally without the assistance of tools. A variety of names are used to refer to different designs intended for various purpose. Thumb tack and push pin are both sometimes compounded (thumbtack or pushpin) or hyphenated (thumb-tack or push-pin). Thumb tacks made of brass, tin or iron may be referred to as brass tacks, brass pins, tin tacks or iron tacks, respectively.  Drawing pin or drawing-pin refers to thumb tacks used to hold drawings on drawing boards. Map pin or map tack refers to thumb tacks used to mark locations on a map and to hold the map in place.

values.label: Pin Safety
values.definition: The safety pin, also known as a baby pin, is a variation of the regular pin which includes a simple spring mechanism and a clasp. The clasp serves two purposes: to form a closed loop thereby properly fastening the pin to whatever it is applied to, and to cover the end of the pin to protect the user from the sharp point.  Safety pins are commonly used to fasten pieces of fabric or clothing together. Safety pins, or more usually a special version with an extra safe cover, called a nappy pin were widely used to fasten cloth diapers (nappies), as the safety clasp prevents the baby from being jabbed. Similarly, they can be used to patch torn or damaged clothing. Safety pins can also be used as an accessory or jewelry, such as earrings, chains, and wristbands. Sometimes they are used to attach an embroidered patch.

values.label: Pin Straight
values.definition: A pin is a device used for fastening objects or material together. Pins often have two components: a body or shaft with a sharp tip and a head or crown at the opposite end. The sharpened body penetrates the material, while the head provides a driving surface as wel las preventing the pin from oushing all the way through the material.

values.label: Rubber Band
values.definition: A rubber band, also known as a binder, elastic band, lackey band, laggy band, or elastic, is a short length of rubber and latex, elastic in nature and formed in the shape of a circle which is commonly used to hold multiple objects together.

values.label: Snap
values.definition: Snaps are fasteners that should be used to secure areas where there is little strain. They are primarily used to hold something in place, and can therefore be used in place of buttons and buttonholes or selfgripping devices.  The sew-in styles are generally in two parts: the ball and the socket (Figure 6). The ball part of the snap is positioned on the overlap side of the placket, and the socket on the underlap.

values.label: Snap Prong Type Press Stud
values.definition: This type of product is manufactured in 3 standards sizes of open prongs, LIGNE 14, LIGNE15 and LIGNE 16.  The snap is produced on this product by the construction of a petal like socket (female) which engages the stud (male).  This product is suitable for use on knitted fabrics due to the construction of the five pronged ring which attaches with either the socket or the stud.   A LIGNE is a measurement equivalent to 1/40th of an inch and the size of the product relates to the diameter of the open prong.

values.label: Snap Spring Type
values.definition: A two part snap fastener so called as the socket (female part) incorporates a spring which engages the stud (male part) to securely fasten the item.

values.label: Staple
values.definition: A staple is a type of two-pronged fastener, usually metal, used for joining or binding materials together. Large staples might be used with a hammer or staple gun for masonry, roofing, corrugated boxes and other heavy-duty uses. Smaller staples are used with a stapler to attach pieces of paper together; such staples are a permanent and durable fastener for paper documents, unlike the paper clip.

values.label: Strap
values.definition: A strap, sometimes also called strop, is an elongated flap or ribbon of material.  Thin straps are used as part of clothing or baggage, or bedding such as a sleeping bag (For example spaghetti strap, shoulder strap). A strap differs from a belt mainly in that a strap is usually integral to the item.  Straps are also used as fasteners to attach and bind items, to objects, animals (for example a saddle on a horse) and people (for example a watch on a wrist). Occasionally a strap is specified after what it binds or holds, e.g. chin strap.

values.label: Thread Eyes
values.definition: Whether it is for decoration or as a substitute for a metal eye, a thread eye can be used on a garment. The thread eyes are not as strong as a metal eye, but can be less conspicuous, and are therefore recommended for use in areas that do not have a lot of pull or strain, such as a neckline opening above a zipper.

values.label: Tie or Tie Handle
values.definition: A piece of material which can be tied around an opening or is integrated as a handle which can be tied at an opening to close the item.

values.label: Toggle Fasteners
values.definition: In contrast to the disc-shaped button, the toggle is usually long and narrow.  The toggle fastenings insert through loops of rope or leather to help fasten an item.

values.label: Treasury Tag
values.definition: A treasury tag or India tag is an item of stationery used to fasten sheets of paper together or to a folder.  A treasury tag is a lace with a sharp metal tag at one end which could be threaded through the holes in a stack of documents or cards and then inserted into a female tag at the other end to form a loop, so binding the documents. The tags in that case were in line with the string, like a shoelace. An India tag was similar but the metal tags were orthogonal to the string, so forming a cross-piece. The India tag did not form a loop as the cross-pieces were sufficiently wide that they did not slip back through the holes

values.label: Zipper
values.definition: A zipper, zip, fly or zip fastener, formerly known as a clasp locker, is a commonly used device for binding the edges of an opening of fabric or other flexible material, as on a garment or a bag.  A zipper is based on interlocking teeth. Initially it was called the “hookless fastener” and was later redesigned to become more reliable.

values.label: sRGB
values.definition: sRGB defines the chromaticities of the red, green, and blue primaries, the colours where one of the three channels is nonzero and the other two are zero. The gamut of chromaticities that can be represented in sRGB is the colour triangle defined by these primaries. As with any RGB colour space, for non-negative values of R, G, and B it is not possible to represent colours outside this triangle, which is well inside the range of colours visible to a human with normal trichromatic vision. sRGB is sometimes avoided by high-end print publishing professionals because its colour gamut is not big enough, especially in the blue-green colours, to include all the colours that can be reproduced in CMYK printing.

values.label: Hex-Value
values.definition: Colour-hex gives information about colours including colour models (RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK), Triadic colours, monochromatic colours and analogous colours calculated in colour page. Colour-hex.com also generates a simple css code for the selected colour. Common is the hexadecimal colour definition in six-digit form, that is, as a series of three hexadecimal numbers each written in two digits, according to the scheme: #RRGGBB. Reference for sample content: https://www.color-hex.com/

values.label: European-Brewing-Convention (EBC) colour scale
values.definition: The EBC colour scale is a system used to measure and describe the colour of beer and wort. It is standardized by the European Brewery Convention and is widely used in Europe and internationally. The EBC value represents the depth of colour, with lower values indicating paler beers (like lagers) and higher values indicating darker beers (like stouts or porters).

values.label: PANTONE MATCHING SYSTEM

The PANTONE formula guide, a three-guide set consisting of 1,114 solid PANTONE Colours on coated, uncoated and matte stock, shows corresponding printing ink formulas for each colour, and the three-book set of solid chips provides coated, uncoated and matte perforated tear-out chips that can be used for quality control. Pantone® Inc

values.label: PANTONE Process Colour System®
values.definition: Provides a comprehensive palette of more than 3,000 colours achievable in four-color (CMYK) process printing. The PANTONE solid to process guide compares a solid PANTONE Colour to the closest possible match in CMYK four-color process that can be achieved on a computer monitor, output device or printing press. Other PANTONE Colour Reference Guides for the graphic arts include metallic, pastels, tints, duotones, film and foil. The PANTONE Hexachrome® Color System. Pantone® Inc

values.label: The PANTONE Hexachrome® Color System
values.definition: A six-colour ultra high quality printing process, reproduces a dynamic range of more brilliant continuous-tone images and simulates brighter, more vivid colours than standard four-color process printing. Pantone® Inc

values.label: PANTONE TEXTILE Colour System®

The System - consisting of 1,932 colours in cotton or paper format - is ideal for assembling creative palettes and conceptual colour schemes, and for providing colour communication and control in the manufacturing process. values.label: 3D Active
values.definition: The 3 dimensional illusion is created using glasses that block the images to each eye in rapid succession. The glasses shutter open and closed faster than you can see. The end result is that each eye sees a different image, producing a 3D effect.

values.label: 3D Digital

values.label: 3D Passive

values.label: 3D Projection

values.label: Dispersible
values.definition: Dispersing agents have been added to the substance. Dispersing agents are added to process liquids to prevent unwanted deposits by keeping them finely dispersed. They function in both aqueous and non-aqueous media.

values.label: Emulsifiable
values.definition: An emulsion is a mixture of two immiscible (unblendable) liquids. One liquid is dispersed in the other. Many emulsions are oil/water emulsions, with dietary fats being one common type of oil encountered in everyday life. Examples of emulsions include butter and margarine, milk and cream, and vinaigrettes. In butter and margarine, fat surrounds droplets of water (a water-in-oil emulsion). In milk and cream, water surrounds droplets of fat (an oil-in-water emulsion).

values.label: Insoluble
values.definition: The substance is not capable of being dissolved in a solvent.

values.label: Not or Hardly Miscible
values.definition: The substance is immiscible or nearly immiscible. Substances are said to be immiscible if in any proportion, they do not form a solution. For example, diethyl ether is fairly soluble in water, but these two solvents are not miscible since they are not soluble in all proportions.

values.label: Suspended
values.definition: The substance is in suspension. A suspension is a homogeneous fluid containing solid particles that are sufficiently large for sedimentation. When the solid is mixed with liquid, suspended particles will eventually settle. An example of a suspension would be sand in water. The suspended particles are visible under a microscope and will settle over time if left undisturbed.

values.label: Water Soluble
values.definition: The substance is soluble. Solubility is the ability of a given substance to dissolve in a solvent. It is measured in terms of the maximum amount of solute dissolved in a solvent at equilibrium. Certain liquids are soluble in all proportions with a given solvent, such as ethanol in water.

values.label: Calendar Date
values.definition: A date in a calendar is a reference to a particular day represented within a calendar system. The calendar date allows the specific day to be identified. The date uses a format expressed in three parts: year, month and day.  Other format orders may be used - The month may be expressed as a number or in alphabetic form (optionally abbreviated). This format is sometimes referred to as Numeric Date.

values.label: Ordinal Date
values.definition: A calendar date consisting of a year and a day of year ranging between 1 and 366 (starting on January 1). The two numbers can be formatted as YYYY-DDD.  The date uses a format based on the year and the number of the day within the year. Example: 2009-036 = 5 February 2009. This format is sometimes referred to as a Julian Date.

values.label: Week of year number
values.definition: The number of a week in a calendar year. This format is a numeric value between 1-52 or 53. WW: week of year.

values.label: Round
values.definition: Round implants have a lenticular shape, with a symmetrical curved anterior side (dome) and a flat round posterior base, with no apparent differences in the shape between the top and bottom of the implant.

values.label: Shaped/Anatomical
values.definition: Anatomically shaped implants are designed to mimic natural anatomical contours. They often have an asymmetric form, with variations in contour and projection to support alignment and integration with surrounding anatomy. Surfaces may combine curved and flat areas, and the overall geometry can differ depending on the intended application.

values.label: Macro texture
values.definition: Surface roughness greater than 50 µm, classified according to ISO 14607:2018.

values.label: Micro texture
values.definition: Surface roughness between 10 µm and 50 µm, classified according to ISO 14607:2018.

values.label: Polyurethane
values.definition: The device outer shell is made of polyurethane foam.

values.label: Smooth
values.definition: Surface roughness less than 10 µm, classified according to ISO 14607:2018.

values.label: Ambidextrous
values.definition: Designed to be used by left-handed and right-handed people with equal ease.

values.label: Left Handed
values.definition: Designed to be used by left-handed people with ease.

values.label: Right Handed
values.definition: Designed to be used by right-handed people with ease.

values.label: Coeliac
values.definition: Denotes a product that can be safely consumed by a person with coeliac disease. Coeliac disease is caused by a reaction to gladin (a gluten protein found in wheat) and similar proteins found in other crops.

values.label: Diabetic
values.definition: Denotes a product that intends to decrease the need for insulin or oral diabetic agents by adjusting caloric and carbohydrate intake.

values.label: Dietetic
values.definition: Denotes a product that is specially prepared or processed for people on restrictive diets.

values.label: Low FODMAP diet
values.definition: The low Fermentable Oligosaccharides Disaccharides Monosaccharides And Polyols (FODMAP) diet is a specialized dietary plan designed to help individuals manage symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and other functional gastrointestinal disorders. FODMAP are poorly absorbable short-chain carbohydrates and sugar alcohols that can be found in various everyday food products (such as various fruits and vegetables, honey, milk, and sweeteners).

values.label: Free From Gluten
values.definition: Denotes a product that can be used in a gluten free diet, as specified by the appropriate authority within a target market.

values.label: Grain free
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a grain-free diet that eliminates all grains, including wheat, spelt, barley, rye, dried corn, millet, rice, and oats, as well as foods — and sometimes even ingredients — derived from them.

values.label: Halal
values.definition: Denotes selling or serving food ritually fit according to Islamic dietary laws.

values.label: High Carb
values.definition: High Carb is not a fast diet but much more a complete diet. "High Carb" means that most of the calories in your daily diet come from carbohydrates. At the same time, it is also a low fat diet because the fat content in the diet is relatively low.

values.label: High protein
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a protein-defined diet in which protein foods are dominant, calories are low, carbohydrates are largely avoided and fat is avoided to a limited extent.

values.label: Infant Formula
values.definition: Infant formulas come in powder, liquid concentrate, and ready-to-feed forms. Infant formulas come in a variety of types: Cow's milk formula is the most commonly used type. The milk has been altered to resemble breast milk. Soy protein based formulas are frequently used for infants allergic to cow's milk or lactose.

values.label: Keto
values.definition: A ketogenic diet is a form of low carb diet. It is characterized by an extremely low carbohydrate and very high-fat diet. Due to the lack of carbohydrates, the metabolism changes and gets into the so-called "ketosis".

values.label: Kosher
values.definition: Denotes selling or serving food ritually fit according to Jewish dietary laws.

values.label: Lactase Enzyme
values.definition: This product is an enzyme supplement used to help people who have trouble digesting milk and other dairy products (lactose intolerance). Lactase enzyme is normally produced by the body to help break down (digest) lactose.

values.label: Lactose free
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a those with an intolerance to lactose as the product does not contain the lactose sugar that is normally found in a dairy product.

values.label: Low calorie
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a calorie-defined diet in which the calorie intake is restricted.

values.label: Low Carb
values.definition: Low-carb diets is a diet that restrict carbohydrate consumption. Foods high in carbohydrates (e.g., sugar, bread, pasta) are limited or replaced with foods containing a higher percentage of fats and moderate protein (e.g., meat, poultry, fish, shellfish, eggs, cheese, nuts, and seeds) and other foods low in carbohydrates (e.g., most salad vegetables such as spinach, kale, chard and collards), although other vegetables and fruits (especially berries) are often allowed.

values.label: Low Fat
values.definition: A low-fat diet is one that restricts fat and often saturated fat and cholesterol as well. Low-fat diets are intended to reduce the occurrence of conditions such as heart disease and obesity.

values.label: Low protein
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a protein-defined diet in which the protein intake with food is restricted.

values.label: Low salt
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for a salt-defined diet in which the salt intake with food is restricted.

values.label: Meal Replacement
values.definition: A calorie-controlled, pre-packaged product in the form of a bar or a beverage (ready-to-drink or powder) that is used to replace a meal.

values.label: Mothers Milk Substitute
values.definition: The item is approved as substitute mother's milk the appropriate authority of the target market.

values.label: No special diet code
values.definition: Indicates that the product does not relate to any special diet program or dietary needs.

values.label: Nutrition Supplement
values.definition: Nutritional supplements are any dietary supplement that is intended to provide nutrients that may otherwise not be consumed in sufficient quantities; for example, vitamins, minerals, proteins, amino acids or other nutritional substances.

values.label: Organic
values.definition: Denotes a food product that was produced with the use of feed or fertiliser of plant or animal origin, without employment of chemically formulated fertilisers, growth stimulants, antibiotics or pesticides.

values.label: Paleo
values.definition: Paleo diet, is a fad diet type requiring the sole or predominant eating of foods presumed to have been available to humans during the Paleolithic era.

values.label: Pescatarian
values.definition: A pescatarian diet excludes meat and poultry but includes fish or seafood (and may include dairy products and eggs).

values.label: Plant based
values.definition: A plant-based diet is a way of eating that focuses on vegetables fruits, whole grains, legumes (beans, peas, and lentils), nuts and seeds. (i.e. foods that come from plants. It is not a vegan/vegetarian diet that avoids animal products, but it de-emphasizes animal products and its contribution to our meals).

values.label: Pollotarian
values.definition: A pollotarian diet, also known as a pollo-vegetarian diet, incorporates poultry, including turkey and duck, as the only source of meat in an otherwise vegetarian diet.

values.label: Probiotics
values.definition: Probiotics are live bacteria and yeasts that are good for you, especially your digestive system.

values.label: Raw food diet
values.definition: A dietary practice of eating food that is uncooked and unprocessed. Also known as Raw foodism, rawism.

values.label: Total Diet Supplement
values.definition: Dietary supplements include vitamins, minerals, herbs, botanicals, enzymes, amino acids, or other dietary ingredients. You take these products by mouth in pill, capsule, tablet, or liquid form to replace your diet.

values.label: Vegan
values.definition: Products that are not of animal origin and at no stage of production and processing has use been made of, or the product been supplemented with ingredients or processing aids or substances that are of animal origin. The product has not been tested on animals. Local regulations, where they exist, prevail since the term may be a combination or all of the above statements.

values.label: Vegetarian
values.definition: Denotes a product that contains no meat or other animal products but depending upon the local market regulations may also contain milk, eggs, products from bees (and in some markets also fish), and their components. Please refer to local regulations.

values.label: Without Beef
values.definition: Denotes a product that contains no beef or beef-products. Beef is considered to be a taboo food product by some religions most notable Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism.

values.label: Without Pork
values.definition: Denotes a product that contains no pork meat.

values.label: Lacto-pesca
values.definition: A lacto pesca pescatarian/vegetarian diet excludes meat, poultry and eggs, but includes fish and dairy products.

values.label: Dairy
values.definition: Kosher or Halal or any other diet certified dairy product.

values.label: Dairy for Passover
values.definition: Kosher certified dairy product for Passover.

values.label: Kosher Dairy Equipment
values.definition: A hot product, while pareve in its essence, has been manufactured using equipment that was also used to manufacture hot dairy products where no kosherization occurred in between. It is important to note that a thorough cleaning of the equipment still occurs between production runs and there is absolutely no dairy products contained in an item labeled DE. Link: https://cor.ca/view/183/what_does_dairy_equipment_mean.html

values.label: Fish
values.definition: Kosher or Halal or any other diet certified fish product.

values.label: Fish for Passover
values.definition: Kosher certified fish product for Passover.

values.label: Kosher for Passover
values.definition: Kosher certificate product for passover

values.label: Kosher for Passover-Mevushal
values.definition: Kosher for Passover Mevushal wine has been boiled or undergone flash pasteurisation.

values.label: Lacto
values.definition: A lacto vegetarian diet excludes meat, fish, poultry, and eggs, but includes dairy products.

values.label: Lacto-Ovo
values.definition: A lacto ovo vegetarian diet excludes meat, fish, and poultry but includes dairy products and eggs.

values.label: Lacto-Ovo-Pesca
values.definition: A lacto ovo pesca pescatarian/vegetarian diet excludes meat, and poultry but includes fish, dairy products, and eggs.

values.label: Meat
values.definition: Kosher or Halal or any other diet certified meat product.

values.label: Meat for Passover
values.definition: Kosher certified meat product for Passover.

values.label: Kosher Mevushal
values.definition: Mevushal wine has been boiled or undergone flash pasteurisation.

values.label: Ovo
values.definition: A ovo vegetarian diet excludes meat, fish, poultry, and dairy products, but includes eggs.

values.label: Pareve
values.definition: Kosher certified pareve product.

values.label: Pareve for Passover
values.definition: Kosher certified pareve product for Passover.

values.label: Pesca
values.definition: A pesca pescatarian/vegetarian diet excludes meat, poultry, dairy products, and eggs, but includes fish.

values.label: AAD

values.label: ADD
values.definition: The record was produced as follows: Recording = analogue,  editing/mixing = digital dubbing/transfer = digital.

values.label: DDD
values.definition: The record was produced as follows: Recording = digital,  editing/mixing = digital dubbing/transfer = digital.

values.label: Display Item Folded On Shelf

values.label: Display Item Hanging
values.definition: Item has been assembled for display and it has been set to hang from a frame or ceiling. The product may have a hanger in some cases (e.g. apparel).

values.label: Display Item Hanging From  Shelf
values.definition: Item has been assembled for display and it has been set to hang from the shelf itself. The product may have a hanger in some cases.

values.label: Display Item Standing
values.definition: Item has been assembled for display and it has been placed for display directly on the floor.

values.label: Display Item Standing On Shelf

values.label: In Package
values.definition: Product is measured as the package was supplied.

values.label: Maximum Squash
values.definition: The specific measurement for the product that when squashed will safely fit on the shelf without damage.

values.label: Max Door Drawer Lid Clearance
values.definition: Item is displayed with the door or lid open to require the maximum clearance. Applies for example to Refrigerators, dishwashers, ovens, Washers, dryers, furniture, and laptop computers.

values.label: Max Door Drawer Lid Clearance With Handle
values.definition: Item is displayed with the door or lid including its handle open to require the maximum clearance.  Applies for example to refrigerators, dishwashers ovens and furniture.

values.label: Out Of Package
values.definition: Product is removed from consumer packaging, assembled if necessary for final use and its dimensions. For example: Computer desk; entertainment centre; microwave oven; lawnmower; a floor cleaner; a grouping of table and chairs; stove; telephone; camera; large appliance (e.g. washing machines); small appliance (e.g. food processors).

values.label: Product without stand
values.definition: Product is removed from consumer packaging and the included stand is not installed. The associated dimensions are of the product without the stand as fully assembled. For example: Television dimensions without the included stand.

values.label: Product with stand
values.definition: Product is removed from consumer packaging and has an included stand installed. The associated dimensions are of the product and the stand as fully assembled. For example: Television dimensions with the included stand.

values.label: Retail Display
values.definition: Product is measured as modified for display. For example: Display Ready Packaging with fold-up lid or fold-forward front; a box of chocolate bars with display flap; display stand for dishware; merchandise for consumer purchase that is in a ‘display’ carton that requires modification, such as a product in cans contained within a carton; free-standing displays for a variety of grocery products, candles, decorative items like picture frames); a laptop computer.

values.definition: Aerosol is a type of dispensing system which creates an aerosol mist of liquid particles. When used the system contains a payload and propellant under pressure.

values.label: Drip

values.label: Hand pump
values.definition: A manually operated device under mechanical assistance to move a liquid or air from one place to another.

values.label: Rim block

values.label: Roller

values.label: Motion activated sensor

values.label: Touch activated sensor
values.definition: Dispenser is activated by touch.

values.label: Spray
values.definition: A product dispenser that can squirt, spray or mist fluids. A common use for spray dispensers for cleaners, cosmetics, and chemical specialties.

values.label: Squeeze
values.definition: A container allowing the act of squeezing in order to push out the substance that is inside.

values.label: Stick
values.definition: A stick is packaged in hollow tubes with an elevator platform inside that moves up and down to dispense the product. This platform can be elevated by turning a screw or push up that causes it to travel up along a central post.

values.label: Time interval activated
values.definition: Dispenser is activated at a time interval. The time interval may be pre-set or adjustable.

values.definition: Active Matrix Organic Light Emitting Diode (AMOLED) is an advanced display technology where each pixel emits its own light without the need for backlighting.

values.label: Front projection
values.definition: Display method where an image is projected onto a screen from the front, typically using a projector placed in front of the viewing surface. It is commonly used in home theaters, classrooms, and cinemas.

values.label: LCD
values.definition: Liquid Crystal Display (LCD): an electro-optical amplitude modulator realized as a thin, flat display device made up of any number of colour or monochrome pixels arrayed in front of a light source or reflector. For example, Apple’s Retina, Liquid Retina, Liquid Retina XDR display are using the LCD technology.

values.label: Liquid Crystal on Silicone

values.label: Light Emitting Polymer

values.label: Organic Light Emitting Diode
values.definition: Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED): any Light Emitting Diode (LED) whose emissive electroluminescent layer is composed of a film of organic compounds. For example, Apple’s Super Retina XDR is using the OLED technology.

values.label: Plasma

values.label: Quantum dot
values.definition: Quantum dot is a display technology that uses quantum dots to enhance colour and brightness. Unlike OLED, quantum dot screens still require a backlight (usually LED), but they offer high brightness, vibrant colours, and long lifespan. Also known as Quantum Dot Light Emitting Diode (QLED), Triluminos, Quantum Color, or Quantum Nano-Emitting Diode (QNED).

values.label: Rear Projection

values.label: Surface Conduction Electronic Emitter Display

values.label: 4K Ultra-High Definition
values.definition: 4K Ultra-high-definition television (UHDTV or UHD) or simply 4K is a resolution standard for video products (television, playback devices, and storage media). The term "4K" refers to a horizontal resolution of approximately 4,000 pixels. The use of width to characterise the overall resolution marks a switch from previous television standards such as 480i and 1080p, which categorise media according to its vertical dimension. Using that same convention, 4K UHD would be named 2160p since it has twice the horizontal and vertical resolution of 1080p. It has a resolution of 3840 x 2160 (16:9, or approximately a 1.78:1 aspect ratio).

values.label: Cross Dock
values.definition: The supplier picks and packs the goods per retail store location and delivers the goods to the retailers’ distribution centre for transfer across the loading dock to local delivery vehicles. In this case the goods are not stored in the distribution centre.

values.label: Factory Gate

values.label: Imported

values.definition: A document used to authorise or de-authorise an item for sale to one or many business locations.

values.label: Catalogue Item Authorisation Response
values.definition: Response Document used to Accept or Reject a Catalogue Item Authorisation.

values.label: Catalogue Item Hierarchical Withdrawal
values.definition: A business message used to transmit trade item information from a data source or a data pool to a data recipient with the Global Data Synchronisation Network with regards to a correction that is required to an item hierarchy that has already been synchronised.

values.label: GS1 Response
values.definition: The standard response sent within the GDSN.

values.definition: An electronic document used to synchronise pricing information including pricing relationship, pricing elements and item price depiction between trading partners in order to facilitate an invoice amount equal to the expected payment amount equal to the actual payment.

values.label: Price Synchronisation Confirmation
values.definition: The electronic communication from the Data Recipient to the Data Source indicating what action has been taken on the price synchronisation

values.label: GDSN

values.label: GLN Registries

values.label: UNECE (United Nations Economic Commission for Europe)
values.definition: The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) is one of the five regional commissions under the jurisdiction of the United Nations Economic and Social Council. It was established in order to promote economic cooperation and integration among its member states.

values.label: Animal detail category
values.definition: Refers to the detail of the animal that may be age, gender, or specific type of animal.

values.label: Cut
values.definition: Refers to the cut/anatomical form or such of the animal based on the standard.

values.label: Feeding system
values.definition: Refers to the feeding system according to regulation of the importing country. If no regulation exists then the exporting country regulation.

values.label: Production system
values.definition: Refers to the production system according to regulation of the importing country. If no regulation exists then the exporting country regulation.

values.label: Quality level
values.definition: Refers to the quality level of the product based upon some classification of quality.

values.label: Refrigeration
values.definition: Refers to the refrigeration method used, tolerances for product weight to be agreed between buyer and seller.

values.label: Compact Flash
values.definition: A mass storage device format used in portable electronic devices.

values.label: HC MMC Plus
values.definition: A flash memory card standard.

values.label: Impact Flash
values.definition: Impact Flash

values.label: Memory Stick
values.definition: A removable flash memory card format.

values.label: Memory Stick Duo
values.definition: A smaller flash memory card for pocket-sized digital cameras and cell phones.

values.label: Memory Stick Pro
values.definition: A removable flash memory card format.

values.label: Alcohol
values.definition: Alcohol is an organic compound in which a hydroxyl group is bound to a carbon atom. CAS number: 64-17-5

values.label: Butane
values.definition: Butane is a highly volatile, colourless hydrocarbon gas with an odour similar to petroleum. Also known as n-butane. CAS number: 106-97-8

values.label: Carbon dioxide
values.definition: Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2. It appears as a colourless odourless gas at atmospheric temperature and pressure. CAS number: 124-38-9

values.label: Dry sieve
values.definition: Dry Sieve is a concentrate free of chemicals and water, created by dry sifting material through a series of screens.

values.label: Ethanol
values.definition: Ethanol is an organic compound, a volatile, flammable, colourless liquid with a characteristic wine-like odour and pungent taste. It is the active ingredient in alcoholic drinks. Also known as ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol. CAS number: 64-17-5

values.label: Heat
values.definition: Heat is a form of energy crossing the boundary of a thermodynamic system by virtue of a temperature difference across the boundary.

values.label: Hexane
values.definition: Hexane is an organic compound, a colourless liquid and odourless when pure. It is widely used as solvent. CAS number: 110-54-3

values.label: Isopropanol
values.definition: Isopropanol is a clear, colourless liquid flammable organic compound with a pungent alcoholic odour. Also known as isopropyl alcohol. CAS number: 67-63-0

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Water
values.definition: Water is a substance with the chemical formula H2O. Water is an inorganic, transparent, tasteless, odourless, and nearly colourless substance. CAS number: 7732-18-5

values.label: AC DC Adapter
values.definition: A power supply that is built into a plug and is not built into the unit it is powering.

values.label: Additional Attachments
values.definition: Indicates whether a product comes with separate accessories for example a shower hose sold with a shower head.

values.label: Adjustable
values.definition: Code indicating the ability, or lack of ability, to change to conform to a specific user's needs, usually as it relates to size.

values.label: Animated
values.definition: The trade item having the appearance of something alive, animated in anyway.

values.label: Antibacterial
values.definition: The product is designed to contribute to hygiene or odour reduction by inhibiting the growth of bacteria on its surface or on the applied surface.

values.label: Antique
values.definition: Is item old and considered to be an antique?  This varies by different qualifications depending on market and item what is considered an antique.

values.label: Anti-slip Property
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got anti-slip properties or is slip-resistant for example the floor of a drain whirlpool tub or right drain soaking tub.

values.label: Approved for Tube Feeding
values.definition: The item may be physically marked that it is approved for tube feeding by the appropriate authority of the target market.

values.label: Aspect Ratio Control
values.definition: A feature providing the means to set different viewing window sizes for a television.

values.label: Automatic heating element
values.definition: Refers to a device that is designed to heat up automatically when a certain condition or trigger is met. These heating elements are commonly found in various appliances and systems to ensure proper temperature control, energy efficiency, and consumer convenience.

values.label: Automatic safety switch
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has got a automatic safety switch or automatic shut-off that prevents unintended or unsupervised use of e.g. an oven.

values.label: Auto-channel Setup
values.definition: A feature which automatically sets up all channels available and tunes the television channels at the touch of a button.

values.label: Benzoyl peroxide resistant
values.definition: Code indicating that the product is resistant to Benzoyl Peroxide contact.

values.label: Built-in Alarm Clock
values.definition: A clock that is designed to make a loud sound at a specific time and is built into the unit.

values.label: Centre Channel Capable
values.definition: A fifth speaker output for replication of crisp and clear sound.

values.label: Ceramic Cooktop Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable for ceramic cooktop hob or stove. A ceramic cooktop consists of a low-expansion thermal glass-ceramic that is transparent to infrared, which houses halogen heaters below it.

values.label: Child Lock Software
values.definition: Software security used to prevent unwanted tampering with feature settings.

values.label: Clip On
values.definition: Designed to attach by means of a clip

values.label: Clothing label
values.definition: Code indicating the presence of a label on clothing. Examples: product size, wash details, branding, etc.

values.label: Coated Wire
values.definition: Indicates that the wire is coated with a plastic, vinyl or other sleeve-like protection,

values.label: Cold
values.definition: The product is designed to be used with or keep contents which are cold or chilled. Example: Ice chest.

values.label: Collectible or Memorabilia
values.definition: The trade item considered collectible by consumer or evokes memories to the end consumer

values.label: Coloured
values.definition: Indicates that a product is coloured.

values.label: Common Interface Module
values.definition: An extensible digital interconnect found in digital Televisions. This feature enables the viewing of pay channels without the need for cable box or set top boxes.

values.label: Computer Programmable
values.definition: Indicates that a product is computer enabled to be programmed by a consumer (non-manual).

values.label: Convertible
values.definition: Code indicating the presence of the ability to be changed in form, function, or character.

values.label: Cordless
values.definition: The product does not require a cord. Example or cordlessproducts  phone, battery powered drill.

values.label: Corner Element
values.definition: Indicates that a product is a corner element.

values.label: Cover
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has a cover included  for example garden furniture that comes with a PVC cover.

values.label: Customer Cuttable
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be easily cut for custom use for example foam.

values.label: Datalogging
values.definition: Indicates that a product has digital recording capabilities for example a Datalogging Sound Level Meter, Digital Multimeter Meter, Digital Temperature Meter.

values.label: Decorated
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is delivered with decoration for example a pre-lit pine flocked artificial Christmas tree with white incandescent lights.

values.label: Delicate surfaces
values.definition: Indicates the product is marked as to be used for delicate surfaces.

values.label: Detachable hood
values.definition: Code indicating a hood can be detached from the product.

values.label: Detachable strap
values.definition: Code indicating a strap can be detached from the product.

values.label: Digital Cable Ready
values.definition: The ability to project digital cable with the use of a separate tuner.

values.label: Dimmable
values.definition: It covers both, switches that change the electric power output as well as lamps that are capable of emitting light at varying degrees of brightness.

values.label: Dishwasher Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable for dishwasher.

values.label: DVBC Cable Ready
values.definition: The ability to project DVB-C cable with the use of a separate tuner. DVB-C stands for Digital Video Broadcasting.

values.label: Eco-friendly
values.definition: The product is not harmful to the environment.

values.label: Elastic or Flexible
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is elastic or flexible for example a shower hose.

values.label: Electric Stove Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable and safe to use for an electric stove.

values.label: Electronic Safety Features
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has got electronic safety features or system.

values.label: Embossed
values.definition: The product has a design or pattern which stands out in relief.

values.label: Endurance Burning
values.definition: Specifies whether a furnace/oven has a slow-burning feature. For example a closed heating device where the amount of air entering the fire box is controlled to slow down combustion.

values.label: Energy Saving
values.definition: Indicates that a product saves energy for example an energy saving LED desk lamp or Energy Star window air conditioner.

values.label: Engraved
values.definition: The item has been engraved or etched with a logo, monogram, or other image.

values.label: Estate Bottled
values.definition: Means that the winery listed on the label owns or controls 100 percent of the grapes that went into the bottle, and the wine was crushed, fermented, finished, aged and bottled all in the same place, and that place has to be located in the same viticultural area.

values.label: Exterior Pockets
values.definition: The trade item contains pockets on the exterior or outside of the item.

values.label: Extractable Shower
values.definition: Indicates that a product has an extractable shower.

values.label: Extremely Clean
values.definition: The package is physically marked as extremely clean which slightly lower level of cleanness than sterile is. This means that it is free from bacteria and other microorganisms to a level defined as extremely clean by the appropriate authorities of the target market.

values.label: Factory Finished
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has been factory finished and does not require any after treatment.

values.label: Fast Curing
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is a fast curing one for example adhesives, mortar or concrete.

values.label: Filter System
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is supplied with a filter system for example a water dispenser with water filtration system.

values.label: Fire Resistant
values.definition: Treated so as to be non-flammable.

values.label: Flexible Head
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has got a flexible head for example water tap.

values.label: Flicker Free
values.definition: A feature that increases the frequency of which the picture refreshes measured in hertz (50 to 200Hz) Flicker-free technology noticeably improves viewing quality.

values.label: Flight Approved
values.definition: The item is approved to be safe for travel by authorities that control flight security like in the US the TSA.

values.label: Fog Resistant
values.definition: The item is designed to resist fogging or condensation.

values.label: Foldable
values.definition: Whether the trade item, device or appliance is foldable, collapsible or not. Example Ironing board

values.label: Framed
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is framed (e.g. mirror).

values.label: Frame Grounded
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is grounded by frame for example a plug socket.

values.label: Freezer Safe
values.definition: Indicates that the product is suitable for using in a freezer. E.g. the product is a plastic box in which a consumer can freeze food.

values.label: Fretted
values.definition: A fret is a raised element on the neck of a stringed instrument.

values.label: Frost Resistant
values.definition: Resistant to frost and can thus be used outside.

values.label: Gas Cooktop Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable to use for gas cooktop hob or stove.

values.label: Gearbox Housing From Aluminium
values.definition: Indicates whether a gearbox housing is made from aluminium.

values.label: Glazed
values.definition: Indicates that a product is glazed for e.g. Glazed Polished Tiles, Glazed Brown bricks.

values.label: Grounded
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is electrically grounded for example a 3-Wire 16-Gauge Grounded Indoor/Outdoor Extension Cord, Outdoor Plug-In Mechanical Timer with 2 Grounded Outlets, 6-Outlet Grounded Power Strip.

values.label: Ground Sleeves
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is delivered with ground sleeves for example small goals with ground sleeve.

values.label: Handmade
values.definition: Code indicating the product was made by hand, not by machine.

values.label: Hand-painted
values.definition: Code indicating the product contains hand-painting on one or more of its surfaces.

values.label: Hand wash only
values.definition: Product is meant to be washed by hand only.

values.label: Hard-sided
values.definition: The construction of the exterior or the sides of the item are rigid or hard as opposed to being soft (fabric).

values.label: Heated
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got a possibility to heat (e.g. heated toilet seat).

values.label: Heat Resistant
values.definition: Indicates that a product is heat resistant.

values.label: Height Adjustable
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is adjustable in height for e.g. a Electric Height Adjustable Desks, Height Adjustable A/V Steel Cart .

values.label: High Definition Copy Protection
values.definition: High Definition Copy Protection (HDCP) is a chip that descrambles a High Definition (HD) broadcast to allow one to watch HD broadcasts.

values.label: High Definition Ready
values.definition: The ability to receive a High Definition signal. The Television can show the required screen resolution and have the necessary connections to be able to show High Definition content.

values.label: Hood
values.definition: Code indicating the product has a hood.

values.label: Hot
values.definition: The product is designed to be used with or keep contents which are hot or heated. Example: Padded delivery bag, or beverage container.

values.label: HR Plus Glass
values.definition: Indicates whether the insulation of the glass is HR+.

values.label: HR Plus Plus Glass
values.definition: Indicates whether the insulation of the glass is HR++.

values.label: HR Plus Plus Plus Glass
values.definition: Indicates whether the insulation of the glass is HR+++.

values.label: Humidity Resistant
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is humidity resistant or moisture proof for example moisture resistant medium-density fibreboard (MDF).

values.label: Hydraulic
values.definition:
Indicates that a product  is hydraulic for e.g. a 2-Ton Hydraulic Trolley Jack,  
Timber Champ 7-Ton Electric Log Splitter, Hydraulic Bottle Jack.

values.label: Hypoallergenic
values.definition: A claim the product causes fewer allergic reactions than other ones.

values.label: Induction Cooktop Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable for induction hob or stove cooktop. In an induction cooktop a coil of copper wire is placed under the cooking pot and an alternating electric current is passed through it. The resulting oscillating magnetic field induces an electrical current in the pot.

values.label: Inflatable
values.definition: Indicates that a product is inflatable for example an Inflatable Round Kiddie Pool.

values.label: Instruments readable from multiple sides.
values.definition: Indicates whether the instruments of the product are readable from multiple sides.

values.label: Instruments readable from two sides.
values.definition: Indicates whether the instruments of the product are readable from two sides.

values.label: Insulated
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is insulated to protect against environmental factors such as cold, heat, etc..

values.label: Interconnectable
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be connected with other products for example lamps or smoke detectors.

values.label: Iron Cooktop Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable for iron cooktop hob or stove.

values.label: Ladder Included
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is delivered with a ladder.

values.label: Lamp Equipped
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is delivered with lamps/bulbs/illuminants.

values.label: Lighting Dimmer Switch
values.definition: Indicates whether a product has got a lighting dimmer switch.

values.label: Lightweight Construction
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is a lightweight construction use of lighter or smaller sized materials for e.g. a Lightweight climbing painted h frame scaffolding for construction.

values.label: Light Source Attached
values.definition: Indicates whether a light source is attached to the product.

values.label: Light Source Built In
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got a light source built in (e.g. mirror).

values.label: Limescale remover
values.definition: The product removes limescale, a hard white or grey substance that forms on the inside of pipes, taps and water containers or on tiles.

values.label: Lined
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is lined with a material for e.g. lined steel pipes.

values.label: Lockable
values.definition: Indicates that a product is lockable for example Chrome Plated Showcase Window Key Lock, Sliding Door Outside Pull with Key, Rolling Stacking Portable Metal Trolley Tool Box.

values.label: Machine Washable
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is washable in a washing-machine.

values.label: Magnetic
values.definition: The trade item has a magnetic ability to attach to other items.

values.label: Magnetic Closure
values.definition: Indicates that a product  has magnetic mechanism to shut or close.

values.label: Memory Card Reader
values.definition: A computer peripheral that is used to transfer the content of a memory card without the use of another device.

values.label: Metal feet
values.definition: Code indicating the presence of metal feet on a product.

values.label: Microwave Safe
values.definition: Indicates that the product is safe to use in a microwave oven. E.g. the consumer can put a microwave safe plate in a microwave to heat food.

values.label: Mounted Flange
values.definition: Indicates that a flange is mounted on the trade item. A flange is a part for sealing.

values.label: Night Vision
values.definition: Denotes devices that enhance night-time vision.

values.label: Noise Cancelling
values.definition: Active noise control (ANC), also known as noise cancellation, or active noise reduction (ANR), is a method for reducing unwanted sound by the addition of a second sound specifically designed to cancel the first.

values.label: Non comedogenic
values.definition: Non-Comedogenic Products don't clog pores & assist with breaking down excess oils.

values.label: Non-toxic
values.definition: Non-toxic items aren't poisonous. It's generally safe to eat or breathe non-toxic substances, and they don't harm the environment.

values.label: Nut Mount
values.definition: Indicates whether a product for example a vice has a nut mount to attach it to a workbench.

values.label: Oil Free
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is oil free, to eliminates the need for maintenance for example a Compressor.

values.label: On Screen Clock
values.definition: A clock visible on the screen.

values.label: On Screen Menu
values.definition: Interactive menus that come up when changing television set-up options such as brightness and contrast.

values.label: Opens from both sides.
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be mounted for right or left opening for example a door.

values.label: Opens from left side.
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be mounted for left opening only for example a door.

values.label: Opens from right side.
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be mounted for right opening only for example a door.

values.label: Oven
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is supplied with an oven.

values.label: Oven Safe
values.definition: Indicates that a product is safe and suitable to use in an oven.

values.label: Overrun Brake
values.definition: Indicates that a product has a overrun brake for e.g. a trailer for a boat has a baking mechanism to stop the trailer from hitting a vehicle.

values.label: Padded
values.definition: Indicates that a product  is padded is added material to protect or shape the trade item for e.g. a padded chair.

values.label: Parental Control
values.definition: Options that allow parents to monitor or limit what a child can see or do and/or time-limit these activities.

values.label: Parfocal Lens
values.definition: A parfocal lens is a lens that stays in focus when magnification/focal length is changed.

values.label: Pedestal Staircase
values.definition: Specifies whether the stairs has (a right angle) on a pedestal.

values.label: Permeable
values.definition:
Indicates that a product is permeable for e.g. permeable flooring, parquet, 
laminate, tiling.

values.label: Personalizable
values.definition: The item is can be personalized by the customer.

values.label: PH neutral
values.definition: pH neutral is when the product is neither acid nor alkaline. At a temperature of 25 °C a pH of 7 is neutral (e.g. pure water).

values.label: Picture Enhancement
values.definition: A brand owner enhancement to the picture quality which may be created by hardware, or software, or both.

values.label: Picture Viewing Capability
values.definition: The ability to view digital photographs via a digital card reader.

values.label: Pin Grounded
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is grounded by pin for example a plug with a hole for a ground pin as well as the tabs on the side.

values.label: Plant Based
values.definition: A plant-based diet or product is one consisting mostly or entirely derived from plants, including vegetables, grains, nuts, seeds, legumes and fruits, and with few or no animal products.

values.label: Polished
values.definition: Indicates that a product can be used for polishing, for example Polished Aluminium Wheel Cleaner, Polished Granite Cleaner and Resealer, Hard-Surface and Polished Concrete Concentrated Cleaner.

values.label: Portable
values.definition: Whether the trade item is capable of being travel enabled or easily portable to various locations.

values.label: Power Saving
values.definition: Indicates whether a product saves power/energy.

values.label: Pre-programmable
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be pre-programmed for example a programmable thermostat.

values.label: Protective Layer

values.label: Railing

values.label: Red Eye Reduction
values.definition: The item has red-eye reduction capabilities. The red-eye effect in photography is the common appearance of red pupils in colour photographs of eyes. It occurs when using a photographic flash very close to the camera lens (as with most compact cameras), in ambient low light. The effect appears in the eyes of humans and animals that have tapetum lucidum.

values.label: Refillable

values.label: Removable Flash

values.label: Battery Replacement
values.definition: Indicates whether a rechargeable battery in a product can be replaced e.g. in case of a Cordless Drywall Screwdriver.

values.label: Retractable Cord
values.definition: Indicates that the part of the item can be withdrawn into a holder or trade item, as in a cord or leash.

values.label: RFID Blocking
values.definition: The item is constructed in a way to prevent Radio Frequency Identification devices from penetrating through the item. This ensures that RFID embedded items inside can not be read through the item.

values.label: Risers
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has risers (e.g. stairs with steps and risers that fit into).

values.label: Rotatable
values.definition: Indicates whether a product is rotatable (able to be turned around on an axis).

values.label: Rotation or Turning Stop
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got a rotation stop or an activated turning stop for example a drill hammer with SDS-plus admission.

values.label: Safety Facilities
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got safety facilities for example guards on a grinder or safety features on gas installations.

values.label: Safe For Food Use
values.definition: Indicates that a product is suitable for food use. User can use the item for food preservation.

values.label: Saw Blade Replacement
values.definition: Indicates whether a saw blade can be replaced for example a reciprocating saw with a removable blade.

values.label: Scratch Resistant
values.definition: The trade item's material is strong enough to prevent scratches under certain conditions.

values.label: Self-levelling
values.definition: Indicates whether the product has got a functionality for self levelling for e.g. a self-levelling underlayment. Self levelling products have high flow characteristics and do not require the addition of excessive amounts of water for placement.

values.label: Self Timer Mechanism
values.definition: The trade item has a self timing mechanism, meaning trade item can operate independently for a set period of time.

values.label: Shock absorbing
values.definition: Indicates whether the product is shock absorbing at the ends or in general for example a handle axe with shock reduction grip.

values.label: Short Time Burning
values.definition: Indicate whether a furnace/oven is suitable for short-time burning.

values.label: Simultaneous Picture Teletext

values.label: Single lever mixer

values.label: Small Parts Holder

values.label: Soft Close Mechanism

values.label: Sound Levelling Capability

values.label: Spinner Wheels

values.label: Sprayable
values.definition: Indicates whether the product can be sprayed for example an MS-Polymer multi-texture sealer.

values.label: Stretch

values.label: Swivel Head

values.label: Tear Resistant

values.label: Temperature Limiter

values.label: Adolescent

values.label: Adult

values.label: Baby

values.label: Senior

values.label: Complementary
values.definition: A compound feed which has a high content of certain substances but which, by reason of its composition, is sufficient for a daily ration only if used in combination with other feed.

values.label: Complete

values.label: Compound

values.label: Feed Materials

values.label: Mineral

values.label: Penny Loafer
values.definition: Flat closed toe shoe with detailing on the top that allowed wearer to insert a coin on the top.

values.label: Platform
values.definition: Platform shoes are shoes, boots, or sandals with an obvious thick sole, which may also have a high heel.

values.label: Pumps
values.definition: Closed toe shoe with heel.

values.label: Rain Boots
values.definition: Waterproof footwear for wearing in the rain, usually pull on.

values.label: Riding Boots
values.definition: High boot styled to resemble boots used for equestrian activity.

values.label: Running
values.definition: Footwear for running or jogging.

values.label: Sandals
values.definition: Open toed shoe most often worn in the summer.

values.label: Slide
values.definition: Footwear with no back strap.

values.label: Sling Back
values.definition: Thin back strap footwear.

values.label: Slipper
values.definition: Footwear for use with sleepwear.

values.label: Smoking Slipper
values.definition: Casual often velvet footwear, appearing frequently with a crest or embroidery.

values.label: Sneaker
values.definition: Athletic style footwear.

values.label: Sneakers
values.definition: Athletic style footwear.

values.label: Snow Boots
values.definition: Shoes made to protect wearer from snow and slush.

values.label: Steel Toe
values.definition: Shoe with steel insert in the toe, designed to protect wearer in industrial situations.

values.label: Tennis
values.definition: Athletic shoe for tennis.

values.label: Thong
values.definition: Shoe with divider between big and second toe.

values.label: Walking
values.definition: Shoe designed for exercise walking.

values.label: Water Shoes
values.definition: Footwear for pool or ocean use.

values.label: Wingtip
values.definition: Shoe with toe cap of a full brogue is both perforated and serrated along its edges and includes additional decorative perforations in the centre of the toe cap.

values.label: Ball
values.definition: A product formed or naturally the shape of a ball(s). Example: Cotton balls, bath ball, etc.

values.label: Balm
values.definition: A balm is a soothing substance with a consistency somewhere between solid and liquid.

values.label: Bar
values.definition: A rectangular solid piece or block of something.

values.label: Bath Salt
values.definition: Bath salts are water-soluble, pulverized minerals that are added to water to be used for bathing.

values.label: Beads
values.definition: Tiny beads or pearls that are designed to dissolve in water or by hot air that enables the product abilities to be performed. Examples: Clothes Freshener, Bath skin softener.

values.label: Brew bag
values.definition: Refers to various types of bags used for brewing beverages, particularly tea or coffee.

values.label: Brew pad/pod
values.definition: Refer to a disposable filter pad that holds the tea leaves or coffee grounds.

values.label: Butter (Cosmetics)
values.definition: Butters are a class of materials that have a melting point between 20-40.5°C. Partial hydrogenation of soybean oil results in a waxy butter. Partial hydrogenation can result in formation of trans esters, due to the presence of the hydrogenation catalyst.

values.label: Capsule
values.definition: A capsule is a shell or a container prepared from gelatin containing one or more medicinal and/or inert substances.

values.label: Chewing Gum
values.definition: Chewing gum is a soft, cohesive substance designed in order to be chewed without being swallowed.

values.label: Clay
values.definition: Clays are a soft, loose, earthy material mainly found in mineral clay deposits that lay on or just below the surface of the Earth. Clays have the ability to exfoliate, absorb excess oils, cleanse dirt and impurities and invigorate the skin.

values.label: Concentrate
values.definition: Concentrates contain three times as much active ingredients as a cream, in the highest possible concentration. Through the high concentration of active substances they unfold their effects even in the deepest layers of the skin.

values.label: Cotton wool bud
values.definition: A cotton wool bud or swab is a short spindle with one or both ends coated with an absorbent cotton/wool padding.

values.label: Cotton wool pad
values.definition: Cotton wool pads are pads made of cotton which are used for medical or cosmetic purposes.

values.label: Cotton wool pleat
values.definition: Cotton wool pleat is made from cotton making it super soft and absorbent. Ideal for gently cleansing , skincare and beauty needs. The pleat is usually perforated.

values.label: Cream
values.definition: This term is used to describe cream which contains equal parts water and oil.

values.label: Crystal
values.definition: Crystals are made of natural mineral salt called potassium alum , which has been shown to have antimicrobial properties.

values.label: Cushion
values.definition: A cushion is a liquid formula housed in a sponge-like cushion

values.label: Emulsion
values.definition: An emulsion is a mixture of two or more liquids that are normally immiscible (unmixable or unblendable).

values.label: Flakes
values.definition: Flakes are designed to dissolve in water or by hot air that enables the product abilities to be performed. Examples: bathing soaps, several soaps used in washing machines.

values.label: Gas/Gaseous
values.definition: A substance without a constant volume which evaporates after leaving its container. Examples are air fresheners.

values.label: Gel
values.definition: This term is used to describe gel, which is a colloid in which solids are dispersed in a liquid medium.

values.label: Granules
values.definition: A small compact particle of a substance.

values.label: Gum/Putty
values.definition: Gum/Putty is a material with high plasticity, similar in texture to clay or dough.

values.label: Impregnated pad
values.definition: A pad that is impregnated with a substance that provides the function the product produces.

values.label: Interfolded sheet
values.definition: A sheet is interfolded with the proceeding sheet so that it can dispense easily for the consumer.

values.label: Liquid
values.definition: A substance that flows freely but is of constant volume.

values.label: Lotion
values.definition: A liquid multi-ingredient topical application usually containing a cleansing, moisturising or astringent agent.

values.label: Mask - Absorb
values.definition: A product applied to the part of the body that is absorbed by the body.

values.label: Mask - Peel off
values.definition: A product applied to the part of the body that is peeled off.

values.label: Mask - Sheet
values.definition: A product applied to the part of the body that is laid on the body and removed after desired effect.

values.label: Mask - Wash out
values.definition: A product applied to the part of the body that can be washed away.

values.label: Milk (Cosmetics)
values.definition: A cosmetic or soap product containing natural milk proteins in the form of micelles formed by the addition of calcium to an aqueous solution of casein. These micelles give the product light reflection properties analogous to those produced by the addition of a natural milk.

values.label: Mist
values.definition: A cloud of tiny liquid droplets suspended in the air.

values.label: Mousse/Foam
values.definition: An aerosol foam made of very small bubbles to apply to skin, hair, etc.

values.label: Oil
values.definition: A liquid preparation used on the hair or skin as a cosmetic.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Paste
values.definition: A thick, soft, moist substance typically produced by mixing dry ingredients with a liquid.

values.label: Patch
values.definition: An adhesive patch that is placed on the body to deliver a specific dose or achieve a certain result through the skin.

values.label: Powder
values.definition: Fine, dry particles produced by the grinding, crushing, or disintegration of a solid substance.

values.label: Powder - Compact/Pressed
values.definition: Pressed powders are pressed into a compact: Primarily used to set liquid foundation/concealer so that the makeup lasts longer and does not move around, or rub off of your skin.

values.label: Powder - Loose
values.definition: Loose powders are more finely milled so they contain less oils, and are typically used on oily skin types to control the oil your face develops throughout the day.

values.label: Roll
values.definition: The product is rolled either on a tube or without.

values.label: Salt
values.definition: Salts are packed with minerals like potassium, magnesium, and calcium that can help to reduce inflammation, brighten, and even strengthen the skin.

values.label: Serum
values.definition: Serums are skin care products that are designed to deliver high concentrations of specific active ingredients to the designated part of the body.

values.label: Soap
values.definition: A substance used with water for washing and cleaning, made of a compound of natural oils or fats with sodium hydroxide or another strong alkali, and typically having perfume and coloring added.

values.label: Solid
values.definition: Firm and stable in shape; not liquid or fluid.

values.label: Sponge
values.definition: A piece of a soft, light, porous substance originally consisting of the fibrous skeleton of an invertebrate but now usually made of synthetic material. Sponges absorb liquid and are used for washing and cleaning.

values.label: Spray
values.definition: Liquid that is blown or driven through the air in the form of tiny drops.

values.label: Stick
values.definition: A trade item is referred to as a "stick" if the solid item has been cut or formed in to individual strips. Even in the stick state the item is still a solid product. Specifically excludes products which may appear as a stick but are classified as strings.

values.label: Strip
values.definition: A plastic or other material may be abrasive to remove or take away to create a desired effect. Made from metal or plastic, these thin strips have an abrasive side that can be used for interproximal reduction, contouring or finishing the restoration.

values.label: Tablet
values.definition: A small disk or cylinder of a compressed solid substance, typically a measured amount of a medicine or drug.

values.label: Wax
values.definition: Any of various substances resembling the wax of bees.

values.label: Wipe
values.definition: A disposable cloth treated with a cleansing agent or other function, for wiping things clean or applying the product.

values.definition: GPPS_2DOT0

values.definition: Code value not available in code list.

values.definition: RECIPE

values.definition: TRACI

values.definition: CTU Per Functional Unit

values.definition: Kilograms 1 4 DB equivalent per functional unit.

values.definition: The Depth of the Shelf Ready Package (SRP) as determined by the GS1 non-consumer unit dimension rules for the orientation of the package in the GS1 Standard Measurement Rules.

values.label: Depth or Width
values.definition: Depth or width of the Shelf Ready Package (SRP) as determined by the GS1 non-consumer unit dimension rules for the orientation of the package in the GS1 Standard Measurement Rules.

values.label: Width
values.definition: The width of the Shelf Ready Package (SRP) as determined by the GS1 non-consumer unit dimension rules for the orientation of the package in the GS1 Standard Measurement Rules.
