values.definition: Grams Per Cubic Centimetre: Grams Per Cubic Centimetre

values.label: Microlitre
values.definition: Microlitre: A microlitre is one millionth of a litre

values.label: Micrometre
values.definition: Micrometre: A micrometre is one millionth of a metre, also termed Micron.

values.label: Net kilogram
values.definition: Net kilogram: A unit of mass defining the total number of kilograms after deductions.

values.label: Part per million
values.definition: Part per million: A unit of proportion equal to 10-6 (ppm).

values.label: Batch
values.definition: Batch: A unit of count defining the number of batches (batch: quantity of material produced in one operation or number of animals or persons coming at once).

values.label: Year
values.definition: Year: Unit of time equal to 365,25 days.

values.label: Troy Ounce or Apothecary Ounce
values.definition: Troy ounce or apothecary ounce: The troy ounce is a unit of imperial measure. In the present day it is most commonly used to gauge the weight and therefore the price of precious metals.  One troy ounce equals 480 grains or 31.1035 grams.

values.label: Assortment
values.definition: Assortment: A unit of count defining the number of assortments (assortment: set of items grouped in a mixed collection).

values.label: Base box
values.definition: Base box: A unit of area of 112 sheets of tin mil products (tin plate, tin free steel or black plate) 14 by 20 inches, or 31,360 square inches.

values.label: Board Foot
values.definition: Board Foot: A specialized unit of measure for the volume of rough lumber (before drying and planing with no adjustments) or planed/surfaced lumber. It is the volume of a one-foot length of a board one foot wide and one inch thick. Some countries utilize the synonym super foot or superficial foot.

values.label: Barrel US
values.definition: Barrel US: There are varying standards for barrel for some specific commodities, including 31 gal for beer, 40 gal for whiskey or kerosene, and 42 gal for petroleum. The general standard for liquids is 31.5 gal or half a hogshead; the general standard for dry contents is 7,056 Cubic Inches.

values.label: Hundred board Foot
values.definition: Hundred board foot: A unit of volume equal to one hundred board foot.

values.label: British Thermal Unit
values.definition: British thermal unit: The British thermal unit (BTU or Btu) is a traditional unit of energy. It is approximately the amount of energy needed to heat one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit. One Btu is equal to about 1.06 kilojoules. It is used in the power, steam generation, heating and air conditioning industries.

values.label: Bushel (US)
values.definition: Bushel (US): A bushel is an imperial and U.S. customary unit of dry volume, equivalent in each of these systems to 4 pecks or 8 gallons. It is used for volumes of dry commodities (not liquids), most often in agriculture

values.label: Bushel (UK)
values.definition: Bushel (UK): A bushel is an imperial and U.S. customary unit of dry volume, equivalent in each of these systems to 4 pecks or 8 gallons. It is used for volumes of dry commodities (not liquids), most often in agriculture

values.label: Millimole
values.definition: Millimole: a millimole is one thousandth of a mole.

values.label: Millisecond
values.definition: Millisecond: A millisecond (from milli- and second; abbreviation: ms) is a thousandth (1/1000) of a second.

values.label: Centigram
values.definition: Centigram: A centigram is one hundredth (1/100) of a gram

values.label: Centilitre
values.definition: Centilitre: A centilitre is one hundredth (1/100) of a litre

values.label: Square Centimetre
values.definition: Square centimetre: A square centimetre is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 centimetre in length.

values.label: Cubic Centimetre
values.definition: Cubic centimetre: A cubic centimetre is the volume of a cube of side length one centimetre (0.01 m) equal to a millilitre.

values.label: Centimetre
values.definition: Centimetre: A centimetre is  equal to one hundredth of a metre.

values.label: Hundred pound (cwt) / hundred weight (US)
values.definition: Hundred pound (cwt) / hundred weight (US): A unit of weight in the U.S. Customary System equal to 100 pounds (45.36 kilograms); also called cental.

values.label: Hundred weight (UK)
values.definition: Hundred weight (UK):  A unit of weight in the British Imperial System equal to 112 pounds (50.80 kilograms); also called quintal.

values.label: Terajoule
values.definition: Terajoule: A terajoule is 10¹² joules

values.label: Terawatt Hour
values.definition: Terawatt hour: A terawatt hour is 109 * kilowat hour or 3.6 petajoules.

values.label: Calorie - International Table (IT)
values.definition: This code is being DEPRECATED. Use code E14 Kilocalorie to express food calories. Calorie - International Table (IT): A calorie is 1/100 of the amount of energy required to warm one gram of air-free water from 0 °C to 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure; this is about 4.190 J.  Its use is archaic, having been replaced by the SI unit of energy, the joule. However, in many countries it remains in common use as a unit of food energy. In the context of nutrition, and especially food labeling, the calorie is approximately equal to 4.1868 joules (J), and energy values are normally quoted in kilojoules (kJ) and kilocalories (kcal).

values.label: Days
values.definition: Days: A day is one three hundreds and sixty fifth (1/365) of a year

values.label: Decigram
values.definition: Decigram: A decigram is one tenth (1/10) of a gram.

values.label: Decilitre
values.definition: Decilitre: A decilitre is one tenth (1/10) of a litre.

values.label: Square decimetre
values.definition: Square decimetre: A square deciimetre is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 deciimetre in length.

values.label: Cubic decimetre
values.definition: Cubic decimetre: A cubic decimetre is the volume of a cube of side length one decimetre (0.1 m)

values.label: Decimetre
values.definition: Decimetre: A decimetre is  equal to one tenth of a metre.

values.label: Dram (US)
values.definition: Dram (US): The dram (archaic spelling drachm) was historically both a coin and a weight. Currently it is both a small mass in the Apothecaries' system of weights and a small unit of volume. This unit is called more correctly fluid dram or in contraction also fluidram. The term also refers to the fluid dram, a measure of capacity equal 1⁄8 of a fluid ounce, which means it is exactly equal to 3.696 691 195 312 5 mL in the United States.

values.label: Dram (UK)
values.definition: Dram (UK): The dram (archaic spelling drachm) was historically both a coin and a weight. Currently it is both a small mass in the Apothecaries' system of weights and a small unit of volume. This unit is called more correctly fluid dram or in contraction also fluidram. The fluid dram is defined as 1⁄8 of a fluid ounce, which means it is exactly equal to 3.551 632 812 500 0 mL in the Commonwealth and Ireland. In England dram came to mean a small draught of cordial or alcohol; hence the term dram-house for the taverns where one could purchase a dram.

values.label: Dozen
values.definition: Dozen: A unit of count defining the number of units in multiples of 12.

values.label: Kilocalorie (international table)
values.definition: Kilocalorie (international table): A unit of energy equal to 1000 calories.

values.label: Dose
values.definition: Dose: A unit of count defining the number of doses (dose: a definite quantity of a medicine or drug).

values.label: Gross kilogram
values.definition: Gross kilogram: A unit of mass defining the total number of kilograms before deductions.

values.label: Use
values.definition: Use: A unit of count defining the number of times an object is used.

values.label: Each
values.definition: Each: A unit of count defining the number of items regarded as separate units.

values.label: Micromole
values.definition: Micromole: One millionth (10 -6 ) of a mole.

values.label: Foot
values.definition: Foot: The international foot is defined to be equal to 0.3048 meters.

values.label: Square Foot
values.definition: Square foot: A square foot is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 foot in length.

values.label: Cubic Foot
values.definition: Cubic foot: A cubic foot is the volume of a cube of side length one foot (0.3048 m) .

values.label: Peck
values.definition: Peck: A peck is an imperial and U.S. customary unit of dry volume, equivalent in each of these systems to 2 gallons, 8 dry quarts, or 16 dry pints.

values.label: Tablespoon
values.definition: Tablespoon: Tablespoon. 1/2 fluid ounces, 3 teaspoons, 15 millilitres

values.label: Teaspoon
values.definition: Teaspoon: Teaspoon. 1/6 fluid ounces or  5 millilitres

values.label: Gallon (UK)
values.definition: Gallon (UK): The imperial (UK) gallon was legally defined as 4.54609 litres.

values.label: Gallon (US)
values.definition: Gallon (US): The U.S. liquid gallon is legally defined as 231 cubic inches, and is equal to exactly 3.785411784 litres or about 0.133680555 cubic feet.

values.label: Gram Per Square Metre
values.definition: "Gram per square metre: In the metric system, the density of all types of paper, paperboard, and fabric, is expressed in terms of grams per square meter (g/m²).  This quantity is commonly called grammage both in English and French (ISO 536), though many English-speaking countries still refer to the "weight". The term density here is used somewhat incorrectly, as density is mass by volume. More precisely, it is a measure of the area density, areal density, or surface density."

values.label: Gram:
values.definition: Gram: A gram is defined as one one-thousandth of the kilogram (1×10-3 kg).

values.label: Grain
values.definition: Grain: A grain or troy grain is precisely 64.79891 milligrams. Exactly 7,000 grains per avoirdupois pound.

values.label: Gross
values.definition: Gross: A unit of count defining the number of units in multiples of 144 (12 x 12).

values.label: Gigawatt Hour
values.definition: Gigawatt hour: A gigaawatt hour is 109 kilowat hour or 3.6 terajoules.

values.label: Piece
values.definition: Piece: A unit of count defining the number of pieces (piece: a single item, article or exemplar).

values.label: Hundred Count
values.definition: Hundred count: A unit of count defining the number of units counted in multiples of 100.

values.label: Half Dozen
values.definition: Half dozen: A unit of count defining the number of units in multiplt of six (6).

values.label: Hectogram
values.definition: Hectogram: A hectogram is one hundred (100) grams

values.label: Hectolitre
values.definition: Hectolitre: A hectolitre is one hundred (100) litres.

values.label: Hour
values.definition: Hour: An hour is a unit of measurement of time of the duration of 60 minutes, or 3600 seconds. It is 1/24 of a median Earth day.

values.label: Inches
values.definition: Inches: An international inch is defined to be equal to 25.4 millimeters.

values.label: Square Inch
values.definition: Square inch: A square inch is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 inch in length.

values.label: Cubic Inch
values.definition: Cubic inch: A cubic inch is the volume of a cube of side length one inch (0.254 m).

values.label: Joule
values.definition: Joule: A joule is the energy exerted by a force of one newton acting to move an object through a distance of one metre.

values.label: Kilolitre
values.definition: Kilolitre: A kilolitre is one thousand (1000) litres.

values.label: Kilogram
values.definition: Kilogram: A unit of mass equal to one thousand grams.

values.label: Kilojoule
values.definition: Kilojoule: A kilojoule is 1000 joules

values.label: Kilometre
values.definition: Kilometre: A kilometre is one thousand (1000) metres

values.label: Kit
values.definition: Kit: A unit of count defining the number of kits (kit: tub, barrel or pail).

values.label: Kilowatt Hour
values.definition: Kilowatt hour: A kilowatt hour is a unit of energy equal to 3.6 megajoules. It is also a common commercial unit of electric energy representing the amount of energy delivered at a rate of 1,000 watts over a period of one hour.

values.label: Kilowatt
values.definition: Kilowatt: A kilowatt is one thousand (1000) watts

values.label: Pound
values.definition: Pound: The international avoirdupois pound of exactly 0.45359237 kilogram.

values.label: Linear Foot
values.definition: Linear foot: A unit of count defining the number of feet (12-inch) in length of a uniform width object.

values.label: Link
values.definition: Link: A unit of distance equal to 0.01 chain.

values.label: Linear Metre
values.definition: Linear metre: A unit of count defining the number of metres in length of a uniform width object.

values.label: Layer
values.definition: Layer: A unit of count defining the number of layers.

values.label: Ton (UK) or long ton (US)
values.definition: Ton (UK) or long ton (US): Ton (UK) = 1016 Kg or 2240 Lb.

values.label: Litre
values.definition: Litre: A litre is defined as a special name for a cubic decimetre (1 L = 1 dm3 = 1000 cm3).

values.label: Megawatt
values.definition: Megawatt: A unit of power defining the rate of energy transferred or consumed when a current of 1000 amperes flows due to a potential of 1000 volts at unity power factor.

values.label: Microgram
values.definition: Microgram: A microgram is one millionth of a gram (0.000001)

values.label: Milligram
values.definition: Milligram: A milligram is one thousandth of a gram (0.001)

values.label: Square mile
values.definition: Square mile: A square mile is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 mile in length.

values.label: Minute (unit of time)
values.definition: Minute (unit of time): A minute is a unit of time equal to 1/60th of an hour or 60 seconds

values.label: Millilitre
values.definition: Millilitre: A millilitre is one thousandth of a litre (0.001)

values.label: Square millimetre
values.definition: Square millimetre: A square millimetre is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 millimetre in length.

values.label: Cubic millimetre
values.definition: Cubic millimetre: A cubic millimetre is the volume of a cube of side length one milliimetre (0.001 m)

values.label: Millimetre
values.definition: Millimetre: A millimetre is one thousandth of a metre (0.001)

values.label: Month: Unit of time equal to 1/12 of a year of 365,25 days
values.definition: Month: Unit of time equal to 1/12 of a year of 365,25 days

values.label: Square Metre
values.definition: Square metre: A square metre is an area of a square whose sides are exactly 1 metre in length.

values.label: Cubic metre
values.definition: Cubic metre: A cubic metre is the volume of a cube of side length one metre.

values.label: Metre
values.definition: Metre: The metre is the basic unit of length in the International System of Units (SI).

values.label: Megawatt Hour
values.definition: Megawatt hour (1000 kW.h): A unit of energy defining the total amount of bulk energy transferred or consumed.

values.label: Load
values.definition: Load: A unit of volume defining the number of loads (load: a quantity of items carried or processed at one time).

values.label: Ounces Per Square Yard
values.definition: Ounces per square yard: The weight of one square yard of the material expressed in ounces.  Commonly used to express the density or weight of all types of paper, paperboard, and fabric, e.g. 20 OZ or 20 weight denim has an area density of 20 oz/yd2. The term density here is used somewhat incorrectly, as density is mass by volume. More precisely, it is a measure of the area density, areal density, or surface density.

values.label: Ounce
values.definition: Ounce:  A unit of mass with several definitions, the most commonly used of which are equal to approximately 30 grams

values.label: Fluid ounce (US)
values.definition: Fluid ounce (US): A fluid ounce (US) is equal to one sixteenth (1/16) of a US pint or   29.5735295625 millilitres.

values.label: Fluid ounce (UK)
values.definition: Fluid ounce (UK): A fluid ounce (UK) is equal to one thirtieth (1/30) of a UK pint or 28.4130625 millilitres.

values.label: Percent:
values.definition: Percent: A unit of proportion equal to 0.01.

values.label: Pad
values.definition: Pad: A unit of count defining the number of pads (pad: block of paper sheets fastened together at one end).

values.label: Pair
values.definition: Pair: A unit of count defining the number of pairs (pair: item described by two's).

values.label: Dry Pint (US)
values.definition: Dry Pint (US): The United States dry pint is equal one eighth of a US dry gallon or one half US dry quarts. It is used in the United States but is not as common as the liquid pint.

values.label: Pint (UK)
values.definition: Pint (UK): A pint (UK) is equal to 1/8 Gallon (UK); used primarily as a measure for beer and cider when sold by the glass.

values.label: Liquid pint (US)
values.definition: Liquid pint (US): The US liquid pint is equal one eighth of a United States liquid gallon.

values.label: Page - Hardcopy
values.definition: Page - hardcopy: A unit of count defining the number of hardcopy pages (hardcopy page: a page rendered as printed or written output on paper, film, or other permanent medium).

values.label: Quart (US dry)
values.definition: Quart (US dry): A US dry quart is equal to 1/32 of a US bushel, exactly 1.101220942715 litres.

values.label: Liquid quart (US)
values.definition: Liquid quart (US): A US liquid quart exactly equals 57.75 cubic inches, which is exactly equal to 0.946352946 litres.

values.label: Second (unit of time)
values.definition: Second (unit of time): A second is a unit of time equal to 1/60th of a minute.

values.label: Set
values.definition: Set: A unit of count defining the number of sets (set: a number of objects grouped together).

values.label: Mile (statute mile)
values.definition: Mile (statute mile): A statute mile of 5,280 feet (exactly 1,609.344 meters).

values.label: Serving

values.label: Zero Suppressed GTIN
values.definition: The Zero-Suppressed identifier, also called a "Zero Suppressed UPC", is a compressed GTIN-12 (6-digits plus a check digit). values.label: HID (High intensity discharge)
values.definition: High Intensity Discharge (HID) is an overarching term for a gas-discharge light. HID lamps produce light by sending an electrical charge or “arc” between two tungsten electrical conductors (electrodes) and through an ionized gas (also known as “plasma”) which is housed inside the bulb.

values.label: High pressure sodium
values.definition: High pressure sodium light is a specific type of gas- discharge light (also known as a high intensity discharge, HID or arc light). The arc tube is made of aluminum oxide and the sodium metal is combined with several other elements like mercury which counter-balances the yellow glow with some white to light emissions.

values.label: LED (Light Emitting Diode)
values.definition: Light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor device that emits light when current flows through it. Electrons in the semiconductor recombine with electron holes, releasing energy in the form of photons.

values.label: Metal halide
values.definition: Metal halide light device produces light by an electric arc through a gaseous mixture of vaporized mercury and metal halides.

values.label: Intensive tint (level 3)
values.definition: Lasts about 6 to 8 weeks. Penetrates deeper into the hair and contains weak developers (hydrogen peroxide) that store the colour pigments in the hair, but cannot completely lighten the hair. E.g., semi-permanent colourations or glossings.

values.label: Permanent colouration (level 4)
values.definition: Permanent dyeing that does not wash out. Penetrates deep into the hair structure and changes the natural pigments through chemical reactions. This often uses ammonia or a similar alkalizing agent that opens the cuticle and hydrogen peroxide to lighten or prepare the hair. Does not wash out, needs to grow out or be refreshed by re-dyeing. E.g., classic hair dyes for a permanent change.

values.label: Temporary colouration (level 1)
values.definition: Lasts until the next hair wash. This type of colour only lays on the outer layer of the hair (cuticle) and does not penetrate the inside of the hair. E.g., colour sprays, chalk or foam colourations.

values.label: Washable colouration / tinting (level 2)
values.definition: About 6 to 10 washes. Penetrates easily into the cuticle, but not deep into the hair. Gradually fades without leaving visible roots. E.g., easily washable tints or foam tints.

values.label: Anti-baldness treatment
values.definition: Product to prevent or slow the progression of baldness.

values.label: Anti-dandruff
values.definition: Used to treat or prevent dandruff. Example anti-dandruff shampoo

values.label: Anti-dry treatment
values.definition: Product to hydrate something that is dry.

values.label: Anti-frizz
values.definition: Product design to reduce frizzy hair. Frizz is hair that does not align with the surrounding hairs, but stands up or curls independently, creating a fuzzy or irregular texture.

values.label: Applied heat protection
values.definition: A heat protectant adds moisture to your hair while forming a protective barrier that reduces moisture loss when heat is applied to your hair shafts.

values.label: Cleansing
values.definition: A product that cleans your hair from dirt, oil, etc. as stated by the product.

values.label: Colour preservation
values.definition: A product to preserve the longevity of the colour, to keep the desired colour intact.

values.label: Combing/Detangler
values.definition: A product for removing tangles from hair.

values.label: Conditioner
values.definition: Conditioner is a hair care product used to improve the feel, appearance and manageability of hair.

values.label: Curl
values.definition: A product that adds curl to hair.

values.label: Daily care
values.definition: A hair care routine for daily use that everyone should follow to keep their hair healthy.

values.label: Discipline
values.definition: A product that controls unruly strands by aligning them into place which assists in managing styles throughout wear time.

values.label: Exfoliate
values.definition: A product that sloughs off dead skin cells on the scalp, promoting healthier growth cycles and rejuvenating follicle activity.

values.label: Glosser
values.definition: A treatment adds noticeable shine to the hair, and can also dip into the cuticle to deposit color and prevent your newly-added hair dye from falling dull.

values.label: Hold
values.definition: A product to apply to a  person's hair to keep it in place.

values.label: Hair loss prevention
values.definition: A hair care benefit aimed at reducing the rate of hair shedding and strengthening the follicles to maintain healthy hair density.

values.label: Moisturising
values.definition: The process of using butters and oils to coat the OUTER surface of the hair fiber sealing and locking down the hair shaft so moisture can not get in or out of the fiber.

values.label: Provide more shine
values.definition: A product that imparts a reflective sheen to the surface of hair strands for an enhanced lustrous finish that catches light beautifully.

values.label: Natural effect
values.definition: A product that enhances the hair's inherent texture and appearance without visible signs of product use, promoting a healthy, effortless look.

values.label: Nourishing
values.definition: A hair product that provides nutrition, vitamin replacement, or moisturising, for general hair care, damaged and colour treated hair.

values.label: Oil reduction
values.definition: A product to reduce oil from scalp and hair as the result of the oil (sebaceous) glands in the scalp producing large amounts of oil.

values.label: Repair

values.label: Wet look

values.label: High fixation
values.definition: Describes a product that has high effect on the hair. It is suitable for strong and stubborn hair with a tendency to frizz.

values.label: Light fixation
values.definition: Describes a product that has very little effect on the hair. It is mostly suitable for fixing fine hair.

values.label: Maximum fixation
values.definition: Describes a product that ensures maximum fixation of the hairstyle. It is suitable for use for social event hairstyles that require long-term fixation of not only fine but also very stiff (unyielding) hair.

values.label: Medium fixation
values.definition: Describes a product that has little effect on the hair. It is mostly suitable for fixing fine hair.

values.label: Very high fixation
values.definition: Describes a product that has very high effect on the hair. It is suitable for strong and stubborn hair with a tendency to frizz.

values.label: Beanie

values.label: Beret
values.definition: Round flattish cap of felt or cloth. This style is inclusive of Tams (a Scottish style of beret cap).

values.label: Boater
values.definition: Stiff straw hat, often with a band; considered to be somewhat formal. Also known as skimmer.

values.label: Bonnet
values.definition: Hat tied under the chin, typically with a brim framing the face.

values.label: Bowler
values.definition: A man's hard felt hat with a round, dome-shaped crown.

values.label: Chef's toque hat
values.definition: A tall, white hat with a pleated crown, associated with professional chefs.

values.label: Cloche
values.definition: A bell-shaped woman's hat associated with the 1920s, often featuring a small visor or brim.

values.label: Cowboy
values.definition: Hat with a broad, often curled, brim and a high crown associated with cowboys. Also known as western.

values.label: Fascinator hat
values.definition: A formal, small, ornamental hat, sometimes referred to as a cocktail hat, affixed to the head by a comb, barette, or clip.

values.label: Fedora
values.definition: Hat with a soft brim and indented crown.

values.label: Fez
values.definition: A stiff, clyndrical, brimless, peakless hat named for the Moroccon city of Fez, often featuring a tassel at its crown.

values.label: Flat cap
values.definition: Originating from Ireland and England, the flat cap is referred to as a "driving cap," "scally cap," "paddy cap," "bunnet," or "cheese cutter," in various places around the world. Commonly made of wool, the fabric of the top of the flat cap is either sewn or attached with a snap to the front of a short, stiff visor.

values.label: Hard hat
values.definition: A protective hat commonly used in the construction industry.

values.label: Homburg
values.definition: A man's hat featuring a wide hatband, an upturned, ribbon-bound brim, and a "gutter" creasing the middle of its crown.

values.label: Jockey cap
values.definition: A cloth hat with a visor, associated with horse riding.

values.label: Mariner's cap
values.definition: Also known as a Greek fisherman's cap, this flat-topped cap features a twist of cord above the visor.

values.label: Newsboy
values.definition: Rounded cap with a small stiff brim in front.

values.label: Panama
values.definition: A wide-brimmed hat of straw-like material, originally made from the leaves of a particular tropical palm tree, worn chiefly by men.

values.label: Pork pie
values.definition: A round, formal hat with a flat top, circular indent, and a short, rolled brim, often associated with 1940s jazz music.

values.label: Rain hood
values.definition: A waterproof hood that may or may not include some coverage of the user's shoulders.

values.label: Santa cap
values.definition: A soft, peaked cap associated with Santa Claus featuring a pom affixed to its peak with a matching trim. Traditionally red with white pom and brim, these hats are made in a variety of colors. This style includes "elf" hats, which are similar to Santa caps, but often are green, have an ornamented brim, and no pom at the cap's peak.

values.label: Sombrero
values.definition: A wide-brimmed hat of woven straw associated with Mexico.

values.label: Sun hat
values.definition: A hat designed to protect from the sun's rays.

values.label: Top hat
values.definition: A formal, tall-crowned, flat-topped formal hat with a round brim. Opera hats (top hats with a collapsible crown) also fall into this style.

values.label: Trapper
values.definition: A hat with a shearling interior and ear flaps.

values.label: Tricorne
values.definition: The tricorne is a three-sided hat whose brim is folded up against a rounded crown. Sometimes referred to as a "pirate hat," the tricorne has a modern association with pirate costuming, as well as an historical association with maritime and 18th and 19th-century military uniforms. Two-sided (or "bicorne," a shape associated with the Napoleonic era) novelty hats bearing the skull-and-crossbones may be included here.

values.label: Trilby
values.definition: Similar to the fedora, but with a smaller, "stingy" brim that is folded up in the back and turned straight in the front, the trilby often features a hat band and has been associated with musicians such as Frank Sinatra and Jason Mraz.

values.label: Turban
values.definition: A type of headwear consisting of a cloth winding. Turbans have an association with traditions of many religions and cultures in the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, the Arabian Peninsula, the Middle East, Central Asia, North Africa, West Africa, and East Africa.

values.label: Visor
values.definition: Headwear featuring a brim. Visors fit around the head, but have no covering at the top.

values.label: Rinse aid
values.definition: Rinse aids contain chemicals called surfactants, which lower the surface tension of water. This helps to remove the water from your dishes in the dishwashing machine and make them dry faster.

values.label: Scouring cleaner

values.label: Out of packaging
values.definition: The image is of the product out of its packaging (i.e., the product as it first arrives “out of packaging” not how it appears after it has been processed or prepared).

values.label: In packaging
values.definition: The image is of the product in its packaging.

values.label: Case
values.definition: The image is of the product in its case as it would appear to the operator upon delivery.

values.label: Innerpack
values.definition: The image is of the product as it would appear inside its packaging inside the case.

values.label: Raw/uncooked
values.definition: The image is of the product which has not been cooked or processed or that needs to be cooked or further prepared.

values.label: Prepared
values.definition: The image is of the product which has been taken from a raw or uncooked state to a cooked state according to the appropriate method of preparation (e.g., baked, fried, grilled or boiled).

values.label: Plated
values.definition: The image is of the product which is prepared food arranged simply on a serving plate, dish or bowl for better visibility. May include an additional step, such as garnishing, icing, seasoning or other enhancement.

values.label: Styled
values.definition: The image is of the product which is carefully and artfully arranged for an attractive visual presentation, and designed to suggest the taste, aroma and appeal of the actual dish. May include complementary items (e.g., an entrée and sides) to present the impression of a complete meal. May also include an additional step, such as garnishing, icing, seasoning or other enhancement. May be presented with different backgrounds and at different angles.

values.label: Staged
values.definition: The image is of the product which has been arranged for display in such a way as to provide clear visibility. The product may be propped up if necessary for optimum viewing, but it should not be held or used in any way by a person.

values.label: Held
values.definition: The image is of the product which has been held out for display by one hand or a pair of hands. When relevant, proper grip should be demonstrated. Apart from the hands and forearms, no part of the person holding the item should be visible.

values.label: Worn
values.definition: The image is of the product, such as a protective item or article of clothing, which is worn by a person. The complete product should be visible inside the frame, but the individual wearing it should be cropped out as much as possible.

values.label: Used
values.definition: The image is of the product as it is meant to be used in its appropriate environment. Small utensils may be held in a hand or hands and used for their intended purpose.

values.label: Family
values.definition: The image is of the product which is a number of related products (e.g., matched sets, place settings) arranged together in a single picture.

values.label: Open Case
values.definition: The image is of the product which is a case, flaps open, that shows how the product(s) would look when an operator receives the product and opens the case.

values.label: Not applicable
values.definition: The image state is not applicable for this image.

values.label: Pallet/Display
values.definition: The image is of the product which is a pallet/display.

values.label: Formed
values.definition: The image is of the product which has the supporting shape/form (for example a model, mannequin, hanger) removed to give the product a 3-D look.

values.label: Delivered at Frontier

values.label: Delivered Duty Paid

values.label: Delivered Duty Unpaid

values.label: Delivered Ex Quay

values.label: Delivered Ex Ship
values.definition: The risk is transferred when the goods have been effectively put at the disposal of the buyer on board the ship at the port of destination. Insurance to be covered by the seller.

values.label: ExWorks
values.definition: The risk is transferred when the goods are put at the disposal of the buyer according to the terms of the agreement. Insurance to be covered by the buyer.

values.label: Free Alongside Ship
values.definition: The risk is transferred when the goods have been effectively delivered alongside the ship at the named port of shipment. Insurance to be covered by the buyer.

values.label: Free Carrier
values.definition: The risk is transferred when the goods are taken into custody of the carrier at the time and named point mentioned in the contract. Insurance to be covered by the buyer (the seller to the named point).

values.label: Free On Board
values.definition: The risk is transferred when the goods have effectively passed the ship's rail at the port of shipment. Insurance to be covered by the buyer.

values.definition: A device with demonstrated safety in the MR environment within defined conditions. At a minimum, address the conditions of the static magnetic field, the switched gradient magnetic field and the radiofrequency fields.  Additional conditions, including specific configurations of the item, may be required.

values.label: MRI Safe

values.label: MRI Unsafe

values.label: Unspecified

values.label: Duochromatic
values.definition: Duochromatic makeup finish refers to a cosmetic effect where two contrasting colours are used to create a dynamic and multidimensional appearance.

values.label: Fluo
values.definition: A finish that exhibits brightly vivid, fluorescent colours that are extremely vibrant and eye-catching under normal light.

values.label: Glitter
values.definition: A makeup finish with sparkly particles that reflect light, creating a sparkling and eye-catching effect.

values.label: Glittery
values.definition: Similar to glitter, this finish contains tiny reflective particles that add a twinkling shine to the skin.

values.label: Glossy
values.definition: A high-shine finish providing a reflective surface, often found in lip products and eyeshadows for a wet or polished look.

values.label: Glow
values.definition: A subtle sheen that gives the skin a healthy and hydrated appearance, often achieved with light-reflecting particles.

values.label: High perfection
values.definition: A flawless finish that aims to create a smooth, impeccable look often through full coverage products.

values.label: High shine
values.definition: A makeup or cosmetic finish that provides a glossy, reflective surface, creating a look of maximum luminosity.

values.label: Holographic
values.definition: This refers to a multi-dimensional finish that reflects a spectrum of colours.

values.label: Iridescent
values.definition: A luminous finish that subtly changes colour when seen from different angles due to the reflection and refraction of light.

values.label: Lacquered
values.definition: A sleek, highly pigmented finish with deep colour saturation and a shiny, varnish-like surface reminiscent of lacquerware.

values.label: Luminous matte
values.definition: A modern twist on matte, this finish has the non-shiny appeal of matte but with an added element of subtle radiance.

values.label: Luminous / radiant / glowy
values.definition: These finishes give the skin a dewy freshness with slight shimmer or sheen for a healthy-looking glow.

values.label: Matte
values.definition: No shine or gloss; this flat finish absorbs light and reducing the appearance of shine on the skin.

values.label: Matte satiny
values.definition: A soft matte appearance with just a hint of sheen for depth.

values.label: Metal / metallic
values.definition: Features a foil-like look with high shine and often rich pigmentation reminiscent of metal surfaces.

values.label: Natural
values.definition: Natural makeup finish refers to a subtle and understated look that enhances one's features with minimal product, aiming to mimic the appearance of bare, healthy skin.

values.label: Pearlescent
values.definition: Contains fine pearl-like particles that offer an elegant glow and dimension without obvious glitter.

values.label: Phosphorescent
values.definition: A glow-in-the-dark finish that absorbs light and emits it slowly; used for creating striking effects in low-light conditions.

values.label: Powder
values.definition: This refers to products applied in powder form but can also describe the mattifying effect these powders leave on the skin.

values.label: Powdery
values.definition: Often describes foundations or blushes that provide good coverage but have finely milled textures which result in a soft-focus effect.

values.label: Radiant
values.definition: Offers an all-over luminosity and freshness, typically achieved through finely milled shimmer or illuminating ingredients.

values.label: Satin
values.definition: Has a silky finish that's neither completely matte nor overly shiny; it provides moderate reflection for dimensionality.

values.label: Satiny
values.definition: Very similar to satin but emphasises its smoothness and silk-like feel upon application.

values.label: Semi-matte
values.definition: Balances between matte and radiant; it's mostly shine-free but has some light-reflective qualities.

values.label: Shimmer
values.definition: A finish with fine light-reflective particles that give the skin or makeup a subtle glow and sparkle without the intensity of full glitter.

values.label: Shiny
values.definition: High glossiness typically found in lip glosses or certain cream-based products giving off intense shine.

values.label: ANSI
values.definition: American National Standards Institute (ANSI) oversees the creation, promulgation and use of thousands of norms and guidelines that directly impact businesses in nearly every sector: from acoustical devices to construction equipment, from dairy and livestock production to energy distribution, and many more. ANSI is also actively engaged in accrediting programs that assess conformance to standards.- http://www.ansi.org/

values.label: ASME
values.definition: The American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) is a professional body, specifically an engineering society, focused on mechanical engineering. The organization's stated vision is to be the premier organization for promoting the art, science and practice of mechanical and multidisciplinary engineering and allied sciences to the diverse communities throughout the world. Its stated mission is to promote and enhance the technical competency and professional well-being of its members, and through quality programs and activities in mechanical engineering, better enable its practitioners to contribute to the well-being of humankind. Http://www.asme.org/

values.label: ASTM
values.definition: American Society for Testing and Materials International (ASTM) specification documents, test methods, classifications, practices, and guides. These standards describe the characteristics of materials, systems, products, and services. ASTM documents are divided into nine sections, Metals, Construction, Paints, Petroleum Products, Plastics, Textiles, Rubber & Electric Insulating Materials, General Test Methods, and Miscellaneous. ASTM technical committees are made up of professionals from around the globe who develop ASTM standards. There are over 130 ASTM technical committees covering diverse industry areas ranging from metals to the environment. http://www.astm.org

values.label: CISPI
values.definition: Cast Iron Soil Pipe Institute (CISPI) The Institute is dedicated to aiding and improving the plumbing industry. Through the preparation and distribution of technical reports, we seek to advance interest in the manufacture, use and distribution of cast iron soil pipe and fittings, and through a program of research and the cooperative effort of soil pipe manufacturers, we strive to improve the industry's products, achieve standardization of cast iron soil pipe and fittings, and provide a continuous program of product testing, evaluation and development. Assurance that pipe and fittings meet the approved standards and tolerances of the Institute is provided either by Ç®; or the CI NO-HUB® trademarks which are the collective marks all member companies may place on their products. www.cispi.org

values.label: CSA
values.definition: Canadian Standards Association (CSA) As a membership-based association serving business, industry, government and consumers in Canada and the global marketplace. As a solutions-oriented organization, CSA works in Canada and around the world to develop standards that address real needs, such as enhancing public health and safety. Advancing the quality of life. Helping to preserve the environment. Facilitating trade. CSA helps people understand standards through education and information products and services.

values.label: DIN60001 Part 4
values.definition: Textile Fibres Codes managed by the Deutsches Institut für Normung.

values.label: GS1
values.definition: Material List is managed by GS1.

values.label: IAPMO
values.definition: International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials (IAPMO) As a membership-based association, IAPMO is proud to utilize an open consensus process in the development of our flagship Uniform Plumbing Code® and Uniform Mechanical Code®. These codes are established through scientific research, debate, and analysis, strengthening our position at the forefront of the plumbing and mechanical industries. Www.iapmo.org

values.label: ISO
values.definition: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) ISO is a non-governmental organization that forms a bridge between the public and private sectors. On the one hand, many of its member institutes are part of the governmental structure of their countries, or are mandated by their government.

values.label: MSS
values.definition: The Manufacturers Standardization Society (MSS) of the Valve and Fittings Industry is a non-profit technical association organized for development and improvement of industry, national and international codes and standards for: Valves, Valve Actuators, Pipe Fittings, Valve Modification, Flanges, Pipe Hangers, and Associated Seals. The primary function of MSS is to provide its members the means to develop engineering standard practices for the use and benefit of the industry and users of its products. The Society, the only organization dedicated solely to the technical needs of the industry, is currently comprised of 25 technical committees to write, revise and reaffirm industry standards. http://mss-hq.org/

values.label: NSF
values.definition: National Sanitation Foundation International (NSF) NSF Internal helps protect you by certifying products and writing standard for food, water and consumer goods. NSF International is The Public Health and Safety Company™, providing public health and safety risk management solutions to companies, governments and consumers around the world. www.nsf.org

values.label: Bamboo
values.definition: Any of various woody or arborescent grasses (as of the genera Bambusa, Arundinaria, and Dendrocalamus of the subfamily Bambusoideae) of tropical and temperate regions having hollow stems, thick rhizomes, and shoots. The packaging may be in the form of paper, wood or leaves.

values.label: Cellulose hydrate
values.definition: A class of materials manufactured by the conversion of natural cellulose to a soluble cellulosic derivative and subsequent regeneration, typically forming a film (e.g., cellophane).

values.label: Ceramic
values.definition: A non-specific material made from clay and hardened by firing at a high temperatures. Examples can include terra-cotta, earthenware, stoneware, porcelain, and high-tech ceramics.

values.label: Cloth or fabric
values.definition: A non specific material made by weaving, felting, knitting, or crocheting natural and/or synthetic fibres.

values.label: Composite
values.definition: A material that is made from multiple materials.

values.label: Natural cork
values.definition: Cork is an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue that is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak).

values.label: Double wall corrugated board
values.definition: A structure formed by two layers of corrugated cardboard (flutes), with a linerboard facing between them.

values.label: Corrugated board other

values.label: Single wall corrugated board
values.definition: A structure formed by three layers of paper that are glued using starch into one single, sturdy sheet; also termed double faced.

values.label: Triple wall corrugated board
values.definition: A structure formed by an inner and outer liner with three fluted sheets in between, each separated by a layer of paper.

values.label: Abaca (Manila hemp)
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the sheathing leaf of Musa textilis.

values.label: Acrylic
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules comprising at least 85% (by mass) in the chain of the acrylonitrilic pattern.

values.label: Alfa
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the leaves of Stipa tenacissima (esparto, esparto grass, halfah grass, alfa grass, or needle grass).

values.label: Alginate
values.definition: Fibre obtained from metallic salts of alginic acid.

values.label: Aramid
values.definition: Fibre formed from synthetic linear macromolecules made up of aromatic groups joined by amide or imide linkages, of which at least 85% are joined directly to two aromatic rings and with the number of imide linkages, if present, not exceeding the number of amide linkages.

values.label: Broom fibre
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the base of Cytisus scoparius and/or Spartium Junceum.

values.label: Burlap fibre
values.definition: The American name for cloth woven from jute plant skins and other vegetable fibres. In other parts of the world it is known as Hessian, Hessian cloth, or gunny from the Indian gain.

values.label: Chlorofibre
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in their chain more than 50% by mass of chlorinated vinyl or chlorinated vinylidene monomeric units.

values.label: Coir (coconut)
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the fruit of Cocos nucifera.

values.label: Cotton
values.definition: A natural cellulosic seed-hair fibre, obtained from the seed pod of the cotton plant.

values.label: Cupro
values.definition: Regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by the cuprammonium process.

values.label: Elastane
values.definition: Elastofibre composed of at least 85% (by mass) of a segmented polyurethane, and which, when stretched to three times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

values.label: Elastodiene
values.definition: Elastofibre composed of natural or synthetic polyisoprene, or composed of one or more dienes polymerised with or without one or more vinyl monomers, and which, when stretched to three times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

values.label: Elastolefin
values.definition: Fibre composed of at least 95% (by mass) of macromolecules partially cross-linked, made up from ethylene and at least one other olefin and which, when stretched to one and a half times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

values.label: Elastomultiester
values.definition: Fibre formed by interaction of two or more chemically distinct linear macromolecules in two or more distinct phases (of which none exceeds 85% by mass) which contains ester groups as the dominant functional unit (at least 85%) and which, after suitable treatment when stretched to one and half times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

values.label: Flax
values.definition: The plant from the stem of which bast fibre is extracted by retting to produce linen. An erroneous term for linen fibre, particularly in blends.

values.label: Fluorofibre
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules made from fluorocarbon aliphatic monomers.

values.label: Glass fibre
values.definition: Fibre made of glass.

values.label: Hemp
values.definition: Hemp is a commonly used term for varieties of the Cannabis plant. Hemp can yield fibre which can be used in ropes, cloths, weaves, as a reinforcement of polymer composites as well as pulps for paper making.

values.label: Henequen
values.definition: Fibre from the bast of Agave fourcroydes.

values.label: Horse hair
values.definition: Fibre made from hair of horses.

values.label: Jute
values.definition: A bast fibre obtained from the round pod jute or the long pod jute of the family Tiliaceae. Jute ribbon is purely made from the jute plant. Grown extensively in Pakistan and India, mainly in the Bengal district of Pakistan.

values.label: Kapok
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the inside of the kapok fruit (Ceiba pentandra).

values.label: Lyocell
values.definition: A regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by dissolution, and an organic solvent (mixture of organic chemicals and water) spinning process, without formation of derivatives.

values.label: Maguey
values.definition: Fibre from the bast of Agave cantala.

values.label: Melamine
values.definition: Fibre formed of at least 85% by mass of cross-linked macromolecules made up of melamine derivatives.

values.label: Metal fibre/Metallic fibre
values.definition: Manufactured fibers composed of pure metals and metallic alloys which can be processed into textile products, porous media, plastic-coated metals, etc.

values.label: Modacrylic
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in the chain more than 50% and less than 85% (by mass) of the acrylonitrilic pattern.

values.label: Modal
values.definition: A regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by a modified viscose process having a high breaking force and high wet modulus.

values.label: Fibre other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of fibre. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.
