values.label: Polyester (PES)
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules comprising at least 85% (by mass) in the chain of an ester of a diol and terephthalic acid.

values.label: Protein
values.definition: Fibre obtained from natural protein substances regenerated and stabilised through the action of chemical agents.

values.label: Ramie
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the bast of Boehmeria nivea and Boehmeria tenacissima.

values.label: Silk
values.definition: Fibre obtained exclusively from silk-secreting insects.

values.label: Sisal
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the leaves of Agave sisalana.

values.label: Sunn hemp
values.definition: Fibre from the bast of Crotalaria juncea.

values.label: Triacetate
values.definition: Cellulose acetate fibre wherein at least 92% of the hydroxyl groups are acetylated.

values.label: Trivinyl
values.definition: Fibre formed of acrylonitrile terpolymer, a chlorinated vinyl monomer and a third vinyl monomer, none of which represents as much as 50% of the total mass.

values.label: True hemp
values.definition: Fibre obtained from the bast of hemp (Cannabis sativa).

values.label: Vinylal
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules whose chain is constituted by poly(vinyl alcohol) with differing levels of acetalisation.

values.label: Viscose
values.definition: Regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by the viscose process for filament and discontinuous fibre.

values.label: Wool
values.definition: Fibre from sheep's or lambs’ fleeces (Ovis aries) or a mixture of fibres from sheep's or lambs’ fleeces and the hair of the following animals: alpaca, llama, camel, kashmir goat, angora goat, angora rabbit, vicuna, yak, guanaco, cashgora goat, beaver, otter.

values.label: Alpaca wool
values.definition: Alpaca hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a alpaca, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

values.label: Angora wool
values.definition: Angora hair or Angora fibre refers to the downy coat produced by the Angora rabbit.

values.label: Camel wool
values.definition: Camel hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a camel, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

values.label: Cashmere wool
values.definition: Wool obtained from cashmere goats, pashmina goats and some other breeds of goat.

values.label: Goat wool
values.definition: Wool obtained from goats.

values.label: Llama wool
values.definition: LIama hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a llama, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

values.label: Mohair wool
values.definition: Mohair is wool made from the hair of the Angora goat.

values.label: Solidified foam
values.definition: A non specific material in a lightweight cellular form resulting from introduction of gas bubbles during manufacture, used to reduce shock and vibration or abrasion.

values.label: Glass
values.definition: A substance mainly consisting of sand, lime and soda, fused at high temperatures and cooled quickly so that it solidifies to a vitreous or noncrystalline condition. This term applies to transparent clear glass or as a generic term if distinction with coloured glass is not desired.

values.label: Coloured glass
values.definition: Glass containing external colouring or glass that has been coloured by the addition of colouring agents/particles in its creation.

values.label: Laminated carton
values.definition: A material made up of laminates of paperboard, foil and polyethylene which combined form a sheet suitable for asceptic processing.

values.label: Aluminium
values.definition: A non specific material made from aluminium or aluminium alloy.

values.label: Brass
values.definition: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

values.label: Metal composite
values.definition:
Refers to an object that is composed of two separate metals joined together. 
Instead of being a mixture of two or more metals, like alloys, metal composites consist of layers of different metals.

values.label: Iron
values.definition: A heavy metallic element (Fe) capable of being fashioned into a variety of forms.

values.label: Lead
values.definition: A bluish-white soft malleable ductile plastic but inelastic heavy metallic element (Pb).

values.label: Metal other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of metal or metal alloy material. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Stainless steel
values.definition: An alloy of steel with chromium and sometimes another element (as nickel or molybdenum) that is practically immune to rusting and ordinary corrosion.

values.label: Steel
values.definition: Commercial iron that contains carbon in any amount up to about 1.7 percent as an essential alloying constituent, is malleable when under suitable conditions, and is distinguished from cast iron by its malleability and lower carbon content.

values.label: Tin
values.definition: Tin is a chemical element that is obtained chiefly from the mineral cassiterite, where it occurs as an oxide, SnO2. This silvery, malleable poor metal is not easily oxidized in air, and is used to coat other metals to prevent corrosion. It is used in many alloys, most notably bronze.

values.label: Calcium carbonate
values.definition: Ground calcium carbonate and precipitated calcium carbonate products serve as functional fillers in plastic and rubber applications. Calcium carbonate is widely used as in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyolefin, polypropylene (PP), polyethylene (PE) and unsaturated polyester resins applications.

values.label: Mineral other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of mineral. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Quartz
values.definition: A hard white or colourless mineral consisting of silicon dioxide, found widely in igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.

values.label: Talc
values.definition: Talc is used to stiffen thermoplastics, mainly polypropylene but also polyethylene and polyamide (Nylon).

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Corrugated paper
values.definition: Heavy paper with ridges and grooves, used in packing fragile articles.

values.label: Kraft paper
values.definition: Kraft paper is the paper grade with the highest strength. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

values.label: Kraft paper (wet strength)
values.definition: The wet-strength kraft paper has a certain tear strength when wet due to special additives. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

values.label: Molded pulp
values.definition: Used for producing pulp-based or fibrous products by pressing; example products: egg packages, trays and boxes for fruits and vegetables.

values.label: Paper other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of paper-based material. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Paper
values.definition: A non-specific sheet material produced by the matting of fibres from wood, rags, or other fibrous materials. Generally, paper is of a lesser thickness or weight than paperboard.

values.label: Paperboard
values.definition: A non specific material, generally made from cotton or wood, that describe a variety or of board materials used in the production of boxes, folding cartons, and solid fibre and corrugated shipping containers; also termed cardboard.

values.label: Rayon paper
values.definition: Generic term for a manmade fibre derived from regenerated cellulose.

values.label: Plant leaves
values.definition: Plant leaves, such as banana leaves, including wet or dry leaves. In some cases, leaves are pre-softened by steaming.

values.label: Bioplastic
values.definition: Plastic materials made from biomass, but may have exactly the same properties as ordinary plastic. Sometimes these plastics are biodegradable.

values.label: Plastic other
values.definition: A non-specific material made of any of numerous organic synthetic or processed materials that are mostly thermoplastic or thermosetting polymers of high molecular weight and that can be made into objects, films, or filaments.

values.label: Thermoplastics
values.definition: A non-specific substance that becomes soft and pliable when heated, without a change in its intrinsic properties. Polystyrene and polyethylene are thermoplastics.

values.label: Polyethylene terephthalate, amorphous (APET)
values.definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET) has a very high transparency, is flame retardant and suitable for direct food contact.

values.label: Polypropylene, longitudinally and laterally stretched (BOPP)
values.definition: Biaxially oriented PP (BOPP) films are characterized by their tear, impact and puncture resistance. The film is mainly used in food packaging, e.g. as candy wrap or wrapping for chocolate bars.

values.label: Acetate
values.definition: Cellulose acetate is one of the most important esters of cellulose. Depending on the way it has been processed cellulose acetate can be used for a wide variety of applications, e.g. films, membranes or fibres.

values.label: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET)
values.definition: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET) is a variation of standard PET which has been crystallized for heat resistance, rigidity, and toughness.

values.label: Epoxy
values.definition: Epoxy resins are thermoset polymers which are frequently used as coatings for metal packaging such as soft-drink cans.

values.label: Expanded polystyrene (EPS)
values.definition: Expanded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured by expanding spherical beads in a mold, using heat and pressure to fuse the beads together. While each individual bead is a closed cell environment, there are significant open spaces between each bead.

values.label: Ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA)
values.definition: Ethylene vinyl acetate, a copolymer of 60 to 90% ethylene and 40 to 10% vinyl acetate. Packaging applications include soft films, coatings, hot melt adhesives, wine cork substitutes, and closure seals for plastic and metal container caps.

values.label: Ethylene vinyl alcohol (EVOH)
values.definition: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, a copolymer of ethylene and vinyl alcohol. A plastic resin commonly used in food applications to provide barrier to oxygen and other gases.

values.label: High density polyethylene (HDPE)
values.definition: High-Density PolyEthylene (HDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum. A strong, relatively opaque form of polyethylene having a dense structure with few side branches off the main carbon backbone. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

values.label: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE)
values.definition: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum. A strong form of polyethylene having a less dense structure with more side branches off the main carbon backbone (on about 2% of the carbon atoms) than HDPE; therefore its tensile strength is lower, and its resilience is higherMade in translucent or opaque variations, it is quite flexible, and tough to the degree of being almost unbreakable. It is widely used for manufacturing various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, plastic bags for computer components, and various moulded laboratory equipment. Its most common use is in plastic bags.

values.label: Linear low density polyethylene
values.definition: Linear low density polyethylene is a linear polyethylene with a significant number of short branches on the polymer backbone. It is commonly made by copolymerization of ethylene with longer-chain olefins. It is different from LDPE due to the absence of long chain branches which gives it higher tensile strength, impact and puncture resistance than LDPE. Common uses of LLDPE are plastic bags, wraps, stretch wraps, pouches, covers and lids.

values.label: Medium-density polyethylene
values.definition: Medium-density polyethylene is a type of polyethylene defined by a density range of 0.926-0.940 g/cm3. MDPE is typically used in shrink films, sacks, packaging film and carrier bags.

values.label: Nylon
values.definition: Packaging applications include oven-baking bags (nylon 6 and nylon 66) and barrier layers (MXD6 and nylon 6) for PET and HDPE bottles. Very occasionally, bottles can be made of nylon.

values.label: Oriented polypropylene (OPP)
values.definition: Oriented polypropylene (OPP) is made of a soft polypropylene material which is stretched in a transverse or longitudinal direction (monoaxial) and becomes therefore brittle. Also known as: biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), CAS Registry Number: 9003-07-0

values.label: Polymers Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of polymer. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Polyamide (PA)
values.definition: A polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds. Polyamides (PA) occur both naturally and artificially, examples of naturally occurring polyamides are proteins, such as wool and silk. Artificially made polyamides can be nylons, aramids, and sodium poly(aspartate).

values.label: Polyacrylonitril (PAN)
values.definition: Polyacrylonitril is a organic polymer which is frequently used in fibres for textiles. As fibres the material is frequently referred to as acrylic.

values.label: Polycarbamide (PB)
values.definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in the chain the recurring ureylene (NH-CO-NH) functional group.

values.label: Polycarbonate (PC)
values.definition: Polycarbonate, a transparent thermoplastic which is used in a wide variety of applications including CDs and DVDs, eyeglasses, cell phone covers, laptops as well as packaging applications such as bottles.

values.label: Polycaprolactone (PCL)
values.definition: Polycaprolactone is a biodegradable polyester which is also used in in the manufacturing of polyurethanes. It is also used in blends with thermoplastic starch to improve properties and can also be used as a plasticizer to PVC.

values.label: Polyethylene (PE)
values.definition: A thermoplastic composed of the polymers of ethylene.

values.label: Polyethylene naphthalate (PEN)
values.definition: Polyethylene naphthalate is a polymer with good barrier properties (unlike Polyethylene terephthalate). It is well-suited for production of the amber-coloured bottles meant for packing beverages like beer.

values.label: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET)
values.definition: Polyethylene terephthalate is a thermoplastic polymer resin of the polyester family and is used in synthetic fibres. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

values.label: Polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG)
values.definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) is a PET modified with glycol, which is characterized by its aqueous properties (viscosity). Applications are found in injection molding.

values.label: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA)
values.definition: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are linear polyesters produced in nature by bacterial fermentation of sugar or lipids.

values.label: Polyimide (PI)
values.definition: Fibre formed from synthetic linear macromolecules having in the chain recurring imide units.

values.label: Polylactic acid or Polylactide (PLA)
values.definition: Polylactic acid or Polylactide is a biodegradable, thermoplastic, aliphatic polyester derived from lactic acid.

values.label: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)
values.definition: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) is often used as a lightweight and shatterproof alternative to glass, due to its transparency, brilliance and scratch resistance, PMMA is therefore often referred to as acrylic glass.

values.label: Polyoxymethylene (POM)
values.definition: Polyoxymethylene (POM) is a thermoplastic with good mechanical properties and high dimensional stability. Fields of application are the automotive industry and electrical engineering, in packaging it is used for e.g. spray cans, gas lighter tanks, gas ampoules. Also known as acetal, polyacetal, and polyformaldehyde.

values.label: Polypropylene (PP)
values.definition: A non-specific material made of various thermoplastic plastics or fibres that are polymers of propylene.

values.label: Polystyrene (PS)
values.definition: A polymer prepared by the polymerization of styrene as the sole monomer.

values.label: Polyurethane (PU)
values.definition: Polyurethanes are primarily thermoset resins which are used in the manufacture of flexible and rigid foams, microcellular foam seals and gaskets, as well as high performance adhesives, surface coatings and sealants. Polyurethane can also be used to make synthetic fibres.

values.label: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)
values.definition: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA or PVOH) is a biodegradable and highly water soluble polymer with high gas and grease barrier. Common uses for PVA are paper adhesives, paper coatings, as a self-standing water soluble films as well as blends to improve processability of thermoplastic starch.

values.label: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
values.definition: A polymer of vinyl chloride used especially for electrical insulation, films, and pipes.

values.label: Polyvinylidene chloride (PVDC)
values.definition: Polyvinylidene chloride is primarily used as a barrier coating to provide barrier against fat, vapour and gases.

values.label: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN)
values.definition: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN) is a copolymer transparent and rigid plastic. Examples of applications are kitchenware and cosmetic packaging.

values.label: Thermoplastic starch (TPS)
values.definition: Thermoplastic starch is obtained through destructurization of natural starch through exposure to shear and heat. TPS is most frequently used in blends with biodegradable synthetic polymers such as PCL and PVA.

values.label: Extruded polystyrene (XPS)
values.definition: Extruded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured using a process of extrusion that produces a homogeneous "closed cell" matrix with each cell fully enclosed by polystyrene walls.

values.label: Rubber
values.definition: A strong elastic synthetic substance made either by improving the qualities of natural rubber or by an industrial process using petroleum and coal products.

values.label: Natural rubber
values.definition: A strong elastic material made by drying the sap from various tropical trees, especially the American rubber tree.

values.label: Vinyl
values.definition: A non-specific polymer of a vinyl compound or a product (as a resin or a textile fibre) made from such a polymer.

values.label: Hardboard
values.definition: Hardboard (not to be confused with hardwood), also called High-Density Fiberboard (HDF), is a type of fibreboard, which is similar to particle board and medium-density fiberboard, but is denser, much stronger and harder because it is made out of exploded wood fibres which have been highly compressed. Consequently, the density of hardboard is 31 lbs or more per cubic foot (500 kg/m³)[2] and is usually about 50-65 lbs per cubic foot (800–1040 kg/m³). It differs from particle board in that the bonding of the wood fibers requires no additional materials, although resin is often added. Unlike particle board, it will not split or crack.

values.label: Hardwood
values.definition: A general term referring to any variety of broad-leaved, deciduous trees, and the wood from those trees. The term has nothing to do with the actual hardness of the wood; some hardwoods are softer than certain softwood (evergreen) species.

values.label: Medium density fibreboard
values.definition: Medium-Density Fibreboard (MDF) is an engineered wood product made by breaking down hardwood or softwood residuals into wood fibres, combining them with wax and a resin binder, and forming panels by applying high temperature and pressure. MDF is generally denser than plywood. It is made up of separated fibres, but can be used as a building material similar in application to plywood. It is stronger and much more dense than particle board.

values.label: Oriented strand board (OSB)
values.definition: Oriented Strand Board (OSB), also known as sterling board, sterling OSB, aspenite, and smartply, is an engineered wood particle board formed by adding adhesives and then compressing layers of wood strands (flakes) in specific orientations. OSB may have a rough and variegated surface with the individual strips of around 2.5 × 15 cm (1" × 6"), lying unevenly across each other and comes in a variety of types.

values.label: Wood other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of wood. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Particle board
values.definition: Particle Board, also known as particleboard, chipboard, and Low-Density Fibreboard (LDF), is an engineered wood product manufactured from wood chips, sawmill shavings, or sawdust, and a synthetic resin or other suitable binder, which is pressed and extruded. Particle board is a composite material.

values.label: Plywood
values.definition: Plywood, a manufactured wood panel similar to LDF, MDF, and HDF, is made from layering thin sheets of wood. Plywood layers (called veneers or plies) are glued together, with adjacent plies having their wood grain rotated relative to adjacent layers up to 90 degrees. All plywoods bind resin and wood fibre sheets (cellulose cells are long, strong and thin) to form a composite material.

values.label: Softwood
values.definition: General term used to describe lumber produced from needle and/or cone bearing trees (Conifers).

values.label: Cork
values.definition: Made with the outer bark of a cork oak.

values.label: Leather
values.definition: Made of hide from cow or other mammal.

values.label: Metallic
values.definition: Made from metal or a metallic looking plastic.

values.label: Metal band
values.definition: Also known as a heel cap, is an optional piece of metal nailed on to the back of the boot where the heel meets the bottom of the boot.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Rope
values.definition: Rope covering the heels as decoration.

values.label: Synthetic
values.definition: Non natural materials.

values.label: Wood
values.definition: Material made from tree products.

values.label: Antimicrobial
values.definition: Material that resists microbe growth.

values.label: Cotton
values.definition: Made from the cotton plant.

values.label: Fabric
values.definition: Woven from natural or manmade fibers.

values.label: Faux fur
values.definition: Material meant to resemble animal fur of synthetic materials.

values.label: Faux leather
values.definition: Material meant to leather of synthetic materials.

values.label: Faux shearling
values.definition: Material meant to shearling of synthetic materials.

values.label: Fleece
values.definition: The wooly covering of a sheep or goat.

values.label: Gel
values.definition: Silicone gel padding.

values.label: Leather
values.definition: Made from the hide of cow, sheep, etc.

values.label: Memory foam
values.definition: Made from synthetic material that reshapes after compression.

values.label: Mesh
values.definition: Open weave texture fabric.

values.label: Nylon
values.definition: Tough, lightweight, elastic synthetic polymer.

values.label: Organic material
values.definition: Made from non synthetic materials.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Polyester
values.definition: Synthetic resin in which the polymer units are linked by ester groups.

values.label: Polyurethane
values.definition: Polyurethane is a polymer composed of organic units joined by carbamate (urethane) links.

values.label: Poly vinyl chloride
values.definition: Polyvinyl chloride colloquial: polyvinyl, vinyl; abbreviated: PVC is the world's third-most widely produced synthetic plastic polymer (after polyethylene and polypropylene).

values.label: Quilted
values.definition: Two layers of cloth filled with padding held in place by lines of stitching.

values.label: Shearling
values.definition: Made of shearling wool.

values.label: Sherpa
values.definition: Polyester lining with a deep pile and large, fuzzy “naps” that give it a bumpy texture.

values.label: Straw
values.definition: Straw is an agricultural byproduct consisting of the dry stalks of cereal plants after the grain and chaff have been removed.

values.label: Taffeta
values.definition: A fine lustrous silk or similar synthetic fabric with a crisp texture.

values.label: 16 pounds dozen
values.definition: Measurement often used in textiles, that indicate a heavier towel where 12 items weigh 16lbs.

values.label: Extremely heavy
values.definition:
Densitys: 14+ ounces/square yard, 475+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Tweed.
Example uses: Thick hoodies, woven outerwear, or sports coats made of thick material.

values.label: Heavy
values.definition:
Densitys: 11+ ounces/square yard, 373+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Wool.
Example uses: A typical 100% worsted wool suit.

values.label: Light
values.definition:
Density: 4+ ounces/square yard, 136+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Cotton, chambray, PVC.
Example uses: Regular t-shirt, lightweight shirts.

values.label: Light medium
values.definition:
Density: 6+ ounces/square yard, 203+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Cotton.
Example uses: Thick t-shirt.

values.label: Medium
values.definition:
Densitys: 7+ ounces/square yard, 237+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Linen, canvas.
Example uses: Lightweight trousers, light suits and blazers.

values.label: Medium heavy
values.definition:
Densitys: 9+ ounces/square yard, 305+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Polyester, linen-wool blends, velvet.
Example uses: Trousers, thicker shirts.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Ultra heavy
values.definition:
Densitys: 19+ ounces/square yard, 610+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Variety, usually thick.
Example uses: Very dense material is generally used in furniture upholstery, such as cushions and chair coverings.

values.label: Very heavy
values.definition:
Densitys: 12+ ounces/square yard, 406+ grams/square metre. 
Example mterials: Denim, wool flannel.
Example uses: Trousers, thicker shirts.

values.label: Very light/Fine
values.definition:
Density: 2.5+ ounces/square yard, 84+ grams/square metre. 
Example materials: Viscose, jersey. 
Example uses: Jacket linings, undergarments and lightweight performance wear. Also know as tissue weight.

values.label: Jet Fresh
values.definition: Freshly picked and immediately packed and shipped at mature stage and flown to destination for adequate distribution (i.e. imports from South America, Africa or Europe). Flown by jet to market; the carton will be labelled Jet Fresh, when applicable, stickered Jet Fresh. For the produce industry, most common with berries, stonefruits and pineapples

values.label: Preconditioned
values.definition: Product stored at proper temperature prior to shipment to allow ripening and/or colouring, adequate for distribution and/or consumption. Pre- conditioned product is matured to a specific maturity level as a result of ripening through either temperature, gas treatment, humidity or any combination thereof.

values.label: Ready to Eat
values.definition: Fruit/Vegetable is ready to be eaten and no ripening is needed.

values.label: Tree Vine  Ripe
values.definition: Product that is picked at optimum maturity or just shy of. It is almost ‘ripe’ or ‘ready to eat’. This fruit will be shipped immediately (imported = flown) from the pack-house and stickered as Tree or Vine Ripe.

values.label: Triggered
values.definition: Fruit/Vegetable ripening has been triggered using some artificial method, such as gas ethylene. The fruit or vegetable will be edible in a short time after it reaches the store.

values.label: About
values.definition: To indicate when the number of servings per package has rounded according to allowable rounding rules for the target market. This will add some values as exist in the TM today.

values.label: Abcence
values.definition: The method used to analyse the products resulted in absence value of the content.

values.label: Approximately
values.definition: The method used to analyse the products resulted in approximate value of the nutritional content.

values.label: Exact
values.definition: The method used to analyse the products resulted in exact value of the nutritional content.

values.label: Greater Than
values.definition: To indicate presence when the measurement value is allowable to be designated greater than as such by target market regulations.

values.label: Greater Than Or Equal
values.definition: To indicate presence when the measurement value is allowable to be designated greater than or equal to as such by target market regulations.

values.label: Less Than
values.definition: To indicate presence when the measurement value is too small to be measured precisely (rule states less than 0.5).

values.label: Less Than Or Equal
values.definition: To indicate presence when the measurement value is allowable to be designated less than or equal to as such by target market regulations.

values.label: Not detected
values.definition: The method used to analyse the products did not detect the presence of the related element.

values.label: Not Significant Source of
values.definition: To indicate trace amounts below measurable limits as set forth by target market regulations. This value is primarily for food, beverage and tobacco use.

values.label: Trace
values.definition: To indicate presence when the measurement value is too small to be measured precisely or measurable by target market regulations.

values.label: Undetectable
values.definition: The method used to analyse the products resulted in that the measurement value was below the limit of detection.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Precision not specified.

values.label: Usually
values.definition: To indicate when the servings per package are generally around a value such as when the item is referencing a drained solids (the number varies because of a natural variation in unit size, for example pickles).

values.label: Varied
values.definition: To indicate when the servings per package can be a variable number such as with random weight products.

values.label: per litre (/L)
values.definition: Per Litre [/L] (Unified code)

values.label: per millilitre (/mL)
values.definition: Per millilitre [/mL] (Unified Code)

values.label: per millimole (/mmol)
values.definition: Per millimole [/mmol] (Unified code)

values.label: Count
values.definition: Count

values.label: Grams Per Cubic Centimetre
values.definition: Grams Per Cubic Centimetre

values.label: Kilogram per square metre
values.definition: A unit of pressure equal to 9.80665*10-05 Bar

values.label: Cubic Foot Per Minute
values.definition: Cubic foot per minute

values.label: Centimetre Per Second
values.definition: The number of centimetre per second the trade item or part of the trade item moves.

values.label: Decibel
values.definition: A measurement for sound in air and other gases, relative to 20 micropascals (μPa) = 2×10−5 Pa, the quietest sound a human can hear. This is roughly the sound of a mosquito flying 3 metres away. This is often abbreviated to just "dB"; however the correct abbreviation is dB(SPL), indicating decibel for Sound Pressure Level.

values.label: Kilobyte
values.definition: A unit of information equal to 103 (1000) bytes.

values.label: Kilo Becquerel
values.definition: kBq is 103 Bq

values.label: Metre Per Minute
values.definition: Metre Per Minute

values.label: Microlitre
values.definition: A microlitre is one millionth of a litre

values.label: Micrometre
values.definition: A micrometre is one millionth of a metre, also termed Micron.

values.label: Megabyte
values.definition: A unit of information equal to 10 (1000000) bytes.

values.label: Megabecquerel
values.definition: Megabecquerel: 106 Bq1 Bq is defined as the activity of a quantity of radioactive material in which one nucleus decays per second.

values.label: Net kilogram
values.definition: A unit of mass defining the total number of kilograms after deductions.

values.label: Part per million
values.definition: A unit of proportion equal to 10-6 (ppm).

values.label: Batch
values.definition: A unit of count defining the number of batches (batch: quantity of material produced in one operation or number of animals or persons coming at once).

values.label: Pound per square inch - Gauge
values.definition: Psig (pound-force per square inch gauge) is a unit of pressure relative to the surrounding atmosphere. At sea level, Earth's atmosphere actually exerts a pressure of 14.7 psi. Humans do not feel this pressure because internal pressure of liquid in their bodies matches the external pressure. If a pressure gauge is calibrated to read zero in space, then at sea level on Earth it would read 14.7 psi. Thus a reading of 30 psig, on Earth, on a tire gauge represents an absolute pressure of 44.7 psi (lb/in2).

values.label: Pound per square inch - Absolute
values.definition: Psia (pound-force per square inch absolute)is a unit of pressure pressure relative to a vacuum (such as that in space).At sea level, Earth's atmosphere actually exerts a pressure of 14.7 psi. Humans do not feel this pressure because internal pressure of liquid in their bodies matches the external pressure. If a pressure gauge is calibrated to read zero in space, then at sea level on Earth it would read 14.7 psi. Thus a reading of 30 psig, on Earth, on a tire gauge represents an absolute pressure of 44.7 psi (lb/in2).

values.label: Angstrom
values.definition: A unit of length equal to one hundred-millionth of a centimetre, 10–10 metre, used mainly to express wavelengths and interatomic distances.

values.label: Candela per Square Metre

However, the US National Institute of Standards and Technology recommends that, to avoid confusion, any modifiers be instead applied to the quantity being measured rather than the unit of measure[1] For example, "Pg = 100 psi" rather than "P = 100 psig".

values.label: Medical device that incorporates software
values.definition: Software as part of a medical device that is essential for the functioning of that device. This software is sometimes referred to as SiMD (software in a medical device) and is usually supplied with the hardware device. Please refer to local regulations for a regulatory definition.

values.label: Software as a medical device
values.definition: The term software as a medical device (or SaMD) refers to software that can function on, for example, a laptop computer, smartphone or tablet, and has an intended purpose consistent with the definition of a medical device. This could be any kind of software, including but not limited to: computer programs and applications, mobile apps, software as a service (cloud based), websites and browser delivered products. Please refer to local regulations for a regulatory definition.

values.label: GS1 Exception
values.definition: A standard message used to express exceptions within GDSN that happen at the Document, Command, Message, Transaction or Attribute Level.

values.label: Catalogue Item Confirmation
values.definition: This refers to electronic communication from the Data Recipient to the Data Source indicating what action has been taken on the item

values.label: Catalogue Item Notification
values.definition: A business message used to transmit new or updated trade item information from a Source Data Pool to a Recipient Data Pool and further to the Data Recipient within the Global Data Synchronisation Network.

values.label: Registry Catalogue Item
values.definition: A business message used to register basic Catalogue Item information from the Data Source to the GS1 Global Registry via the Source Data Pool within the GDSN (Global Data Synchronisation Network).

values.label: Request For Catalogue Item Notification
values.definition: The RFCIN allows a Recipient to request data from the Source after synchronisation has taken place, as well as to allow the retailer to undo a CIC REJECTED.

values.label: Search Request
values.definition: A request to receive information stored at the Global Registry.

values.label: Search Result
values.definition: A response message detailing the results of a registry search.

values.label: Catalogue Item Publication
values.definition: A business message standard from the Data Source to the Source Data Pool to publish an item within the Global Data Synchronisation Network. The CIP can be used to publish the item to a specific Data Recipient or a specific Target Market.

values.label: Catalogue Item Registration Response
values.definition: A business message used to notify a data pool of the status of the registration in the Global Registry for a trade item.

values.label: Catalogue Item Subscription
values.definition: A business message used by the Data Recipient to establish a request for trade item information. The subscription criteria can be any combination of the GTIN, ​GLN, Target Market and GPC at the exception of the combination with GTIN and GPC that are mutually exclusive. The Recipient Data Pool will forward the CIS to the GS1 Global Registry.

values.label: Basic Party Registration
values.definition: A message used to register parties at the Global Registry.

values.label: Registry Party Data Dump
values.definition: A message containing information on parties registered at the Global Registry.

values.label: Party Registration Response
values.definition: A response message from the Global Registry regarding the status of  a party registration.

values.label: Catalogue Item Authorisation
values.definition: A document used to authorise or de-authorise an item for sale to one or many business locations.

values.label: Catalogue Item Authorisation Response
values.definition: Response Document used to Accept or Reject a Catalogue Item Authorisation.

values.label: Catalogue Item Hierarchical Withdrawal
values.definition: A business message used to transmit trade item information from a data source or a data pool to a data recipient with the Global Data Synchronisation Network with regards to a correction that is required to an item hierarchy that has already been synchronised.

values.label: Aerobic plate count
values.definition: Aerobic Plate Count (APC) is used as an indicator of bacterial populations on a sample. The test is based on an assumption that each cell will form a visible colony when mixed with agar containing the appropriate nutrients.

values.label: Flow cytometry
values.definition: Flow cytometry (FC) is a technique used to detect and measure physical and chemical characteristics of a population of cells or particles. In this process, a sample containing cells or particles is suspended in a fluid and injected into the flow cytometer instrument. The sample is focused to ideally flow one cell at a time through a laser beam, where the light scattered is characteristic to the cells and their components.

values.label: Kit
values.definition: Kit means a set of components that are packaged together and intended to be used to perform a specific in vitro diagnostic examination, or a part thereof.

values.label: Procedure pack
values.definition: Procedure pack means a combination of products packaged together and placed on the market with the purpose of being used for a specific medical purpose.

values.label: System
values.definition: System means a combination of products, either packaged together or not, which are intended to be inter-connected or combined to achieve a specific medical purpose.

values.label: Mono material
values.definition: Layers are made of the same material type.

values.label: Multi material
values.definition: Layers are made of different material types.

values.label: Not Applicable

values.label: Picture and Picture
values.definition: Picture and Picture: split screen of the same size picture, would be the same as picture-in-picture

values.label: Picture and Text
values.definition: Picture and Text: used in the UK. Teletext services with second source in the corner.

values.label: Picture in Picture
values.definition: Picture in Picture: full screen with second source in the corner.

values.label: Auburn
values.definition: Auburn hair is a variety of red hair, most commonly described as reddish-brown in colour or dark ginger. Auburn hair ranges in shades from medium to dark.

values.label: Black
values.definition: Black hair is the darkest and most common of all human hair colours globally, due to larger populations with this dominant trait. It is a dominant genetic trait, and it is found in people of all backgrounds and ethnicities. It has large amounts of eumelanin and is less dense than other hair colours.

values.label: Blonde
values.definition: Blonde or fair hair is a hair colour characterized by low levels of the dark pigment eumelanin.

values.label: Brown
values.definition: Brown hair  varies from light brown to almost black hair. It is characterized by higher levels of the dark pigment eumelanin and lower levels of the pale pigment pheomelanin.

values.label: Grey
values.definition: Grey hair is a combination of normally pigmented hairs interspersed with white ones. Hair turns white when the pigmentation cells responsible for colour (melanin) stop being produced.

values.label: Red
values.definition: Red hair varies in hue from a deep burgundy or bright copper to burnt orange or red-orange to strawberry blond. Characterized by high levels of the reddish pigment pheomelanin and relatively low levels of the dark pigment eumelanin.

values.label: White
values.definition: White hair is not caused by a true gray or white pigment, but is due to a lack of pigmentation and melanin. The clear hairs appear white because of the way light is reflected from the hairs.

values.label: Chain
values.definition: Necklace that is primarily a series of interlinked metal loops.

values.label: Choker
values.definition: Fitting snuggly around the neck.

values.label: Collar
values.definition: Fitting near the base of the neck.

values.label: Locket
values.definition: Small ornamental case worn on chain.

values.label: Multi Strand
values.definition: Single necklace with different sized pieces.

values.label: Pearl Strand

values.label: Pendant
values.definition: Decoration that moves freely on the chain of a necklace.

values.label: Y-Necklace

values.label: Bandana
values.definition: Large handkerchief, typically having a colourful pattern.

values.label: Boa
values.definition: Feathered accessory worn around neck.

values.label: Bolo
values.definition: Slim tie made of leather, with a decorative closure that is used to adjust its position.

values.label: Bow Tie
values.definition: Neckwear formed with 2 loops and a knot.

values.label: Clip-On Tie
values.definition: Tie that is pre-tied and attaches to the collar with a clip.

values.label: Cravat
values.definition: Loosely knotted neckwear.

values.label: Infinity Scarf
values.definition: Scarf that is a continuous piece of fabric that can be twisted into different shapes.

values.label: Muffler
values.definition: Scarf worn around the head and neck for warmth.

values.label: Neck Tie
values.definition: Garment to be worn around the neck , most often with a collared shirt.

values.label: Oblong Scarf
values.definition: Scarf that is longer than wide with two pairs of parallel sides.

values.label: Other

values.label: Sarong/Pareo
values.definition: Material that can be wrapped and used as a skirt.

values.label: Square Scarf
values.definition: Scarf with even length sides.

values.label: Stole
values.definition: Wrap used with formal dresses or gowns, often made of luxurious materials.

values.label: Wrap/Shawl
values.definition: Outwear that can be worn around the shoulders or torso.

values.label: Horizontal
values.definition: A nesting arrangement where the items hang against each other, like spatulas on a long hanging peg.

values.label: Vertical
values.definition: A nesting arrangement where the items stack on top of each other, like bowls.

values.label: Negative
values.definition: A nesting arrangement where higher items fit partially inside and are partially obscured by lower ones for example bowls.

values.label: Positive
values.definition: A nesting arrangement where the higher item fits over and partially obscures the lower one for example sports caps.

values.label: False
values.definition: Negative value.

values.label: Not Applicable
values.definition: A statement that an affirmative or negative response is not required for the attribute.

values.label: True
values.definition: Affirmative value.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Value not stated.

values.label: Acetaminophen
values.definition: Acetaminophen is an analgesic drug used to treat headaches, arthritis, etc., and also to reduce fever, often as an alternative to aspirin.

values.label: Halogenated Organic Flame Retardants
values.definition: Halogenated organic flame retardants are intended to inhibit ignition and the spread of flames. Halogenated chemicals are chemicals that contain bromine, chlorine, fluorine or iodine bonded to a carbon atom.

values.label: Bisphenol
values.definition: Bisphenol is an organic compound with the chemical formula (CH3)2C(C6H4OH)2. It is a colourless solid that is soluble in organic solvents, but poorly soluble in water. BPA is controversial because it exerts weak, but detectable, hormone-like properties, raising concerns about its presence in consumer products and foods contained in such products

values.label: Chlorhexidine gluconate
values.definition: A gluconate salt form of chlorhexidine, a biguanide compound used as an antiseptic agent.

values.label: DEHP
values.definition: Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a member of the phthalate family used as a softening agent for many PVC applications.  DEHP is sometimes called dioctyl phthalate (DOP) or Bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (BEHP).  In the EU package markings require a mark to show "PHT".

values.label: Mercury
values.definition: Mercury is a naturally occurring element that is found in air, water and soil. It exists in several forms: elemental or metallic mercury, inorganic mercury compounds, and organic mercury compounds.

values.label: Paper or Wood
values.definition: If any portion of this item, including reusable packaging, is made from wood or paper, then answer “Yes”. Reusable packaging is intended to stay in use with the product. Ex: Wooden box in which a lawn game, such as a croquet set, is stored after use.

values.label: Phenylalanine
values.definition: Phenylalanine is an amino acid widely distributed in plant proteins. It is an essential nutrient in the diet of vertebrates.

values.label: Polystyrene (CAS 9003-53-6)
values.definition: Polystyrene (CAS 9003-53-6) is a plastic polymer from the monomer styrene. It comes in many forms: sheet, expanded or extruded foam, or as oriented polystyrene. What is commonly known as Styrofoam™ refers only to the extruded form of polystyrene.

values.label: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
values.definition: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is a plastic polymer used in a wide array of products. It is the third most widely produced plastic.

values.label: Salicylate
values.definition: Salicylate is salt or ester of salicylic acid.

values.label: By alternate serving
values.definition: Nutrient measurement is based on a specified alternate serving amount, typically less than the serving size.

values.label: By child nutrition serving
values.definition: Nutrient measurement is based on the child nutrition serving value. Example: USDA Food and Nutrition Service (USDA FNS).

values.label: By measure
values.definition: Nutrient measurement is based on a measurement value for example grams or ounces.

values.label: By package or container
values.definition: Nutrient measurement is based on the contents of the package or container.

values.label: By serving
values.definition: Nutrient measurement is based on a specified serving amount.

values.label: Supplemented with
values.definition: The element is added to the product to improve the nutritional profile or to provide other benefits.

values.label: Bicarbonate (or hydrogen carbonate)
values.definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Bicarbonate (or hydrogen carbonate) is an intermediate form in the deprotonation of carbonic acid. It is an anion with the chemical formula HCO3. Bicarbonate serves a crucial biochemical role in the physiological pH buffering system. Bicarbonate is a major element in our body, and is present in all body fluids and organs. Secreted by the stomach, it is necessary for digestion. When ingested, for example, with mineral water, it helps buffer lactic acid generated during exercise and also reduces the acidity of dietary components. Finally, it has a prevention effect on dental cavities. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

values.label: L-Carnitine
values.definition:
GS1 Tagname Description: Carnitine is a substance that helps the body turn fat into energy. Your body makes it in the liver and kidneys and stores it in the skeletal muscles, heart, brain, and sperm. Carnitine is available as a supplement in a variety of forms: 
 a. L-carnitine: the most widely available and least expensive
 b. Acetyl-L-carnitine: Often used in studies for Alzheimer's disease and other brain disorders
 c. Propionyl-L-carnitine: Often used in studies for heart disease and peripheral vascular disease - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

values.label: Bacillus coagulans
values.definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Bacillus coagulans is approved for veterinary purposes as GRAS by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Center for Veterinary Medicine, as well as by the European Union, and is listed by AAFCO for use as a direct-fed microbial in livestock production. It is often used in veterinary applications, especially as a probiotic in pigs, cattle, poultry, and shrimp. Many references to use of this bacterium in humans exist, especially in improving the vaginal flora, improving abdominal pain and bloating in irritable bowel syndrome patients, and increasing immune response to viral challenges. There is evidence from animal research that suggests that Bacillus coagulans is effective in both treating as well as preventing recurrence of clostridium difficile associated diarrhea. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacillus_coagulans - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

values.label: Glucosamine
values.definition:
GS1 Tagname Description: Glucosamine (C6H13NO5) is an amino sugar and a prominent precursor in the biochemical synthesis of glycosylated proteins and lipids. Glucosamine is part of the structure of the polysaccharides chitosan and chitin, which compose the exoskeletons of crustaceans and other arthropods, as well as the cell walls of fungi and many higher organisms. Glucosamine is one of the most abundant monosaccharides. It is produced commercially by the hydrolysis of crustacean exoskeletons or, less commonly, by fermentation of a grain such as corn or wheat.
Evidence for the effectiveness of glucosamine as a dietary supplement is mixed. In the United States, it is one of the most common dietary supplements used by adults that is neither a vitamin nor a mineral. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucosamine - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

values.label: Analytical
values.definition: The item’s nutrient values have been determined through direct scientific analysis by a lab.

values.label: Analytical and Calculated
values.definition: Some of the item’s nutrient values have been determined through scientific analysis and some have been determined through a calculation of nutrient values provided for its ingredients.

values.label: Calculated
values.definition: The item’s nutrient values have been determined through a calculation of nutrient values provided for its ingredients or from other published documentation and not by lab analysis.

values.label: Unknown
values.definition: It is not known as to method of the derivation of the item’s nutrient values.

values.label: USDA Food and Nutrition Service
values.definition:
The Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) is an agency of USDA’s Food, Nutrition, and Consumer Services.

FNS works to end hunger and obesity through the administration of 15 federal nutrition assistance programs including WIC, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), and school meals.  In partnership with State and Tribal governments, FNS programs serve one in four Americans  during the course of a year. Working with public, private and non-profit partners, the mission is to increase food security and reduce hunger by providing children and low-income people access to food, a healthful diet and nutrition education in a way that supports American agriculture and inspires public confidence. No American should have to go hungry.   http://www.fns.usda.gov/

deprecated_values.label: Decaffeinated
deprecated_values.definition: NOTE: This code will be deleted in a future release. Use attribute nutritionalClaimTypeCode instead. Decaffeinated is to remove most or all of the caffeine from trade item.

deprecated_values.label: Vegan
deprecated_values.definition: NOTE: This code will be deleted in a future release. Use attribute nutritionalClaimTypeCode instead. Indicates the product has been marked as vegan, and indicates that the product is free of animal products: no meat, milk, eggs, wool, leather, and so forth.

values.label: The USDA Child Nutrition (CN) Labeling Program
values.definition: The USDA Child Nutrition (CN) Labeling Program provides food manufacturers the option to include a standardised food crediting statement on their product label. Labels must be approved by USDA, FNS prior to use and manufacturers must have quality control procedures and inspection oversight that meet the FNS requirements. Products produced in accordance with the CN Labeling Program are generally purchased by foodservice providers for FNS meal programs.

values.label: Packaging Marked With Nutrition Information
values.definition: Trade item packaging contains information pertaining to its nutrition information.

values.label: Packaging Not Marked With Nutrition Information
values.definition: Trade item packaging does not contains information pertaining to its nutrition information.
5 a day. A program designed to encourage the consumption of at least five portions of fruit and vegetables per day,

values.label: Health Star Rating
values.definition: The Health Star Rating is a front-of-pack labelling system that rates the overall nutritional profile of packaged food and assigns it a rating from ½ a star to 5 stars. It provides a quick, easy, standard way to compare similar packaged foods. The more stars, the healthier the choice. (http://healthstarrating.gov.au)

values.label: USDA MyPlate
values.definition: ChooseMyPlate.gov provides practical information to individuals, health professionals, nutrition educators, and the food industry to help consumers build healthier diets with resources and tools for dietary assessment, nutrition education, and other user-friendly nutrition information. - See more at: http://www.choosemyplate.gov.

values.label: Dietary Guidelines for Americans
values.definition: The Dietary Guidelines for Americans encourages individuals to eat a healthful diet — one that focuses on foods and beverages that help achieve and maintain a healthy weight, promote health, and prevent chronic disease. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) jointly publish the Dietary Guidelines every 5 years. www.health.gov/DietaryGuidelines/.

values.label: Fruits & Veggies - More Matters
values.definition: Fruits & Veggies-More Matters is a health initiative focused on helping Americans increase fruit & vegetable consumption for better health. http://www.fruitsandveggiesmorematters.org/.

values.label: 3-Every-Day of Dairy
values.definition: Consuming 3-Every-Day® of Dairy – three daily servings of milk, cheese, or yogurt – is an easy way for families to get a powerful punch of nutrients to help build stronger bones and healthy bodies and reduce the risk of osteoporosis. In addition, a growing body of research suggests that enjoying three servings of dairy foods a day as part of a nutrient-rich, balanced diet may help maintain a healthy weight. www.nationaldairycouncil.org

values.label: American Diabetes Association Food Exchange List
values.definition: If you have diabetes, it’s essential to have a road map for your diet. This road map is a meal plan, and you can either create it by yourself or enlist the help of a registered nutritionist, dietitian or certified diabetes educator. The goal of a meal plan exchange lists is to help control your blood sugar and lose weight by balancing the type and amount of food you eat. Diabetics should follow a diet low in carbohydrates, fat and calories. Exchange lists, which were created by the American Dietetic Association and the American Diabetes Association as a meal planning guide primarily for diabetics, are based on principles of good nutrition that apply to everyone. The foods within each group have similar amounts of calories, carbs, fats, and proteins, which allows for greater flexibility in choosing foods.

values.label: Weight Watchers
values.definition: The item meets criteria set forth by Weight Watchers (https://welcome.weightwatchers.com/) and is eligible for their weight management program.

values.label: Nutri-Score
values.definition: Nutri-Score was created by the French Health Ministry in order to introduce an independent measure of the nutritional quality of food products. The score itself is calculated based on the nutritional data and ingredients, and is displayed as a colored logo (green to red) and letters (A to E).

values.label: Smart Snacks
values.definition: Smart Snacks was established to help students get the nutrition they need to grow and learn during the school day. Any food or beverage sold to students at schools during the school day, other than those foods provided as part of the school meal program, must meet Smart Snack criteria as defined by the USDA Guide to Smart Snacks in Schools - https://fns-prod.azureedge.net/sites/default/files/resource-files/USDASmartSnacks_508_62019.pdf

values.label: Atkins 100
values.definition: Atkins 100 is a low carb plan based on portion control and eating 100 grams of net carbs per day.

values.label: Atkins 20
values.definition: The Atkins 20 is a low carbohydrate-keto diet which is split into four phases of carbohydrate control.

values.label: Atkins 40
values.definition: Atkins 40 is a low carb diet plan based on portion control and eating 40 grams net carbs per day.

values.label: HFSS (High in fat, sugar or salt)
values.definition: The UK government program to reduce childhood obesity includes restrictions in the promotion of food and drink products classified as high in fat, sugar or salt (HFSS) under the UK Department of Health 2004 nutritional profile model. The intent is that the industry will use the nutritional profile model to calculate the score and convey the numeric result.

values.label: Registered

Abridged: Content has been shortened: use for abridged, shortened, concise, condensed.
Adapted: Content has been adapted to serve a different purpose or audience, or from one medium to another: use for dramatization, novelization etc. Use to describe the exact nature of the adaptation.
Alternate: Do not use. This code is now DEPRECATED, but is retained in the list for reasons of backwards compatibility.
Annotated: Content is augmented by the addition of notes
Bilingual edition: Both languages should be specified in the 'Language' group. Use MLL for an edition in more than two languages.
Braille: Braille edition
Combined volume: An edition in which two or more works also published separately are combined in a single volume; AKA 'omnibus' edition.
Critical: Content includes critical commentary on the text
Coursepack: Content was compiled for a specified educational course.
Digital original: A digital product which has no print counterpart and is not expected to have a print counterpart.
Enhanced: Use for e-publications that have been enhanced with additional text, speech, other audio, video, interactive or other content.
Enlarged: Content has been enlarged or expanded from that of a previous edition.
Expurgated: 'Offensive' content has been removed
Facsimile: Exact reproduction of the content and format of a previous edition.
Festschrift: A collection of writings published in honor of a person, an institution or a society.
Illustrated: Content includes extensive illustrations which are not part of other editions
Large type / large print: Large print edition, print sizes 14 to 19 pt - see also ULP
Microprint: A printed edition in a type size too small to be read without a magnifying glass
Media tie-in: An edition published to coincide with the release of a film, TV program, or electronic game based on the same work. Use to describe the exact nature of the tie-in.
Multilingual edition: All languages should be specified in the 'Language' group. Use BLL for a bilingual edition.
New edition: Where no other information is given, or no other coded type is applicable
Edition with numbered copies: A limited edition in which each copy is individually numbered

Prebound edition: In the US, a book that was previously bound, normally as a paperback, and has been rebound with a library-quality hardcover binding by a supplier other than the original publisher. See also the and composites
Revised: Content has been revised from that of a previous edition.
School edition: An edition intended specifically for use in schools.
Simplified language edition: An edition that uses simplified language (Finnish 'Selkokirja')
Special edition: Use for anniversary, collectors', de luxe, gift, limited, numbered, autographed edition. Use to describe the exact nature of the special edition.
Student edition: Where a text is available in both student and teacher's editions.
Teacher's edition: Where a text is available in both student and teacher's editions; use also for instructor's or leader's editions.
Unabridged: Where a title has also been published in an abridged edition; also for audiobooks, regardless of whether an abridged audio version also exists.
Ultra large print: For print sizes 20pt and above, and with typefaces designed for the visually impaired - see also LTE
Unexpurgated: Content previously considered 'offensive' has been restored
Variorum: Content includes notes by various commentators, and/or includes and compares several variant texts of the same work.

values.label: Main content page count

This is the preferred page count for most books for the general reader. For books with substantial front and/or back matter, include also Front matter and Back matter page counts, or Total numbered pages.

values.label: Back matter page count

values.label: Total numbered pages

values.label: Content page count
values.definition: The sum of all Roman- and Arabic-numbered and contentful unnumbered pages.

values.label: Total unnumbered insert page count

values.label: Full
values.definition: Full coverage is very opaque, and used to cover birthmarks, vitiligo, hyperpigmentation and scars. It is sometimes referred to as “corrective” or “camouflage” make-up. Products with full or high coverage contain over 15% pigment.

values.label: Light
values.definition: Light can cover unevenness and slight blotchiness, but is not opaque enough to cover freckles. Products with light coverage have 5-10 percent pigment.

values.label: Medium
values.definition: Medium coverage can cover freckles, discolorations, blotchiness, and red marks left by pimples. Products with medium coverage have 10-15 percent pigment.

values.label: Sheer
values.definition: Sheer is the most transparent and contains the least amount of pigment. It will not hide discolorations on the skin but it can minimize the contrast between the discoloration and the rest of the skin tone. Products with sheer coverage have less than 5 percent pigment.

values.label: Extremely opaque
values.definition: Extremely opaque also known as blackout, light doesn't pass through and textile heavier than very opaque. 100+ denier

values.label: Opaque
values.definition: Opaque materials do not allow light to pass through or penetrate them. 41-69 denier

values.label: Very opaque

GÄA - Gäa is a diverse farming association for farmers, processors and traders inside.Focal point is Germany. Gäa is a special design for the structure of the organic farming. 
Biokreis- The Biokreis is an association for organic farming. Currently more than 800 farms, 80 and 200 processors, consumers are members of Biokreis, committed to working together on more than 33,000 for organic and sustainable farming.

values.label: Naturland
values.definition: Naturland - Naturland is active the world over in promoting organic agriculture. Its members are farmers who produce a wide range of valuable products: coffee from Mexico and Peru, olive oil from Greece, tea from the slopes of India’s mountains, pineapple and other tropical fruit from Uganda, spices from Sri Lanka. Organic agriculture safeguards the existence of smallholders and helps with the sustainable management of what are often fragile ecosystems. On a global scale, over 50,000 Naturland farmers are cultivating an area of over 142,000 hectares.

values.definition:
​The Danish Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA) is part of the Ministry of Environment and Food. DVFA is responsible for food safety and health from farm to fork and maintains a list of Danish food companies, aquacultural farms etc. subject to organic inspection.
Only authorities under the Ministry of Environment and Food carry out inspection under the government rules for organic production. The Danish AgriFish Agency inspects ​the primary production, while the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA) inspects food companies.
