values.label: Warrant holder of the court of Belgium
values.definition: Becoming an official supplier to the Belgian Court is a source of particular pride for a craftsman or company to seeing their talent and professionalism rightly recognized by His Majesty the King.

values.label: Weidemelk
values.definition: A certification given in the Netherlands to dairy products made from milk produced by cattle (bovine) that is allowed to roam free in the pasture for at least a minimum of 120 days in a year.

values.label: Weight Watchers Endorsed
values.definition: Foods and meals in the Weight Watchers program are assigned points, and you're allotted a certain number of points daily depending on your initial body weight and weight loss goals. Some packaged food brands and even certain restaurants have teamed up with Weight Watchers to promote this healthy point-based weight-loss program.

values.label: Welfare Quality
values.definition: Welfare Quality states that the welfare of the animals both on the farm and during slaughter is followed in accordance with the welfare quality procedure. Consumers know that the welfare of the animals is protected.

values.label: Kosher Western Kosher (WK)
values.definition:
Western Kosher provides assistance with Kashruth supervision by certifying bakeries, butcher shops, caterers, restaurants, hotels, manufacturers or processors involved in producing Kosher food products for year-round use for Canada and the United States. 

Western Kosher, formerly the Vaad Ha'ir of Winnipeg, provides its 120 licensees with the North American standard of kashruth – a standard adhered to throughout all of Canada and the U.S.

values.label: Where Food Comes From organic
values.definition: Certificate from Where Food Comes From, Inc., related to organic products.

values.label: World Fair Trade Organization (WFTO) Guaranteed Fair Trade
values.definition: The WFTO Fair Trade Standard specifies criteria for assessing if an enterprise truly implements the 10 Principles of Fair Trade. Demonstrating compliance earns Fair Trade Enterprises the designation "Guaranteed Fair Trade". This Standard is the heart of the WFTO Guarantee System, focusing on the management and operation of Fair Trade Enterprises.

values.label: Whole grains 50 percent Stamp
values.definition: If a product bears the 50%+ Stamp, then at least half of its grain ingredients are whole grain. There is a minimum requirement of 8 grams– a half serving – of whole grain per labelled serving, for products using the 50%+ Stamp.

values.label: Whole Grain 100 Percent Stamp
values.definition: The Whole Grain 100 Percent Stamp is a program of The Whole Grain Council. The Whole Grains Council helps consumers find whole grain foods and understand their health benefits; helps manufacturers and restaurants create delicious whole grain foods; and helps the media write accurate, compelling stories about whole grains. If a product bears the 100% Stamp, then all its grain ingredients are whole grains. There is a minimum requirement of 16g (16 grams) – a full serving – of whole grain per labelled serving, for products using the 100% Stamp.

values.label: Whole Grain Basic Stamp
values.definition: The Whole Grain Basic Stamp is a program of The Whole Grain Council. The Whole Grains Council helps consumers find whole grain foods and understand their health benefits; helps manufacturers and restaurants create delicious whole grain foods; and helps the media write accurate, compelling stories about whole grains. If a product bears the Basic Stamp, it contains at least 8g (8 grams) – a half serving – of whole grain, but may also contain some refined grain. Even if a product contains large amounts of whole grain (23g, 37g, 41g, etc.), it will use the Basic Stamp if it also contains extra bran, germ, or refined flour.

values.label: Whole Grain Council Stamp
values.definition: The Whole Grain Stamp is a certification symbol from the Oldways Whole Grains Council that communicates the gram amount of whole grain in a product. There are three different versions of the Whole Grain Stamp that can appear on packages (the 100% Stamp, the 50%+ Stamp, and the Basic Stamp), depending on what percentage of the grain ingredients are whole grain (or in Canada, what percentage of the product weight is whole grain).

values.label: WIETA (Wine and Agricultural Ethical Trading Association)
values.definition: The Wine and Agricultural Ethical Trading Association (WIETA). WIETA’s vision is to promote fair treatment, respectful relationships and dignified lives toward achieving a transformed agricultural sector.

values.label: Sustainable wineries for climate protection
values.definition: The Sustainable Wineries for Climate Protection (SWfCP) certification, developed by the Spanish Wine Federation (FEV), is aimed at the continuous improvement and sustainability of wineries, acting on four fundamental pillars: Environmental, Social, Economic and Governance to align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

values.label: Kosher Supervisors of Wisconsin Certification
values.definition: Kosher Supervisors of Wisconsin Certification

values.label: Water Quality Association (WQA's)- Tested and Certified
values.definition: WQA's Certified Product Listings are available to help connect consumers with water treatment products that have been tested and certified to industry standards. WQA's Gold Seal Product Certification Program ensures that the product is constructed or formulated from safe materials, the claims listed on the packaging are backed by test data, and the product will hold up under normal usage conditions.

values.label: WSDA
values.definition: Washington State Department of Agriculture Organic Food Program, Washington State Department of Agriculture Organic Food Program (WSDA) Organic Food Program  The WSDA Organic Food Program, a USDA-accredited certifier, upholds the integrity of the organic label through certification and inspection of organic crop and livestock producers, processors, handlers and retailers. Whether you are looking to market your organic product at home or abroad, WSDA offers certification services to meet your needs. Please browse below to find out how WSDA can put your business on the path to certification.

values.label: WWF Panda
values.definition: Products that support the WWF http://www.worldwildlife.org/

values.label: Yolo Certified Organic Agriculture
values.definition: YCOA (Yolo County Agricultural) Commissioner's office is one of the few counties in California to offer an organic certification program to qualified agricultural producers and handlers. The certification standards used by YCOA are the USDA's National Organic Program (NOP).  YCOA is a USDA accredited certification agency.

values.label: Zeldzaam Lekker
values.definition: This label is awarded to companies that support (through their products or services) the preservation of rare or uncommon cattle and animal sorts.

values.label: Zero pesticide residue
values.definition: The "Zero Pesticide Residue" programme guarantees consumers that products bearing the label are free of residues of active substances that are not compatible with this programme.

values.label: Zero Waste Business Council Certified
values.definition: U.S. Zero Waste Business Council Certification Program is created by U.S. Zero Waste Business Council. It is the first third-party Zero Waste Facility Certification program for facilities that meet the requests of Zero Waste Business for a valid, comprehensive verification of their Zero Waste achievements.

deprecated_values.label: European Vegetarian Union
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population.The V Label is intended for the labelling of vegetarian and vegan products. The V Label makes it possible to safely and conveniently select vegetarian and vegan food without having to study the ingredients or make enquiries with the manufacturer. Products bearing the V Label must not contain any of the following ingredients: - Meat, fish and poultry - Ingredients that are produced from dead animals such as gelatine and fish oil - Eggs from hens kept in cages - Gelatine for the clarification of juices or vinegar - Calf-rennet for the production of cheese The V Label always states the vegetarian category the labelled product belongs to. The label must at least indicate the category “vegetarian” or “vegan”. Vegetarian products with milk and without egg can be labelled “lacto-vegetarian” (or “without eggs”) and vegetarian products with egg and without milk can be labelled “ovo-vegetarian” (or “without milk”).

deprecated_values.label: Global Gap
deprecated_values.definition: NOTE: This code will be deleted in a future release, please use code GGN. GLOBALG.A.P. is a private sector body that sets voluntary standards for the certification of production processes of agricultural (including aquaculture) products around the globe. The GLOBALG.A.P. standard is primarily designed to reassure consumers about how food is produced on the farm by minimising detrimental environmental impacts of farming operations, reducing the use of chemical inputs and ensuring a responsible approach to worker health and safety as well as animal welfare.

deprecated_values.label: KAT
deprecated_values.definition:
This code is being deprecated. 
Please use ORIGIN_OF_EGGS.
KAT is a supervisory body in hen rearing and provides for quality and traceability in egg production. The required standards by KAT go beyond the legal requirements of organic, floor and free-range rearing. They are controlled by accredited European examining institutes.

deprecated_values.label: Nix18
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population. The NIX18 campaign is to strengthen the social norm "do not drink and smoke until your 18". The initiative is from the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport and a large number of partners (Koninklijke Horeca Netherlands, KWF Cancer, Lung Fund, Trimbos Institute, NOC * NSF, supermarkets united in the Food Retail, GGD Netherlands, Thuiswinkel.org, the Dutch Food Safety Authority and the Ministry of Security and Justice). The campaign focuses on the whole society, in particular the area of youth.

deprecated_values.label: Pregnancy warning
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population. The purpose of the pregnancy icon is making clear to pregnant women that they should not drink alcoholic beverages. Legislation or self-regulation is country dependent.

values.label: Alkaline soluble
values.definition: An adhesive which is alkaline soluble or releasable.

values.label: Non-water soluble
values.definition: An adhesive that is made with components that are all not water soluble (i.e., will not dissolve in water).

values.label: Water soluble
values.definition: An adhesive which is water soluble or water releasable.

values.label: Hot-melt
values.definition: A solid formulation based on thermoplastic polymers, no water or solvents are involved. Also known as hot glue.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Silicone
values.definition: A versatile water resistant polymer whose primary ingredient is silica, a common form of sand found in quartz.

values.label: Chemically Hardened
values.definition: The material has been treated to have additional resistance to deformation or change.

values.label: Coextruded
values.definition: Coextruded films are melted together without adhesive.

values.label: Compressed
values.definition: The material has been subjected to compressive stress which results in reduction of volume as compared to an uncompressed but otherwise identical state.

values.label: Injection Moulded
values.definition: The material was manufactured by injection moulding, which consists of feeding the material into a heated barrel, mixed, and forced into a mold cavity where it cools and hardens to the configuration of the cavity.

values.label: Insulated
values.definition: The material has been designed or processed to reduce heat transfer.

values.label: Laminated with adhesive
values.definition: Laminated films are glued together with adhesive.

values.label: Moisture Resistant
values.definition: The material property that resists uptake or passage of water. The resistance of a packaging material to deterioration or change when in contact with water. To be water resistant is not to be waterproof.

values.label: Moulded
values.definition: The material was manufactured by moulding, which consists of filling a mold with the material on liquid form and allowing it to harden so it takes the shape of the mold.

values.label: Vacuum Formed
values.definition: A process through which a material is heated to a forming temperature, stretched onto or into a single-surface mould, and held against the mould by applying a vacuum between the mould surface and the sheet.

values.label: Water Repellent
values.definition: The material has been treated or processed so it can resist the ingress of water under specified conditions

values.label: Absorbing blotter
values.definition: An absorbent piece of material for products, such as meat or fish, to absorb liquids such as blood or water.

values.label: Applicator
values.definition: Device to facilitate the direct application of the product.

values.label: Base to stand up vertically
values.definition: A general term applied to the support or pedestal of an object.

values.label: Bung seal
values.definition: A bung is an apparatus used to seal a container, such as a bottle, barrel or tube. A bung is partially inserted inside the container to act as a seal.

values.label: Cage/Muzzle
values.definition: A cage that fits over the cork of a bottle of champagne, sparkling wine or beer to prevent the cork from emerging under the pressure of the carbonated contents.

values.label: Cap
values.definition: A cap that seals a bottle or other form of packaging.

values.label: Carrier
values.definition: A device of various types attached to or hang from trolleys to support the load.

values.label: Collar
values.definition: Decorative element generally imprinted and placed on the neck of bottles.

values.label: Consumption utensil
values.definition: An item which allows the user to extract and/or consume the content of a container or product (straws, spoons, ice cream stick).

values.label: Cork
values.definition: A small cylinder that is pushed into the packaging to close it.

values.label: Coupler
values.definition: A device for connecting parts of barrel, cask etc.

values.label: Divider/Protector
values.definition: A component in packaging to serve as protecting the product and/or also the packaging shape.

values.label: Edge protection
values.definition: A right-angle piece placed over the outermost perimeter edges of a container to distribute pressure and prevent collapse or cutting from banding, strapping, or handling.

values.label: Film
values.definition: A flexible or semi-rigid material, usually roll-fed, which commonly forms bottom part of the package. It could either be flat or formed on the packaging line where it is sealed together with a peel off lid or tray to enclose the products securely.

values.label: Flap
values.definition: A piece of material, hinged or attached only on one side, that covers an opening or hangs down from the packaging.

values.label: Handle
values.definition: A grip attached to an object for using or moving the object, usually with the hands.

values.label: Humidity Pack
values.definition: A humidity pack added in the product container maintains storage content at a relative humidity level and prevents the content from degradation.

values.label: Label
values.definition: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article (or printed directly upon it), which usually carries information about the article to which it has been attached.

values.label: Lid
values.definition: In packaging, the top or bottom of a container, usually the part that closes the opening; may also be known as cap, over, or top.

values.label: Liner
values.definition: An internal chamber within a container which separates the content of the container from the walls. Inner liners provide additional isolation and protection to the content of a container. Sometimes coatings of certain materials may be applied as an alternative to inner liners.

values.label: Lightning stopper swing-top (LSST)
values.definition: The LSST is a pin with a spring and a toggle lever principle, usually made of porcelain or plastic, with a sealing ring, mainly for closing bottles. Opening and closing can be done by hand as often as desired and does not require any aid such as a bottle opener. Also known as a flip-top.

values.label: Main package type
values.definition: The code to designate the material that pertains to the value defined in packageTypeCode.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Peg
values.definition: A fastener which allows a product to be hanged.

values.label: Pump
values.definition: A pump is a device that is used to force a liquid or gas to flow in a particular direction. It's commonly used in combination with a bottle or tube on household cleaning products or cosmetics such as hand soap, lotions and creams.

values.label: Sleeve
values.definition: A tubular form, open at both ends, that is slipped over an item or package.

values.label: Spigot
values.definition: A small peg, plug or tapl, especially for insertion into the vent of a cask.

values.label: Spout
values.definition: A spout is a protruding edge which allows the pouring of the contents of the package. Example: extracting / dispensing liquid products from a container.

values.label: Strip
values.definition: A material used to hold, fasten, seal or secure an object or packaging. It can involve the use of adhesives on one or both sides.

values.label: Tab
values.definition: A flexible cover which can be easily removed in order to open a container.

values.label: Tag
values.definition: A hanging card made of any material which is used to identify or provide additional information of a product.

values.label: Tap
values.definition: A device that controls the flow of liquid/gas.

values.label: Threaded spindle
values.definition: Device with a screw system that contains a lead the consumer can lower or raise the platform. Example: Deodorant with a twist mechanism to use the product.

values.label: Window
values.definition: Transparent element affixed to a packaging to allow the consumer to see the product through it.

values.label: First Submission of Packaging
values.definition: First submission of packaging (use for new trade items or existing trade items without packaging changes.

values.label: Similar or Equa to Current Packaging
values.definition: Similar or equal to current packaging (use if there is no change to the performance of the packaging.

values.label: Improved Packaging Performance
values.definition: Improved packaging performance (use if the new packaging improves the performance than the previous packaging.

values.label: Reduced Packaging Performance
values.definition: Reduced packaging performance (use if the new packaging reduces the performance than the previous packaging.

values.label: Aluminum Oxide (AlOx)
values.definition: Coating barrier which can be used in various applications to provide barrier towards gases and moisture and is composed of aluminum (Al) and oxygen (O) atoms.

values.label: Bamboo
values.definition: Any of various woody or arborescent grasses (as of the genera Bambusa, Arundinaria, and Dendrocalamus of the subfamily Bambusoideae) of tropical and temperate regions having hollow stems, thick rhizomes, and shoots. The packaging may be in the form of paper, wood or leaves.

values.label: Cellulose hydrate
values.definition: A class of materials manufactured by the conversion of natural cellulose to a soluble cellulosic derivative and subsequent regeneration, typically forming a film (e.g., cellophane).

values.label: Ceramic
values.definition: A non-specific material made from clay and hardened by firing at a high temperatures. Examples can include Terra-cotta, Earthenware, Stoneware, Porcelain, and High-Tech Ceramics.

values.label: Cloth or Fabric
values.definition: A non specific material made by weaving, felting, knitting, or crocheting natural and/or synthetic fibers.

values.label: Composite
values.definition: A material that is made from multiple materials.

values.label: Natural cork
values.definition: Cork is an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue that is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak).

values.label: Corrugated Board, A-Flute
values.definition: Corrugated cardboard, with flute type/size A in between the layers of linerboard.

values.label: Corrugated Board, B-Flute
values.definition: Corrugated cardboard, with flute type/size B in between the layers of linerboard.

values.label: Corrugated Board, C-Flute
values.definition: Corrugated cardboard, with flute type/size C in between the layers of linerboard.

values.label: Double Wall Corrugated Board
values.definition: A structure formed by five layers of cardboard: two fluted sheets and three linerboards (two outer liners and one intermediate liner). Also known as 5-layer type.

values.label: Corrugated Board, E/B-Flute
values.definition: Corrugated cardboard, double wall, with a combination of flute types/sizes E and B in between the layers of linerboard.

values.label: Corrugated Board, E-Flute
values.definition: Corrugated cardboard, with flute type/size E in between the layers of linerboard

values.label: Corrugated Board Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of corrugated boards. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Single Wall Corrugated Board
values.definition: A structure formed by three layers of cardboard: one fluted sheet and two outer linerboards. Also known as 3-layer type or double faced.

values.label: Triple Wall Corrugated Board
values.definition: A structure formed by seven layers of cardboard: three fluted sheets and four linerboards (two outer liners and two intermediate liners). Also known as 7-layer type.

values.label: Fibre Burlap
values.definition: The American name for cloth woven from jute plant skins and other vegetable fibres. In other parts of the world it is known as Hessian, Hessian cloth, or gunny from the Indian gain.

values.label: Cotton
values.definition: A natural cellulosic seed-hair fiber, obtained from the seed pod of the cotton plant. First known in India about 3000 B.C.

values.label: Flax
values.definition: The plant from the stem of which bast fiber is extracted by retting to produce linen. An erroneous term for linen fiber, particularly in blends.

values.label: Hemp
values.definition: Hemp is a commonly used term for varieties of the Cannabis plant. Hemp can yield fibre which can be used in ropes, cloths, weaves, as a reinforcement of polymer composites as well as pulps for paper making.

values.label: Jute
values.definition: A bast fiber obtained from the round pod jute or the long pod jute of the family Tiliaceae. Jute ribbon is purely made from the jute plant. Grown extensively in Pakistan and India, mainly in the Bengal district of Pakistan.

values.label: Fibre Other
values.definition: A non specific material made of a unit of matter, either natural or manufactured, that forms the basic element of fabrics and other textile structures.

values.label: Solidified Foam
values.definition: A non specific material in a lightweight cellular form resulting from introduction of gas bubbles during manufacture, used to reduce shock and vibration or abrasion.

values.label: Glass
values.definition: A substance mainly consisting of sand, lime and soda, fused at high temperatures and cooled quickly so that it solidifies to a vitreous or noncrystalline condition. This term applies to transparent clear glass or as a generic term if distinction with coloured glass is not desired. Example: sodocalcite.

values.label: Borosilicate glass
values.definition: Glass composed of silicon, boron, sodium and aluminum oxides (+ other alkaline oxides). It is a technical glass, not recyclable.

values.label: Coloured Glass
values.definition: Glass containing external colouring or glass that has been coloured by the addition of colouring agents/particles in its creation

values.label: Crystal glass
values.definition: Glass rich in lead oxide. It is a technical glass, not recyclable, typically used in decorative objects and also in certain cosmetic packaging.

values.label: Laminated Carton
values.definition: A material made up of laminates of paperboard, foil and polyethylene which combined form a sheet suitable for asceptic processing.

values.label: Aluminum
values.definition: A non specific material made from aluminum or aluminum alloy.

values.label: Aluminum Metallized layer
values.definition: Metallized layers are thin layers of aluminium which is vapor-deposited on the material (as opposed to aluminium as a separate layer).

values.label: Brass
values.definition: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

values.label: Metal Composite
values.definition:
Refers to an object that is composed of two separate metals joined together. 
Instead of being a mixture of two or more metals, like alloys, metal composites consist of layers of different metals.

values.label: Iron
values.definition: A heavy metallic element (Fe) capable of being fashioned into a variety of forms.

values.label: Lead
values.definition: A bluish-white soft malleable ductile plastic but inelastic heavy metallic element (Pb)

values.label: Metal other
values.definition: A non specific material made from metal or metal alloy material.

values.label: Stainless Steel
values.definition: An alloy of steel with chromium and sometimes another element (as nickel or molybdenum) that is practically immune to rusting and ordinary corrosion

values.label: Steel
values.definition: Commercial iron that contains carbon in any amount up to about 1.7 percent as an essential alloying constituent, is malleable when under suitable conditions, and is distinguished from cast iron by its malleability and lower carbon content.

values.label: Tin
values.definition: Tin is a chemical element that is obtained chiefly from the mineral cassiterite, where it occurs as an oxide, SnO2. This silvery, malleable poor metal is not easily oxidized in air, and is used to coat other metals to prevent corrosion. It is used in many alloys, most notably bronze

values.label: Metal zamac
values.definition: Zamac is a family of alloys with a base metal of zinc and alloying elements of aluminium, magnesium, and copper.

values.label: Calcium Carbonate
values.definition: Ground calcium carbonate and precipitated calcium carbonate products serve as functional fillers in plastic and rubber applications. Calcium carbonate is widely used as in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyolefin, polypropylene (PP), polyethylene (PE) and unsaturated polyester resins applications.

values.label: Mineral Other
values.definition: Any other mineral-based material not available in this list.  Should be used as a temporary measure while a proper code is established

values.label: Talc
values.definition: Talc is used to stiffen thermoplastics, mainly polypropylene but also polyethylene and polyamide (Nylon).

values.label: Natural rubber
values.definition: A strong elastic material made by drying the sap from various tropical trees, especially the American rubber tree.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Corrugated Paper
values.definition: Heavy paper with ridges and grooves, used in packing fragile articles.

values.label: Kraft paper
values.definition: Kraft paper is the paper grade with the highest strength. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

values.label: Kraft paper (wet strength)
values.definition: The wet-strength kraft paper has a certain tear strength when wet due to special additives. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

values.label: Molded Pulp
values.definition: Used for producing pulp-based or fibrous products by pressing; example products: egg packages, trays and boxes for fruits and vegetables.

values.label: Paper Other
values.definition: Any other paper-based material not available in this list.  Should be used as a temporary measure while a proper code is established.

values.label: Paper
values.definition: A non-specific sheet material produced by the matting of fibres from wood, rags, or other fibrous materials.  Generally, paper is of a lesser thickness or weight than paperboard.

values.label: Paperboard
values.definition: A non specific material, generally made from cotton or wood, that describe a variety or of board materials used in the production of boxes, folding cartons, and solid fibre and corrugated shipping containers; also termed cardboard

values.label: Rayon Paper
values.definition: Generic term for a manmade fiber derived from regenerated cellulose.

values.label: Plant Leaves
values.definition: Plant leaves, such as banana leaves, including wet or dry leaves. In some cases, leaves are pre-softened by steaming.

values.label: Bioplastic
values.definition: Plastic materials made from biomass, but may have exactly the same properties as ordinary plastic. Sometimes these plastics are biodegradable.

values.label: Plastic Other
values.definition: A non-specific material made of any of numerous organic synthetic or processed materials that are mostly thermoplastic or thermosetting polymers of high molecular weight and that can be made into objects, films, or filaments.

values.label: Thermoplastics
values.definition: A non-specific substance that becomes soft and pliable when heated, without a change in its intrinsic properties. Polystyrene and polyethylene are thermoplastics.

values.label: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS)
values.definition: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) is a thermoplastic polymer.

values.label: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET)
values.definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET) has a very high transparency, is flame retardant and suitable for direct food contact. It is used for packaging of all kinds.

values.label: Biaxially Oriented Polyethylene (BOPE)
values.definition: Biaxially Oriented Polyethylene (BOPE), is a type of flexible plastic film characterised by its good heat seal strength, high puncture strength, high wear resistance, and high tensile strength. The film is used in tote bags, food packaging, pet food packaging, agricultural packaging, etc.

values.label: Polypropylene, longitudinally and laterally stretched (BOPP)
values.definition: Biaxially oriented PP (BOPP) films are characterized by their tear, impact and puncture resistance. The film is mainly used in food packaging, e.g. as candy wrap or wrapping for chocolate bars.

values.label: Cellulose Acetate
values.definition: Cellulose acetate is one of the most important esters of cellulose. Depending on the way it has been processed cellulose acetate can be used for a wide variety of applications, e.g. films, membranes or fibers.

values.label: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET)
values.definition: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET) is a variation of standard PET which has been crystallized for heat resistance, rigidity, and toughness

values.label: Cast Propylene (CPP)
values.definition: Cast Polypropylene (CPP) is an un-oriented film. CPP has stronger tear and impact resistance, cold temperature performance, and heat-sealing qualities than other plastics. CPP film is fully recyclable.

values.label: Expanded Polyethylene
values.definition: EPE is foamed polyethylene, which is a type of environmentally friendly material, that is, pearl cotton like. EPE is made of low-density polyethylene grease through a physical foaming process to produce a non-crosslinked closed cell structure. EPE can be recycled and allows a certain amount of EPE recycled material to be matched in the manufacturing process. Also known as EPE Foam.

values.label: Epoxy
values.definition: Epoxy resins are thermoset polymers which are frequently used as coatings for metal packaging such as soft-drink cans.

values.label: Expanded Polypropylene (EPP)
values.definition: Expanded polypropylene is a polypropylene based foamed material. Provides impact resistance, thermal insulation and water resistance properties.

values.label: Expanded polystyrene (EPS)
values.definition: Expanded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured by expanding spherical beads in a mold, using heat and pressure to fuse the beads together. While each individual bead is a closed cell environment, there are significant open spaces between each bead.

values.label: Ethylene vinyl acetate, (EVA)
values.definition: Ethylene vinyl acetate, a copolymer of 60 to 90% ethylene and 40 to 10% vinyl acetate.  Packaging applications include soft films, coatings, hot melt adhesives, wine cork substitutes, and closure seals for plastic and metal container caps.

values.label: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, (EVOH)
values.definition: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, a copolymer of ethylene and vinyl alcohol. A plastic resin commonly used in food applications to provide barrier to oxygen and other gases.

values.label: High Density Polyethylene (HDPE)
values.definition: High-Density PolyEthylene (HDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum.  A strong, relatively opaque form of polyethylene having a dense structure with few side branches off the main carbon backbone. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

values.label: Polymer ionomer
values.definition: Ionically is a cross-linked polyethylene (ionomer), can be used in combination with PE for its barrier properties.

values.label: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE)
values.definition: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum.  A strong form of polyethylene having a less dense structure with more side branches off the main carbon backbone (on about 2% of the carbon atoms) than HDPE; therefore its tensile strength is lower, and its resilience is higherMade in translucent or opaque variations, it is quite flexible, and tough to the degree of being almost unbreakable.  It is widely used for manufacturing various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, plastic bags for computer components, and various moulded laboratory equipment. Its most common use is in plastic bags.

values.label: Linear Low Density Polyethylene
values.definition: Linear low density polyethylene is a linear polyethylene with a significant number of short branches on the polymer backbone. It is commonly made by copolymerization of ethylene with longer-chain olefins. It is different from LDPE due to the absence of long chain branches which gives it higher tensile strength, impact and puncture resistance than LDPE. Common uses of LLDPE are plastic bags, wraps, stretch wraps, pouches, covers and lids.

values.label: Medium-density Polyethylene
values.definition: Medium-density polyethylene is a type of polyethylene defined by a density range of 0.926-0.940 g/cm3. MDPE is typically used in shrink films, sacks, packaging film and carrier bags.

values.label: Polymer mix
values.definition: A polymer blend or mixture of least two polymers that are blended to create a new material with different physical properties. These tend to be a proprietary mix of polymers and cannot be separated. The individual materials may not be known by the seller.

values.label: Nylon
values.definition: Packaging applications include oven-baking bags (nylon 6 and nylon 66) and barrier layers (MXD6 and nylon 6) for PET and HDPE bottles. Very occasionally, bottles can be made of nylon.

values.label: Oriented polypropylene (OPP)
values.definition: Oriented polypropylene (OPP) is made of a soft polypropylene material which is stretched in a transverse or longitudinal direction (monoaxial) and becomes therefore brittle. Also known as: biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), CAS Registry Number: 9003-07-0

values.label: Polymers Other
values.definition: A non-specific chemical compound or mixture of compounds formed by polymerization and consisting essentially of repeating structural units

values.label: Polyamide (PA)
values.definition: A polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds. Polyamides (PA) occur both naturally and artificially, examples of naturally occurring polyamides are proteins, such as wool and silk. Artificially made polyamides can be  nylons, aramids, and sodium poly(aspartate).

values.label: Polyacrylonitril (PAN)
values.definition: Polyacrylonitril is a organic polymer which is frequently used in fibres for textiles. As fibres the material is frequently referred to as Acrylic.

values.label: Polycarbonate (PC)
values.definition: Polycarbonate, a transparent thermoplastic which is used in a wide variety of applications including CDs and DVDs, eyeglasses, cell phone covers, laptops as well as packaging applications such as bottles.

values.label: Polycaprolactone (PCL)
values.definition: Polycaprolactone is a biodegradable polyester which is also used in in the manufacturing of polyurethanes. It is also used in blends with thermoplastic starch to improve properties and can also be used as a plasticizer to PVC.

values.label: Polyethylene (PE)
values.definition: A thermoplastic composed of the polymers of ethylene.

values.label: Polyethylene Naphthalate (PEN)
values.definition: Polyethylene naphthalate is a polymer with good barrier properties (unlike Polyethylene terephthalate). It is well-suited for production of the amber-colored bottles meant for packing beverages like beer.

values.label: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
values.definition: Polyethylene terephthalate is a thermoplastic polymer resin of the polyester family and is used in synthetic fibers. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

values.label: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG)
values.definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) is a PET modified with glycol, which is characterized by its aqueous properties (viscosity). Applications are found in injection molding.

values.label: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA)
values.definition: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are linear polyesters produced in nature by bacterial fermentation of sugar or lipids.

values.label: Polylactic Acid or Polylactide (PLA)
values.definition: Polylactic acid or Polylactide is a biodegradable, thermoplastic, aliphatic polyester derived from lactic acid.

values.label: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA)
values.definition: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) is often used as a lightweight and shatterproof alternative to glass, due to its transparency, brilliance and scratch resistance, PMMA is therefore often referred to as acrylic glass.

values.label: Polyoxymethylene (POM)
values.definition: Polyoxymethylene (POM) is a thermoplastic with good mechanical properties and high dimensional stability. Fields of application are the automotive industry and electrical engineering, in packaging it is used for e.g. spray cans, gas lighter tanks, gas ampoules. Also known as acetal, polyacetal, and polyformaldehyde.

values.label: Polypropylene (PP)
values.definition: A non-specific material made of various thermoplastic plastics or fibers that are polymers of propylene.

values.label: Polystyrene (PS)
values.definition: A polymer prepared by the polymerization of styrene as the sole monomer

values.label: Polyurethanes (PU)
values.definition: Polyurethanes are primarily thermoset resins which are used in the manufacture of flexible and rigid foams, microcellular foam seals and gaskets, as well as high performance adhesives, surface coatings and sealants. Polyurethane can also be used to make synthetic fibers.

values.label: Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA)
values.definition: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA or PVOH) is a biodegradable and highly water soluble polymer with high gas and grease barrier. Common uses for PVA are paper adhesives, paper coatings, as a self-standing water soluble films as well as blends to improve processability of thermoplastic starch.

values.label: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)
values.definition: A polymer of vinyl chloride used especially for electrical insulation, films, and pipes

values.label: Polyvinylidene Chloride (PVDC)
values.definition: Polyvinylidene chloride is primarily used as a barrier coating to provide barrier against fat, vapour and gases.

values.label: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN)
values.definition: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN) is a copolymer transparent and rigid plastic. Examples of applications are kitchenware and cosmetic packaging.

values.label: Polymer silicone
values.definition: Polymer is generally composed of organic chains linked together by the silicon-oxygen bond. Used in particular for valves. Also know as polysiloxane.

values.label: Thermoplastic Starch (TPS)
values.definition: Thermoplastic starch is obtained through destructurization of natural starch through exposure to shear and heat. TPS is most frequently used in blends with biodegradable synthetic polymers such as PCL and PVA.

values.label: Extruded polystyrene (XPS)
values.definition: Extruded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured using a process of extrusion that produces a homogeneous "closed cell" matrix with each cell fully enclosed by polystyrene walls.

values.label: Rubber
values.definition: A strong elastic synthetic substance made either by improving the qualities of natural rubber or by an industrial process using petroleum and coal products

values.label: Silicon Oxide (SiOx)
values.definition: Coating barrier which can be used in food applications to provide barrier towards gases and moisture and is composed of silicon (Si) and oxygen (O) atoms.

values.label: Vinyl
values.definition: A non-specific polymer of a vinyl compound or a product (as a resin or a textile fiber) made from such a polymer

values.label: Hardboard
values.definition: Hardboard (not to be confused with hardwood), also called High-Density Fiberboard (HDF), is a type of fiberboard, which is similar to particle board and medium-density fiberboard, but is denser, much stronger and harder because it is made out of exploded wood fibers which have been highly compressed. Consequently, the density of hardboard is 31 lbs or more per cubic foot (500 kg/m³)[2] and is usually about 50-65 lbs per cubic foot (800–1040 kg/m³). It differs from particle board in that the bonding of the wood fibers requires no additional materials, although resin is often added. Unlike particle board, it will not split or crack.

values.label: Hardwood
values.definition: A general term referring to any variety of broad-leaved, deciduous trees, and the wood from those trees. The term has nothing to do with the actual hardness of the wood; some hardwoods are softer than certain softwood (evergreen) species.

values.label: Medium density fibreboard
values.definition: Medium-Density Fibreboard (MDF) is an engineered wood product made by breaking down hardwood or softwood residuals into wood fibres, combining them with wax and a resin binder, and forming panels by applying high temperature and pressure. MDF is generally denser than plywood. It is made up of separated fibres, but can be used as a building material similar in application to plywood. It is stronger and much more dense than particle board.

values.label: Oriented strand board (OSB)
values.definition: Oriented Strand Board (OSB), also known as sterling board, sterling OSB, aspenite, and smartply, is an engineered wood particle board formed by adding adhesives and then compressing layers of wood strands (flakes) in specific orientations. OSB may have a rough and variegated surface with the individual strips of around 2.5 × 15 cm (1" × 6"), lying unevenly across each other and comes in a variety of types.

values.label: Wood other
values.definition: A non specific material made from the hard fibrous lignified substance under the bark of trees.

values.label: Particle board
values.definition: Particle Board, also known as particleboard, chipboard, and Low-Density Fiberboard (LDF), is an engineered wood product manufactured from wood chips, sawmill shavings, or sawdust, and a synthetic resin or other suitable binder, which is pressed and extruded. Particle board is a composite material.

values.label: Plywood
values.definition: Plywood, a manufactured wood panel similar to LDF, MDF, and HDF, is made from layering thin sheets of wood. Plywood layers (called veneers or plies) are glued together, with adjacent plies having their wood grain rotated relative to adjacent layers up to 90 degrees.  All plywoods bind resin and wood fibre sheets (cellulose cells are long, strong and thin) to form a composite material.

values.label: Softwood
values.definition: General term used to describe lumber produced from needle and/or cone bearing trees (Conifers).

deprecated_values.label: Wire
deprecated_values.definition:
THIS CODE is being deprecated. 
Please use attribute Package Type Code - A packaging made of a non-specific material in the form of very flexible thread or slender rod.

values.label: Bio-based polymer
values.definition: The packaging material is made from bio-based polymers whole or partially from renewable biological resources, like sugar cane, starch.

values.label: Crude Oil
values.definition: The packaging material is made from crude oil.

values.label: Virgin/new raw material other
values.definition: The packaging material is made from virgin, non-recycled raw materials, such as aluminium or wood.

values.label: Recycled
values.definition: The packaging material is made from post consumer recycled content.

values.label: Composting Organic Recovery
Energy Recovery
values.definition: To allow optimization of energy recovery in a real industry system, the theoretical calorific gain shall be well above zero. To claim energy recovery qnet shall be equal to greater than qnet,min,real as defined for various incineration conditions.  Reference ISO18605:2013(E) Annex A.

values.label: Material Recycling
values.definition: The supplier shall be able to demonstrate that the procedures defined in normative ISO 18604:2013(E) Annexes A and ISO 18604:2013(E) B have been followed in arriving at the final design of the finish

values.label: Other
values.definition: Code value not available in code list.

values.label: Deutscher Mindeststandard
values.definition: The German minimum standard for determining the recyclability of packaging, subject to system packaging pursuant to section 21 (3) VerpackG (Verpackungsgesetz–Packaging Act).

values.label: Entirely recyclable
values.definition: The packaging is fully recyclable. The determination of this information is made by the supplier and is subject to target market regulations or trade organisation guidelines.

values.label: Mostly recyclable
values.definition: The packaging is mostly recyclable. The determination of this information is made by the supplier and is subject to target market regulations or trade organisation guidelines.

values.label: No information about recyclability
values.definition: There is no information about the packaging recyclability.

values.label: Recyclable same type
values.definition: The packaging is recyclable into a packaging of the same type or function. The determination of this information is made by the supplier and is subject to target market regulations or trade organisation guidelines.

values.label: Other
values.definition: Code value not available in code list.

values.label: Post-consumer Recycled Content
values.definition: The ratio of post-consumer recycled material (post-consumer and pre consumer as defined by ISO 14021) to total material used in packaging constituents, packaging components, or packaging systems.

values.label: Pre-consumer Recycled Content
values.definition: The ratio of pre-consumer recycled material (post-consumer and pre consumer as defined by ISO 14021) to total material used in packaging constituents, packaging components, or packaging systems

values.label: Compostable
values.definition: Packaging that can biodegrade generating a relatively homogeneous and stable humus-like substance.

values.label: Energy Recoverable
values.definition: Packaging which allows for a net calorific gain in energy recovery operations.

values.label: Recyclable
values.definition: Packaging material and format which can be diverted from the waste stream through available processes and programmes and can be collected, processed and returned to use in the form of raw materials or products.

values.label: Refillable
values.definition: Packaging that can be reused several times by the consumers instead of being thrown away after a single use.

values.label: Reusable
values.definition: Packaging that has been conceived and designed to accomplished within its life cycle a certain number of trips, rotations or uses for the same purpose for which it was conceived.

values.label: Reusable different function
values.definition: Packaging that has been designed to be reused multiple times by the consumer but for a different purpose, without being part of an organized collection and redistribution system. Example: a plastic container or a glass jar kept at home for personal use.

values.label: Polyethylene Terephthalates
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 1 relates to Polyethylene terephthalates.  These recyclables represent polyester fibres' (Polar Fleece), thermoformed sheet, strapping, soft drink bottles, tote bags, furniture, carpet, panelling and (occasionally) new containers which can be picked up through most curb side recycling programs.

values.label: High-density Polyethylenes
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 2 relates to High-density polyethylenes.  These recyclables represent bottles, grocery bags, milk jugs, recycling bins, agricultural pipe, base cups, car stops, playground equipment, and plastic lumber which can be picked up through most curb side recycling programs, although some allow only those containers with necks.

values.label: Corrugated fibreboard (cardboard)
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 20 relates to corrugated fibreboard (cardboard).

values.label: Mixed paper/Non-corrugated fibreboard
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 21 relates to mixed paper/non-corrugated fibreboard. These recyclable represent magazines, mail.

values.label: Paper
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 22 relates to paper. These recyclables represent letter, printer paper etc.

values.label: Polyvinyl Chlorides
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 3 relates to Polyvinyl chlorides.  These recyclables represent pipe, window profile, siding, fencing, flooring, shower curtains, lawn chairs, non-food bottles and children's toys which can be extensively recycled in Europe.

values.label: Low-density Polyethylenes
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 4 relates to Low-density polyethylenes.  These recyclables represent plastic bags, 6 pack rings, various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, and various moulded laboratory equipment which is not often recycled through curb side programs, but some communities will accept it. Plastic shopping bags can be returned to many stores for recycling.

values.label: Steel
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 40 relates to steel.

values.label: Aluminium
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 41 relates to aluminium.

values.label: Polypropylenes
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 5 relates to Polypropylenes.  These recyclables represent auto parts, industrial fibres, food containers, and dishware which can be recycled through some curb side programs.

values.label: Wood
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 50 relates to wood

values.label: Cork
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 51 relates to cork.

values.label: Polystyrenes
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 6 relates to Polystyrenes.  These recyclables represent desk accessories, cafeteria trays, plastic utensils, toys, video cassettes and cases, clamshell containers, packaging peanuts, and insulation board and other expanded polystyrene products (e.g., Styrofoam) which can be recycled through some curb side programs.

values.label: Cotton
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 60 relates to cotton.

values.label: Jute
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 61 relates to jute.

values.label: Plastics Other
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 7 relates to Other plastics, such as acrylic, nylon, polycarbonate, and polylactic acid (a bioplastic), and multilayer combinations of different plastics.  These recyclables represent Bottles, plastic lumber applications, headlight lenses, and safety shields/glasses which have traditionally not been recycled, though some curb side programs now take them.

values.label: Colourless glass
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 70 relates to colourless glass.

values.label: Green glass
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 71 relates to green glass.

values.label: Brown glass
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 72 relates to brown glass.

values.label: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Miscellaneous Metals
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 80 relates to composite materials paper and fibreboard/miscellaneous metals.

values.label: Composite: Paper/Fibreboard and Plastic
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 81 relates to composite materials paper/fibreboard and plastic.  These recyclables represent consumer packaging, pet food bags, cold store grocery bags, Ice cream containers, cardboard cans, disposable plates.

values.label: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Aluminium
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 82 relates to composite material paper and fibreboard/aluminium.

values.label: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Tinplate
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 83 relates to composite material paper and fibreboard/tinplate.

values.label: Composite: Paper and fibreboard/Plastic/Aluminium
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 84 relates to composite materials paper and cardboard/plastic/aluminium. These recyclables represent liquid storage containers, juice boxes, cardboard cans, cigarette pack liners, gum wrappers, cartage shells for blanks, fireworks colouring material.

values.label: Composite:  Paper and Fibreboard/Plastic /Aluminium/Tinplate
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 84 relates to composite materials paper and fibreboard/plastic/aluminium/tinplate.

values.label: Composite: Card-stock Laminate or Biodegradable Plastic
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 87 relates to composite materials card-stock laminate or biodegradable plastic. These recyclables represent laminating material, special occasion cards, bookmarks, business cards, flyers/advertising.

values.label: Composite: Plastic/Aluminium
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 90 relates to composite materials plastic/aluminium.

values.label: Composite: Plastic/Tinplate
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 91 relates to composite materials plastic/tinplate.

values.label: Composite: Plastic/Miscellaneous Metals
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 92 relates to composition materials plastic/miscellaneous metals.

values.label: Composite: Glass/Plastic
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 95 relates to composite materials glass/plastic.

values.label: Composite: Glass/Aluminium
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 96 relates to composite materials glass/aluminium.

values.label: Composite: Glass/Tinplate
values.definition: Recycling scheme code 97 relates to composite materials glass/tinplate.

values.label: Bar
values.definition: A relatively long, evenly shaped piece of some solid substance

values.label: Coil
values.definition: A spiral structure made by winding a material into a series of loops. A coil may or may not have a spindle around which the loops are formed.

values.label: Cone
values.definition:
A cone is a three-dimensional geometric
shape that tapers smoothly from a flat, round base to a point.

values.label: Cylindrical
values.definition: A long shape that has a circular base and an equally-sized circular top.

values.label: Polygon
values.definition: A plane figure that is bounded by a closed path or circuit composed of a finite sequence of equally-sized straight line segments. A polygon may have a varying number of segments or ‘faces’ resulting in different configurations, for example a 5-faced polygon: pentagon, 6-faced: hexagon, 8-faced: octagon, 12-faced: dodecahedron, etc.

values.label: Rectangular
values.definition: A closed planar quadrilateral with four right angles.

values.label: Spherical
values.definition: A perfectly round geometrical object in three-dimensional space, such as the shape of a round ball. Like a circle in two dimensions, a perfect sphere is completely symmetrical around its centre, with all points on the surface lying the same distance from the centre point.

values.label: Tablet
values.definition: The result of different materials being compressed into a solid block usually of small dimensions.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Shape is not currently specified in the list. To be used as a temporary means until a specific missing value is added to the list.

values.label: Sweatpant

values.label: Tap

values.label: Track

values.label: Trouser

values.label: Accepting Party
values.definition: Party accepting goods, products, services etc.

values.label: Bill of Lading Receipient
values.definition: Party to receive Bill of Lading.

values.label: Bill To
values.definition: Party which receives goods and invoice.

values.label: Brand Owner
values.definition: The organisation that owns the specifications of the Party regardless of where and by whom it is manufactured is normally responsible for the allocation of the Global Trade Item Number (GTIN).

values.label: Breeder
values.definition: The party which breeds the animal.

values.label: Broker Agent
values.definition: A person who buys or sells for another entity without having title to the property.

values.label: Buyer
values.definition: Party to which merchandise are sold.

values.label: Buyers Agent Representative
values.definition: Third party who arranged the purchase of merchandise on behalf of the actual buyer.

values.label: Carrier
values.definition: A company, which physically transports goods from one place to another.

values.label: Central Payment Service
values.definition: Master of the conveyance.  A party providing central (or consolidated payment) services.

values.label: Checking Party
values.definition: Party or contact designated on behalf of carrier or his agent to establish the actual figures for quantities, weight, volume and/or (cube) measurements of goods or containers which are to appear in the transport contract and on which charges will be based

values.label: Cheque Order
values.definition: Party to which the cheque will be ordered, when different from the beneficiary.

values.label: Consignee
values.definition: Party to which goods are consigned.

values.label: Consolidator
values.definition: Party consolidating various consignments, payments etc.

values.label: Consumer
values.definition: The end user of a trade item or a service.

values.label: Cooperative
values.definition: An autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise.

values.label: Corporate Identity
values.definition: Identity of the party to whom all other parties of the same commercial organization are linked.

values.label: Customs
values.definition: Identification of customs authority relevant to the transaction or shipment.

values.label: Customs Broker
values.definition: Party responsible for the preparation of documents and/or electronic submissions, the calculation on behalf of the client of taxes, duties and excises, and facilitating communication between the importer/exporter and governmental authorities.

values.label: Cutter
values.definition: One engaged in carving meat (In EANCOM as Meat Cutter).

values.label: Declarants Agent Representative
values.definition: Any natural or legal person who makes a declaration to an official body on behalf of another natural or legal person, where legally permitted (CCC).

values.label: Delivery Party
values.definition: Party to which goods are delivered.

values.label: Designer
values.definition: A Party who designs.

values.label: Despatch Party
values.definition: Party where goods are collected or taken over by the carrier.

values.label: Distributor
values.definition: Party distributing goods, financial payments or documents.

values.label: Dock Door
values.definition: A door or collection of doors where trucks or rail cars are loaded (shipping) or unloaded (receiving). Used to load or unload trade items for logistics.

values.label: Empty Equipment Despatch Party
values.definition: Party from whose premises empty equipment will be or has been despatched.

values.label: Empty Equipment Return Party
values.definition: Party to whose premises empty equipment will be or has been returned.

values.label: Equipment Owner
values.definition: Owner of equipment (container, etc.).

values.label: Exporter
values.definition: Party who makes - or on whose behalf a Customs clearing agent or other authorized person makes - an export declaration. This may include a manufacturer, seller or other person. Within a Customs union, consignor may have the same meaning as exporter

values.label: Factror
values.definition: A party that purchases financial receiving instruments e.g. invoices

values.label: Farm
values.definition: Land used wholly or partly for agricultural production purposes, without having regard to title, legal form or size. It includes land rented, land owned and land being effectively used by the management under whatever type of other arrangement.

values.label: Farmer
values.definition: An individual engaged in agriculture, raising living organisms for food or raw materials.

values.label: Fattener
values.definition: The Party which fattens the animal.

values.label: Freight Forwarder
values.definition: A person or firm that arranges for a pick up or deliver goods by a carrier on instructions of a shipper or consignee from or to a point by various necessary conveyances and common carriers.

values.label: Goods Owner
values.definition: The party which owns the goods.

values.label: Grower
values.definition: A party which is responsible for the growth or production of the unit specifically refers to vegetation. This organization may or may not be a producer or packer.

values.label: Head Office
values.definition: The executive or main office of an enterprise.

values.label: Importer
values.definition: Party who makes - or on whose behalf a Customs clearing agent or other authorized person makes - an import declaration. This may include a person who has possession of the goods or to whom the goods are consigned.

values.label: Information Provider
values.definition: The Party providing the information contained in the document.

values.label: Insurer
values.definition: A person or company offering insurance policies for premiums.

values.label: Intermediary Bank 1
values.definition: A financial institution between the ordered bank and the beneficiary's bank.

values.label: Intermediary Bank 2
values.definition: A financial institution between the ordered bank and the beneficiary's bank.

values.label: Inventory Controler
values.definition: To specifically identify the party in charge of inventory control.

values.label: Inventory Reporting Party
values.definition: Party reporting inventory information.

values.label: Invoicee
values.definition: Party which receives an invoice.

values.label: Issuer of Invoice
values.definition: Party which issues an invoice.

values.label: Logistics Service Provider
values.definition: An umbrella term for an entity, which provides a combination of many different logistics services for another entity.

values.label: Manufacturer of Goods
values.definition: Party who manufactures the goods.

values.label: Manufacturing Plant
values.definition: A physical location consisting of one or more buildings with facilities for manufacturing.

values.label: Mark For
values.definition: The ultimate destination of a unit load or transport package of goods where the Ship-To is a different location.

values.label: Message From
values.definition: Party where the message comes from.

values.label: Message Receipient
values.definition: Party receiving the message.

values.label: Mincer
values.definition: One engaged in the cutting or chopping of meat into very small pieces.

values.label: Operating Division
values.definition: An entity that is part of another entity. For example, a Regional Marketing Office. Operating Divisions may have multiple days and times of operation.

values.label: Operator
values.definition: A person or persons who own or operate a business establishment, which services consumers directly. For example a restaurant owner as part of a chain or an independent operation.

values.label: Ordering Party
values.definition: To be used only if ordering party and buyer are not identical.

values.label: Owner of Equipment
values.definition: Party who owns equipment.

values.label: Owner of Means of Transport
values.definition: Party owning the means of transport. Not a synonym of carrier

values.label: Party Declaring the Value Added Tax
values.definition: A code to identify the party who is responsible for declaring the Value Added Tax (VAT) on the sale of goods or services.

values.label: Party For Whom Item is Ultimately Intended
values.definition: Party for whom item is ultimately intended.

values.label: Party Receiving Private Data
values.definition: The party who is allowed access to master data information by the data owner when the data is viewed as private.

values.label: Party Recovering the Value Added Tax
values.definition: A code to identify the party who is eligible to recover the Value Added Tax (VAT) on the sale of goods or services.

values.label: Party to Receive All Documents
values.definition: A party which is named to be the recipient of all documents.

values.label: Party To Receive Commercial invoice
values.definition: Party to whom payment for a commercial invoice or bill should be remitted.

values.label: Party to Receive Electronic Memo of the Invoice
values.definition: Party being informed about invoice issue (via EDI).

values.label: Party To Receive Freight Bill
values.definition: Party to whom the freight bill should be sent.

values.label: Party To Receive Refund
values.definition: Party to whom a refund is given.

values.label: Payee
values.definition: Party, which receives payment.

values.label: Payer
values.definition: Party which initiates payment.

values.label: Point of Sale
values.definition: Refers to the retail type checkout where bar code symbols are normally scanned.

values.label: Price Location Party
values.definition: A party to which a price for a trade item is applicable. Within the context of GDSN Price Synchronization, it is also known as the ‘Price Location’ which is a GLN.

values.label: Proxy
values.definition: A company that is selected by the Brand Owner to maintain their baseline attributes and Administrative Records in the GDSN.

values.label: Public Warehouse
values.definition: A building, or a part of one, where storage space is offered to other companies for compensation (fee), for the storage of their goods, merchandise, etc.

values.label: Purchase Order Receiver
values.definition: The party that receives the purchase order for the goods or services.

values.label: Registered Agent
values.definition: The party having legal responsibility for the product in the target market for example a company to which market authorization has been issued.

values.label: Remit To
values.definition: Party to whom funds are directed for payment of a commercial invoice.

values.label: Returnable Asset Service Centre
values.definition: The location where a returnable asset is serviced.

values.label: Seller
values.definition: Party which sells products or services to a buyer.

values.label: Service privider
values.definition: A party providing services for another party (e.g re- packing supplier’s products).

values.label: Ship From
values.definition: Party from where goods will be or have been shipped.

values.label: Ship To
values.definition: Party which receives goods and invoices.

values.label: Slaughterer
values.definition: The Party who has undertaken or will undertake a slaughter.

values.label: Store
values.definition: A physical entity that sells trade items to a consumer.

values.label: Substitute Supplier
values.definition: Party which may be in a position to supply products or services should the main usual supplier be unable to do so.

values.label: Supplier
values.definition: A party that provides goods or services.

values.label: Trade Item Return Location
values.definition: A code to qualify the locations to which a retailer or wholesaler can send unsold product. Examples are expired product, damaged, reclamation or general product returns.

values.label: Transportation Carrier
values.definition: Party undertaking or arranging transport of goods between named points.

values.label: Visiting Address
values.definition: An enterprise’s physical location where guests are received during set working hours

values.label: Warehouse And Or Depot
values.definition: Industrial department of a company equipped with appropriate equipment and fit-tings in which goods are stored in appropriate conditions.

values.label: Warehouse Keeper
values.definition: Party taking responsibility for goods entered into a warehouse.

values.label: Wholesaler
values.definition: Seller of articles, often in large quantities, to be retailed by others.

values.label: Animal Print
values.definition: Animal print is a clothing and fashion style in which the garment is made to resemble the pattern of the skin and fur of an animal such as a leopard, zebra, tiger, snake, giraffe, alligator, etc.

values.label: Architectural
values.definition: The product has an architectural pattern. This is the idea of capturing architectural design ideas as archetypal and reusable descriptions.

values.label: Bubble Foam
values.definition: The product has a bubble/foam pattern. A soap bubble is an extremely thin film of soapy water enclosing air that forms a hollow sphere with an iridescent surface. Foam is an object formed by trapping pockets of gas in a liquid or solid.

values.label: Camouflage
values.definition: The product has a camouflage pattern. Originally used to protect military force personnel and equipment from observation by enemy forces, today also common in fashion.

values.label: Crack
values.definition: The pattern of dense cracking formed on the surface or appearance on the product.

values.label: Floral
values.definition: Floral is a term used to describe something that is relative or related to the flower, that concerns the flower or its characteristics.

values.label: Gingham
values.definition: The product has a gingham pattern: Gingham is woven like Pepita body-bindingly, but with wider body ridges. This creates such wide black-and-white diagonal stripes when white warp and black weft threads collide that the blocks no longer appear clearly delimited, but merge with the adjacent blocks of the same colour into a shape.

values.label: Gradient
values.definition: The product has a gradient colour.  A colour gradient (sometimes called a colour ramp or colour progression) specifies a range of position-dependent colours. Example: Pink transitioning to Dark Red.

values.label: Herringbone
values.definition: The product has a herringbone pattern. An arrangement of rectangles, so named for a fancied resemblance to the bones of a fish such as herring. The blocks can be rectangles or parallelograms.

values.label: Houndstooth
values.definition: The product has a houndstooth pattern. Created in canvas-binding fabrics, when the chain and the shot each have two thread-wide stripes. The encounter of white warp threads with black weft threads gives the impression of tiny wind turbines.

values.label: Mottled
values.definition: The product has a mottled pattern. Irregular marks, spots, streaks, blotches or patches of different shades or colours.

values.label: Other Pattern
values.definition: The product has a pattern but has not been specified in this code list. This code will be used for any new pattern that is not specified.

values.label: Paisley
values.definition: The product has a paisley pattern. An abstract, decorative fabric pattern that represents the Persian Boteh pattern. In its basic form, it represents a leaf with a pointed, curved end, in the style of a large comma and recalls the Gothic fish bubble ornament.

values.label: Pepita
values.definition: The product has a pepita pattern: Created when warp and firing strips of mostly eight threads wide are woven body-bindingly, typically as 2/1 bodies. Those blocks in which white warp threads meet black weft threads appear diagonally striped.

values.label: Photoprint
values.definition: The product has a photo printed on its material.

values.label: Pinstripe
values.definition: The product has a pinstripe pattern. Very thin stripes of any colour running in parallel. The colour-highlighted warp threads are incorporated into a base fabric, which appear as fine longitudinal strips.

values.label: Plaid
values.definition: The product has a plaid pattern. Squares and lines known as a sett. The plaid pattern best characterized by horizontal and vertical lines intersecting each other that together form different sizes of squares or checks all throughout the fabric is also known as Tartan or the Scottish plaid.

values.label: Polka Dot
values.definition: The product has a polka dot pattern. Equally large, filled, regularly arranged circles. The dots are not woven, but printed on the fabric, sometimes embroidered.

values.label: Spiral
values.definition: The product has a spiral pattern that is a flat curve that describes revolutions around a fixed point (pole) as it moves further and further away from it.

values.label: Stripes
values.definition: A stripe(s) pattern is a long, narrow band or strip differing in colour or texture from the surface on either side of it.

values.label: Symmetry
values.definition: 'The product has a symmetrical pattern that has a regular distribution of parts or objects on either side of an axis or around a centre point

values.label: Tiling
values.definition: The product has a tiling pattern. Tiling is a two-dimensional pattern resembling a tiled surface.

values.label: Turbulence
values.definition: The product has a turbulence pattern that is a formation of vortices in a fluid. Many natural patterns are shaped by this complexity, including vortex streets, other effects of turbulent flow such as meanders in rivers. Or nonlinear interaction of the system.

values.label: Unicoloured
values.definition: The product has a unicoloured pattern (one unique colour for the product). Also known in some markets as Solids.

values.label: Wave, Dune
values.definition: The product has a wave/dune pattern. Wave is inequality of the surface of a liquid expanse (sea, lake...) due to currents, wind; mass of water that rises and falls. And dune is mound, a hill of fine sand formed by the wind on the seaside or in the interior of deserts.

values.label: Eau de Cologne
values.definition: Eau de Cologne with a concentration of fragrances between 3 - 8 % (typical ~5%) within the mixture. The percentage is not precisely defined and may vary between prestige and mass market products as well as from region to region.

values.label: Eau de Parfum
values.definition: Eau de Parfum (EdP) or Parfum de Toilette (PdT) with a concentration of fragrances between 10 - 20 % (typical ~15%) within the mixture. The percentage is not precisely defined and may vary between prestige and mass market products as well as from region to region.

values.label: Eau de Solide
values.definition: Eau de Solide with a concentration of fragrances between 1 - 3 % within the mixture. The percentage is not precisely defined and may vary between prestige and mass market products as well as from region to region. Also known as Eau Fraiche.

values.label: Eau de Toilette
values.definition: Eau de Toilette with a concentration of fragrances between 5 - 15 % (typical ~10%) within the mixture. The percentage is not precisely defined and may vary between prestige and mass market products as well as from region to region.

values.label: Extrait Parfum
values.definition: Perfume extract (extrait) with a concentration of fragrances between 15 - 40 % (typical ~20%) within the mixture. The percentage is not precisely defined and may vary between prestige and mass market products as well as from region to region. Also known as Perfume.
