values.label: Gas
values.definition: A material, which has a vapor pressure greater than 300 kPa (43.5 psia) at 50°C (122°F) or is completely gaseous at 20°C (68°F) at a standard pressure of 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).  Including: ·       Aerosol:  Any non-refillable receptacle containing a gas compressed, liquefied or dissolved under pressure, the sole purpose of which is to expel a nonpoisonous (other than a Division 6.1 Package Group III Material) liquid, paste, or powder and fitted with a self-closing release device allowing the contents to be ejected by the gas. ·       Asphyxiant Gas:  A gas, which dilutes or replaces the oxygen normally in the atmosphere. ·       Compressed Gas in Solution:  A non-liquefied compressed gas, which is dissolved in a solvent. ·       Liquefied Compressed Gas: A gas, which when packaged under pressure for transportation is partially liquid at temperatures above -50° C (-58° F).  A liquefied compressed gas is further categorized as follows:  o    High Pressure Liquefied Gas: A gas with a critical temperature between -50 °C (-58° F) and + 65° C (149° F). o    Low Pressure Liquefied Gas:  A gas with a critical temperature above + 65° C (149° F).  ·       Non-Liquefied Compressed Gas:  A gas, which when packaged under pressure for transportation is entirely gaseous at -50° C (-58° F) with a critical temperature less than or equal to -50° C (-58° F). Oxidizing Gas:  A gas, which may, generally by providing oxygen, cause or contribute to the combustion of other material more than air does.

values.label: Liquid
values.definition: A material, other than an elevated temperature material, with a melting point or initial melting point of 20°C (68°F) or lower at a standard pressure of 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).  A viscous material for which a specific melting point cannot be determined must be subjected to the procedures specified in ASTM D 4359 "Standard Test Method for Determining Whether a Material is Liquid or Solid”.

values.label: Mixed
values.definition: Any combination of the other states.

values.label: Refrigerant or Dispersant Gas
values.definition: All non-toxic refrigerant gases, dispersant gases (fluorocarbons) and mixtures thereof, or any other compressed gas having a vapor pressure not exceeding 260 psia at 54°C (130°F), used only as a refrigerant, dispersant or blowing agent.

values.label: Refrigerated Liquid
values.definition: Cryogenic Liquid . A refrigerated liquefied gas having a boiling point colder than -90°C (-130°F) at 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia).

values.label: Solid
values.definition: A material that does not meet the definition of a liquid or gas (i.e., powder, pellet, flake).

values.label: Air
values.definition: Air is a mixture of gases that make up the Earth's atmosphere. atmosphere.

values.label: Diesel
values.definition: Any liquid fuel used in diesel engines. The most common is a specific fractional distillate of petroleum fuel oil, but alternatives that are not derived from petroleum, such as biodiesel, biomass to liquid (BTL) or gas to liquid (GTL) diesel, are increasingly being developed and adopted.

values.label: Electricity
values.definition: A movement or flow of electrically charged particles, typically measured in amperes.

values.label: Energy
values.definition: Energy is a property of objects which can be transferred to other objects or converted into different forms.

values.label: Fuel Oil
values.definition: Any liquid petroleum product that is burned in a furnace or boiler for the generation of heat or used in an engine for the generation of power, except oils having a flash point of approximately 40 °C (104 °F) and oils burned in cotton or wool-wick burners. Fuel oil is made of long hydrocarbon chains, particularly alkanes, cycloalkanes and aromatics. The term fuel oil is also used in a stricter sense to refer only to the heaviest commercial fuel that can be obtained from crude oil, heavier than gasoline and naphtha.

values.label: Gasoline
values.definition: Gasoline or petrol is a transparent petroleum-derived liquid that is primarily used as a fuel in internal combustion engines. It consists mostly of organic compounds obtained by the fractional distillation of petroleum, enhanced with a variety of additives. Some gasolines also contain ethanol as an alternative fuel. In North America the term "gasoline" is often shortened in colloquial usage to "gas" but some people use the term "petrol".

values.label: Natural Gas
values.definition: A naturally occurring hydrocarbon gas mixture consisting primarily of methane, with other hydrocarbons, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and hydrogen sulfide. Natural gas is widely used as an important energy source in many applications including heating buildings, generating electricity, providing heat and power to industry, as fuel for vehicles and as a chemical feedstock in the manufacture of products such as plastics and other commercially important organic chemicals.

values.label: Other
values.definition: A physical resource other than those listed in the Physical Resource Type Code List.

values.label: Propane
values.definition: A three-carbon alkane with the molecular formula C3H8, normally a gas, but compressible to a transportable liquid. A by-product of natural gas processing and petroleum refining, it is commonly used as a fuel for engines, oxy-gas torches, barbecues, portable stoves, and residential central heating. Propane is one of a group of liquefied petroleum gases. The others include butane, propylene, butadiene, butylene, isobutylene and mixtures thereof.

values.label: Water
values.definition: A chemical substance with the chemical formula H2O. A water molecule contains one oxygen and two hydrogen atoms connected by covalent bonds. Water is a liquid at ambient conditions, but it often co-exists on Earth with its solid state, ice, and gaseous state (water vapor or steam). Water also exists in a liquid crystal state near hydrophilic surfaces.

Quantitative relation that describes the amount of the base molecule within its salt                   Divides the mass of the base by the mass of the salt.

Testosterone Propionate package 100g 
Testosterone Base amount

•  Example for the Pure Base Ratio
Testosterone base (C19H28O2) molecular mass: 288.43 g/mol
Testosterone propionate (C22H32O3) molecular mass: 344.49 g/mol
288.43/344.49 = 0.8373 (Ratio).

values.label: Pallet 400 X 300 mm

values.label: Australian Pallet
values.definition: Standardised square pallet with dimensions of 1165 x 1165 mm, which perfectly fits in the RACE container of the Australian Railway.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Platform of Unspecified Weight or Dimension: Pallet level hierarchy is being shipped on a shipping platform of unknown dimensions or unknown weight. The platform weight or dimension may differ within the same shipment. All other values including null would indicate that the weight and dimensions include the shipping platform.

values.label: Pallet 1000 X 600 mm
values.definition: Half size flat pallet with dimensions of 1000 x 600 mm. 1/2 ISO 2 Pallet.

values.label: Block Pallet
values.definition: A pallet constructed with blocks at the corners and middle to which three stringers boards are attached with top deck boards attached perpendicular to the stringers. Block pallets can have a variety of bottom deck configurations; no bottom boards, boards parallel to the top deck boards or a full parameter base similar to a picture frame.

values.label: Dolly
values.definition: A portable, horizontal, rigid platform on wheels or rollers, used as a base for assembling, storing, stacking, handling and transporting goods as a unit, suitable for manually positioning.

values.label: Pallet 1000 X 1200 mm
values.definition: Standard EuroPallet (EUR3) size with dimensions of 1000 x 1200 mm. EUR 3 Pallet

values.label: Horizontal Drum Pallet
values.definition:
A rigid platform with integrated restraints to prevent horizontally orientated cylindrical containers from slipping.
Horizontal Drum Pallets are used for assembling, storing, stacking, handling and transporting cylindrical containers, e.g. drums, barrels, or kegs, as a unit load, suitable for lifting by a forklift, pallet jack, or other jacking device.

values.label: IBC Pallet
values.definition:
An IBC Pallet is a Rigid Intermediate Bulk Container (RIBC) that is attached to a pallet or has the pallet integrated into the RIBC. The container is used for the transport and storage of fluids and other bulk materials. The construction of the IBC container and the materials used are chosen depending on the application. There are various types available in the market place. Foldable (collapsible) IBC Container,
Plastic composite IBC Container, Wire Cage IBC Container,
Steel IBC Container, and Stainless steel IBC Container

values.label: Pallet 1219 X 1016 mm
values.definition: ISO 3 Pallet Flat pallet with dimensions of 1219 x 1016 mm (48 x 40 In)  primarily used in the Americas region. ISO 3 Pallet

values.label: Pallet 1067 X 1067 mm
values.definition: Flat pallet with dimensions of 1067 x 1067 mm (42 x 42 in) primarily used in the Americas region. ISO 4 Pallet.

values.label: Pallet 1100 X 1100 mm
values.definition: Flat pallet with dimensions of 1100 x 1100 mm primarily used in the Asia Pacific region.  Also referred to as the "T11" pallet. ISO 5 Pallet

values.label: Pallet 1140 X 1140 mm
values.definition: Flat pallet with dimensions of 1140 x 1140 mm primarily used in the European region. ISO 6 Pallet.

values.label: Skid
values.definition: A group of parallel wooden runners attached to the undersides of boxes, crates, and machines to allow entry of platform trucks or fork lift tines.

values.label: Stringer Pallet
values.definition: A pallet constructed with boards (stringers) on edge to which the top deck and bottom deck boards are attached. The stringers may be notched to facilitate four way entry and lifting by a fork lift or other pallet jacking device.

values.label: Vertical Drum Pallet
values.definition: A rigid platform with integrated restraints to prevent vertically orientated cylindrical containers from slipping. Vertical Drum Pallets are used for assembling, storing, stacking, handling and transporting cylindrical containers, e.g. drums, barrels, or kegs, as a unit load, suitable for lifting by a forklift, pallet jack, or other jacking device.

values.label: Pallet 800 X 400 mm
values.definition: One third size of the standard Euro Pallet size with dimensions of 800 x 400 mm. 1/3 European Pallet.

values.label: 1/2 ISO 3 Pallet
values.definition: Half size flat pallet with dimensions of 610 x 1016 mm (24 x 40 In); primarily used in the Americas region.

values.label: 1/4 ISO 3 Pallet
values.definition: Quarter size flat pallet with dimensions of 610 x 508 mm (24 x 20 In); primarily used in the Americas region.

values.label: Custom Platform
values.definition: A portable, horizontal, rigid platform used as a base for assembling, storing, stacking, handling and transporting goods as a unit load, suitable for lifting by a forklift, pallet jack, or other jacking device.

values.label: Pallet 1000 x 1100 mm
values.definition: Pallet 1000 x 1100 mm (100cms X 110cms). Standard sized pallet of dimensions 100 centimetres by 110 centimetres (cms). EDIFACT X9. This is contained in Recommendation 21 as AH https://www.unece.org/uncefact/codelistrecs.html

values.label: Double mobilrack
values.definition: A portable, horizontal, perforated metal platform for storing, stacking and handling transporting goods as unit load, with dimensions 2025 x 1180 mm, suitable for lifting by a forklift, pallet jack, or other jacking device. Fits in the space of  2 EUR pallets.

values.label: Single mobilrack
values.definition:
A portable, horizontal, perforated metal platform for storing, stacking and handling transporting goods as unit load, with dimensions 1545 x 1180 mm, suitable for lifting by a forklift, pallet jack, or other jacking device. 
Fits in the space of  1 EUR pallet.

values.label: Cage
values.definition: A cage container or cage pallet is a type of storage or transportation unit designed with a rigid framework of bars or mesh, resembling a cage. It is typically used to securely hold, protect, and transport goods, materials while allowing for ventilation, visibility, and containment.

values.label: Slip sheet
values.definition: A firm sheet of plastic, cardboard or other material which may be hooked or attached to a forklift or other transportation equipment. The slip sheet is used to pull products stacked on top of it. Use packaging dimension attributes to specify the size of the slip sheet.

values.label: Non-palletised goods
values.definition: Indication that the unit is despatched without a standardised layer (pattern) or platform type, e.g. individually packed and despatched.

values.label: Floor Loaded (Container)
values.definition: A shipping container of freight that is loaded with freight from the floor up, rather than on pallets. A full floor-loaded container can hold more freight than a palletized load.

values.label: Bare Stem No Operator
values.definition: This control is a peg or stem extending from the unit. There is no handle or lever on the end of the stem.

values.label: Cross Handwheel
values.definition: The control is a device, which resembles a cross or "+", which when attached to the stem can be turned to operate the unit.

values.label: Electric Actuators
values.definition: An electronic actuator converts energy (in the form of electricity) into motion. The motion can be rotary or linear, depending on the type of actuator.

values.label: Extended Lever Handle
values.definition: The control is a flat piece of material made such as for one end to fit over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit. The unit is considered an extended lever as it has another piece of material into which the stem is inserted thereby causing the handle to be set away from the unit it operates

values.label: Extended Lever Handle With Memory Stop
values.definition: The control is a flat piece of material made to fit over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit. The unit is considered an extended lever as it has another piece of material into which the stem is inserted thereby causing the handle to be set away from the unit it operates. Memory stop is a device which allows the user to set the range of motion allowable for the handle.

values.label: Extended Rpund Handle
values.definition: The control is a circular device which when attached to the stem can be turned to operate the unit. The unit is considered an extended lever as it has another piece of material into which the stem is inserted thereby causing the handle to be set away from the unit it operates.

values.label: Gear Operator
values.definition: The control is a device which contains a gear box and having a circular handle, thereby increasing the number of turns of the handle required to change the direction of the closure member, and reducing the force needed to operate the unit.

values.label: Horizontal Chain Lever Handle
values.definition: The control is a bar attached to a unit, designed to be mounted horizontally. A chain is attached on each end of the bar. By pulling on one chain or the other, the unit can be set into operation.

values.label: Insulation Handle
values.definition: The control is a device comprised of non-conductive materials which can be turned to operate the unit even when thermal pipe insulation is affixed around the unit.

values.label: Lever Handle
values.definition: The control is a flat piece of material made such as for one end to fit over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit.

values.label: Lever Lock Operator
values.definition: The control is a long handle with a catch mechanism. The position lock can be used to set the valve in the full open or full closed position. This type of control may or may not have the ability to be locked with a padlock.

values.label: Locking Lever Handle
values.definition: The control is a flat piece of material made such as for one end to fit over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit. The lever has a secondary piece of material, which when engaged can hold the lever in one position. This type of control may or may not have the ability to be locked with a padlock. The control is a flat piece of material made such as for one end to fit over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit. The lever has a secondary piece of material, which when engaged can hold the lever in one position. This type of control may or may not have the ability to be locked with a padlock.

values.label: Lockshield Operator
values.definition: The control is a stem with a keyed end. The control is operated by a lock shield key. The Key can be a simple as an allen key or more complex depending on the security required.

values.label: Pneumatic Actuators
values.definition: A pneumatic actuator converts energy (in the form of compressed air, typically) into motion. The motion can be rotary or linear, depending on the type of actuator.

values.label: Position Lock Operator
values.definition: The control is a long handle with a catch mechanism. The position lock can be used to set the valve in any position or as a memory stop so the valve may be reopened to the previous position. This type of control may or may not have the ability to be locked with a padlock.

values.label: Round Handle
values.definition: The control is a circular device which when attached to the stem can be turned to operate the unit.

values.label: Slotted
values.definition: A groove or slot which allows for screwdrivers to be used to operate the control.

values.label: Solenoid
values.definition: A solenoid is a transducer device which converts energy into linear motion.

values.label: Solid Tee Operator
values.definition: The control is a piece of material in the shape of a "T" in which the stem can be inserted. The Tee can then be rotated to operate the unit.

values.label: Square Operating Nut
values.definition: The control comprises a nut at the top of the stem. This nut is square in shape. Turning the nut turns the stem causing the unit to operate.

values.label: Vertical Chain Lever Handle
values.definition: The control is a bar attached to a unit, designed to be mounted vertically. A chain is attached on each end of the bar. By pulling on one chain or the other, the unit can be set into operation.

values.label: Wing Handle
values.definition: The control is a flat piece of material made such that the center of the device can over the stem and can be turned to operate the unit. The section of the bar are bent allowing for an easier grip and resemble wings.

values.label: Ansi
values.definition: American National Standards Institute (ANSI) oversees the creation, promulgation and use of thousands of norms and guidelines that directly impact businesses in nearly every sector: from acoustical devices to construction equipment, from dairy and livestock production to energy distribution, and many more. ANSI is also actively engaged in accrediting programs that assess conformance to standards.- http://www.ansi.org/

values.label: Asme
values.definition: The American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) is a professional body, specifically an engineering society, focused on mechanical engineering. The organization's stated vision is to be the premier organization for promoting the art, science and practice of mechanical and multidisciplinary engineering and allied sciences to the diverse communities throughout the world. Its stated mission is to promote and enhance the technical competency and professional well-being of its members, and through quality programs and activities in mechanical engineering, better enable its practitioners to contribute to the well-being of humankind. Http://www.asme.org/

values.label: Astm
values.definition: American Society for Testing and Materials International (ASTM) specification documents, test methods, classifications, practices, and guides. These standards describe the characteristics of materials, systems, products, and services. ASTM documents are divided into nine sections, Metals, Construction, Paints, Petroleum Products, Plastics, Textiles, Rubber & Electric Insulating Materials, General Test Methods, and Miscellaneous. ASTM technical committees are made up of professionals from around the globe who develop ASTM standards. There are over 130 ASTM technical committees covering diverse industry areas ranging from metals to the environment. http://www.astm.org

values.label: Cispi
values.definition: Cast Iron Soil Pipe Institute (CISPI) The Institute is dedicated to aiding and improving the plumbing industry. Through the preparation and distribution of technical reports, we seek to advance interest in the manufacture, use and distribution of cast iron soil pipe and fittings, and through a program of research and the cooperative effort of soil pipe manufacturers, we strive to improve the industry's products, achieve standardization of cast iron soil pipe and fittings, and provide a continuous program of product testing, evaluation and development. Assurance that pipe and fittings meet the approved standards and tolerances of the Institute is provided either by Ç®; or the CI NO-HUB® trademarks which are the collective marks all member companies may place on their products. www.cispi.org

values.label: Csa
values.definition: Canadian Standards Association (CSA) As a membership-based association serving business, industry, government and consumers in Canada and the global marketplace. As a solutions-oriented organization, CSA works in Canada and around the world to develop standards that address real needs, such as enhancing public health and safety. Advancing the quality of life. Helping to preserve the environment. Facilitating trade. CSA helps people understand standards through education and information products and services.

values.label: Iapmo
values.definition: International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials (IAPMO) As a membership-based association, IAPMO is proud to utilize an open consensus process in the development of our flagship Uniform Plumbing Code® and Uniform Mechanical Code®. These codes are established through scientific research, debate, and analysis, strengthening our position at the forefront of the plumbing and mechanical industries. Www.iapmo.org

values.label: Iso
values.definition: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) ISO is a non-governmental organization that forms a bridge between the public and private sectors. On the one hand, many of its member institutes are part of the governmental structure of their countries, or are mandated by their government.

values.label: Mss
values.definition: The Manufacturers Standardization Society (MSS) of the Valve and Fittings Industry is a non-profit technical association organized for development and improvement of industry, national and international codes and standards for: Valves, Valve Actuators, Pipe Fittings, Valve Modification, Flanges, Pipe Hangers, and Associated Seals. The primary function of MSS is to provide its members the means to develop engineering standard practices for the use and benefit of the industry and users of its products. The Society, the only organization dedicated solely to the technical needs of the industry, is currently comprised of 25 technical committees to write, revise and reaffirm industry standards. http://mss-hq.org/

values.label: Nsf
values.definition: National Sanitation Foundation International (NSF) NSF Internal helps protect you by certifying products and writing standard for food, water and consumer goods. NSF International is The Public Health and Safety Company™, providing public health and safety risk management solutions to companies, governments and consumers around the world. www.nsf.org

values.label: Other
values.definition: Other agency not defined in the list

values.label: American Mechanical Joint
values.definition: An American Mechanical Joint is a rubber gasket is compressed by a ductile iron gland drawn up with low-alloy steel bolts which affords liberal deflection and allows expansion and contraction of the line without leakage and is rated for a water working pressure of up to 350 psi.

values.label: Belled
values.definition: The end length of increased diameter into which a pipe end can be fitted.

values.label: Butt
values.definition: The connection is a flat cut end designed to mate directly to the end of another product. This connection is to connect the same sized pipes or valve ends together.

values.label: Compression Joint
values.definition: A compression joint kind of tubing or pipe connection where a nut, and then a sleeve or ferrule is placed over a copper or plastic tube and is compressed tightly around the tube as the nut is tightened, forming a positive grip and seal without soldering. Also a flexible compression fitting.

values.label: Crimped
values.definition: This type of joint requires the joint be crimped once sections are fit together. Some of the necessary connection parts must be added or acquired separately.

values.label: Female Threaded
values.definition: Female threaded

values.label: Flanged Joint
values.definition: Flange generally refers to the actual raised rim or lip of a fitting which can be bolted to the flange of an opposite unit.

values.label: Flare Joint
values.definition: A Flare Joint is where a pipe or tube is widened to join with a larger diameter pipe, for example between a copper tube and a main water feed line.

values.label: Grooved Joint
values.definition: Outer diameter of item has a groove which is designed to be joined together using external gaskets and couplings.

values.label: Lug
values.definition: The lug body has protruding lugs that provide bolt holes matching those in the flanges. An advantage of the lug body type is that piping on one side of the valve may be disassembled while the valve remains bolted in place, allowing for the remainder of the system to continue in operation.

values.label: Male Threaded
values.definition: Male Threaded

values.label: Mechanical Joint
values.definition: A Mechanical Joint is a joint which typically consists of: (a) a flange which is integrally cast with the bell of the pipe, (b) a rubber gasket which fits into the recess in the socket, (c) a follower ring which compresses the gasket, and (d) nuts and bolts used to tighten the joint.

values.label: No Hub Iron
values.definition: A connector for no-hub iron pipe consisting of a rubber sleeve and a stainless steel band secured by hose clamps. A variation, a neoprene sleeve with two adjustable steel bands, is used for connecting dissimilar materials, as when connecting new plastic pipe to an existing cast iron drain pipe.

values.label: Pack Joint
values.definition: Pack Joint

values.label: Plain
values.definition: SPG - Spigot, FTG- Fitting, M- Male Pipe Size- Straight end to connect or insert into the bell end or fitting to join to connecting pipe.

values.label: Press
values.definition: This type of joint requires the joint be crimped once sections are fit together. All of the necessary connection parts are present.

values.label: Push
values.definition: A joint which can be pushed onto the opposite end manually to form a solid connection. This type of connection fits around an inserted pipe or fitting end.

values.label: Quick Connect
values.definition: A connection which has the ability to joined and un-joined repeatedly or at will. This type of joint does not degrade the product over time. This type of joint is not considered by the industry to be a push joint.

values.label: Socket
values.definition: The connection is a female socket end designed to allow for the insertion of straight pipe/tubing and joined using soldering, sweating, brazing, welding, or cementing. This connection is also called solder cup, hub, or slip joint.

values.label: Swivel Joint
values.definition: This type of joint uses a pressure type seal while allowing rotation of the units being joined.

values.label: Union Joint
values.definition: This type of joint can connect and disjoint two pipes very easily without deformation to the pipe or tube.

values.label: Wafer
values.definition: A wafer is a seal using a tightly fitting seal, i.e., gasket, o-ring, precision machined, and a flat valve face on the upstream and downstream sides of the valve.

values.label: Yoke Joint
values.definition: A connection whereby a piece is expanded on one end into a seal face to form a joint.

values.label: Chemically Treated After Harvesting
values.definition: The fruit or vegetable has been treated chemically after harvesting e.g. Treated with a Chemical Preservative

values.label: Not Treated After Harvesting
values.definition: The fruit or vegetable has been not been treated chemically or waxed after harvesting.

values.label: Waxed
values.definition: The fruit or vegetable has had a layer of wax applied after harvesting.

values.label: Crown Removed
values.definition: Product has had the plant part of itself removed e.g. the top of a pineapple.

values.label: Cut
values.definition: Cut

values.label: Fattened
values.definition: Fattened

values.label: Leafless
values.definition: Produce all leaves removed  e.g. celery, radish.

values.label: Minced
values.definition: Minced

values.label: Packed In Ice
values.definition: Produce has been packed in ice.

values.label: Slaughtered
values.definition: Slaughtered

values.label: Split
values.definition: Produce has been cut/split into sections.

values.label: Stem Removed
values.definition: Stem of produced has been removed e.g. cherry or broccoli.

values.label: Trimmed
values.definition: Produce has been cut or removal of parts of item.

values.label: Washed
values.definition: Produce has been cleaned by washing.

values.label: Battery
values.definition: Trade Item is provided with batteries

values.label: Mains
values.definition: Trade Item is provided with a mains power connection devices

values.label: Solar
values.definition: Trade Item is provided with a solar power system

values.label: USB
values.definition: Trade Item is provided with a USB power connection device

values.label: Vehicle DC  Adapter
values.definition: Trade Item is provided with a vehicle DC Adapter

values.label: Final
values.definition: Item has attribute values that reflect go to market state.

values.label: Preliminary
values.definition: The trade item has data that the information provider intends to correct or add values to due to pre-production unknowns.

values.label: Air Fry
values.definition: Cooking by circulating hot air around the food, allowing to fry, grill and roast without the use of fat or oil.

values.label: As Drained
values.definition: The state of the product after it has been separated from any liquid within the package’’ – For example, a can of apricots in syrup would have a different nutritional composition if the apricots are consumed with the syrup rather than if the syrup is drained before consuming the apricots (because of the high sugar and energy content of the syrup).

values.label: Bain-marie/Water bath
values.definition: A bain-marie is placing a container with food in a hot (or cold) water bath to heat (or cool) the food gently, or to keep it warm (or cold). Also known as a water bath or double boiler.

values.label: Bake
values.definition: Cooking food in an oven by dry heat applied evenly throughout the oven.

values.label: Barbecue
values.definition: Method of cooking meat with the heat and hot gasses of a fire

values.label: Baste
values.definition: Basting is a cooking technique that involves cooking meat with either its own juices or some type of preparation such as a sauce or marinade. Similar to Pre-basted, Deep-basted and Self-basting.

values.label: Blanch
values.definition: Food preparation wherein the food substance is rapidly plunged into boiling water and then removed after a brief, timed interval and then plunged into iced water or placed under cold running water.

values.label: Blind Bake
values.definition: Baking a pie crust or other pastry without the filling

values.label: Block form
values.definition: A product is formed or shaped into a larger geometric shape than what would be used for a serving or use. It is intended that the user would cut, slice, or otherwise separate portions of the item for individual consumption or use.

values.label: Boil
values.definition: Cooking food in boiling water, or other water-based liquid such as stock or milk

values.label: Boneless
values.definition: The bones (vertebrae) have been removed from the flesh portion.

values.label: Braise
values.definition: Cooking with "moist heat", typically in a covered pot with a small amount of liquid

values.label: Bread
values.definition: A process where a piece of uncooked meat, poultry, fish or other seafood is coated with a combination of batter and breading or cracker crumbs.

values.label: Breast bone remove
values.definition: A meat or poultry product has had the sternum bone removed.

values.label: Brew
values.definition: Brew: to prepare by steeping, boiling, and fermentation or by infusion and fermentation, to prepare (a drink or other liquid) by infusion in hot water

values.label: Broil
values.definition: Cooking food with high heat with the heat applied directly to the food, most commonly from above. Heat transfer to the food is primarily via radiant heat

values.label: Chop
values.definition: Refers to the action of cutting or dividing something, usually food, into smaller pieces.

values.label: Chunk
values.definition: A product is broken up into medium or larger pieces of irregular shape.

values.label: Combi Heat
values.definition:
Type of preparation in devices in which the heating of food is possible with different methods used together. For example:
• Microwave combined with hot air: Use this function to rapidly bake the foods. 
• Grill combined with fan: Use this function to bake evenly the food and at the same time brown their surface.

values.label: Combi Steam
values.definition: Type of preparation in a device that additional to the function of a convection oven is able to generate steam. By transmitting the temperature to the food via steam and convection cooking, times in Combi ovens are shorter than in general preparation types and the product loses less moisture.

values.label: Convection
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes a convection oven which imparts heat assisted by fans to force air movement, as opposed to a conventional oven, which relies on convective heat transfer unassisted by fans. By moving fast hot air past the food, a convection oven operates at a lower temperature than a conventional oven. The air circulation, or convection, tends to eliminate "hot spots" and thereby cooking food more quickly and evenly.

values.label: Cook
values.definition: Subjected to heat for a time sufficient to produce the characteristics of a cooked product. The product must be ready-to-eat. Also referred as fully cooked.

values.label: Corn
values.definition: The treatment of meat with large-grained rock salt, also called "corns" of salt, together with sodium nitrite, potassium nitrite, or any combination of them.

values.label: Crumble
values.definition: A product is broken up into medium or smaller sized pieces of irregular shape.

values.label: Cube
values.definition: A product is cut into small to medium sized squares or rectangles.

values.label: Culture
values.definition: Bacterial cultures are added to pasteurized cream, to develop flavour, before it is churned into butter.

values.label: Deep Fry
values.definition: Cooking method whereby food is submerged in hot oil or fat.

values.label: Double Steam
values.definition: Cooking technique to prepare delicate food such as bird nests, shark fins etc. The food is covered with water and put in a covered ceramic jar

values.label: Dry
values.definition: The product is dried, a process to remove the moisture of the product. The product must be ready-to-eat.

values.label: Fillet
values.definition: A fleshy boneless piece of meat from near the loins or the ribs of an animal.

values.label: Filter wood smoke
values.definition: The use of smoke derived from burning select (hard) woods, then filtered to remove large particles. The bioactive compounds found in smoke are used to impart colour and flavour.

values.label: Flake
values.definition: Flaked is the leftover pieces of meat, poultry or fish.  It consists of small sized pieces, or "flakes"

values.label: Form/Shape
values.definition: Refers to food items that have been processed, shaped, or manufactured into specific shapes, sizes, or forms.

values.label: Form slices
values.definition: A product is formed separately as slices.

values.label: Freeze
values.definition: Convert the product from room temperature to a frozen state.Simple

values.label: Freeze dry
values.definition: The product is dried by a process of freeze-drying.

values.label: Fry
values.definition: The cooking of food in hot fats or oils.

values.label: Gas oven
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes an oven heated by gas.

values.label: Grate
values.definition: A product is reduced into smaller pieces by rubbing on something rough.

values.label: Griddle Fry
values.definition: Form of cooking where the food is fried with its own fat.

values.label: Grill
values.definition: Form of cooking that involves direct heat. The definition varies widely by region and culture

values.label: Grind
values.definition: Refers to the process of reducing something into smaller particles or fragments by crushing, pounding, or mechanically breaking it down.

values.label: Gutted
values.definition: Remove the intestines and other internal organs of an animal.

values.label: Heat_And Serve
values.definition: Prepare the item by simply heating or warming to a desired temperature or visual state prior to serving

values.label: High-speed oven
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes a high-speed oven, also known as a rapid cook oven or speed oven, which is a compact appliance that combines microwave technology with vertical hot air impingement and convection to cook food at a faster speed compared to a traditional oven or grill.

values.label: Impingement oven
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes an impingement oven. An impingement nozzle(s) blasts hot air on food as it passes through the oven. The concentrated air jet blasts through the cold air “halo” which typically lingers around food after it enters the oven.

values.label: In shell
values.definition: A product is with or in its original shell. Can also be referred as "with shell" and shell on".

values.label: Jelly
values.definition: Indicates that a gelling agent (agar, carrageenan or gelatin) has been used in the product.

values.label: Liquid smoke
values.definition: Liquid smoke is a natural by-product of burning wood. The vapor (smoke and steam), is condensed through a cooled tubing, is distilled into a concentrate, and filtered of its impurities (soot and ash). The meat product is subjected to heat in the presence of a vaporized liquid smoke solution.

values.label: Mechanically separated meat
values.definition: A process where an edible meat is obtained by removing most of the bone and cartilage from a comminuted meat product from which the bone and cartilage was not previously removed.

values.label: Mechanically tenderise
values.definition: A process where the integrity of a solid and uncooked meat or poultry surface has been compromised by being pierced by blades, needles or other similar instruments, or the meat/poultry has been injected with a marinade or other tenderising solution.

values.label: Microwave
values.definition: Cooking food by employing microwave radiation

values.label: Mince
values.definition: A food preparation technique in which food ingredients are finely divided into uniform pieces.

values.label: Mix
values.definition: Mixing of ingredients, sometimes includes additional ingredients. Example: Mixing powders in water or milk.

values.label: Multiple see preparation instructions
values.definition: Multiple preparation type steps are required for the product. See the preparation instructions for the needed steps.

values.label: Pan Fry
values.definition: Form of frying characterised by the use of less cooking oil than deep frying

values.label: Par fry/Pre fry
values.definition:
Cooking method where food is partially fried. Final cooking or preparation will be accomplished by the end user of the product (e.g., french fries).
Other common names for this preparation type: parfry, par-fry, par fry and pre-fry.

values.label: Poach
values.definition: Cooking food by gently simmering food in liquid, generally water, stock or wine

values.label: Prepared
values.definition: The state of the product after preparation (e.g. after adding milk or water).

values.label: Pressure Cook
values.definition: Method of cooking in a sealed vessel that does not permit air or liquids to escape below a preset pressure

values.label: Pressure Fry
values.definition: Meat and cooking oil are brought to high temperatures while pressure is held high enough that the water within is prevented from boiling off

values.label: Pressure steam
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes steam generated from a small amount of water in a sealed vessel. The food itself is not in direct contact with the water. Instead, the food is placed on a rack or basket above the water level.

values.label: Protein binders
values.definition: Treatment of meat or poultry products with functionally active proteins such as fibrinogen or transglutaminase to allow the proteins in the meat or poultry to encapsulate fat and hold fat and water together in the final sausage or product.

values.label: Pulled
values.definition: Refers to a method of preparing meat where it's slow-cooked until tender enough to be easily pulled apart into shreds or chunks.

values.label: Purify smoke
values.definition: A wood smoke process of fish and meat whereby the unhealthy substances found in un-purified smoke, such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), ash and tar, have been removed.

values.label: Ready_To Drink
values.definition: No Preparation. The trade Item is ready for use after being taken out of the packaging (if packaging exists) without the need of any further action prior to consumption or use

values.label: Ready_To Eat
values.definition: Besides unpacking no additional preparation required.

values.label: Reconstitute
values.definition: Restore a dry or concentrated food to its original strength or consistency by adding water.

values.label: Refrigerate
values.definition: Convert the product from room temperature to a chilled state.

values.label: Roast
values.definition: Cooking method that uses dry heat, whether an open flame, oven, or other heat source.

values.label: Roll
values.definition: A meat, poultry or fish product which has been boned, rolled and tied.

values.label: Rotisserie
values.definition: Style of roasting where meat is skewered on a spit and revolves over a flame

values.label: Salt
values.definition: Indicates salt (sodium chloride) was added during manufacturing process.

values.label: Sandwich press
values.definition: A product is placed in a cooking appliance that consists of two hinged concave, round or square, cast iron or aluminium plates on long handles which press the sandwich heating/toasting it for consumption. Some presses also seal the sandwich. A sandwich press is also known as a pie iron, pudgy pie iron, sandwich toaster, snackwicher, toastie maker, or panini press.

values.label: Saute
values.definition: Cooking food using a small amount of fat in a shallow pan over relatively high heat

values.label: Sear
values.definition: Technique used in grilling, roasting, braising, sautéing, etc. That cooks the surface of the food (usually meat, poultry or fish) at high temperature so that a caramelised crust forms

values.label: Season
values.definition:
Seasoning is the process of adding herbs, salts or spices to food to enhance the flavour.
Note:  In meat and poultry products it can also designate "Seasoned water".

values.label: Semi boneless
values.definition: A meat or poultry product which has been at least 45% deboned.  Partial removal of bones can facilitate rolling or stuffing product.

values.label: Semi dry
values.definition: The product is partially dried, process to reduce the moisture of the product. The product must be ready-to-eat.

values.label: Shankless
values.definition: A meat or poultry which the forelimb or foreleg has been removed at the elbow joint or the hind limb of hind leg removed at the knee joint.

values.label: Shave
values.definition: A product is cut off in thin layers that is larger than what would be termed shredded, but not as uniform as sliced.

values.label: Shell remove
values.definition: A product is without its shell. It can also be referred as peeled for shellfish.

values.label: Shred
values.definition: A product is pushed across or through a shredding surface to make long, narrow strips.

values.label: Simmer
values.definition: Cook food by heating it in water kept just below the boiling point (same as coddling)

values.label: Skinned (skin removed)
values.definition: Remove the skin from an animal.

values.label: Slice
values.definition: A product is cut into thin, flat piece from a larger portion.

values.label: Slit shell
values.definition: A product is within their original shell with one exception that the shell has been slit along the back. Can also be referred to as Easy Pell, EZ peel and Zipperback

values.label: Slow cooker
values.definition: Cooking method used to cook food slowly over a long period of time.

values.label: Smoke
values.definition: Process of curing, cooking, or seasoning food by exposing it for long periods of time to the smoke from a wood fire

values.label: Smoke flavour
values.definition: A flavour additive, "flavouring", based on liquid smoke.

values.label: Soak
values.definition: To immerse in liquid for a period of time. E.g. Soak the Chia seeds 10 minutes in water before eating.

values.label: Solid
values.definition: This term indicates how the meat, poultry or fish was packaged: Solid means it was packaged as a whole loin piece.

values.label: Split fish
values.definition: Split Fish is fish cut open from throat to vent or tail; or from nape to tail. Gills, guts and roe removed; head may sometimes be removed. The backbone may be left in or removed except for an inch or two at the tail.

values.label: Spreadable form
values.definition: A product is formulated in such a fashion as to be easily smoothed out onto another item.

values.label: Steam
values.definition: Cooking by first boiling the water so it will evaporate into steam, then the steam will carry heat to the food, thus achieving heating the food

values.label: Stew
values.definition: Preparing meat cut into smaller pieces or cubes by simmering it in liquid, usually together with vegetables

values.label: Stick form
values.definition: A product is cut or formed into individual strips. Even in the stick state the item is still a solid product.

values.label: Stir Fry
values.definition: Chinese cooking technique used because of its fast cooking speed

values.label: String form
values.definition: A product is cut or formed into individual strips which when separated form or appear to be strings. While in its combined state, the item may appear to be a stick, but it is when the item is separated or consumed it takes on the string state.

values.label: Stuff
values.definition: Stuffing, filling, or dressing is an edible mixture, composed of bread, grain, herbs, fruit, nuts, vegetables, fat or other ingredients, used to fill a cavity in the preparation of another food item.

values.label: Thaw
values.definition: Convert the product from a frozen state to a chilled or room temperature state.

values.label: Tips
values.definition: Fish trimmings, not minced, from the tail and nape sections of a fish.

values.label: Toast
values.definition: Preparation method that uses dry heat to warm and brown the surface of the product.

values.label: Unprepared
values.definition: The initial state of the product.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Unknown, not applicable

values.label: Waffle iron
values.definition: A product is cooked between two hinged metal plates. Both plates have gridded indentations to shape the waffle from the batter or dough placed between them. The plates are heated and the iron is closed while the waffle bakes.

values.label: Wedge
values.definition: A product is cut in triangular shaped pieces. In some cases, one side of the triangle may be an arc, specifically if the wedge was cut from an item which is in the shape of a wheel or circle.

values.label: Wheel form
values.definition: A product is formed in a round shape resembling a wheel or circle.

values.label: Whip
values.definition: To beat ingredient(s), such as egg whites, cream, etc., using a wire whisk or rotary/electric beater in order to incorporate air into the existing product, thereby increasing volume/stability.

values.label: Wood oven
values.definition: A cooking method which utilizes an oven heated by wood. Similar terms: Wood oven cooked/baked, wood fired.
Available only through a hospital when prescribed by a doctor.
This pharmaceutical or medical device must be prescribed for the first time at a hospital.

values.label: No_Prescription Required
values.definition: No prescription is needed for this trade item
A prescription is required and may be prescribed by any licensed prescriber.

values.label: Prescription Under Monitoring
values.definition: The healthcare product can be prescribed only after specific exams. The result of the exam (such as radiography, blood count, scanner, etc.) will determine if the product can be prescribed or not.

values.label: Specialist Prescription Required
values.definition: Medical Device of pharmaceutical must be prescribed under the direction of a specialist authorised to prescribe the trade item.

values.label: Acidification
values.definition: Dropping pH of food

values.label: Alcohol Curing
values.definition: Treatment of food by adding alcohol in order to preserve the product

values.label: Alive
values.definition: Living animal or plant,  not dead.

values.label: Attested Milk
values.definition: Raw Milk (without heat treatment)

values.label: Boiling
values.definition: Cooking

values.label: Brining
values.definition: Water saturating or strongly impregnating with salt

values.label: Canning
values.definition: Preserved in a sealed airtight container, usually made of tin-coated iron

values.label: Cold Smoke Curing
values.definition: To smoke the food at between 70 degrees to 90 degrees F.

values.label: Conserve
values.definition: Keep from harm or damage

values.label: Dehydration
values.definition: To remove water from food

values.label: Drying
values.definition: Making with moisture having evaporated, drained away

values.label: Fermentation
values.definition: Any of a group of chemical reactions induced by living or nonliving ferments that split complex organic compounds into relatively simple substance

values.label: Fine-filtered/Microfiltered
values.definition: Microfiltration (MF) is mainly used for the reduction of bacteria in skim milk, whey and brine. It is also used for defatting whey intended for whey protein concentrate (WPC) and for protein fractionation. MF membranes have a pore size of 10-1 to 101 µm. The resulting permeate of MF separation is water, minerals, lactose and some proteins.

values.label: Freeze Drying
values.definition: Preserving food by freezing and then drying in a vacuum

values.label: Freezing
values.definition: Turning into ice or another solid by cold

values.label: Fresh
values.definition: Recently made or obtained food in its' natural conditions and not altered by any preservation methods

values.label: Fry
values.definition: The cooking of food in hot fats or oils.

values.label: Heated
values.definition: Preserving the food by exposure to heat (e.g. cooking, grilling, etc.). Specific heating requirements may be regulated by local legislation. Example: exposure to at least a temperature of 70 °C/158 °F for at least 10 minutes.

values.label: High Pressure Pasteurisation
values.definition: High Pressure Pasteurisation is a pasteurisation process where the product is treated with pressure of up to 10'000 bar and heat between 0°C and 120°C

values.label: High Pressure Processing
values.definition: High Pressure Processing (HPP) is a pasteurisation process where the product is treated with pressure of up to 6’000 bar without the use of heat

values.label: High Temperature Pasteurisation
values.definition: High Temperature Pasteurisation is a pasteurisation process where the product is treated with heat between 85°C and 135°C

values.label: High temperature short time (HTST)
values.definition: High temperature short time (HTST) pasteurization requires fluid milk to be heated to 72°C for 15 seconds (continuous flow pasteurization).

values.label: High Temperature Treated Milk
values.definition: Legally also pasteurisation, MHD for longer (about 2 to 3 weeks), ESL-milk

values.label: Hot Smoke Curing
values.definition: Hot-smoking partially or totally cooks the food by treating it at temperatures ranging from 100 degrees to 190 degrees F.

values.label: Ionisation
values.definition: To convert into an ion or ions

values.label: Irradiation
values.definition: Food irradiation is the process of exposing food to ionising radiation in order to disinfest, sterilise, or preserve food.

values.label: Marinated
values.definition: Marinate a food in a mixture of e.g. oil, vinegar, spices, or herbs, before cooking it, so that it can develop a special flavour. This preserves the product.

values.label: Milk mixture
values.definition: A mixture of raw milk and pasteurised or thermised milk, or a mixture of microfiltered skimmed milk and whole raw milk or raw cream.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Pasteurisation
values.definition: Pasteurisation is a process where the product is treated with heat from 60°C to 85°C

values.label: Preserved Without Artificial Nitrates
values.definition: A food is treated with natural curing agents and without artificial nitrates, e.g. celery powder.

values.label: Quick Freezing
values.definition: Freezing (food) rapidly so as to preserve its qualities

values.label: Refrigerated
values.definition: Preserving the food by chilling and keeping it cold.

values.label: Salt Curing
values.definition: Preserving by using a salt brine

values.label: Sous Vide
values.definition: Low temperature long time cooking under vacuum

values.label: Sterilisation
values.definition: A process that effectively kills or eliminates transmissibleagents (such as fungi, bacteria, viruses, spore forms, etc.).

values.label: Sugar Curing
values.definition: Treatment of food by adding sugar in order to preserve the product.

values.label: Thermisation
values.definition: Thermisation is a heat treatment process applied at lower temperature than pasteurisation. The product is heated to a temperature of more than 40°C and less than 72°C for at least 15 seconds, e.g., for milk.

values.label: Ultra-filtered
values.definition: A pasteurized product that is passed through filters which permit the smaller lactose, water, mineral, and vitamin molecules to pass through the membrane, while the larger protein and fat molecules are retained and concentrated.  As a result, the water and lactose (sugar) content is reduced; whereas the protein and calcium are increased.

values.label: Ultra High Temperature
values.definition: Ultra High Temperature (UHT) is a pasteurisation process where the product is treated with high heat between 135°C and 155°C

values.label: Under Modified Atmosphere
values.definition: Packed with a gas with protective proprieties

values.label: Vacuum Packed
values.definition: Sealed after the partial removal of air

values.label: The introduction of a new item.
values.definition: The introduction of a new item.

values.label: Price decrease.
values.definition: Price decrease.

values.label: A price increase.
values.definition: A price increase.

values.label: Range extension.
values.definition: Range extension.

values.label: Size change (Pack or Pallet).
values.definition: Size change (Pack or Pallet).

values.label: Temporary price reduction.
values.definition: Temporary price reduction.

values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Count
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Length
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Volume
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Weight
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE
The weight of a product when all liquids used in the packaging of the product have been removed.
