values.label: UNI
values.definition: Size code of the Italian National Unification Body (UNI).

values.label: BSI
values.definition: Size code of the British Standards Institution (BSI).

values.label: Australia
values.definition: The Australian size system.

values.label: Continental
values.definition: The Continental European size system.

values.label: Europe
values.definition: The European size system.

values.label: France
values.definition: The French size system.

values.label: Germany
values.definition: The German size system.

values.label: Italy
values.definition: The Italian size system.

values.label: Japan
values.definition: The Japanese size system.

values.label: Mexico
values.definition: The Mexican size system.

values.label: UK
values.definition: The United Kingdom size system.

values.label: US
values.definition: The United States size system.

values.label: World
values.definition: The world size system.

values.label: Adjustment Height
values.definition: The maximum height of the adjustment or compensation, e.g. levelling-, casting- and bonding-compound.

values.label: Air Draft
values.definition: The term used to describe the distance from the top of a vessel's highest point to its waterline.

values.label: Air Inlet
values.definition: The size of the air intake for things like a Valve or Actuator, etc.

values.label: American Football
values.definition: The size of ball and gear used in American football. Examples  Junior; Youth; Pee Wee

values.label: Arbor Diameter
values.definition: The arbor is the shaft that a blade is mounted to. The size of the arbor is the diameter of this shaft.

values.label: Area Covered Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum area coverage, e.g. sprinkler, lawn sprinkler.

values.label: Area Covered Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum area coverage, e.g. sprinkler, lawn sprinkler.

values.label: Axle Width
values.definition: Measurement of between the wheels on the front axle.

values.label: Back
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Backset Size
values.definition: The horizontal distance between the face through which the bolt passes and the centre-line of the knob stem or keyhole.

values.label: Back Rise
values.definition: Measurement from the top of the waistband to the crotch at the back of the pants.

values.label: Bag Height
values.definition: Measurement of how tall the bag stands from the bottom surface to the top of the bag not including straps/handles.

values.label: Bag Strap Drop
values.definition: Measurement of a bag's shoulder/handle length from the top of the bag to the peak of the strap/ handle

values.label: Bag Strap Length
values.definition: Measurement of a bag's shoulder/handle length from end to end

values.label: Barrel diameter
values.definition: Measurement of the internal width of a barrel.

values.label: Baseball Bat Drop
values.definition: A length to weight ratio, representing how many ounces a bat weighs compared to its length.

values.label: Base Measurement Depth
values.definition: Indicates the depth of the product's outer base measurement in contact with the floor, table or other surface.

values.label: Base Measurement Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of the product's outer base in contact with the floor, table or other plane surface.

values.label: Base Measurement Width
values.definition: Indicates the width of the product's outer base measurement in contact with the floor, table or other surface.

values.label: Base thickness
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of  thickness of the product's base/bottom when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The thickness of heavy-bottomed pot.

values.label: Basketball
values.definition: Basketball is a sport that is played by two teams of five players on a rectangular court. This refers to the ball used in play.  Examples: 5 (Youth); 7 (Men's)

values.label: Belt Length
values.definition: Measurement of length of the belt from where the belt band begins to the first band hole.

values.label: Belt Width
values.definition: Measurement of width of the belt. Measured from the top of the waist to the bottom of the waist as worn.

values.label: Bench Plain Blade Length
values.definition: The length of the bench plane blade e.g. hand plane. A hand plane is a tool for shaping wood. When powered by electricity, the tool may be called a planer. Planes are used to flatten, reduce the thickness of, and impart a smooth surface to a rough piece of lumber or timber. Planing is used to produce horizontal, vertical, or inclined flat surfaces on workpieces usually too large for shaping. Special types of planes are designed to cut joints or decorative mouldings.

values.label: Bend angle
values.definition: Angle formed between a bent structures parts, typically used to describe the deflection of material.

values.label: Bicycle Frame
values.definition: Identify the top of the seat tube, where the seat clamp holds the seat post. Identify the centre of the bottom bracket (it's the axle that holds the crank arms together). Measure the distance between the two points- this is the length of the seat tube.

values.label: Blade Length
values.definition: The length of the product blade for example of a hedge shears or knife.

values.label: Blade Width
values.definition: The width of a blade for example a bench plain blade.

values.label: Boat Beam
values.definition: The beam of a ship is its width at the widest point as measured at the ship's nominal waterline.

values.label: Boot Circumference
values.definition: Measurement of the inside of the boot at the largest part of the upper calf.

values.label: Boot Shaft
values.definition: Measurement from the middle of the arch up the outsole to the top of the boot shaft

values.label: Borehole Diameter
values.definition: The maximum borehole diameter of for a example an impact drill.

values.label: Bore Diameter Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum bore diameter, of for example an impact drill.

values.label: Bore Diameter Steel Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum bore diameter for steel of for example an impact drill.

values.label: Bore Diameter Stone Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum bore diameter for stone of for example an impact drill.

values.label: Bore Diameter Wood Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum bore diameter for wood of for example an impact drill.

values.label: Bore Stroke Ratio
values.definition: In a reciprocating piston engine, the stroke ratio, defined by either bore/stroke ratio or stroke/bore ratio, is a term to describe the ratio between cylinder bore diameter and piston stroke. 83.0 mm x 69.2 mm

values.label: Bra Band
values.definition: Measure around the bottom of the band, directly under the bust.

values.label: Bra Cup
values.definition: The difference between the measurement around the chest plus five inches for imperial measures, then Measure around the breast at the fullest part and round to the nearest whole number. a one inch (imperial) difference is an A cup, 2 is a B cup, 3 inch is a C cup, etc.

values.label: Brim
values.definition: Measurement of a hat's brim from the edge to where the brim meets the sideband.

values.label: Bristle length
values.definition: Measurement of the length of the product's bristles. Place the product on a surface as the user would for use. The length is measured from the surface to the highest portion of the bristles.

values.label: Bristle width
values.definition: Measurement of the width of the product's bristles. Place the product on a surface as the user would for use. The width is measured from the left to the right of the bristles.

values.label: Chain Length
values.definition: Measurement of a chain's longest measurement as laid stretched out flat

values.label: Chest Bust
values.definition: The measurement around the widest part of the chest/bust.

values.label: Chuck Size
values.definition: The measurement refers to the size of the drill chuck — the part that holds the bit — and indicates the maximum-diameter bit shank that fits the drill.

values.label: Circumference
values.definition: Measurement of the circumference of the piece.

values.label: Cleaning Path Width Without Attachments
values.definition: The working or cleaning path width of the product without attachments or accessories, e.g. rake.

values.label: Cleaning Path Width Withough Attachments Max
values.definition: The maximal working or cleaning path width of the product without attachments or accessories, e.g. rake.

values.label: Cleaning Path Width Without Attachments Minimum
values.definition: The minimal working or cleaning path width of the product without attachments or accessories, e.g. rake.

values.label: Cleaning Path Width With Attachments
values.definition: The working or cleaning path width of the product with accessories, e.g. road sweeper incl. side brushes info: attachment.

values.label: Clearing Width
values.definition: Indicates the width of space that can be cleared by for example a snowplough.

values.label: Clip Back Width Tools
values.definition: Indicates the width of a clip back  for tools for example a brad nailer. A clip back secures a tool to a person's waist.

values.label: Collar
values.definition: Collar

values.label: Collet Size
values.definition: Collet Size is a subtype of chuck that forms a collar around an object to be held and exerts a strong clamping force on the object when it is tightened, usually by means of a tapered outer collar. It may be used to hold a work piece or a tool.

values.label: Compatible Conduit
values.definition: An electrical conduit is a tube used to protect and route electrical wiring in a building or non-building structure. Electrical conduit may be made of metal, plastic, fibre, or fired clay.

values.label: Cooking Area
values.definition: The area that can be used for cooking stove top, grill, etc.

values.label: Core Height
values.definition: Indicates the height of the foam core of a product for example a mattress.

values.label: Cup
values.definition: Cup

values.label: Cutting Depth Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting depth of a product such as a slide compound miter saw.

values.label: Cutting Depth Metal Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting depth of metal of a product such as a slide compound miter saw.

values.label: Cutting Depth Steel Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting depth of steel of a product such as a slide compound miter saw.

values.label: Cutting Depth Metal Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting depth of wood of a product such as a slide compound miter saw.

values.label: Cutting Diameter or Cutting Width
values.definition: Indicates the cutting diameter or the cutting width, e.g. bypass lopper, hedge trimmer, saw blade.

values.label: Cutting Diameter or Cutting Width Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting diameter or the cutting width, e.g. bypass lopper, hedge trimmer, saw blade.

values.label: Cutting Height
values.definition: Indicates the cutting height of a product such as a lawn mover.

values.label: Cutting Height 45 Degree Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting height at 45 degrees.

values.label: Cutting Height 90 Degree Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting height at 90 degrees.

values.label: Cutting Height Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting height of a product such as a lawn mover.

values.label: Cutting Height Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum cutting height of a product such as a lawn mover.

values.label: Cutting Thickness Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum cutting thickness of a product such as a slide compound miter saw.

values.label: Cutting Wheel Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the tile cutting wheel.

values.label: Cutting Width
values.definition: The width of the cut of a product such as lawn mowers.

values.label: Cutting Width Max
values.definition: The maximum width of the cut of a product such as lawn mowers.

values.label: Cylinder Length Internal
values.definition: The internal length of the cylinder, e.g. security lock.

values.label: Cylinder Length Outside
values.definition: The outer length of the cylinder, e.g. security lock.

values.label: Depth Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum depth.

values.label: Inner diameter
values.definition: The measurement of the internal diameter, e.g., of a tube or pipe, measured from one inner wall to the opposite inner wall, passing through the centre.

values.label: Diameter Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum diameter.

values.label: Diameter Min
values.definition: Indicates the minimal diameter.

values.label: Outer diameter
values.definition: The measurement of the total diameter, e.g., of a tube or pipe, measured from one outer wall to the opposite outer wall, passing through the centre.

values.label: Diameter Up To
values.definition: Indicates a variety of diameters up to the maximum diameter.

values.label: Dirt Particles Size Max
values.definition: Indicate the maximum size of dirt particles that can be picked up.

values.label: Disc Size
values.definition: The size of the disc examples in DIY being  round blade, pad, etc.

values.label: Distance Between Two Stairs
values.definition: The distance between two stairs.

values.label: Door or Passage Width
values.definition: Indicates the door passing width.

values.label: Door Thickness Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum thickness of the door.

values.label: Door Thickness Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum thickness of the door.

values.label: Drawer Dimension
values.definition: The textual representation of the size dimension specified by the size type.Example 15 Inches wide X 20 inches deep X 6 inches high.

values.label: Drawer Length Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum length of the drawer.

values.label: Drawer Length Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum length of the drawer.

values.label: Dress Length
values.definition: Measurement of dress length from the collar to the bottom hem

values.label: Drill Length
values.definition: The length of the drill included straight shank, cutting wedge and head.

values.label: Duct Width Range Hood
values.definition: The width of the duct for a range hood.  A range hood is a device that hangs above the stove or cooktop for ventilation.

values.label: Egg Size
values.definition: Indicates the egg size as recommended by the local regulation. Examples 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 with weight in grams  or  Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large, Jumbo

values.label: Envelope
values.definition: Envelopes come in various size types. These vary through out the world. #9, A-1, DL, C1, C2, C6.

values.label: Extended Depth
values.definition: Measurement of the expanded depth of an item for items where the item can be expanded such as a duffle bag with closures which open to allow size folds to open and allow more contents inside.

values.label: Eyewear Bridge Width
values.definition: Measurement of the width of the bridge.  Measured as worn from the edge of one lens/frame to the edge of the opposite lens/frame opposite wear the eyewear would rest on the nose of the wearer.

values.label: Eyewear Frame Width
values.definition: Measurement of the width of the frame.  Measured as worn from the wearer's temple to the wearer's opposite temple.

values.label: Eyewear Lens Height
values.definition: Measurement of the height of the lens not including the frames.  Measured as worn from the wearer's check to the wearer's forehead.

values.label: Eyewear Lens Width
values.definition: Measurement of the width of the lens not including the frames.  Measured as worn from the wearer's nose to the wearer's temple.

values.label: Eyewear Temple Length
values.definition: Measurement of the length of the arm.  Measured as worn from the wearer's temple to the end of the ear wrap/stem.

values.label: Fan Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the blades of a fan.

values.label: Firearm Chamber Length
values.definition: The portion of the barrel or firing cylinder in which the cartridge is inserted prior to being fired.

values.label: Flow Rate Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum flow rate, e.g. pumps, sprayers or showerheads.

values.label: Flue Gas Outlet Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the flue gas outlet. A flue is a pipe or channel for conveying exhaust gases from a fireplace, oven, boiler etc.

values.label: Football
values.definition: The size of the ball used in Football, also know as a soccer ball, not to be confused with an American Football. 3, 5

values.label: Footies Shoulder To Toe
values.definition: Measurement from the top of the shoulder to the base of the heel as measured along the back of the garment.

values.label: Front Rise
values.definition: Measurement from the top of the waistband to the crotch at the front of the pants.

values.label: Front View Width
values.definition: The width of the front view of the product.

values.label: Front Wheel Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of the front wheel.

values.label: Fuel Capacity
values.definition: the capacity measurement of that the trade item was designed to be able to hold fuel.

values.label: Fuel Reserve Capacity
values.definition: the capacity measurement of that the trade item was designed to be able to hold fuel in reserve as supplemental. In a car, a fuel tank may show empty but has a reserve capacity

values.label: Gateway Height
values.definition: Indicates the gateway height of e.g. a garage or carport.

values.label: Gateway Width
values.definition: Indicates the gateway width of e.g. a garage or carport.

values.label: Gauge
values.definition: A measurement of the thickness, size, or capacity of an object or material.

values.label: Gradient Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum gradient, e.g. a lawn mowers can handle.

values.label: Grain Size Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum grain size, e.g. sandpaper.

values.label: Grind Width
values.definition: The width of the grind for example for a  sheet sander.

values.label: Grit size
values.definition: The size of the abrasive particles in a material, often used in sanding and polishing.

values.label: Ground Clearance
values.definition: Measurement of height from the bottom of the wheel to the top of the board or chassis.

values.label: Growth Height Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximal growth height, e.g. plants.

values.label: Growth Height Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimal growth height, e.g. plants.

values.label: Handle diameter
values.definition: The measurement of the width across the circular cross-section of a handle.

values.label: Handle Length
values.definition: Measurement of a handle from it's attachment to an item to the tip

values.label: Handle width
values.definition: Measurement of the side-to-side dimension of a handle.

values.label: Heel Height
values.definition: The measurement of the heel of footwear is measured at the outsole from the middle of the heel to the sole.

values.label: Height Between Floor and  Bottom Stair
values.definition: The distance between the floor and the bottom stair.

values.label: Height maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum measurement of the product's outer height. Example: Cookware from base to rim.

values.label: Height of Plant Container
values.definition: Indicates the height of a plant container, e.g. a plant bowl.

values.label: Height of Plant Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum height of a plant without container.

values.label: Hidden Platform Height
values.definition: Measurement at the outsole from the foot bed to the sole where the platform is wrapped with material to hide the platform making it appear as part of the shoe.

values.label: Hips
values.definition: The measurement around the fullest part of the hips.

values.label: Hitch Shank
values.definition: A device which attaches directly to the tow vehicle providing the connection between the tow vehicle and the trailer. A fixed tongue hitch includes the ball platform, while a receiver style hitch has a receptacle (typically 1-1/4" or 2") for inserting special ball mounts or bike racks.

values.label: Hole Size
values.definition: Indicates hole size in inches for paper, paper punches, and other paper products.

values.label: Hose Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of a hose for example a high pressure hose, shower hose or water pumps suction hose.

values.label: Hose Length
values.definition: The length of a hose e.g. high pressure hose, shower hose or water pumps suction hose.

values.label: Hull Length
values.definition: Is the maximum length of a vessel's hull measured parallel to the waterline.

values.label: Illuminated Area
values.definition: The area that is illuminated by lighting for example by  Christmas lights or  lamps.

values.label: Inlet Spud
values.definition: A threaded opening on the water heater tank. Also a tool for digging having characteristics of a shade and chisel. Examples of sizes 2 X 1 1/4 fits a 1 1/4 " flush tube and a bowl with a 2 11/16" opening.

values.label: Inseam
values.definition: Inseam

values.label: Installation Depth Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum installation depth for a product. Installation depth is the depth of a cut out for example the a cut out of a counter made for a range.

values.label: Installation Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the installation diameter.

values.label: Intake Height
values.definition: The intake height will be need for gardening machines.

values.label: Ironing Surface Width
values.definition: The width of the ironing surface area, e.g. of a steam iron or ironing board.

values.label: Jaw Capacity Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum jaw capacity, e.g. groove pliers or plain vice.

values.label: Jaw Opening Maximum
values.definition: The jaw is any opposable articulated structure, typically used for grasping and manipulating something. The term jaws is also broadly applied to the whole of the structures constituting the vault of the trade item and serving to open and close it.

values.label: Jewellry Height
values.definition: Measurement of a piece of jewellery as measured from top to bottom across the face of the piece as it is worn.

values.label: Jewellry Width
values.definition: Measurement of a piece of jewellery as measured from left to right across the face of the piece as it is worn.

values.label: Kerb Weight
values.definition: Is the total weight of a vehicle with standard equipment, all necessary operating consumables such as motor oil, transmission oil, coolant, air conditioning refrigerant, and a full tank of fuel, while not loaded with either passengers or cargo. This definition may differ from definitions used by governmental regulatory agencies or other organizations. Curb Weight in US

values.label: Ladder Height
values.definition: Indicates the ladder height see: http://bulkydelivery.xeesa.com/gif/safety-ladder-6-step.jpg

values.label: Lawn Size Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximal area of a lawn that can be covered by a lawn mower.

values.label: Leg height
values.definition: Vertical measurement from the bottom to the top of a leg, often referring to furniture or anatomy.

values.label: Leg opening
values.definition: Measurement of diameter of the leg opening at the bottom of the pant leg.

values.label: Length
values.definition: Length is the single dimension from one point to another point. Example: Length of a rope, garden hose, etc.

values.label: Length maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum length of an expandable product. Example: An expandable umbrella.

values.label: Length minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum length of an expandable product. Example: An expandable umbrella.

values.label: Length Retracted or Rolled Up State
values.definition: The length of the product when fully retracted.

values.label: Length Spread or Unrolled State
values.definition: The length of the product when fully extended e.g. length of a rolled out wallpaper.

values.label: Length Up To
values.definition: Indicates a variety of lengths up to the maximum length.

values.label: Lens Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the lens in a camera, telescope or any optical type lens that measures in diameter

values.label: Lens dioptre
values.definition: The dioptre of the optical lens. Dioptre is defined as the inverse of the focal length. It is mostly used in optics, typically to indicate strength of prescription eyeglasses.

values.label: Light Beam Angle
values.definition: Light Beam Angle is the degree of width that light emits from its source. Specifically, this is the angle between opposing points of the beam axis where the intensity drops to 50% of max intensity.

values.label: Light Beam Spread
values.definition: Light Beam Spread indicates amount of divergence of the light beam and is defined as the length within which the minimum illumination on a surface normal to the axis of the beam is 1/10th of the maximum.

values.label: Liquid Capacity
values.definition: The capacity measurement of water, beverages, milk, etc. that the trade item was designed to hold. Example: watercraft, fish tanks, etc.

values.label: Mast Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of the mast for example the mast of a sunshade.

values.label: Maximum travel distance
values.definition: The furthest distance a mechanism or vehicle can move within its designed limits.

values.label: Miter Cut Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum miter cut, e.g. compound meter saw or sliding meter saw.

values.label: Nail Length Including Head
values.definition: The length of the nail including the head.

values.label: Nettings Horizontal Wire Diameter
values.definition: The thickness of the netting’s horizontal wires.

values.label: Nettings Vertical Wire Diameter
values.definition: The thickness of the netting’s vertical wires.

values.label: One  Dimension
values.definition: One Dimension

values.label: Onsies Shoulder To Toe
values.definition: Measurement from the top of the shoulder to the crotch as measured along the back of the garment.

values.label: Operating Distance Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum operating distance. In case of an electric bikes it is the riding range up to.

values.label: Operating Height
values.definition: The operating height at which the user is permitted to work, e.g. steel work platform.

values.label: Operating Height Maximum
values.definition: The maximum operating height at which the user is permitted to work, e.g. steel work platform.

values.label: Outside Leg
values.definition: The measurement of the outside leg seam. This is the distance from the waist to the bottom of the trousers.

values.label: Overall Depth
values.definition: Indicates the depth overall.

values.label: Padlock Shackle Height
values.definition: Indicates the height of the shackle of a padlock. A shackle is a u-shaped piece of metal secured with a clevis pin or bolt across the opening.

values.label: Pant Rise
values.definition: The distance between the middle of the crotch seam to the top of the waistband. Determines where pant will sit on the body to create a perceived waistline.

values.label: Paper
values.definition: Paper comes in various size types. These vary throughout the world. 8 1/2 X 11, A4, etc.

values.label: Paper weight
values.definition: Weight of the paper portion of the product as used to differentiate the product with the user. Example: 20 lb Bond, 200 g/m2.

values.label: Parasol Opened Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the parasol when opened.

values.label: Passage Height Front
values.definition: The height of a passage or entrance for example the doorway of a garden house or the clearance of a bridge.

values.label: Passage Height Rear
values.definition: The passage height of the rear of a structure such as a garden house.

values.label: Pedestal Height
values.definition: Indicates the pedestal height for example of a Swing-N-Slide.

values.label: Pile Height
values.definition: Indicates the height of the pile for example rug pile. Pile height is the thickness of a rug measured from the surface of a rug to its backing.

values.label: Plane Depth
values.definition: Indicates the maximum depth of the plane, e.g. block plane, bench plane or trimming plane.

values.label: Plane Width
values.definition: The width of the plane for example block plane, bench plane or trimming plane.

values.label: Planter Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of a planter or pot for a plant.

values.label: Plant Diameter Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum diameter of a plant without container as sold to consumer.

values.label: Plant New Shoot Length
values.definition: Indicates the new shoot length of a plant. In botany, shoots consist of stems including their appendages, the leaves and lateral buds, flowering stems and flower buds.[1][2] The new growth from seed germination that grows upward is a shoot where leaves will develop. In the spring, perennial plant shoots are the new growth that grows from the ground in herbaceous plants or the new stem and/or flower growth that grows on woody plants.

values.label: Platform Height
values.definition: Measurement at the outsole from the foot bed to the sole

values.label: Pond Size Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum size of a pond.

values.label: Power Cord Length Without Plug
values.definition: The length of the power cord without plug.

values.label: Power cord length with plug
values.definition: The length of the power cord including the plug.

values.label: Precious Metal Purity
values.definition: Measurement or descriptive terms to describe the purity of the precious metal.  For example, 24 karats, or 950Plat.

values.label: Precious Metal Weight
values.definition: Measurement of the weight of the precious metal.

values.label: Pump Delivery Head
values.definition: Indicates the delivery head of pumps. Head is the height at which a pump can raise water up.

values.label: Pump Delivery Head Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum delivery head of pumps.

values.label: Racquet Length
values.definition: Measurement of the length of a racquet from the tip of the handle to the top of the head

values.label: Ramp width
values.definition: The horizontal measurement from one side of a ramp to the other, affecting accessibility and use.

values.label: Reach Height
values.definition: Indicates the reach height of an item for example the reach height of a ladder.

values.label: Rear Wheel Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of rear wheel.

values.label: Removal Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximal removable by use a special devise, e.g. topsoil.

values.label: Ridge Height Garage Carports
values.definition: Indicates the ridge height of a garage or carport.

values.label: Roll Length
values.definition: The length of rolled out products, e.g. the rolled out wallpaper.

values.label: Roll Width
values.definition: Indicates the width of a roller for example paint roller.

values.label: Room Height Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum height of a retracted ladder or stair.

values.label: Rope Length
values.definition: The potential length of a rope included in a product for example the potential drying area of a clothesline dryer.

values.label: Running Length
values.definition: Measurement of longest measure for the item which comes in contact with a surface (snow, ground, etc.) during normal use.

values.label: Sanding Area Length
values.definition: The length of the sanding area for example of an angle grinder.

values.label: Sanding Area Length
values.definition: The width of the sanding area for example for a sheet sander.

values.label: Saw Band Length
values.definition: The length of the saw band for example for a band saw.

values.label: Saw Band Width
values.definition: The width of the saw band for example for a reciprocating saw.

values.label: Saw Wheel Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the saw blade of e.g. an angle grinder.

values.label: Scaffold Height
values.definition: Indicates the height of scaffolding, Scaffolding is a structure  used by workers while building, repairing, or cleaning the buildings.

values.label: Screw Diameter Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum diameter of a screw. Generally this refers to the outside diameter of the threads.

values.label: Seam Depth Max
values.definition: The maximum depth of a joint or seam.

values.label: Seat Back Height
values.definition: The seat back height from the base of the seat to the top of the back.

values.label: Seat Height
values.definition: The height from the floor to the top of the seat.

values.label: Self-priming Height Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum self priming height, e.g. of a pump.

values.label: Shackle Clearance
values.definition: Usable clearance the area between the shackles that allows to pass them through a hasp or hole, around a bar or, indeed, onto a cable. A shackle is a metal link, typically U-shaped, closed by a bolt, used to secure a chain or rope to something.

values.label: Shackle Diameter
values.definition: Shackle sizes are measured by the diameter of the bow, not the pin.

values.label: Shackle Length
values.definition: Is measured from the top of the lock body to the inside of the shackle.

values.label: Shank Size
values.definition: The shank is the end of a drill bit grasped by the chuck of a drill.

values.label: Sheets Per Item
values.definition: The number of sheets when attached within an item examples Pads of paper, Sticky Notes, etc.

values.label: Sheet Depth
values.definition: Measurement of height of a sheet from the elastic band to the top of the mattress.

values.label: Shelf Depth
values.definition: The depth from the front to the back of the shelf.

values.label: Shower Head Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the shower head.

values.label: Side Burner Area
values.definition: The area that can be used for cooking stove top, grill, on the side burner, off the main cook top, etc.

values.label: Side View Depth
values.definition: Indicates the side view depth. See: http://www.hifi-regler.de/images_c/media/gallery/z_tiefe_sharp-lc-40-le-705-e_100003140.p800x600.jpg.

values.label: Single Stair Width
values.definition: Indicates the width of a single stair.

values.label: Sleeve
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Splitting Length
values.definition: The splitting length, e.g. wood splitter

values.label: Spout Height
values.definition: Spout height is measured from the sink/countertop surface vertically up to the highest point..

values.label: Spout Reach
values.definition: Spout reach is measured from the centre of the spout base horizontally out to the water stream.

values.label: Staircase Width
values.definition: The width of stairs for example loft stairs or spiral staircase.

values.label: Standing Height
values.definition: The maximum height at which the user can stand, e.g. on a steel work platform.

values.label: Stick Diameter Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum diameter of a stick, e.g. broom stick or telescopic stick.

values.label: Stick Diameter Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum diameter of a stick, e.g. broom stick or telescopic stick.

values.label: Stick Length Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum length of a stick, e.g. broom stick or telescopic stick.

values.label: Stick Length Minimum
values.definition: Indicates the minimum length of a stick, e.g. broom stick or telescopic stick.

values.label: Storage Length
values.definition: The length of the product in its storage state.

values.label: Storey Height
values.definition: Indicates the height of storey. A storey (or story in American English) is any level part of a building that could be used by people (for living, work, storage, recreation, etc.). The terms "floor", "level", or "deck" can also be used in this sense.

values.label: Stove Pipe Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the diameter of a stove pipe of e.g. a pellet stove, wood stove or a wood furnace.

values.label: Stroke Length
values.definition: Is back-and-forth motion. Each cycle of reciprocation consists of two opposite motions: there is a motion in one direction, and then a motion back in the opposite direction. Each of these is called a stroke. The term is also used to mean the length of the stroke.

values.label: Supply Line Length to Illuminant
values.definition: The supply line length until the first illuminant for example for length of cord until the first light on Christmas lights.

values.label: Tabletop thickness
values.definition: Measurement of the vertical dimension of a table's surface.

values.label: Table Size Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum size of the table top for example the table top of a table saw.

values.label: Take-off Maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum take-off, e.g. jointer or planer.  Take-off is defined as the amount of material removed in a single pass.

values.label: Tank Size
values.definition: The measurement  large receptacle or storage chamber, especially for liquid or gas. This is usually a volume.

values.label: Thickness
values.definition: Indicates the measurement from top to bottom or front to back. Example: Mattress, pillows, cushions, etc.

values.label: Thread Cutting Width
values.definition: Indicates the width of a cutting thread/line for example the cutting line of string trimmer.

values.label: Tire Width
values.definition: Indicates the tire width.

values.label: Torso Length
values.definition: Measurement of torsos length from the neck line to the bottom hem

values.label: Total Height Workbench
values.definition: Indicates the total height of the work surface of a workbench.

values.label: Total Stone karat
values.definition: The number of karats of the stones in the item as related to the descriptiveSizeDimension.

values.label: Total Strength Product
values.definition: Indicates the total strength of a product.

values.label: Total Width Workbench
values.definition: Indicates the total width of the work surface of a workbench.

values.label: Towing Capacity
values.definition: the capacity measurement of that the trade item was designed to be able to pull or tow.

values.label: Tread Depth
values.definition: The measurement between the top of the tread rubber to the bottom of the tire's deepest grooves. Because it is difficult to accurately measure tread depth with a ruler, tread depth is best measured with a tire tread depth gauge.

values.label: Tread Width
values.definition: The measurement between the outboard and inboard edges of a new tire's tread design. Ideally it approximates the width of the tread that comes into contact with the road.

values.label: Tree Height  Stand Max
values.definition: Indicates the maximum tree height that is suitable for a stand such as a Christmas tree stand.

values.label: Turntable Diameter
values.definition: The diameter of the product’s turntable.

values.label: Tyre Rim Size
values.definition: The rim of a tyre carries different measures both width and depth to make a rim size. The calculation fits into a rim size that would be stated here, Examples 30c, 2.2, 3.0, 2.5

values.label: Tyre Size
values.definition: The size of the tyre there are various ways US, EU, ISO, Auto, Bicycle etc. For Example A bicycle tyre sequence: "28-622, 700 x 28C, 28 x 1 5/8 x 1 1/8" you at least have a useful deciphering reference. The rim diameter is 622mm and tyre outer diameter is around 700mm (the actual outer diameter will depend on the tyre's height). The tyre width is 28mm.

values.label: Usable Depth
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable depth of the product's inner rims when it is  placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The inner depth of a food storage container.

values.label: Usable Diameter
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable diameter of the product's inner rims when it is  placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: An inner section of a bowl or inner diameter of a flower pot.

values.label: Usable Height
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable height of the product's inner rim to the inner base when it is  placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The inner height of a food storage container.

values.label: Usable inner bottom depth
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable depth of the product's bottom inner rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The bottom inner depth of a food storage container.

values.label: Usable inner bottom diameter
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable diameter of the product's inner bottom rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: An inner bottom section of a bowl or inner bottom diameter of a flower pot.

values.label: Usable inner bottom width
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable width of the product's bottom inner rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The bottom inner width of a food storage container.

values.label: Usable Length
values.definition: Total length of the product minus the length of additional elements for its usage. Example: The length of a nail file rocky surface. Note: There are specific sizeTypeCodes for specific type of product lengths.

values.label: Usable Width
values.definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable width of the product's inner rims when it is  placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The inner width of a food storage container.

values.label: Vehicle Dry Weight
values.definition: Is the weight of a vehicle without any consumables, passengers, or cargo.

values.label: Volume Capacity
values.definition: The capacity measurement that the trade item was designed to hold. Example Toilets, Plumping, storage bins all have an amount of volume capacity. 4 Cubic Metres

values.label: Waist
values.definition: NOT AVAILABLE

values.label: Waist Width
values.definition: Measurement of width at the narrowest part of the item.

values.label: Watch Case Depth
values.definition: Measurement of the watch case as measured from the top of the bezel to the watch back.

values.label: Watch Case Height
values.definition: Measurement of the watch case as measured from the top most point (above the 12) to the lowest most point (below the 6).

values.label: Watch Case Width
values.definition: Measurement of the watch case as measured from the left most point (left of the9) to the right most point (right of the 3).

values.label: Watch Strap Length
values.definition: Measurement of the watch band/strap from tip to tip as laid flat.  If the band/strap is one piece, this is also known as the watch strap/band circumference.

values.label: Watch Strap Width
values.definition: Measurement of the watch band/strap width from side to side as laid flat.

values.label: Wheelbase
values.definition: Measurement of the distance between axles as measured from wheel to wheel.

values.label: Wheel Depth
values.definition: Measurement of depth of the wheel across the tread from left to right.

values.label: Wheel Diameter
values.definition: Measurement of the wheel across its face.

values.label: Width maximum
values.definition: Indicates the maximum width.

values.label: Window Drop Distance
values.definition: A method for controlling movement of a window glass in a vehicle using an electric motor associated with a drive mechanism through a cable.

values.label: Tool Table Length
values.definition: The length of a workbench.

values.label: Working Platform Length
values.definition: The length of the working platform.

values.label: Worktop Depth
values.definition: The depth of the worktop, countertop, tool table or head of  the product or integrated in the product (without accessories or attachments, e.g. rake ).

deprecated_values.label: Cookware Depth
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated in a future release. Please use code: HEIGHT_MAX. Measurement of depth of the cookware as measured from the rim to the bottom.

deprecated_values.label: Cookware Diameter
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated in a future release. Please use code: DIAMETER_MAX. Measurement of diameter of the cookware from rim to rim.

deprecated_values.label: Cookware First Handle Length
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated in a future release. Please use code: HANDLE_LENGTH. Measurement of length of the handle from its attachment point to the end of the handle.

values.label: Acne or blackheads
values.definition: The occurrence of inflamed or infected sebaceous glands in the skin; in particular, a condition characterized by red pimples on the face.

values.label: Anti-aging
values.definition: Product or technique designed to prevent the appearance of getting older.

values.label: Anti-cellulite
values.definition: Product intended to prevent or reduce cellulite.

values.label: Color/Pigmentation control
values.definition: A product which refines controls skin pigmentation disorders that affect the colour of your skin. Your skin gets its colour from a pigment called melanin.

values.label: Exfoliant
values.definition: A product for removing dead skin cells from the surface of your skin using a chemical, granular substance, or exfoliation tool.

values.label: Fine lines and wrinkles
values.definition: A product reducing fine lines and wrinkles, which are the depth of the crease in the skin. Fine lines are very mild, while wrinkles are deeper set.

values.label: General use
values.definition: A skin care product for general use that everyone can follow to keep their skin healthier or vibrant.

values.label: Lifting
values.definition: These non-invasive treatments can significantly rejuvenate the look and feel of the skin.* These innovative technologies works by delivering energy deep into the skin, naturally stimulating a healing response.* The body then develops new, fresh collagen that results in gradual lifting and tightening of the skin.

values.label: Lightening
values.definition: Practice of using chemical substances in an attempt to lighten the skin or provide an even skin colour by reducing the melanin concentration in the skin.

values.label: Milk substitute based
values.definition: A nut-based milk, like coconut, macadamia and tiger nuts are the best options for keeping inflammation down and your omega-6 levels in check. They contain a balanced ratio of omega-3:omega-6. 'Gluten-free oat milk is another dairy free alternative recommended for acne prone skin.

values.label: Moisturising
values.definition: Moisturiser is a cosmetic preparation used for protecting, moisturising, and lubricating the skin.

values.label: Nourishing
values.definition: A skin product that provides nutrition, vitamin replacement, or moisturising, for damaged or general skin care.

values.label: Other
values.definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Skin refinement/Pore management
values.definition: Skin refinement is a way of making more subtle changes to aging or sun-damaged skin.

values.label: Specific use
values.definition: Product was designed for a specific use.

values.label: Sun protection
values.definition: Product has ability to provide UV protection.

values.label: Superior hydration
values.definition: Hydrated can help maintain your skin's elasticity and combat the appearance of wrinkles. Improve the appearance of your skin.

values.label: A-Line
values.definition: Dress fitted at the hips and gradually widens towards the hem, giving the impression of the shape of a capital letter A.

values.label: Circular
values.definition: Skirt cut in sections to make one or more circles with a hole for the waist, so the skirt is very full but hangs smoothly from the waist without darts, pleats, or gathers.

values.label: Faux Wrap
values.definition: Dress that appears to cross in the front but is secured and not open.

values.label: Flared
values.definition: Dress that flairs out from the waist.

values.label: Full
values.definition: Skirt that fits loosely below the waistband.

values.label: Mermaid/Trumpet
values.definition: Skirt that fits snuggly at the knees and flares out below.

values.label: Skort

values.label: Straight

values.label: Tiered

values.label: Wrap
values.definition: To cover or surround, arrange or coil, to enclose or enfold around something such as a body, wrist etc. such as a bracelet, shawl or stole.

values.label: Alligator

values.label: Antelope
values.definition: A common name referring to many species of even-toed ruminant that are indigenous to various regions in Africa and Eurasia. Bovidae

values.label: Camel

values.label: Duckling

values.label: Starling

values.label: Thrush

A trade item delivered from a manufacturer to the retail selling floor that is not considered inventory and has no retail value.
The trade item is a unit which is designed to demonstrate the product to the end user or consumer.  For example a perfume tester, a lotion dispenser, or an air freshener sprayer/atomizer.

values.label: Dynamic assortment
values.definition: A trade item that comprises two or more different trade items, with a fixed total count, where the count of each trade item contained may change. Refer to the GS1 General Specification Section 2.1.1.7 for more information.

values.label: Eco Chèques
values.definition: Eco-chèques are an extra-legal benefit that employers can give to their employees and are intended to support the green economy by promoting the purchase of environmentally friendly, eco-designed and/or sustainable products.

values.label: Employee Meal Vouchers
values.definition: Employee meal-vouchers are an extra-legal benefit that employers can give to their employees that are intended for meals or food purchases in restaurants, grocery and convenience stores.

values.label: FSA Eligible
values.definition: The trade item is eligible to be sold to someone with a Flexible Spending Account (FSA).  FSAs are special accounts you put money into to pay for certain out-of-pocket health care costs.

values.label: Gift_With Purchase
values.definition: A trade item given to a consumer as part of a promotional event, contin-gent on the consumer making a purchase of another item or items. A Gift with Purchase is considered inventory and has no retail value.

values.label: HSA Eligible
values.definition: The trade item is eligible to be sold to someone with a Health Savings Account (HSA).  HSAs are special accounts a consumer puts money into to pay for certain out-of-pocket health care costs.

Limited Production Run by the Manufacturer/Supplier. This does not mean that retailers will order only once (not a one time buy product), retailers can order until the supplier runs out of stock. Those products are typically called one shot , limited edition.

values.label: Nonfunctioning_Display Unit
values.definition: Indicates that a trade item is a non-functioning Trade Item, used for display purposes only. Typically it is the shell of the trade item that it represents. Relevant to when the non-functioning Trade Item has to actually be ordered from the supplier.
Trade items purchased by a retailer for internal use only, not for sale to consumers.

values.label: Purchase_With Purchase
values.definition: A trade item sold to a consumer at a special price as part of a promotional event, contingent on the consumer purchasing another item or items. A Purchase with Purchase is considered inventory and has a retail value.

values.label: SNAP Eligible
values.definition: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) - SNAP offers nutrition assistance to millions of eligible, low-income individuals and families and provides economic benefits to communities. SNAP is the largest program in the US hunger safety net. The Food and Nutrition Service works with State agencies, nutrition educators, and neighbourhood and faith-based organisations to ensure that those eligible for nutrition assistance can make informed decisions about applying for the program and can access benefits. Products are set to be SNAP eligible.

values.label: Travel Size
values.definition: The item is specifically designed in size to be convenient for traveling.

values.label: Value Pack
values.definition: A trade item which is marketed as a value pack to the consumer by special markings on the package for example by printed wording "value pack". A value pack is a package containing multiple items (for example, tubes of toothpaste) that is less expensive than the same number of the items purchased singly or a trade item containing more net content for the same price than the original item. These items are not promotional products nor gadgets but are sold regularly.

values.label: WIC Eligible
values.definition: WIC - Women, Infants & Children WIC is administered by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). WIC gives access to healthy food, nutrition education and breastfeeding guidance. Pregnant, a caregiver, or a mom with a child under 5, can get the right personalized support for their family from products eligible to the WIC program.

values.label: Compressed Liquid
values.definition: A fluid under mechanical and or thermodynamic conditions that force it to be a liquid. It is a liquid at a temperature lower than the saturation temperature at a given pressure.

values.label: Chamois sponge
values.definition: A piece of a chamois leather full of small holes, wrapped around a super absorbent sponge, which can suck up liquid and is used for cleaning.

values.label: Melamine sponge
values.definition: A sponge made from melamine foam. Also known as wonder or magic sponge/eraser.

values.label: Scourer
values.definition: An object meant to be used to clean or wash by scrubbing vigorously. They are made of usually of metal (Stainless steel, copper, etc.) or plastic mesh. They are usually used to clean dirty cookware or a dirty oven.

values.label: Scouring pad
values.definition: A scouring pad is a small pad, sometimes flat used for scouring or scrubbing a surface.

values.label: Scrub sponge
values.definition: The product features two sides: a soft, spongy side, and a rougher, scrubber side. This has the benefit of offering two cleaning tools in one.

values.label: Soap pad
values.definition: A small pad of steel wool impregnated with soap.

values.label: Sponge
values.definition: A piece of a soft, light, porous absorbent substance originally consisting of the fibrous skeleton of an aquatic invertebrate but now usually made of synthetic material, used for washing and cleaning.

values.label: Active Workout
values.definition: Use during athletics or at the gym.

values.label: Arm Wrestling
values.definition: A trial of strength in which two people sit opposite each other with one elbow resting on a table, clasp each other's hands, and try to force each other's arm down onto the table.

values.label: Badmiton
values.definition: A game with rackets in which a shuttlecock is played back and forth across a net.

values.label: Baseball
values.definition: A ball game played between two teams of nine on a field with a diamond-shaped circuit of four bases.

values.label: Basketball
values.definition: A game played between two teams of five players in which goals are scored by throwing a ball through a netted hoop fixed above each end of the court.

values.label: Billiards
values.definition: A game usually for two people, played on a billiard table, in which three balls are struck with cues into pockets around the edge of the table.

values.label: Bocce
values.definition: An Italian game similar to lawn bowling but played on a shorter, narrower green.

values.label: Bowling
values.definition: The game of tenpin or candlepin bowling as a sport or recreation.

values.label: Boxing
values.definition: The sport or practice of fighting with the fists, especially with padded gloves in a roped square ring according to prescribed rules.

values.label: Car Racing
values.definition: A form of motorsport road racing which utilises sports cars that have two seats and enclosed wheels.

values.label: Climbing
values.definition: The sport or activity of ascending mountains or cliffs.

values.label: Cricket
values.definition: A bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven players on a field at the centre of which is a 20-metre (22-yard) pitch with a wicket at each end, each comprising two bails balanced on three stumps.

values.label: Cross Country
values.definition: Across fields or countryside, as opposed to on roads or tracks.

values.label: Cross-Training
values.definition: The action or practice of training or being trained in more than one role or skill.

values.label: Curling
values.definition: A game played on ice using round, flat stones that are slid across the surface toward a mark. Members of a team use brooms to sweep the surface of the ice in the path of the stone to control its speed and direction.

values.label: Cycling
values.definition: The sport or activity of riding a bicycle. Bicycle racing has three main forms: road racing (typically over long distances), track racing (on an oval track), and cyclocross (over rough, open country).

values.label: Dance
values.definition: Move rhythmically to music, typically following a set sequence of steps.

values.label: Darts
values.definition: An indoor game in which small pointed missiles with feather or plastic flights are thrown at a circular target marked with numbers in order to score points.

values.label: Eventing
values.definition: An equestrian sport in which competitors must take part in each of several contests, usually cross-country, dressage, and show jumping.

values.label: Field Hockey
values.definition: A game played between two teams of eleven players who use hooked sticks to drive a small hard ball toward goals at opposite ends of a field.

values.label: Football American
values.definition: A form of team game played with an oval ball on a field marked out as a gridiron. Points are scored mainly through touchdowns and field goals. Each side has eleven players on the field at any time.

values.label: Football soccer
values.definition: A game played by two teams of eleven players with a round ball that may not be touched with the hands or arms during play except by the goalkeepers. The object of the game is to score goals by kicking or heading the ball into the opponents' goal.

values.label: Golf
values.definition: A game played on a large open-air course, in which a small hard ball is struck with a club into a series of small holes in the ground, the object being to use the fewest possible strokes to complete the course.

values.label: Handball
values.definition: A team sport in which two teams of seven players each (six outfield players and a goalkeeper) pass a ball using their hands with the aim of throwing it into the goal of the other team.

values.label: Hiking
values.definition: Walk for a long distance, especially across country or in the woods.

values.label: Horse Racing
values.definition: The sport in which horses and their riders take part in races, typically with substantial betting on the outcome.

values.label: Hunting
values.definition: The activity of hunting wild animals or game, especially for food or sport.

values.label: Ice Hockey
values.definition: A fast contact sport played on an ice rink between two teams of six skaters, who attempt to drive a small rubber disk (the puck) into the opposing goal with hooked or angled sticks.

values.label: Lacrosse
values.definition: A team game in which the ball is thrown, caught, and carried with a long-handled stick having a curved L-shaped or triangular frame at one end with a piece of shallow netting in the angle.

values.label: Martial Arts
values.definition: Various sports or skills, mainly of Japanese origin, that originated as forms of self-defense or attack, such as judo, karate, and kendo.

values.label: Racquetball
values.definition: A sport played with a hollow rubber ball in anindoor or outdoor court.

values.label: Rowing
values.definition: The sport or pastime of propelling a boat by means of oars.

values.label: Running
values.definition: The action or movement of a runner.

values.label: Snow Boarding
values.definition: The sport or pastime of sliding downhill on a snowboard.

values.label: Snow Ski
values.definition: A recreational activity or a competitive winter sport in which the participant uses skis to glide on snow.

values.label: Softball
values.definition: A modified form of baseball played on a smaller field with a larger ball, seven rather than nine innings, and underarm pitching. The game evolved during the late 19th century from a form of indoor baseball.

values.label: Squash
values.definition: A ball sport played by two (singles) or four players (doubles squash) in a four-walled court with a small, hollow rubber ball. The players must alternate in striking the ball with their racquet and hit the ball onto the playable surfaces of the four walls of the court.

values.label: Strength Training
values.definition: A type of physical exercise specialising in the use of resistance to induce muscular contraction which builds the strength, anaerobic endurance, and size of skeletal muscles.

values.label: Swimming
values.definition: The sport or activity of propelling oneself through water using the limbs.

values.label: Tennis
values.definition: A game in which two or four players strike a ball with rackets over a net stretched across a court. The usual form (originally called lawn tennis ) is played with a felt-covered hollow rubber ball on a grass, clay, or artificial surface.

values.label: Track and Field
values.definition: Athletic events that take place on a running track and a nearby field; track events and field events.

values.label: Volleyball
values.definition: A game for two teams, usually of six players, in which a large ball is hit by hand over a high net, the aim being to score points by making the ball reach the ground on the opponent's side of the court.

values.label: Waterski
values.definition: Skim the surface of water on skis.

values.label: Wrestling
values.definition: The sport or activity of grappling with an opponent and trying to throw or hold them down on the ground, typically according to a code of rules.

values.label: Yoga
values.definition: A discipline,that includes breath control, simple meditation, and the adoption of specific bodily postures, is widely practiced for health and relaxation.

values.label: Storage Unspecified
values.definition: Applicable for goods in storage, irrespective of type of storage.

values.definition: Applicable for goods during air transport.

values.label: Transport inland water
values.definition: Applicable for goods being transported by inland water

values.label: Transport Rail

values.label: Transport Road

values.label: Transport Unspecified
values.definition: Applicable for goods being transported by unknown or irrelevant means.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Applicable for goods irrespective of transport or storage.

values.label: Chimney
values.definition: The product is stacked on a logistics unit in a pattern that has boxes inserted between the stacked layers or tiers to maximize the pallet configuration.

values.label: Column
values.definition: The product is stacked on a logistics unit in a column pattern.

values.label: Interlocking
values.definition: The product is stacked on a logistics unit in an interlocking pattern.

values.label: Aseptic filtering
values.definition: A mechanical sterilisation method where a fluid passes through a sterile filter which removes micro-organisms and is then poured into a pre-sterilised container under aseptic conditions.

values.label: Autoclave
values.definition: Autoclave (Steam) is a method of sterilisation that utilizes pressure and heat to achieve a sterile environment.

Beta particles are able to penetrate living matter to a certain extent (radiation intensity from a small source of radioactive material decreases as one over the distance squared) and can change the structure of struck molecules.

Gaseous chlorine dioxide systems for sterilization of healthcare products are not mutagenic or carcinogenic in humans. As the chlorine dioxide concentration increases, the time required to achieve sterilization becomes progressively shorter.

This method should be used only for materials that might be damaged by moist heat or that are impenetrable to moist heat (e.g., powders, petroleum products, sharp instruments). There are two types of dry-heat sterilizers: the static-air type and the forced-air type.

values.label: Electron_Beam Irradiation
values.definition: A commercially successful technology for sterilizing a variety of disposable medical devices with a wide range of densities. The e-beam inactivates micro-organisms either by causing microbial death as a direct effect of the destruction of a vital molecule or by an indirect chemical reaction. This is the same mechanism as in gamma irradiation, and the dose required is the same.

values.label: Ethanol
values.definition: A chemical sterilisation method that utilizes ethanol as the sterilisation method.

values.label: Eto_Ethylene Oxide
values.definition: A gas that is commonly used to sterilize objects sensitive to temperatures greater than 60 °C such as plastics, optics and electrics. Ethylene oxide treatment is generally carried out between 30 °C and 60 °C with relative humidity above 30% and a gas concentration between 200 and 800 mg/L for at least three hours. Ethylene oxide penetrates well, moving through paper, cloth, and some plastic films and is highly effective.

values.label: Formaldehyde
values.definition: A chemical sterilisation agent used to provide sterilisation. Items being sterilized are usually immersed in the formaldehyde for a pre determined time period.

Gamma rays are very penetrating and are commonly used for sterilisation of disposable medical equipment, such as syringes, needles, cannulas and IV sets. Gamma radiation requires bulky shielding for the safety of the operators; they also require storage of a radioisotope (usually Cobalt- 60), which continuously emits gamma rays (it cannot be turned off, and therefore always presents a hazard in the area of the facility).

values.label: Glutaraldehyde
values.definition: A colourless liquid with a pungent odour used to sterilize medical and dental equipment. It is also used for industrial water treatment and as a chemical preservative. Glutaraldehyde is an oily liquid at room temperature (density 1.06 g/mL), and miscible with water, alcohol, and benzene.
Pulsed light is a non-thermal sterilization method that uses brief intense pulses or flashes of white light to kill micro-organisms.

values.label: High_Level Disinfectant
values.definition: A germicide that inactivates all microbial pathogens, except small numbers of bacterial endospores.
Another chemical sterilizing agent. It is relatively non-toxic once diluted to low concentrations (although a dangerous oxidizer at high concentrations), and leaves no residue.
A sterilization process that uses liquid chemical as its sterilant to kill microorganisms.

Microwaves are used in medicine for disinfection of soft contact lenses, dental instruments, dentures, milk, and urinary catheters for intermittent self-catheterization. However, microwaves must only be used with products that are compatible (e.g., do not melt). Microwaves are radio-frequency waves, which are usually used at a frequency of 2450 MHz.
A sterilization process that uses nitrogen dioxide radicals that are formed from dinitrogen tetroxide dimers to kill microorganisms.

values.label: Not sterilised
values.definition: The product is not sterilised by the manufacturer.

values.label: No sterilisation required
values.definition: Sterilisation by a healthcare provider prior to use of the healthcare product is not required.

values.label: Ozone
values.definition: Is a method often times used in industrial settings to sterilize water and air, as well as a disinfectant for surfaces. It has the benefit of being able to oxidize most organic matter. It is a toxic and unstable gas that must be produced on-site, so it is not practical to use in many settings.

A chemical in the organic peroxide family. It is a bright, colorless liquid with a characteristic acrid acetic acid type odor. It has a strong oxidizing potential, is highly corrosive, and can explode at temperatures exceeding 110 °C.

values.label: Plasma
values.definition: A method of sterilisation that utilizes hydrogen peroxide vapour to sterilize heat sensitive equipment.

Sound waves of frequency >20,000 cycle/second kills bacteria and some viruses on exposing for one hour. High frequency sound waves disrupt cells. They are used to clean and disinfect instruments as well as to reduce microbial load.

values.label: Supercritical_Carbon Dioxide
values.definition: A sterilization process that uses supercritical carbon dioxide in combination with a small percentage of additive to kill microorganisms.

values.label: Unspecified
values.definition: Trade Item Manufacturer has not specified the sterilisation method(s) of the trade item.

Useful for sterilisation of surfaces and some transparent objects. Many objects that are transparent to visible light absorb UV. UV irradiation is routinely used to sterilize the interiors of biological safety cabinets between uses.

values.label: Previously Frozen

values.label: Soft-ripened Mould Rind
values.definition: Soft-ripened cheeses begin firm and rather chalky in texture, but are aged from the exterior inwards by exposing them to mould. The mould may be a velvety bloom of penicillium candida or P. camemberti that forms a flexible white crust and contributes to the smooth, runny, or gooey textures and more intense flavours of these aged cheeses. Brie and Camembert, the most famous of these cheeses.

values.label: Biodegradable
values.definition: The trade item is capable of degrading over time by exposure to the environment.

values.label: Carbon neutral
values.definition: Carbon neutral (or carbon-free) is removing the same amount of carbon dioxide as it's emitting into the atmosphere to achieve a net-zero carbon emission.

values.label: Circular economy
values.definition: The trade item is supporting circular economy, a system of production and consumption that tackles global challenges like climate change, biodiversity loss, waste, and pollution by involving reuse, repair, refurbish and recycle of existing materials and products for as long as possible.

values.label: Incinerable
values.definition: Capable of being incinerated or reduced to ashes.

values.label: Oxo-degradable
values.definition: A conventional plastic mixed with an additive to imitate biodegredation. Oxo-degradable plastics quickly fragment into smaller and smaller pieces, called microplastics, but don’t break down at the molecular or polymer level. The resulting microplastics are left in the environment indefinitely until they eventually fully break down.

values.label: Reusable
values.definition: Indicates the item can be used more than once.

deprecated_values.label: Recycled Material
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population. Trade item is made from recycled material based on target market regulations. In the recycling process waste products are recycled to their starting materials or into secondary raw materials. Recyclable materials include many kinds of glass, paper, metal, plastic, tires, textiles and electronics.

deprecated_values.label: Made From Renewable Material
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population. The trade item is made from materials which are considered to be renewable. A renewable resource material is an organic natural resource which can replenish to overcome usage and consumption, either through biological reproduction or other naturally reoccurring processes in a finite amount of time, for example wood.

deprecated_values.label: Made With Percent Renewable Wind Power
deprecated_values.definition: Note: This code is being deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please follow the migration for correct population. The trade item was made with wind power Instead of using electricity and other non-renewable energy resources to make.  Wind energy is a free and a renewable resource

Trade item where separate portions are made from new and recycled material. In the recycling process waste products are recycled to their starting materials or into secondary raw materials. Recyclable materials include many kinds of glass, paper, metal, plastic, tires, textiles and electronics.

values.label: Durability index
values.definition: The durability index indicates the level of repairability and reliability of the product. The criteria taken into account are defined by local regulations. For example, the availability of technical documents, the ease with which the product can be dismantled, the availability of spare parts, the resistance to stress and wear, the ease of maintenance and servicing, the existence of a commercial guarantee, etc.

values.label: Green-score
values.definition: The Green-score is a label that classes food products from A+ (low) to F (high) according to their impact on the environment. It is an experimental method developed by a consortium of food tech actors led by the French Ministry for Ecological Transition. The method is transparent and can be easily understood and applied by all stakeholders who wish to commit to environmental labeling for their products. It can be applied to both agro-industrial raw materials and processed or convenience foods.

values.label: Other sustainability score

This may be due to legal issues and/or local regulations pending (Example: Eco-score from France under litigation). Please work with a GS1 organisation to send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

values.label: Repairability index
values.definition: The repairability index indicates the level of repairability of the product. The criteria taken into account are defined by local regulations. For example, the availability of technical documents, the ease with which the product can be dismantled, the availability of spare parts, etc.

values.label: Aboveground
values.definition: An above-ground swimming pool is installed on the surface of the ground without the need for digging. It can be a frame or inflatable type of pool.

values.label: Frame
values.definition: A frame swimming pool is composed of a metal tube structure and a PVC pool liner. The metal tubes form a rigid frame that ensures the stability of the pool.

values.label: Inflatable
values.definition: An inflatable swimming pool is composed of modular structures made of flexible materials that fill with air. It is fully inflatable, with no liner, and relies on air pressure to maintain its structure.

values.label: Inflatable top ring
values.definition: An inflatable top ring swimming pool is an above-ground pool with a flexible, air-filled ring at the top that provides stablility. It does not require a metal frame. It can be considered a type of inflatable pool.

values.label: Inground
values.definition: An inground swimming pool is a structure designed to be fully embedded in the ground.

values.label: Semi-inground
values.definition: A semi-inground swimming pool is a hybrid type of pool that is partially buried in the ground and partially above ground.

values.label: Shell
values.definition: A shell swimming pool (also known as a monocoque pool) is a prefabricated, one-piece pool, usually made of fibreglass-reinforced polyester resin or composite material, delivered directly to the site and installed in a pre-dug hole.

values.label: Age
values.definition: The consumer usage criteria will be expressed as an age.

values.label: Height
values.definition: The consumer usage criteria will be expressed as a height.

values.label: Weight
